अदृश्य तां जनकसुतां सुपूजितां सुदुःखितः पतिगुणवेगवर्जिताम्
5.7.16.e: Then Hanuman moved about that cherished city ruled by the strength of arms of the tenheaded king. Unable to find venerable Sita, who was deprived of the benefit of her husband's virtuous proximity, he became deeply sad.

w: thinking of many things in his mind
of the followers of righteous path
5.7.17.t:
ततस्तदा बहुविधभावितात्मनः कृतात्मनो जनकसुतां सुवर्त्मनः ।
अपश्यतोऽभवदतिदुःखितं मनः सुचक्षुषः प्रविचरतो महात्मनः
5.7.17.e: Unable to find Sita, the disciplined and foresighted Hanuman, who always kept the righteous path, felt distressed while moving about, his mind oppressed by all kinds of thought. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये सुन्दरकाण्डे सप्तमस्सर्गः।। Thus ends the seventh sarga of Sundarakanda of the holy Ramayana, the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

w: rendered beautiful with gems and diamonds
adorned with latticed windows of barnished gold
5.8.1.t:
स तस्य मध्ये भवनस्य संस्थितं महद्विमानं मणिवज्रचित्रितम् ।
प्रतप्तजाम्बूनदजालकृत्रिमं ददर्श वीरः पवनात्मजः कपिः
5.8.1.e: The courageous son of the Windgod, Hanuman, the vanara saw the aerial chariot kept in the middle of the mansion inlaid with gems and diamonds latticed with artificial windows of barnished gold.

w: with images of incomparable beauty and immeasureable skill
which was placed in the aerial path
in the orbit of the Sun
5.8.2.t:
तदप्रमेयाप्रतिकारकृत्रिमं कृतं स्वयं साध्विति विश्वकर्मणा ।
दिवं गतं वायुपथप्रतिष्ठितं व्यराजतादित्यपथस्य लक्ष्मवत्
5.8.2.e: The immeasurable Pushpaka fashioned by Visvakarma with images of incomparable beauty was not possible to describe. An excellent  product of his achievement, it was placed in the aerial path appearing as a beaconlight (signpost) in the orbit of the Sun.

w: which can reach the places desired by the thought of its master
5.8.4.t:
तपः समाधानपराक्रमार्जितं मनः समाधानविचारचारिणम् ।
अनेकसंस्थानविशेषनिर्मितं ततस्ततस्तुल्यविशेषदर्शनम्
5.8.4.e: (The Pushpaka) was designed by dint of divine efforts and prowess (of Kubera). It could touch any place its master commanded with a cool mind. It had many beautiful places of rest.

5.8.5.t:
विशेषमालम्ब्य विशेषसंस्थितं विचित्रकूटं बहुकूटमण्डितम् ।
मनोऽभिरामं शरदिन्दुनिर्मलं विचित्रकूटं शिखरं गिरेर्यथा
5.8.5.e: The Pushpaka was specially designed in a unique manner. It was decorated with many colourful peaks. It was delghtful and pleasing to the mind and bright like the autumnal fullmoon. It looked like a mountain with many wonderful towers around.

w: with big rolling and frightening eyes
5.8.6.t:
वहन्ति यं कुण्डलशोभिताननाः महाशना व्योमचरा निशाचराः ।
विवृत्तविध्वस्तविशाललोचनाः महाजवा भूतगणाः सहस्रशः
5.8.6.e: The Pushpaka was borne by multitudes of Bhutas whose faces were shining with earrings, who were demons ranging in the night sky. They were gluttons endowed with great speed, and they had big, rolling and frightening eyes.

5.9.1.t:
तस्यालयवरिष्ठस्य मध्ये विपुलमायतं ।
ददर्श भवनश्रेष्ठं हनुमान्मारुतात्मजः
5.9.1.e: The son of the Windgod, Hanuman, saw a huge, spacious and excellent of all mansions in the centre of the palace.

5.9.2.t:
अर्धयोजनविस्तीर्णमायतं योजनं हि तत् ।
भवनं राक्षसेन्द्रस्य बहुप्रासादसङ्कुलम्
5.9.2.e: The mansion of the lord of demons was a conglomeration of palaces half a yojana long and half a yojana wide.

w: home of the lord of the ogres
5.9.4.t:
उत्तमं राक्षसावासं हनुमानवलोकयन् ।
आससादाथ लक्ष्मीवान् राक्षसेन्द्रनिवेशनम् चतुर्विषाणैर्द्विरदैस्त्रिविषाणैस्तथैव च ।
परिक्षिप्तमसम्बाधं रक्ष्यमाणमुदायुधैः
5.9.4.e: Searching the excellent residences of important demons, Hanuman finally reached  the palace of the lord of ogres guarded by armed demons with elephants with two or three or four tusks.

w: shaken by the force of the wind
5.9.6.t:
राक्षसीभिश्च पत्नीभी रावणस्य निवेशनम् ।
आहृताभिश्च विक्रम्य राजकन्याभिरावृतम् तन्नक्रमकराकीर्णं तिमिङ्गिलझषाकुलम् ।
वायुवेगसमाधूतं पन्नगैरिव सागरम्
5.9.6.e: Hanuman entered the palace of Ravana crowded with shedemons who were the wives of Ravana and the princesses brought by him after winning them in wars. To Hanuman, it looked like an ocean filled with crocodiles, sharks, whales, and a variety of fishes and snakes tossed by the force of the wind.

5.9.8.t:
या हि वैश्रवणे लक्ष्मीर्या चेन्द्रे हरिवाहने ।
सा रावणगृहे सर्वा नित्यमेवानपायिनी
5.9.8.e: Whatever wealth was possessed by Vaisravana (Kubera, the son of sage Vishrava) and also Indra who rides the Ucchaisrava green horse, was there in the palace of Ravana.

5.9.9.t:
या च राज्ञः कुबेरस्य यमस्य वरुणस्य च ।
तादृशी तद्विशिष्टा वा ऋद्धी रक्षोगृहेष्विह
5.9.9.e: The wealth stored in Ravana's palace was akin to what lay in the palaces of Kubera, Yama or Varuna, and ever more exquisite.

5.9.10.t:
तस्य हर्म्यस्य मध्यस्थं वेश्म चान्यत्सुनिर्मितं ।
बहुनिर्यूहसङ्कीर्णं ददर्श पवनात्मजः
5.9.10.e: Hanuman saw in the centre of that palace a complex of many wellbuilt houses.

w: decorated with all kinds of gems
5.9.11.t:
ब्रह्मणोऽर्थे कृतं दिव्यं दिवि यद्विश्वकर्मणा ।
विमानं पुष्पकं नाम सर्वरत्नविभूषितम् परेण तपसा लेभे यत्कुबेरः पितामहात् ।
कुबेरमोजसा जित्वा लेभे तद्राक्षसेश्वरः
5.9.11.e: There was a wonderful aerial chariot called Pushpaka embellished with all kinds of gems built by Visvakarma for Brahma. It was the same one that Kubera had won from his grandfather, the creator Brahma, through his supreme penance. The lord of ogres acquired it (as a memento for his victory) by defeating Kubera with his might.

w: made of Kartaswara and Hiranmaya two types of gold
5.9.13.t:
ईहामृगसमायुक्त्तै: कार्तस्वरहिरमण्मयैः ।
सुकृतैराचितं स्तम्भैः प्रदीप्तमिव च श्रिया मेरुमन्दरसङ्काशैरुल्लिखद्भिरिवाम्बरं ।
कूटागारैश्शुभाकारैस्सर्वतस्समलङ्कृतम्
5.9.13.e: It was supported by finely built pillars of two types of gold (Kartaswara and Hiranmaya) with images of wolves carved on them and blazing. It was tall as if scraping the sky and resembled mountains like Meru and Mandara. It was graced with multitudes of  auspicious and decorated pleasurehouses everywhere.

w: glowing like fire and the Sun
5.9.15.e: It was well built by Visvakarma and and had golden stairways, with radiant platforms glowing like fire and Sun.

w: platforms encrusted with saphires called Indraneela and Mahaneela.
5.9.16.e: It had latticed windows made of gold inlaid with crystals. The platforms were encrusted with saphires called Indraneela and Mahaneela appropriately.

5.9.17.t:
विद्रुमेण विचित्रेण मणिभिश्च महाघनैः ।
निस्तुलाभिश्च मुक्ताभिस्तलेनाभिविराजितम्
5.9.17.e: It was shining bright with colourful corals, precious gems and peerless pearls fixed on its floor.

5.9.20.t:
तत्रस्थस्स तदा गन्धं पानभक्ष्यान्नसम्भवम् ।
दिव्यं सम्मूर्छितं जिघ्रद्रूपवन्तमिवानिलम्
5.9.20.e: There he smelt the stupefying, unearthly odour of food and drink. He felt as though the fragrance had taken a potentially solid form. (Note: The wind has no form. But when he carried the aroma of food and drink it appeared like the personification of wind which could be smelt. गन्धवती पृथवी fragrance comes from earth पृथवीतत्त्व the poet transmits the same to the wind who has got only स्पर्श sense of touch).

5.9.22.t:
ततस्तां प्रस्थितश्शालां ददर्श महतीं शुभाम् ।
रावणस्य मनः कान्तां कान्तामिव वरस्त्रियम्
5.9.22.e: Then he proceeded to an auspicious hall, which was Ravana's favourite like his chief queen dear to his heart.

w: inlaid with silver set in ivory frame.
5.9.23.e: The stairways of the mansion were inlaid with special gems, windows were latticed with gold, floors were covered with crystals, figures of ivory with silver.

5.9.24.e: It was decorated with pillars of silver and gold inlaid with pearls and corals and gems.

5.9.25.e: It had highly ornamented pillars all over, some slightly bent and others straight. With lofty columns looking like wings it appeared as if the mansion had started on its journey to heaven.

w: having the garland of places and houses drawn on it
5.9.26.t:
महत्या कुथयास्तीर्णां पृथिवीलक्षणाङ्कया ।
पृथिवीमिव विस्तीर्णां सराष्ट्रगृहमालिनीम्
5.9.26.e: The floor was covered with a wide carpet spread from wall to wall with designs of different murals of many places and houses drawn in a row (garland like). The big carpet appeared like the expanse of earth itself.

w: inhabitted by the king of demons.
5.9.27.e: The mansion was resounding with the noise of birds singing in heat. It had wonderful fragrance. It was laid with exquisite tapestries and served as a dwelling place for the king of demons.

5.9.28.t:
धूम्रामगरुधूपेन विमलां हंसपाण्डुराम् ।
चित्रां पुष्पोपहारेण कल्माषीमिव सुप्रभाम्
5.9.28.e: It was smoky with fumes of agaru incence though spotless like a swan. It was colourful and radiant like Kamadhenu, the wishfulfilling cow, because of the offering of flowers.

5.9.29.t:
मनस्संह्लादजननीं वर्णस्यापि प्रसादिनीम् ।
तां शोकनाशिनीं दिव्यां श्रियः सञ्जननीमिव
5.9.29.e: (The mansion) was so full of effulgence and soul ravishing that it served as an adornment even to splendour. It looked as though it banished all sorrow and was a source of prosperity.

5.9.30.t:
इन्द्रियाणीन्द्रियार्थैस्तु पञ्च पञ्चभिरुत्तमैः ।
तर्पयामास मातेव तदा रावणपालिता
5.9.30.e: The chamber of Ravana, like a mother, gratified all the five senses of Hanuman with proper objects of the senses.

w: wearing clothes and garlands of different colours
5.9.34.e: He found thousands of beautiful women seated on carpets wearing different clothes and garlands and dressed in various attires.

5.9.36.t:
तत्प्रसुप्तं विरुरुचे निश्शब्दान्तरभूषणम् ।
निःशब्दहंसभ्रमरं यथा पद्मवनं महत्
5.9.36.e: Fast asleep, sounds of their ornaments silenced, the young women looked like a large bed of lotuses with swans and bees sitting calm without their usual noise.

5.9.38.t:
प्रबुद्धानीव पद्मानि तासां भूत्वा क्षपाक्षये ।
पुनस्संवृतपत्राणि रात्राविव बभुस्तदा
5.9.38.e: The faces of the women looked like blooming lotuses at daybreak, their petals closed up again at night.

5.9.39.t:
इमानि मुखपद्मानि नियतं मत्तषट्पदाः ।
अम्बुजानीव फुल्लानि प्रार्थयन्ति पुनः पुनः
5.9.39.e: The intoxicated bees would again and again long to enjoy these beautiful faces which were like blooming lotuses.

5.9.40.t:
इति चामन्यत श्रीमानुपपत्त्या महाकपिः ।
मेने हि गुणतस्तानि समानि सलिलोद्भवैः
5.9.40.e: The illustrious Hanuman felt it to be correct to compare those faces with lotuses for their fragrance.

5.9.41.t:
सा तस्य शुशुभे शाला ताभिस्त्रीभिर्विराजिता ।
शारदीव प्रसन्ना द्यौस्ताराभिरभिशोभिता
5.9.41.e: Brightened by (the beauty of) the maidens, the mansion shone like the autumnal sky endearing  and pleasing with stars.

5.9.42.t:
स च ताभिः परिवृतश्शुशुभे राक्षसाधिपः ।
यथा ह्युडुपतिश्शीमांस्ताराभिरभिसंवृतः
5.9.42.e: The lord of demons surrounded by women shone like the beautiful Moon encircled by stars.

5.9.43.t:
याश्च्यवन्तेऽम्बरात्ताराः पुण्यशेषसमावृताः ।
इमास्तास्सङ्गताः कृत्स्ना इति मेने हरिस्तदा
5.9.43.e: Seeing those women lying together Hanuman imagined them to be numerous meteors dropped from heaven after enjoying their merits, enjoyed and exhausted.

5.9.44.t:
ताराणामिव सुव्यक्तं महतीनां शुभार्चिषाम् ।
प्रभावर्णप्रसादाश्च विरेजुस्तत्र योषिताम्
5.9.44.e: It was clear that the grace and lustre of those women looked brilliant like the lustre and grace of brilliant stars releasing an auspicious glow.

w: had vermilion mark (on the forehead) smudged
5.9.46.e: A few young women had their circular vermilion mark (on the forehead) smudged, some had their anklets loosened and a few had their necklaces.

w: had broken pearl strings on girdle
5.9.47.t:
मुक्ताहाराऽवृताश्चान्याः काश्चिद्विस्रस्तवाससः ।
व्याविद्धरशनादामाः किशोर्य इव वाहिताः
5.9.47.e: Some had their strings of pearl broken, others had their clothes slipped off, and some had their waist belts snapped. They were like young mares fallen to rest after carrying heavy loads.

w: resembling the rays of the Moon
5.9.49.t:
चन्द्रांशुकिरणाभाश्च हाराः कासांचिदुत्कटाः ।
हंसा इव बभुस्सुप्ताः स्तनमध्येषु योषिताम्
5.9.49.e: The pearl chains, large and shining like rays of the Moon in the space between the breasts looked like sleeping swans.

w: crowded with swans and Karandava birds
5.9.51.t:
हंसकारण्डवाकीर्णाश्चक्रवाकोपशोभिताः ।
आपगा इव ता रेजुर्जघनैः पुलिनैरिव
5.9.51.e: Their hips were like river banks crowded with swans, karandava and Chakravaka birds shining like rivers.

w: tiny bells tied round the waist looking like buds
bold golden ornaments looking like lotuses
their amorous gestures of love play like crocodiles
5.9.52.t:
किङ्किणीजालसङ्कोशास्ता हैमविपुलाम्बुजाः ।
भावग्राहा यशस्तीराः सुप्ता नद्य इवाऽऽबभुः
5.9.52.e: With their tiny bells round their girdle looking like buds, the bold golden ornaments like lotuses, their gestures of love like crocodiles and their radiant beauty like silver banks, the women looked like smoky rivers.

w: and on the nipples of breasts
5.9.53.t:
मृदुष्वङ्गेषु कासाञ्चित्कुचाग्रेषु च संस्थिताः ।
बभुर्वर्भूषणानीव शुभा भूषणराजयः
5.9.53.e: The beautiful imprints made by the (heavy) ornaments on the tender limbs, breasts and nipples of some women appeared like many ornaments.

w: shaken by the breath released by their mouth
5.9.54.t:
अंशुकान्ताश्च कासाञ्चिन्मुखमारुतकम्पिताः ।
उपर्युपरि वक्त्राणां व्याधूयन्ते पुनः पुनः
5.9.54.e: Shaken by the breath released from their mouths the fringes of the garments of some women were drawn towards their faces again and againfluttering.

w: of the women of different beautiful hues
on the edges of their faces
5.9.55.t:
ताः पताका इवोद्धूताः पत्नीनां रुचिरप्रभाः ।
नानावर्णसुवर्णानां वक्त्रमूलेषु रेजिरे
5.9.55.e: The fringes of their garments glowing beautifully close to the faces of the wives (of Ravana) with different beautiful hues, shone splendid like flags.

w: by the touch of their breath
5.9.56.t:
ववल्गुश्चात्र कासांचित्कुण्डलानि शुभार्चिषाम् ।
मुखमारुतसंसर्गान्मन्दं मन्दं सुयोषिताम्
5.9.56.e: The eartops of some women endowed with auspicious charm were swinging softly generating a gentle sound by the touch of their breath.

w: the sweet smell of wine (made from sugarcane juice)
5.9.57.t:
शर्कराऽसवगन्धैश्च प्रकृत्या सुरभिः सुखः ।
तासां वदननिश्वासस्सिषेवे रावणं तदा
5.9.57.e: The sweet smell of wine emitted from their mouth and the natural fragrance of their breath was refreshing to Ravana  as if it was serving him at that time.

w: assuming it to be Ravana's face
5.9.58.t:
रावणाननशङ्काश्च काश्चिद्रावणयोषितः ।
मुखानि स्म सपत्नीनामुपाजिघ्रन्पुनः पुनः
5.9.58.e: Some women of Ravana (overcome by blind passion) smelt again and again the mouths of their cowives next to them  assuming it to be Ravana's.

5.9.59.t:
अत्यर्थं सक्तमनसो रावणे ता वरस्त्रियः ।
अस्वतन्त्राः सपत्नीनां प्रियमेवाऽचरंस्तदा
5.9.59.e: Even though the beautiful wives (should have been angry with their cowives for smelling their mouths) they behaved pleasingly, having no freedom to act with Ravana

5.9.60.t:
बाहूनुपनिधायान्याः पारिहार्यविभूषितान् ।
अंशुकानि च रम्याणि प्रमदास्तत्र शिश्यिरे
5.9.60.e: Some women slept pillowed on their arms, laying aside their adornments and others had their garment under the head as pillows and lay in sleep.

w: on thighs side hips and back on the lap of the other
lay intertwined one on the other.
5.9.62.e: Given to intoxication and sex, the women slept touching one another's thighs, sides, hips, back and lap of the other, with their limbs intertwined.

w: by the blowing of the wind
5.9.64.t:
लतानां माधवे मासि फुल्लानां वायुसेवनात् ।
अन्योन्य मालाग्रथितं संसक्तकुसुमोच्चयम् व्यतिवेष्टितसुस्कन्धमन्योन्यभ्रमराकुलम् ।
आसीद्वनमिवोद्धूतं स्त्रीवनं रावणस्य तत्
5.9.64.e: The women of Ravana appeared like a garden in spring. They were as if a cluster of creepers blossomed in spring due to the caresses of the breeze. They were knit together as one string forming a garland, flowers of one creeper striking the other. The joints of these creepers had grown strong when tangled together. Shaken by the breeze, the bees resting on one creeper would go to the other.

w: of ornaments garments limbs and garlands
5.9.66.t:
उचितेष्वपि सुव्यक्तं न तासां योषितां तदा ।
विवेकः शक्य आधातुं भूषणाङ्गाम्बरस्रजाम्
5.9.66.e: It was not possible to distinguish clearly between their jewels, limbs, garments and garlands and to place them in the right spots.

w: of royal sages ancestral gods and demons
5.9.68.t:
राजर्षिपितृदैत्यानां गन्धर्वाणां च योषितः ।
राक्षसानां च याः कन्यास्तस्य कामवशं गताः
5.9.68.e: The women halled from the families of royal sages, ancestral deities, daityas and demons who were infatuated with him.

w: on account of his love for war
5.9.69.t:
युद्धकामेन ताः सर्वा रावणेन हृताः स्त्रियः ।
समदा मदनेनैव मोहिताः काश्चिदागताः
5.9.69.e: Many were brought by Ravana as captives of war and some came on their own deluded by lust.

w: an unfit act not befitting a noble one
5.9.73.t:
पुनश्च सोऽचिन्तयादात्तरूपो ध्रुवं विशिष्टा गुणतो हि सीता ।
अथायमस्यां कृतवान्महात्मा लङ्केश्वरः कष्टमनार्यकर्म
5.9.73.e: Hanuman once again assuming his true form said to himself, 'Sita is surely a virtuous lady superior to and more distinguished than them all. Alas, this lord of Lanka committed an ignoble, act (by abducting her). इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये सुन्दरकाण्डे नवमस्सर्गः। Thus ends the ninth sarga of Sundarakanda of the holy Ramayana, the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

w: inlaid with colourful ivory and gold
5.10.1.t:
तत्र दिव्योपमं मुख्यं स्फाटिकं रत्नभूषितम् ।
अवेक्षमाणो हनुमान् ददर्श शयनासनम् दान्तकाञ्चनचित्राङ्गैर्वैडूर्यैश्च वरासनैः ।
महार्हास्तरणोपेतैरुपपन्नं महाधनैः
5.10.1.e: Looking around, Hanuman noticed a bed chamber, with a heavenly dais on which he saw a couch encrusted with crystals, vaidurya, and inlaid with colourful ivory and gold. It had an exquisite rich covering.

5.10.3.t:
तस्य चैकतमे देशे सोऽग्य्रमालाविभूषितम् ।
ददर्श पाण्डुरं छत्रं ताराधिपतिसन्निभम्
5.10.3.e: Hanuman saw an umbrella in one spot decorated with the best of garlands. The white umbrella looked like the Moon, lord of stars.

w: women holding fans made of the hair of chamari deer
spread with the best of bedspreads
5.10.4.t:
जातरूपपरिक्षिप्तं चित्रभानुसमप्रभम् ।
अशोकमालाविततं ददर्श परमासनम् वालव्यजनहस्ताभिर्वीज्यमानं समन्ततः ।
गन्धैश्च विविधैर्जुष्टं वरधूपेन धूपितम् परमास्तरणास्तीर्णमाविकाजिनसंवृतम् ।
दामभिर्वरमाल्यानां समन्तादुपशोभितम्
5.10.4.e: He saw an exquisite couch made of gold shining wonderfully like the Sun. It was decorated with ashoka flowers. Women were holding fans of chamari deer. It was upholstered with the best of bedspreads made of soft sheep skin and adorned with beautiful strings of flower garlands. Scented with aromatic smoke, it was refreshed with fragrance which had spread all over the place.

w: adorned in robes of silver texture
one who  could change form at free will
rich with trees and wild bushes
5.10.7.t:
तस्मिन् जीमूतसंकाशं प्रदीप्तोत्तमकुण्डलम् ।
लोहिताक्षं महाबाहुं महारजतवाससम् लोहितेनानुलिप्ताङ्गं चन्दनेन सुगन्धिना ।
सन्ध्यारक्तमिवाकाशे तोयदं सतटिद्गणम् वृतमाभरणैर्दिव्यैः सुरूपं कामरूपिणम् ।
सवृक्षवनगुल्माढ्यं प्रसुप्तमिव मन्दरम् क्रीडित्वोपरतं रात्रौ वराभरणभूषितम् ।
प्रियं राक्षसकन्यानां राक्षसानां सुखावहम् पीत्वाऽप्युपरतं चापि ददर्श स महाकपिः ।
भास्वरे शयने वीरं प्रसुप्तं राक्षसाधिपम्
5.10.7.e: Hanuman saw the mightyarmed, heroic lord of demons, sleeping with huge bloodshot eyes looking like a cloud, he was adorned with flashing earrings, and clad in robes of silver texture. His body was smeared with red sandal paste of sweet fragrance. Therefore, he looked like a cloud reddened by twilight and flashing with the lightning of his ornaments. He was handsome and could assume any form at will. He looked like Mandara mountain surrounded thickly with  trees and wild bushes. Decked with exquisite ornaments, he was sleeping after dalliance at night on that glittering couch. He was the beloved of the ogresses and bringer of joy to them

5.10.13.t:
अथाऽऽरोहणमासाद्य वेदिकाऽन्तरमाश्रितः ।
सुप्तं राक्षसशार्दूलं प्रेक्षते स्म महाकपिः
5.10.13.e: The great vanara ascended the stairway and reached another altar and once again looked at the sleeping Ravana, the tiger among demons.

w: like the pair of flag staff of Indra
torn by Iravata the vehicle of Indra
arms with scars caused by the thunderbolt of Indra
like the colour of the hare's blood
massaged by the best of women
which can make yakshas pannagas gandharvas gods and demons cry in terror
5.10.15.t:
काञ्चनाङ्गदसन्नध्दै च ददर्श स महात्मनः ।
विक्षिप्तौ राक्षसेन्द्रस्य भुजाविन्द्रध्वजोपमौ ऐरावतविषाणाग्रैरापीडनकृतव्रणौ ।
वज्रोल्लिखितपीनांसौ विष्णुचक्रपरिक्षतौ पीनौ समसुजातांसौ संगतौ बलसंयुतौ ।
सुलक्षणनखाङ्गुष्ठा स्वङ्गुलीतललक्षितौ संहतौ परिघाकारौ वृत्तौ करिकरोपमौ ।
विक्षिप्तौ शयने शुभ्रे पञ्चशीर्षाविवोरगौ शशक्षतजकल्पेन सुशीतेन सुगन्धिना ।
चन्दनेन परार्ध्येन स्वनुलिप्तौ स्वलङ्कृतौ उत्तमस्त्रीविमृदितौ गन्धोत्तमनिषेवितौ ।
यक्षपन्नगगन्धर्वदेवदानवराविणौ
5.10.15.e: Hanuman saw the great Ravana's arms, which were like a pair of Indra's flag staff adorned with golden straps. The arms bore the marks of wounds caused by Airavata, (Indra's elephant), torn by the thunderbolt of Indra in war, and wounded by the discus of Lord Visnu. His strong, fleshy, wellbuilt arms, having auspicious thumbnails, shapely fingers and palms, pressed together, resembled the iron crowbars or beam used for main doors. The arms resembled elephant's trunks, tossed on a clean bed, resembling two fivehooded snakes (fingers like hoods), besmeared with cool, fragrant, red sandalpaste of excellent quality which looked red like the hare's blood. They were well massaged  by the best of women with fine, fragrant sandal paste. They were the arms which could make yakshas, pannagas, gods and demons roar in fear at their sight.

5.10.21.t:
ददर्श स कपिस्तत्र बाहू शयनसंस्थितौ ।
मन्दरस्यांतरे सुप्तौ महाही रुषिताविव
5.10.21.e: The vanara, gazed at the arms of Ravana placed on the couch that appeared like two angry snakes asleep in a cave on (the lap) of mount Mandara.

5.10.22.t:
ताभ्यां स परिपूर्णाभ्यां भुजाभ्यां राक्षसेश्वरः ।
शुशुभेऽचलसङ्काशः शृङ्गाभ्यामिव मन्दरः
5.10.22.e: The lord of demons looked splendid like a mountain with his long, fully developed arms. He appeared like Mandara mountain with two lofty peaks.

w: of that of lion of demons
fragrance of Punnaga and Mango blossoms
and mixed with the fragrance of the best of Bakula flowers
mixed with aroma of rich food
and also of the aroma of drinks
5.10.23.t:
चूतपुन्नागसुरभिर्वकुलोत्तमसंयुतः ।
मृष्टान्नरससंयुक्तः पानगन्धपुरस्कृतः तस्य राक्षससिंहस्य निश्चक्राम महामुखात् ।
शयानस्य विनिःश्वासः पूरयन्निव तद् गृहम्
5.10.23.e: The breath released from the huge mouth of that lion of demons carried the fragrance of mango and punnaga as well as excellent Bakula flowers. It exuded the aroma of rich and delicious food and different drink. It was as though pervading the whole chamber.

w: of Ravana the lord of demons
smeared with bright red sandal paste
5.10.25.t:
मुक्तामणिविचित्रेण काञ्चनेन विराजितम् ।
मकुटेनापवृत्तेन कुण्डलोज्वलिताननम् रक्तचन्दनदिग्धेन तथा हारेण शोभिना ।
पीनायतविशालेन वक्षसाऽभिविराजितम् पाण्डरेणापविद्धेन क्षौमेण क्षतजेक्षणम् ।
महार्हेण सुसंवीतं पीतेनोत्तमवाससा माषराशिप्रतीकाशं निश्श्वसन्तं भुजङ्गवत् ।
गाङ्गे महति तोयान्ते प्रसुप्तमिव कुञ्जरम् चतुर्भिः काञ्चनैर्दीपैद्धीप्यमानचतुर्दिशम् ।
प्रकाशीकृतसर्वाङ्गं मेघं विद्युद्गणैरिव पादमूलगताश्चापि ददर्श सुमहात्मनः ।
पत्नी: स प्रियभार्यस्य तस्य रक्षःपतेर्गृहे
5.10.25.e: Hanuman saw Ravana, whose face was lit up by his earrings. His shining headgear studded with gold and pearls was set aside. His fleshy, broad chest on which the pearl necklace had slightly receded from its position(as he was asleep)  was shining along with the red sandal paste. He had put on a splendid white silken cloth which had also slipped a little and was covered with exquisitely  rich yellow upper garment. His eyes were bloodred. His body was comparable to a heap of blackbeans. He was sighing heavily like a hissing snake. He appeared like an elephant sleeping on the banks of the great river Ganges. With four golden lamps glowing on four sides of the bed,the four directions were illuminated. All his limbs lit up bright (with the glow of lamps), he looked like a cloud with streaks of lightning. His dear wives were seen resting at his feet in the palace of the lord of demons.

w: women with faces splendid like the Moon
wearing ever fresh garlands of flowers
5.10.31.e: Hanuman, the leader of vanaras found the wives of Ravana,  whose  faces were bright as the Moon, adorned with beautiful earrings and fresh floral garlands.

w: women proficient in dancing and playing musical instruments
resting on his arms and lap
5.10.32.t:
नृत्तवादित्रकुशला राक्षसेन्द्रभुजाङ्कगाः ।
वराभरणधारिण्यो निषण्णा ददृशे हरिः
5.10.32.e: Hanuman saw  the women there wearing fine jewellery, performing dances, playing musical instruments, and resting on the lap or leaning on the arms of the demon king.

5.10.34.e: There the beautiful moonlike faces of women Illumined by the lovely earrings lay on the cot which looked resplendent like the sky lit up with hosts of stars.

5.10.35.t:
मदव्यायामखिन्नास्ता राक्षसेन्द्रस्य योषितः ।
तेषु तेष्ववकाशेषु प्रसुप्तास्तनुमध्यमाः
5.10.35.e: Exhausted by drinking and indulging in amorous sport, the consorts of Ravana slept here and there with their visible slender waists.

w: held her limbs in a dance posture
5.10.36.e: Another woman exceedingly beautiful and a delicate danseuse of beautiful complexion and rhythmic movements held her limbs in a dancing posture (though asleep) due to her habit .

5.10.37.t:
काचिद्वीणां परिष्वज्य प्रसुप्ता सम्प्रकाशते ।
महानदीप्रकीर्णेव नलिनी पोतमाश्रिता
5.10.37.e: Another woman slept hugging her veena. She shone like a lotus plant flung in a large river, clinging on to a boat. (Veena is compared to a boat and the woman to a lotusplant in the ambience of flowing waters of the river. The entire hall had put up such a dynamic view showing hectic life of the inmates).

5.10.38.t:
अन्या कक्षगतेनैव मड्डुकेनासितेक्षणा ।
प्रसुप्ता भामिनी भाति बालपुत्रेव वत्सला
5.10.38.e: A woman with dark eyes asleep with a drum placed in her armpit looked like a beautiful mother holding her loving baby (the drum was hung to her arm with a rope).

5.10.39.t:
पटहं चारुसर्वाङ्गी पीड्य शेते शुभस्तनी ।
चिरस्य रमणं लब्ध्वा परिष्वज्येव भामिनी
5.10.39.e: Another charming beauty endowed with beautiful breasts lay hugging a tambourine as though a passionate woman lay embracing her lover whom she secured after a long time.

5.10.40.t:
काचिद्वंशं परिष्वज्य सुप्ता कमललोचना ।
रहः प्रियतमं गृह्य सकामेव च कामिनी
5.10.40.e: Yet another lotuseyed lady slept embracing a lute as if a lovelorn woman lay clasping her lover.

5.10.41.t:
विपञ्चीं परिगृह्यान्या नियता नृत्तशालिनी ।
निद्रावशमनुप्राप्ता सह कान्तेव भामिनी
5.10.41.e: Another selfpossessed lady, graceful in dance, holding a sevenstringed lute  was as though lying asleep with her beloved.

5.10.42.t:
अन्या कनकसङ्काशैर्मृदुपीनैर्मनोरमैः ।
मृदङ्गं परिपीड्याङ्गैः प्रसुप्ता मत्तलोचना
5.10.42.e: Another lady with drunken eyes lay fast asleep holding a drum close to her beautiful bosom with her soft limbs. (These images show that these women were singing and dancing till late night and slept exhausted).

5.10.44.t:
डिण्डिमं परिगृह्यान्या तथैवासक्तडिण्डिमा ।
प्रसुप्ता तरुणं वत्समुपगूह्येव भामिनी
5.10.44.e: One lovely woman and another held a drum and slept as if they were hugging their young child.

5.10.45.t:
काचिदाडम्बरं नारी भुजसंयोगपीडितम् ।
कृत्वा कमलपत्राक्षी प्रसुप्ता मदमोहिता
5.10.45.e: Yet another with her eyes like lotus petals deluded with passion tightly held in her arms a musical instrument known as Adambaram and slept.

5.10.47.t:
पाणिभ्यां च कुचौ काचित्सुवर्णकलशोपमौ ।
उपगूह्याबला सुप्ता निद्राबलपराजिता
5.10.47.e: Overcome with sleep another woman lay pressing with her own hands her golden gobletlike breasts.

5.10.48.t:
अन्या कमलपत्राक्षी पूर्णेन्दुसदृशानना ।
अन्यामालिङ्ग्य सुश्रोणीं प्रसुप्ता मदविह्वला
5.10.48.e: One woman with eyes like lotus petals and face like the fullmoon embraced another young woman of beautiful hips  and slept tipsy with drink.

5.10.49.t:
आतोद्यानि विचित्राणि परिष्वज्य वरस्त्रियः ।
निपीड्य च कुचैस्सुप्ता कामिन्यः कामुकानिव
5.10.49.e: Some charming maidens held wonderful musical instruments pressing against their bosom and slept like passionate women embracing their loved ones.

5.10.50.t:
तासामेकान्तविन्यस्ते शयानां शयने शुभे ।
ददर्श रूपसम्पन्नामपरां स कपिः स्त्रियम्
5.10.50.e: Hanuman saw some maidens lying on separate excellent beds, women richly  endowed with beautysleeping.

5.10.51.t:
मुक्तामणिसमायुक्तैर्भूषणैः सुविभूषिताम् ।
विभूषयन्तीमिव तत्स्वश्रिया भवनोत्तमम् गौरीं कनकवर्णाभामिष्टामन्तः पुरेश्वरीम् ।
कपिर्मन्दोदरीं तत्र शयानां चारुरूपिणीम्
5.10.51.e: Then the vanara saw  a very beautiful woman of golden complexion decked with pearls and gems and with ornaments as if illuminating the excellent mansion with her splendour She was the king's favourite and the chief queen, Mandodari.

w: by the wealth of her beauty and charm
5.10.53.t:
स तां दृष्ट्वा महाबाहुर्भूषितां मारुतात्मजः ।
तर्कयामास सीतेति रूपयौवनसम्पदा ।
 ।
.. ।
हर्षेण महता युक्तो ननन्द हरियूथपः ।
5.10.53.e: On seeing her embellished with ornaments, beauty and charm, the long armed son of the Windgod, the chief of the vanaras thought her to be Sita and rejoiced.

5.10.54.t:
आस्फोटयामास चुचुम्ब पुच्छं ननन्द चिक्रीड जगौ जगाम ।
स्तम्भानरोहन्निपपात भूमौ निदर्शयन् स्वां प्रकृतिं कपीनाम्
5.10.54.e: He rejoiced clapping his palms, kissing his tail and jumping up, climbing up the pillars and jumping down on the ground in joy. Thus he exhibited his monkey nature. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये सुन्दरकाण्डे दशमस्सर्गः। Thus ends the tenth sarga of Sundarakanda of the holy Ramayana, the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

w: eager for the sight of Sita
5.11.3.1.t:
अन्येयमिति निश्चित्य भूयस्तत्र चचार सः ।
पानभूमौ हरिश्रेष्ठः सीतासंदर्शनोत्सुकः
5.11.3.1.e: Concluding that this was another woman, the best of monkeys, eager for the sight of Sita, ranged once more through the drinking hall.

w: worn out due to continuous drinking.
5.11.4.t: क्रीडितेनापराः क्लान्ता गीतेन च तथाऽपराः नृत्तेन चापराः क्लान्ताः पानविप्रहतास्तथा ।
5.11.4.e: Some women were fatigued after sporting, similarly some were exhausted after singing. Others were tired through dancing and some were worn out by continuous drinking.

w: acquainted with the appropriateness of time and place
5.11.6.t:
अङ्गनानां सहस्रेण भूषितेन विभूषणैः रूपसल्लापशीलेन युक्तगीतार्थभाषिणा ।
देशकालाभियुक्तेन युक्तवाक्याभिधायिना रताभिरतसंसुप्तं ददर्श हरियूथपः ।
5.11.6.e: The monkey leader saw thousands of  beautiful women asleep after long dalliance. Some of them were adorned with ornaments, some were good at arguments and versed in the appreciation of songs, some were aware of the appropriate time and place and some were adept in right expressions.

5.11.8.t: तासां मध्ये महाबाहुः शुशुभे राक्षसेश्वरः गोष्ठे महति मुख्यानां गवां मध्ये यथा वृषः ।
5.11.8.e: In the midst of these women the longarmed lord of demons shone like a (majestic) bull in a big cowshed.

5.11.9.t: स राक्षसेन्द्रः शुशुभे ताभिः परिवृतस्स्वयम् करेणुभिर्यथाऽरण्ये परिकीर्णो महाद्विपः ।
5.11.9.e: Surrounded by the women, the demon king shone like a proud elephant attended by many female elephants scattered in a dense forest.

5.11.10.t: सर्वकामैरुपेतां च पानभूमिं महात्मनः ददर्श हरिशार्दूलस्तस्य रक्षःपतेर्गृहे ।
5.11.10.e: The tiger among vanaras saw at the great Ravana's palace a drinking place where everything one desires was provided.

5.11.12.t: रौक्मेषु च विशालेषु भाजनेष्वर्धभक्षितान् ददर्श हरिशार्दूलो मयूरान् कुक्कुटांस्तथा ।
5.11.12.e: The tiger among vanaras also saw there meat of peacocks and chicken placed in large golden vessels, some half eaten.

w: seasoned with sour and salty ingredients
with those drinks spilt from the glasses
5.11.16.t:
तथाऽऽम्ललवणोत्तंसैर्विविधैरागषाडबैः ।
हारनूपुरकेयूरैरपविद्धैर्महाधनैः पानभाजनविक्षिप्तैः फलैश्च विविधैरपि ।
कृतपुष्पोपहारा भूरधिकं पुष्यति श्रियम्
5.11.16.e: The banquet hall looked splendid with food seasoned with salt and sour ingredients. There was ragashadavas (syrup made with grapes, pomegranates, different juices like half ripe mangoes and seasoned with ginger cardomom, butter etc). Heavy chains, anklets and shouldersstraps were thrown aside. (The people relaxed while eating and drinking and discarded heavy ornaments). Many glasses were found scattered or drinks spilt on the floor after use.Many fruits and flowers were kept.

5.11.18.t:
तत्र तत्र च विन्यस्तै: सुश्लिष्टैश्शयनासनैः ।
पानभूमिर्विना वह्निं प्रदीप्तेवोपलक्ष्यते
5.11.18.e: Good couches and different kinds of seats were wellarranged in the banquet hall. The place appeared as if it was glowing witout fire.

w: by those seasoneed with many types of ingredients
5.11.19.e: In the banquet hall there were many types of meat arranged in a number of ways. They were cooked by experts by seasoning them with choicest ingredients.

w: sugercanejuices honey juices made from flowers and fruits
5.11.20.t:
दिव्याः प्रसन्ना विविधाः सुराः कृतसुरा अपि ।
शर्कराऽसवमाध्वीकपुष्पासवफलासवाः वासचूर्णैश्च विविधैर्मृष्टास्तैस्तैः पृथक् पृथक् ।
5.11.20.e: There were many types of wonderful and pleasing wine extracted from sugarcane, honey , fruits and flowers. They were good even though fermented and made delicious by seasoning with aromatic spices.

5.11.21.t:
सन्तता शुशुभे भूमिर्माल्यैश्च बहुसंस्थितैः हिरण्मयैश्च विविधैर्भाजनैः स्फाटिकैरपि ।
जाम्बूनदमयैश्चान्यैः करकैरभिसंवृता
5.11.21.e: (The banquet hall) appeared beautiful with many kinds of garlands arranged in different locations. Also there were vessels made of pure gold, crystalware and jars spread all over.

w: in those made of pure gold
5.11.23.t:
राजतेषु च कुम्भेषु जाम्बूनदमयेषु च ।
पानश्रेष्ठं तदा भूरि कपिस्तत्र ददर्श ह
5.11.23.e: Hanuman saw the best of wines in large quantities kept in silver and pure gold pots.

5.11.25.t:
क्वचिदल्पावशेषाणि क्वचित्पीतानि सर्वशः ।
क्वचिन्नैव प्रपीतानि पानानि स ददर्श ह
5.11.25.e: He saw wine jars at one place, some fully drained, and at another place not touched at all.

5.11.26.t:
क्वचिद् भक्ष्यांश्च विविधान् क्वचित्पानानि भागशः ।
क्वचिदन्नावशेषाणि पश्यन्वै विचचार ह
5.11.26.e: He moved about looking at different types of eatables and drinks arranged separately along with the left over food.

5.11.28.t:
शयनान्यत्र नारीणां शुभ्राणि बहुधा पुनः ।
परस्परं समाश्लिष्य काश्चित्सुप्ता वराङ्गनाः
5.11.28.e: Hanuman saw many beds some unused and some occupied by lovely women sleeping, embracing one another.

w: covering their bodies with the same
5.11.29.t:
काश्चिच्च वस्त्रमन्यस्यास्स्वपन्त्याः परिधाय च ।
आहृत्य चाबलाः सुप्ता निद्राबलपराजिताः
5.11.29.e: Overcome with sleep some women pulled clothes of other women and covered their bodies with them.

5.11.30.t:
तासामुच्छवासवातेन वस्त्रं माल्यं च गात्रजम् ।
नात्यर्थं स्पन्दते चित्रं प्राप्य मन्दमिवानिलम्
5.11.30.e: The lovely clothes and garlands on the bodies of women were moving mildly by their exhalations as if shaken by the gentle breeze.

5.11.31.t:
चन्दनस्य च शीतस्य शीधोर्मधुरसस्य च ।
विविधस्य च माल्यस्य धूपस्य विविधस्य च बहुधा मारुतस्तत्र गन्धं विविधमुद्वहन् ।
5.11.31.e: With the many scents of cool sandal, of sweetsmelling wines of diverse kinds, as well as flower garlands of several types and of incense burning in that hall, the cool wind blew spreading several fragrances all over.

w: in the abode of the ogres
5.11.33.t: श्यामावदातास्तत्रान्याः काश्चित्कृष्णा वराङ्गनाः काश्चित् काञ्चनवर्णाङ्ग्यः प्रमदा राक्षसालये ।
5.11.33.e: There in the demons abode were women who were fair, some lovely with dark and others with golden complexion.

5.11.34.t: तासां निद्रावशत्वाच्च मदनेन विमूर्छितम् पद्मिनीनां प्रसुप्तानां रूपमासीद्यथैव हि ।
5.11.34.e: Withered due to indulgence in sex they were overcome with sleep. The charm of the women was like the lotus creepers with closed lotuses .

w: thinking that he transgressed the moral code
5.11.36.t: निरीक्षमाणश्च तदा ताः स्त्रियः स महाकपिः जगाम महतीं चिन्तां धर्मसाध्वसशङ्कितः ।
5.11.36.e: The great monkey was very much worried as he thought he had transgressed the moral code by watching the women.

w: of the inner chambers of others' wives
5.11.37.t: परदारावरोधस्य प्रसुप्तस्य निरीक्षणम् इदं खलु ममात्यर्थं धर्मलोपं करिष्यति ।
5.11.37.e: 'Observing the wives of others in this manner in their inner chambers very much amounts to transgression of moral code  by me'. ( thought he)

5.11.38.t: न हि मे परदाराणां दृष्टिर्विषयवर्तिनी अयं चात्र मया दृष्टः परदारापरिग्रहः ।
5.11.38.e: 'I did see these wives of another, but not with a sensual mind. I have only seen them but not with foul intention'.

w: struck with a bright idea in a single direction
the decision regarding the task ahead
5.11.39.t: तस्य प्रादुरभूच्चिन्ता पुनरन्या मनस्विनः निश्चितैकान्तचित्तस्य कार्यनिश्चयदर्शिनी ।
5.11.39.e: Another  bright idea struck the highly sensible Hanuman, who had a clear vision of the task ahead-- 'I was firm and singleminded in my direction regarding the task ahead' (thought he).

w: are seen indeed without any foul desire
5.11.40.t: कामं दृष्टा मया सर्वा विश्वस्ता रावणस्त्रियः न हि मे मनसः किञ्चिद्वैकृत्यमुपजायते ।
5.11.40.e: 'It is true I saw all the loyal wives of Ravana but without any foul desire. Indeed in my mind no passionate feeling was ever aroused'.

5.11.41.t: मनो हि हेतुः सर्वेषामिन्द्रियाणां प्रवर्तने शुभाशुभास्ववस्थासु तच्च मे सुव्यवस्थितम् ।
5.11.41.e: 'Mind propels the sense organs to do good or bad deeds. (But) my mind is firmly esatablished in righteousness'.

5.11.43.t:
यस्य सत्त्वस्य या योनिस्तस्यां तत्परिमार्ग्यते ।
न शक्या प्रमदा नष्टा मृगीषु परिमार्गितुम्
5.11.43.e: 'One has to search a creature among its own species. It is not possible to find a lost woman in the herd of female deer'.

5.11.44.t: तदिदं मार्गितं तावच्छुद्धेन मनसा मया रावणान्तःपुरं सर्वं दृश्यते न तु जानकी ।
5.11.44.e: 'I searched all over Ravana's harem with a pure mind but I have not seen Janaki'.

5.11.47.t: स भूयस्तु परं श्रीमान् मारुतिर्यत्नमास्थितः आपानभूमिमुत्सृज्य तद्विचेतुं प्रचक्रमे ।
5.11.47.e: Illustrious Hanuman left the banquet hall to renew his effort in search of Sita. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये सुन्दरकाण्डे एकादशस्सर्गः।। Thus ends the eleventh sarga of Sundarakanda of the holy Ramayana, the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

w: who wishes to protect her chastity
5.12.3.t:
सा राक्षसानां प्रवरेण जानकी स्वशीलसंरक्ष्णतत्परा सती ।
अनेन नूनं प्रति दुष्टकर्मणा हता भवेदार्यपथे परे स्थिता
5.12.3.e: 'Janaki, follower of noble path, anxious to protect her chastity must have been killed by the wicked demon king.

5.12.4.t:
विरूपरूपा विकृता विवर्चसो महानना दीर्घविरूपदर्शनाः ।
समीक्ष्य सा राक्षसराजयोषितो भयाद्विनष्टा जनकेश्वरात्मजा
5.12.4.e: 'The daughter of Janaka might have collapsed out of fear, looking at the distorted faces of ugly, tall and monstrous demon maids of Ravana.

5.12.5.t:
सीतामदृष्ट्वा ह्यनवाप्य पौरुषं विहृत्य कालं सह वानरैश्चिरम् ।
न मेऽस्ति सुग्रीवसमीपगा गतिः सुतीक्ष्णदण्डो बलवांश्च वानरः
5.12.5.e: 'I have spent a long time with vanaras. I have not  succeded in my efforts to find Sita. I dare not see Sugriva now without finding Sita and without fulfilling my task. Sugriva will punish me severely. There is no way out.'

5.12.6.t:
दृष्टमन्तःपुरं सर्वं दृष्टा रावणयोषितः ।
न सीता दृश्यते साध्वीवृथा जातो मम श्रमः
5.12.6.e: 'I have searched all over the harem. Ravana's women have been seen. (Yet) I have not been able to see noble Sita. My efforts have been wasted'.

5.12.7.t:
किं नु मां वानराः सर्वे गतं वक्ष्यन्ति सङ्गताः ।
गत्वा तत्र त्वया वीर किं कृतं तद्वदस्व नः
5.12.7.e: 'What will the vanaras say when I return? What should I speak when they ask me: O hero, what did you accomplish there?'

5.12.9.t:
किं वा वक्ष्यति वृद्धश्च जाम्बवानाङ्गदश्च सः ।
गतं पारं समुद्रस्य वानराश्च समागताः
5.12.9.e: 'What will the elderly Jambavan say? What will young prince Angada and other vanaras collected there say when I reach the seashore to meet them'.

5.12.10.t:
अनिर्वेदः श्रियो मूलमनिर्वेदः परं सुखम् ।
अनिर्वेदो हि सततं सर्वार्थेषु प्रवर्तकः
5.12.10.e: Wise Hanuman once again declared, 'being free from despair is the root cause of prosperity. Freedom from despondency gives supreme happiness and leads to success'.

5.12.11.t:
करोति सफलं जन्तोः कर्म यत्तत्करोति सः ।
तस्मादनिर्वेदकृतं यत्नं चेष्टेऽहमुत्तमम् भूयस्तावद्विचेष्यामि देशान्रावणपालितान् ।
5.12.11.e: 'The action of a living being certainly bears fruit. Therefore, I shall put forth my best effort without feeling despondent. I will once again search everywhere in Lanka ruled  by Ravana'.

w: paths through the gardens and mansions female apartments
5.12.12.t:
आपानशाला विचितास्तथा पुष्पगृहाणि च चित्रशालाश्च विचिता भूयः क्रीडागृहाणि च ।
निष्कुटान्तररथ्याश्च विमानानि च सर्वशः
5.12.12.e: 'I have searched the banquet halls, bowers of creepers, picture galleries and gymnasiums. I have searched everywhere through the paths of gardens and mansions, harems and the Pushpaka chariot also.

5.12.15.t:
उत्पतन्निष्पतंश्चापि तिष्ठन्गच्छन् पुनः पुनः ।
अपावृण्वंश्च द्वाराणि कवाटान्यवघाटयन् प्रविशन्निष्पतंश्चापि प्रपतन्नुत्पतन्नपि ।
सर्वमप्यवकाशं स विचचार महाकपिः
5.12.15.e: The great vanara searched all over again and again jumping up and down, stopping for a while and moving, opening and closing doors, by crossing, entering and exiting, jumping up and down. Thus he moved about and searched whereever there was scope to search

5.12.17.t:
चतुरङ्गुलमात्रोऽपि नावकाशः स विद्यते ।
रावणान्तःपुरे तस्मिन् यं कपिर्न जगाम सः
5.12.17.e: Even a space of four fingers in the inner chambers of Ravana was not left out in his search for Sita.

5.12.18.t:
प्राकारान्तररथ्याश्च वेदिकाश्चैत्यसंश्रयाः ।
दीर्घिकाः पुष्करिण्यश्च सर्वं तेनावलोकितम्
5.12.18.e: He moved in the lanes inside the boundary walls, around the shrines, altars, wells and tanks whereever it was possible to look for.

5.12.19.t:
राक्षस्यो विविधाकारा विरूपा विकृतास्तथा ।
दृष्टा हनुमता तत्र न तु सा जनकात्मजा
5.12.19.e: Hanuman could see only ogresses of different typesugly, deformed but could not find the daughter of Janaka.

5.12.20.t:
रूपेणाप्रतिमा लोके वरा विद्याधरस्त्रियः ।
दृष्टा हनुमता तत्र न तु राघवनन्दिनी
5.12.20.e: Hanuman could see even the women of vidyadharas who were matchless in beauty among women in the world but not Janaki the beloved of Raghava.

5.12.21.t:
नागकन्या वरारोहाः पूर्णचन्र्दनिभाननाः ।
दृष्टा हनुमता तत्र न तु सीता सुमध्यमा
5.12.21.e: Hanuman could see there moonfaced daughters of nagas with charming limbs but not the slimwaisted Sita.

5.12.23.t:
सोऽपश्यंस्तां महाबाहुः पश्यंश्चान्या वरस्त्रियः ।
विषसाद मुहुर्धीमान् हनुमान् मारुतात्मजः
5.12.23.e: The longarmed Hanuman, son of the Windgod was able to see other great women but not Sita. So he became despondent.

5.12.24.t:
उद्योगं वानरेन्द्राणां प्लवनं सागरस्य च ।
व्यर्थं वीक्ष्यानिलसुतश्चिन्तां पुनरुपागमत्
5.12.24.e: The son of the Wind god, the great monkey realised the futility of his efforts in crossing the sea. He brooded again.

5.13.1.t:
विमानात्तु सुसम्क्रम्य प्राकारं हरियूथपः ।
हनुमान्वेगवानासीद्यथा विद्युद्घनान्तरे
5.13.1.e: Hanuman, the vanara leader, jumped from the aerial chariot to the boundary wall like a flash of lightning in the clouds.

5.13.2.t:
सम्परिक्रम्य हनुमान्रावणस्य निवेशनात् ।
अदृष्ट्वा जानकीं सीतामब्रवीद्वचनं कपिः
5.13.2.e: Going round the palace of Ravana, unable to see Janaka's daughter Sita, Hanuman spoke thus to himself:

5.13.3.t:
भूयिष्ठं लोलिता लङ्का रामस्य चरता प्रियम् ।
न हि पश्यामि वैदेहीं सीतां सर्वाङ्गशोभनाम्
5.13.3.e: "I have thoroughly surveyed the entire city of Lanka to please Rama, but I am unable to find Sita of flawless beauty.

5.13.4.t:
पल्वलानि तटाकानि सरांसि सरितस्तथा ।
नद्योऽनूपवनान्ताश्च दुर्गाश्च धरणीधराः लोलिता वसुधा सर्वा न तु पश्यामि जानकीम् ।
5.13.4.e: "I have searched for Sita thoroughly in waterlogs, lakes, tanks, streams and rivers and all over the woods and among mountains that are difficult to reach. I have searched all over the land but have not been able to find Janaki.

5.13.6.t: किं नु सीताऽथ वैदेही मैथिली जनकात्मजा उपतिष्ठेत विवशा रावणं दुष्टचारिणम् ।
5.13.6.e: "Can it be that Mythili, daughter of Janaka, dejected and helpless succumbed to the evil intentions of Ravana.

5.13.8.t: अथवा ह्रियमाणायाः पथि सिद्धनिषेविते मन्ये पतितमार्याया हृदयं प्रेक्ष्य सागरम् ।
5.13.8.e: "Or, perhaps while being borne away on the path frequented by siddhas, the beloved of Rama might have fallen down (dead), heart broken, on seeing the (vast) sea.

w: by the high speed in the flight
5.13.9.t: रावणस्योरुवेगेन भुजाभ्यां पीडितेन च तया मन्ये विशालाक्ष्या त्यक्तं जीवितमार्यया ।
5.13.9.e: "He thinks, on account of the high speed during the flight of Ravana under the pressure of his arms, the noble, largeeyed lady might have given up her life.

w: higher and higher over the sea
5.13.10.t: उपर्युपरि वा नूनं सागरं क्रमतस्तदा विवेष्टमाना पतिता सागरे जनकात्मजा ।
5.13.10.e: "Surely, she might have fallen into the sea while wriggling in her effort to extricate herself from the hold of Ravana as he was flying over the sea.

5.13.11.t: अहो क्षुद्रेण वाऽनेन रक्षन्ती शीलमात्मनः अबन्धुर्भक्षिता सीता रावणेन तपस्विनी ।
5.13.11.e: "Oh poor Sita, distanced from relations, while protecting her chastity helplessly she might have been devoured by cruel Ravana.

5.13.12.t: अथवा राक्षसेन्द्रस्य पत्नीभिरसितेक्षणा अदुष्टा दुष्टभावाभिर्भक्षिता सा भविष्यति ।
5.13.12.e: "Or else, the pious, blackeyed Sita might have been eaten by the the cruelnatured wives of the lord of demons.

5.13.13.t: सम्पूर्णचन्द्रप्रतिमं पद्मपत्रनिभेक्षणम् रामस्य ध्यायती वक्त्रं पञ्चत्वं कृपणा गता ।
5.13.13.e: "Or, she might have attained death, meditating on Rama, whose face resembles the fullmoon and eyes the lotus petals.

5.13.15.t: अथवा निहिता मन्ये रावणस्य निवेशने नूनं लालप्यते सीता पञ्जरस्थेव शारिका ।
5.13.15.e: "Or, I think Sita might have been imprisoned in a cage like a myna in Ravana's palace. She will be surely crying.

5.13.16.t: जनकस्य सुता सीता रामपत्नी सुमध्यमा कथमुत्पलपत्राक्षी रावणस्य वशं व्रजेत् ।
5.13.16.e: "How could Janaki, the daughter of Janaka, Rama's wife, the lady with a beautiful waist and eyes like lotus petals, come under the fold of Ravana?

5.13.18.t: निवेद्यमाने दोषस्स्याद्दोषस्स्यादनिवेदने कथं नु खलु कर्तव्यं विषमं प्रतिभाति मे ।
5.13.18.e: "To carry or not to carry this news to Rama would be a mistake. What shall I do? I am facing a tough situation.

w: when things took such a turn
5.13.19.t: अस्मिन्नेवंगते कार्ये प्राप्तकालं क्षमं च किम् भवेदिति मतं भूयो हनुमान्प्रविचारयत् ।
5.13.19.e: "I wonder what the right course of action is when things have taken such a turn? What is proper for me to do? Hanuman once again deliberated.

5.13.21.t: ममेदं लङ्घनं व्यर्थं सागरस्य भविष्यति प्रवेशश्चैव लङ्कायाः राक्षसानां च दर्शनम् ।
5.13.21.e: "My crossing the ocean, my entry into Lanka and my survey of the demons are all futile.

5.13.22.t: किं मां वक्ष्यति सुग्रीवो हरयो वा समागताः किष्किन्धां समनुप्राप्तं तौ वा दशरथात्मजौ ।
5.13.22.e: "What will Sugriva or even the vanaras and the two sons of Dasaratha say when I reach Kishkinda?

5.13.24.t: परुषं दारुणं क्रूरं तीक्ष्णमिन्द्रियतापनम् सीतानिमित्तं दुर्वाक्यं श्रुत्वा स न भविष्यति ।
5.13.24.e: Hearing those harsh, dreadful, cruel and sharp words about Sita, words that could scorch the senses —

w: one who has almost given his life
5.13.25.t: तं तु कृच्छ्रगतं दृष्ट्वा पञ्चत्वगतमानसम् भृशानुरक्तो मेधावी न भविष्यति लक्ष्मणः ।
5.13.25.e: "Seeing Rama in such a painful state, wise Lakshmana who has given his life to Rama, to whom he is deeply devoted will also not survive.

5.13.26.t: विनष्टौ भ्रातरौ श्रुत्वा भरतोऽपि मरिष्यति भरतं च मृतं दृष्ट्वा शत्रुघ्नो न भविष्यति ।
5.13.26.e: "On hearing the death of both the brothers Bharata will also die. On seeing this Satrughna will also not live.

5.13.28.t: कृतज्ञस्सत्यसन्धश्च सुग्रीवः प्लवगाधिपः रामं तथा गतं दृष्ट्वा ततस्त्यक्ष्यति जीवितम् ।
5.13.28.e: "On seeing that Rama has ended his life, the grateful and truthful monkey leader, Sugriva will give up his life.

w: on account of her husband's grief
5.13.29.t: दुर्मना व्यथिता दीना निरानन्दा तपस्विनी पीडिता भर्तृशोकेन रुमा त्यक्ष्यति जीवितम् ।
5.13.29.e: "Distressed, disheartened, pained and grieved on account of her husband's death, the virtuous lady Ruma (wife of Sugriva) will be unhappy and die.

5.13.31.t: मातापित्रोर्विनाशेन सुग्रीवव्यसनेन च कुमारोऽप्यङ्गदः कस्माद्धारयिष्यति जीवितम् ।
5.13.31.e: "On account of his parents death and also because of Sugriva's calamity, Angada will give up his life.

w: on account of the events affecting their king
5.13.32.t: भर्तृजेन तु दुःखेन ह्यभिभूता वनौकसः शिरांस्यभिहनिष्यन्ति तलैर्मुष्टिभिरेव च ।
5.13.32.e: "The grief due to the death of their king will make the vanaras hit their heads with their palms and fists.

5.13.33.t: सान्त्वेनानुप्रदानेन मानेन च यशस्विना लालिताः कपिराजेन प्राणांस्त्यक्ष्यन्ति वानराः ।
5.13.33.e: "The vanaras who were reared by the king's kind words, gifts and care will give up their life.

w: tormented by the suffering of their king's death
5.13.35.t: सपुत्रदारास्सामात्या भर्तृव्यसनपीडिताः शैलाग्रेभ्यः पतिष्यन्ति समेषु विषमेषु च ।
5.13.35.e: "Tormented by their king's death the vanaras with their wives, sons and ministers will drop down from the mountain peaks on the rough ground and die.

w: they will use to put an end.
5.13.36.t: विषमुद्बन्धनं वापि प्रवेशं ज्वलनस्य वा उपवासमथो शस्त्रं प्रचरिष्यन्ति वानराः ।
5.13.36.e: "The vanaras will put an end to their lives by poisoning or by hanging or by selfimmolation or by killing themselves with weapons or by fasting unto death.

5.13.38.t: सोऽहं नैव गमिष्यामि किष्किन्धां नगरीमितः न च शक्ष्याम्यहं द्रष्टुं सुग्रीवं मैथिलीं विना ।
5.13.38.e: "I will not go to the city of Kishkinda from here or to Sugriva without finding Mythili. It will not be possible for me to face him.

5.13.39.t: मय्यगच्छति चेहस्थे धर्मात्मानौ महारथौ आशया तौ धरिष्येते वानराश्च मनस्विनः ।
5.13.39.e: Both the highsouled warrior princes treading a righteous path as well as the vanaras will survive with a hope of my return if I stay back.

w: filled with fruits roots and water
on the shore of the sea
5.13.40.t:
हस्तादानो मुखादानो नियतो वृक्षमूलिकः वानप्रस्थो भविष्यामि ह्यदृष्ट्वा जनकात्मजाम् ।
सागरानूपजे देशे बहुमूलफलोदके
5.13.40.e: "If Janaki is not found I will stay here and live like a hermit subsisting on whatever is available on this sea shore, which has abundance of roots, fruits and water.

5.13.42.t:
चितां कृत्वा प्रवेक्ष्यामि समिद्धमरणीसुतम् ।
उपविष्टस्य वा सम्यग्लिङ्गिनीं साधयिष्यतः शरीरं भक्षयिष्यन्ति वायसाः श्वापदानि च ।
5.13.42.e: "I will prepare a pyre  and enter the fire  so that sea waves wash off the ashes or crows and beasts will eat up my body while i sit fasting unto death.

w: if I am not able to see
5.13.43.t: इदं महर्षिभिर्दृष्टं निर्याणमिति मे मतिः सम्यगापः प्रवेक्ष्यामि न चेत्पश्यामि जानकीम् ।
5.13.43.e: "I shall enter water and drown myself to death if I am not able to find Janaki. I think this way of ending life has been suggested by great ascetics.

w: did not reach of the end.
5.13.48.t: एवं बहुविधं दुःखं मनसा धरायन्मुहुः नाध्यगच्छत्तदा पारं शोकस्य कपिकुञ्चरः ।
5.13.48.e: The elephant among monkeys (Hanuman) worrying over and over again, holding his head for long could not reach the end of his grief.

5.13.49.t: रावणं वा वधिष्यामि दशग्रीवं महाबलम् काममस्तु हृता सीता प्रत्याचीर्णं भविष्यति ।
5.13.49.e: "I will kill Ravana, this mighty, tenheaded demon. Sita was indeed carried away by him. This (killing him) can be a fitting reply to his evil action. My desire would be fulfilled.

w: by lifting across (like a sacrificial prey)
5.13.50.t: अथवैनं समुत्क्षिप्य उपर्युपरि सागरम् रामायोपहरिष्यामि पशुं पशुपतेरिव ।
5.13.50.e: "Or else, I shall carry him across the sea and put him before Rama like a bull as if he is a sacrificial prey to lord Siva."

5.13.51.t: इति चिन्तां समापन्नः सीतामनधिगम्य ताम् ध्यानशोकपरीतात्मा चिन्तयामास वानरः ।
5.13.51.e: Distressed over his inability to find Sita, Hanuman's mind was overcome with anxiety and he started thinking further.

5.13.52.t: यावत्सीतां हि पश्यामि रामपत्नीं यशस्विनीम् तावदेतां पुरीं लङ्कां विचिनोमि पुनः पुनः ।
5.13.52.e: "Till I find the virtuous Sita, wife of Rama in this Lanka, I shall keep searching everywhere again and again.

5.13.54.t: इहैव नियताहारो वत्स्यामि नियतेन्द्रियः न मत्कृते विनश्येयुः सर्वे ते नरवानराः ।
5.13.54.e: "I will stay here itself, restricting my food and controlling my senses. Let not men and monkeys perish for my fault.

5.13.56.t: वसून्रुद्रांस्तथाऽदित्यानश्विनौ मरुतोऽपि च नमस्कृत्वा गमिष्यामि रक्षसां शोकवर्धनः ।
5.13.56.e: "I shall offer salutations to Vasus, Rudras Adityas and Aswinis and proceed to  increase (cause) the sorrow of the demons. (There are eight Vasus, eleven Rudras, twelve Adityas, two Ashwins and fortynine Windgods).

5.13.60.t:
स तेभ्यस्तु नमस्कृत्य सुग्रीवाय च मारुतिः ।
दिशस्सर्वास्समालोक्य ह्यशोकवनिकां प्रति
5.13.60.e: Having offered salutations to all gods as well as to Sugriva, he looked at all quarters and left for the Ashoka grove.

5.13.61.t:
स गत्वा मनसा पूर्वमशोकवनिकां शुभाम् ।
उत्तरं चिन्तयामास वानरो मारुतात्मजः
5.13.61.e: Hanuman started thinking again about his task after reaching the auspicious Ashoka grove.

5.13.63.t:
रक्षिणश्चात्र विहिता नूनं रक्षन्ति पादपान् ।
भगवानपि सर्वात्मा नातिक्षोभं प्रवाति वै संक्षिप्तोऽयं मयाऽत्मा च रामार्थे रावणस्य च ।
5.13.63.e: "The guards posted there are surely protecting the grove. The divinity  pervading all over me (the wind) must also have been controlled as it is also not blowing violently. I have turned my body small for Rama's cause and also to save myself from Ravana.

w: Indra who is invoked several times in sacrifices
5.13.64.t:
सिद्धिं मे संविधास्यन्ति देवाः सर्षिगणास्त्विह ब्रह्मा स्वयंभूर्भगवान् देवाश्चैव दिशन्तु मे ।
सिद्धिमग्निश्च वायुश्च पुरुहूतश्च वज्रभृत् वरुणः पाशहस्तश्च सोमादित्यौ तथैव च ।
अश्विनौ च महात्मानौ मरुतः शर्व एव च सिद्धिं सर्वाणि भूतानि भूतानां चैव यः प्रभुः ।
दास्यन्ति मम ये चान्ये ह्यदृष्टाः पथि गोचराः
5.13.64.e: May all sages, gods, the selfborn Brahma, Windgod, Indra, the wielder of thunderbolt whose name is invoked in sacrifices, Yama, who carries a rope, Varuna give success and Lord Siva help me. May the Sun, Moon, Aswinis  Marutas assist me. May the gods of the quarters and the lord of all beings help me to succeed. May those whom I could not see also bring success to me.

w: who appears like the pleasant Moon
beautiful face of the noble lady
5.13.68.t:
तदुन्नसं पाण्डुरदन्तमव्रणं शुचिस्मितं पद्मपलाशलोचनम् ।
द्रक्ष्ये तदार्यावदनं कदान्वहं प्रसन्नताराधिपतुल्यदर्शनम्
5.13.68.e: 'Oh when and how would I behold that beautiful noble lady of stainless character, with a Moonlike face, prominent nose, white teeth, pleasant smile and with eyes like lotus petals?

5.14.4.t:
अथाम्रवणसञ्छन्नां लताशतसमावृताम् ।
ज्यामुक्त इव नाराचः पुप्लुवे वृक्षवाटिकाम्
5.14.4.e: He penetrated like an arrow released from a bow the cluster of trees covering mango grove and overgrown with hundreds of creepers.

w: rendered noisy by herds of animals and flocks of birds
fringed with abundant flowers and fruits
5.14.5.t:
स प्रविश्य विचित्रां तां विहगैरभिनादिताम् ।
राजतैः कांचनैश्चैव पादपैः सर्वतो वृताम् विहगैर्मृगसङ्घैश्च विचित्रां चित्रकाननाम् ।
उदितादित्यसङ्काशां ददर्श हनुमान् कपिः वृतां नानाविधैर्वृक्षैः पुष्पोपगफलोपगैः ।
कोकिलैर्भृङ्गराजैश्च मत्तैर्नित्यनिषेविताम् प्रहृष्टमनुजे काले मृगपक्षिसमाकुले ।
मत्तबर्हिणसङ्घुष्टां नानाद्विजगणायुताम्
5.14.5.e: Entering deep into the grove, Hanuman saw clusters of trees pleasing to look at, herds of animals and flocks of colourful birds singing melodious notes.The grove was surrounded on all sides by silvery and golden trees which looked colourful with flocks of birds and herds of deer. It was full of lovely thickets looking like the rising sun. It was fringed with various trees bearing abundance of fruits and flowers. It was inhabited by intoxicated cuckoos, bees,  proud peacocks and numerous lovely birds.

5.14.10.t:
उत्पतद्भिर्द्विजगणैः पक्षैः सालास्समाहताः ।
अनेकवर्णा विविधा मुमुचुः पुष्पवृष्टयः
5.14.10.e: As the birds flew away, the trees hit by the wings of birds showered flowers of different colours.

5.14.14.t:
तरस्विना ते तरवस्तरसाभिप्रकम्पिताः ।
कुसुमानि विचित्राणि ससृजुः कपिना तदा
5.14.14.e: ﻿ Shaken vigorously by Hanuman of great speed, the trees shed their blooms of variegated colours.

w: with clothes and ornaments lost in gambling
5.14.15.t:
निर्धूतपत्रशिखराः शीर्णपुष्पफला द्रुमाः ।
निक्षिप्तवस्त्राभरणा धूर्ता इव पराजिताः
5.14.15.e: The tree tops, shorn of their leaves and flowers and fruits fallen, appeared like gamblers who had lost their stakes and had to lay down their clothes and ornaments.

w: with bright teeth and lips kissed
5.14.18.t:
निर्धूतकेशी युवतिर्यथा मृदितवर्णका ।
निष्पीतशुभदन्तोष्ठी नखैर्दन्तैश्च विक्षता तथा लाङ्गूलहस्तैश्च चरणाभ्यां च मर्दिता ।
बभूवाशोकवनिका प्रभग्नवरपादपा
5.14.18.e: The garden of Ashoka with trees shattered and crushed by Hanuman's tail,  hands and feet, appeared like a woman with dishevelled hair, with her vermilion mark effaced, her bright teeth and lips faded for being kissed and wounded with nails and bitten with teeth (by her lover).

5.14.20.t:
महालतानां दामानि व्यथमत्तरसा कपिः ।
यथा प्रावृषि विन्ध्यस्य मेघजालानि मारुतः
5.14.20.e: Hanuman shook with tremendous speed the huge clusters of creepers hanging there just like stormy wind in rainy season scatters masses of clouds on the Vindhya mountain.

w: with sands of corals and pearls
with beds of lotuses in bloom
a flocks of Natyuha birds rubbing together
made noisy with swans and Sarasa birds
lilies in bloom here and there
5.14.22.t:
वापीश्च विविधाकाराः पूर्णाः परमवारिणा ।
महार्हैर्मणिसोपानैरुपपन्नास्ततस्ततः मुक्ताप्रवालसिकताः स्फाटिकान्तरकुट्टिमाः ।
काञ्चनैस्तरुभिश्चित्रैस्तीरजैरुपशोभिताः फुल्लपद्मोत्पलवनाश्चक्रवाकोपकूजिताः ।
नत्यूहरुतसंघुष्टा हंससारसनादिताः दीर्घाभिर्द्रुमयुक्ताभिः सरद्भिश्च समन्ततः ।
अमृतोपमतोयाभिश्शिवाभिरुपसंस्कृताः लताशतैरवततास्सन्तानकुसुमावृताः ।
नानागुल्मावृतघनाः करवीरकृतान्तराः
5.14.22.e: ﻿ He observed ponds of different shapes filled with clear water with steps paved with rich gems, with sands of pearls and corals and bottoms of crystal, which contained beds of lotuses in bloom, adorned with chakravaka birds and resonant with cacklings of swans and sarasas and vatyuhas rubbing their beaks. There were golden platforms built on banks and platforms built of crystals. There were trees on the bank of streams, and nectarlike sacred waters flowing in them surrounded by hundreds of creepers, and Ashoka blossoms scattered everywhere, with thickly grown bushes of different kinds, with lilies in bloom in tanks.

w: with sands of corals and pearls
with beds of lotuses in bloom
a flocks of Natyuha birds rubbing together
made noisy with swans and Sarasa birds
lilies in bloom here and there
5.14.25.t:
वापीश्च विविधाकाराः पूर्णाः परमवारिणा ।
महार्हैर्मणिसोपानैरुपपन्नास्ततस्ततः मुक्ताप्रवालसिकताः स्फाटिकान्तरकुट्टिमाः ।
काञ्चनैस्तरुभिश्चित्रैस्तीरजैरुपशोभितैः फुल्लपद्मोत्पलवनाश्चक्रवाकोपकूजिताः ।
नत्यूहरुतसंघुष्टा हंससारसनादिताः दीर्घाभिर्द्रुमयुक्ताभिः सरद्भिश्च समन्ततः ।
अमृतोपमतोयाभिश्शिवाभिरुपसंस्कृताः लताशतैरवततास्सन्तानकुसुमावृताः ।
नानागुल्मावृतघनाः करवीरकृतान्तराः
5.14.25.e: He observed ponds of different shapes filled with clear water with steps paved with rich gems, with sands of pearls and corals and bottoms of crystal, which  contained beds of lotuses in bloom, adorned with chakravaka birds and resonant with cacklings of swans and sarasas and vatyuhas rubbing their beaks. There were golden platforms built on banks and platforms built of crystals. There were trees on the bank of streams, and nectarlike sacred waters flowing in them surrounded by hundreds of creepers, and Ashoka blossoms scattered everywhere, with thickly grown bushes of different kinds, with lilies in bloom in tanks.

w: with a collection of wonderful peaks
5.14.27.t:
ततोऽम्बुधरसङ्काशं प्रवृद्धशिखरं गिरिम् ।
विचित्रकूटं कूटैश्च सर्वतः परिवारितम् शिलागृहैरवततं नानावृक्षैः समावृतम् ।
ददर्श हरिशार्दूलो रम्यं जगति पर्वतम्
5.14.27.e: The tiger among monkeys beheld a delightingful mountain, resembling the raincloud with tall, pleasing peaks, wonderful peaks spread all over the mountain. There were caves built of stone, with a variety of trees.

w: with the branches bent into water
with water running backwards creating circles
5.14.29.t:
ददर्श च नगात्तस्मान्नदीं निपतितां कपिः ।
अङ्कादिव समुत्पत्य प्रियस्य पतितां प्रियाम् जले निपतिताग्रैश्च पादपैरुपशोभिताम् ।
वार्यमाणामिव क्रुद्धां प्रमदां प्रियबन्धुभिः पुनरावृत्ततोयां च ददर्श स महाकपिः ।
प्रसन्नामिव कान्तस्य कान्तां पुनरुपस्थिताम्
5.14.29.e: Hanuman, the great monkey saw a stream descending from the hill which looked like a beloved jumping down from the thighs of her lover. It was adorned with trees whose boughs touched the water and thus looking like an angry woman leaving her dear lover but detained by her relatives. With the water running backward in circles it appeared as if the beloved has returned to her lover pleased.

w: spread over with pearl dust as sand
5.14.33.t:
कृत्रिमां दीर्घिकां चापि पूर्णां शीतेन वारिणा ।
मणिप्रवरसोपानां मुक्तासिकतशोभिताम् विविधैर्मृगसङ्घैश्च विचित्रां चित्रकाननाम् ।
प्रासादैस्सुमहद्भिश्च निर्मितैर्विश्वकर्मणा काननैः कृत्रिमैश्चापि सर्वतः समलङ्कृताम् ।
5.14.33.e: Hanuman saw an oblong pond, full of cool water provided with steps, embellished with gems and beautified with pearl dust as sand on its bank.  Thronged with many kinds of animals, it looked colourful with large mansions constructed by Visvakarma in the artificial woodlands decorated all over.

w: had abundance of flowers and fruits (easily reachable)
5.14.35.e: There the trees had abundance of flowers and fruits. A few trees were full of leaves and branches spread like parasols. There were raised golden platforms.

5.14.36.t:
लताप्रतानैर्बहुभिःपर्णैश्च बहुभिर्वृताम् काञ्चनीं शिंशुपामेकां ददर्श हरियूथपः ।
वृतां हेममयीभिस्तु वेदिकाभिस्समन्ततः
5.14.36.e: The monkey leader saw one simsupa tree covered all over with canopies of many climbers and leaves. The tree was surrounded by golden platforms.

5.14.39.t:
तेषां द्रुमाणां प्रभया मेरोरिव दिवाकरः ।
अमन्यत तदा वीरः काञ्चनोऽस्मीति वानरः
5.14.39.e: He saw trees resplendent with golden radiance and thought that he was in the midst of gold like the Sungod getting golden hue by the radiance of Meru, the golden mountain.

w: with flowers blossoming on the top
5.14.41.t:
स पुष्पिताग्रां रुचिरां तरुणाङ्कुरपल्लवाम् ।
तामारुह्य महाबाहुश्शिंशुपां पर्णसंवृताम्
5.14.41.e: Strongarmed Hanuman climbed up the simsupa tree shining with flowers on its top and surrounded by tender sprouts and leaves. (He said to himself):

w: a lady eager to see Rama
5.14.42.t:
इतो द्रक्ष्यामि वैदेहीं रामदर्शनलालसाम् ।
इतश्चेतश्च दुःखार्तां सम्पतन्तीं यदृच्छया
5.14.42.e: "I may see by chance( from this point) Vaidehi tormented with grief anxiously waiting to see Rama while moving about here and there casually.

5.14.43.t:
अशोकवनिका चेयं दृढं रम्या दुरात्मनः ।
चम्पकैश्चन्दनैश्चापि वकुलैश्च विभूषिता
5.14.43.e: "Surely this beautiful Ashoka grove with delightful champak, chandan and bakula trees belongs to the wicked Ravana."

w: frequented by flocks of water birds
5.14.44.t:
इयं च नलिनी रम्या द्विजसङ्घनिषेविता ।
इमां सा राममहिषी नूनमेष्यति जानकी
5.14.44.e: "This lovely lotuspond is frequented by flocks of aquatic birds. Surely Rama's queen Janaki will come to this place.

w: of creatures wandering in the forest
5.14.48.t:
वनेचराणां सततं नूनं स्पृहयते पुरा ।
रामस्य दयिता भार्या जनकस्यसुता सती
5.14.48.e: "The daughter of Janaka, the  chaste wife of Rama,  used to for the company of those creatures wandering in the forest.

5.14.49.t:
सन्ध्याकालमनाः श्यामा ध्रुवमेष्यति जानकी ।
नदीं चेमां शुभजलां सन्ध्यार्थे वरवर्णिनी
5.14.49.e: Surely that lady of lovely complexion, the beautiful Janaki will come to this river flowing with sacred waters for performing the evening rituals.

5.14.51.t:
यदि जीवति सा देवी ताराधिपनिभानना ।
आगमिष्यति साऽवश्यमिमां शिवजलां नदीम्
5.14.51.e: "The moonfaced queen will certainly come to this stream of  auspicious water if she is surviving."

w: wife of the lord of the people
5.14.52.t:
एवं तु मत्वा हनुमान्महात्मा प्रतीक्षमाणो मनुजेन्द्रपत्नीम् ।
अवेक्षमाणश्च ददर्श सर्वं सुपुष्पिते पर्णघने निलीनः
5.14.52.e: Pondering thus, the highsouled Hanuman remained concealed on the tree loaded with flowers and leaves and waited, looking eagerly for the wife of the lord of the people. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये सुन्दरकाण्डे चतुर्दशस्सर्गः। Thus ends the fourteenth sarga of Sundarakanda of the holy Ramayana, the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

w: filled with the warble of cuckoos
trees full of blossoms of all seasons
shedding the splendour of the rising Sun
thick with flowers serving as earornaments (of the forest)
with blossoms up to the base of trees
5.15.2.t:
सन्तानकलताभिश्च पादपैरुपशोभिताम् ।
दिव्यगन्धरसोपेतां सर्वतस्समलङ्कृताम् तां स नन्दनसङ्काशां मृगपक्षिभिरावृताम् ।
हर्म्यप्रासादसम्बाधां कोकिलाकुलनिस्स्वनाम् काञ्चनोत्पलपद्माभिर्वापीभिरुपशोभिताम् ।
बह्वासनकुथोपेतां बहुभूमिगृहायुताम् सर्वर्तुकुसुमै रम्यां फलवद्भिश्च पादपैः ।
पुष्पितानामशोकानां श्रिया सूर्योदयप्रभाम् प्रदीप्तामिव तत्रस्थो मारुतिस्समुदैक्षत ।
निष्पत्रशाखां विहगैः क्रियमाणामिवासकृत् विनिष्पतद्भिः शतशश्चित्रैः पुष्पावतंसकैः ।
आमूलपुष्पनिचितैरशोकैश्शोकनाशनैः पुष्पभारातिभारैश्च स्पृशद्भिरिव मेदिनीम् ।
कर्णिकारैः कुसुमितैः किंशुकैश्च सुपुष्पितैः
5.15.2.e: Hanuman surveyed from the Simsupa tree the Ashoka grove of trees full of fine fragrance. It looked welldecorated  like the Nandana garden of Indra. It teemed with animals and birds. It was filled with the voices of the cuckoos. It had tall mansions and underground chamber. There were golden lilies and lotuses in the lakes, enchanting couches with rich coverings and trees full of blossoms of all seasons and fruits in abundance With the  Ashoka tree shedding showers of flowers from time to time the place shone with the splendour of Sunrise. It glittered like inflamed fire. The Ashoka tree had  hundreds of colourful birds on the branches. It appeared as if it had branches without leaves which made them look like earornaments (of the grove). Ashoka flowers in bloom hung down to the base of the tree as if to take away the grief of the onlookers. The blossoms of the Karnikara and kimsuka brightened the whole grove.

5.15.9.t:
स देशः प्रभया तेषां प्रदीप्त इव सर्वतः ।
पुन्नागास्सप्तपर्णाश्च चम्पकोद्दालकास्तथा विवृद्धमूला बहवश्शोभन्ते स्म सुपुष्पिताः ।
5.15.9.e: The grove shone bright as if it were inflamed fire with beautiful trees like purnaga, saptaparna, champak and uddalaka in full bloom.

5.15.10.e: There were thousands of ashoka trees some of which shone like gold, others like the flames of fire and some dark as collyrium.

w: like the Nandana garden of Indra
like the Chaitraratha garden of Kubera
shining with the radiance of countless varieties of blossoms
hundreds of gems in the form of flowers
a second (besides the four oceans which form the boundary of the earth)
5.15.11.t:
नन्दनं विविधोद्यानं चित्रं चैत्ररथं यथा अतिवृत्तमिवाचिन्त्यं दिव्यं रम्यं श्रिया वृतम् ।
वितीयमिव चाकाशं पुष्पज्योतिर्गणायुतम् पुष्परत्नशतैश्चित्रं द्वितीयं सागरं यथा ।
सर्वर्तुपुष्पैर्निचितं पादपैर्मधुगन्धिभिः नानानिनादैरुद्यानं रम्यं मृगगणैर्द्विजैः ।
अनेकगन्धप्रवहं पुण्यगन्धं मनोरमम्
5.15.11.e: The grove with different types of gardens spread over looked like the Nandana garden of Indra and Chaitraratha garden of Kubera. It surpassed every other garden. It was unimaginable in splendour. It was divine and delightful filled with the radiance of countless varieties of blossoms shining like stars, like a second firmament. It was like another ocean filled with precious gems of flowers. It had trees with flowers of honeyscented fragrance. Sounds of animals and birds filled the air. It was pleasing to the heart with various divine fragrances wafted (by the breeze)৷৷

w: having altars of bright molten gold
5.15.15.t:
शैलेन्द्रमिव गन्धाढ्यं द्वितीयं गन्धमादनम् ।
अशोकवनिकायां तु तस्यां वानरपुङ्गवः स ददर्शाविदूरस्थं चैत्यप्रासादमुच्छ्रितम् ।
मथ्ये स्तम्भसहस्रेण स्थितं कैलासपाण्डुरम् प्रवालकृतसोपानं तप्तकाञ्चनवेदिकम् ।
मुष्णन्तमिव चक्षूंषि द्योतमानमिव श्रिया विमलं प्रांशुभावत्वादुल्लिखन्तमिवाम्बरम् ।
5.15.15.e: The monkey leader saw a lofty templelike structure in the midst of the Ashoka grove which was highly fragrant and appeared like another indescribable structure that stood on a thousand pillars like another Gandhamadana mountain. It gleamed white like mount Kailasa. Its stairs were paved with corals. The altars were made of brightly polished gold. This structure glowing with brilliance was as if stealing the eyes. It looked white with light and lofty as though scratching the sky.

w: at the beginning of the bright fortnight
5.15.18.t:
ततो मलिनसंवीतां राक्षसीभिस्समावृताम् उपवासकृशां दीनां निश्श्वसन्तीं पुनः पुनः ।
ददर्श शुक्लपक्षादौ चन्द्ररेखामिवामलाम्
5.15.18.e: Then he beheld a lady surrounded by female demons. Clad in soiled clothes she looked dejected, emaciated through fasting and was sighing repeatedly. She appeared thin and pale like the crescent Moon at the beginning of the bright fortnight.

5.15.20.t:
मन्दप्रख्यायमानेन रूपेण रुचिरप्रभाम् ।
पिनद्धां धूमजालेन शिखामिव विभावसोः
5.15.20.e: Her form was faintly recognisable. She had a lovely radiance on account of her beautiful form. She looked like the tip of burning fire engulfed in a cloud of smoke.

5.15.21.t:
पीतेनैकेन संवीतां क्लिष्टेनोत्तमवाससा ।
सपङ्कामनलङ्कारां विपद्मामिव पद्मिनीम्
5.15.21.e: She was wearing an excellent single yellow cloth which was soiled. Unadorned, she looked like a muddy lotuspond bereft of lotuses.

5.15.22.t:
व्रीडितां दुःखसन्तप्तां परिम्लानां तपस्विनीम् ।
ग्रहेणाङ्गारकेणेव पीडितामिव रोहिणीम्
5.15.22.e: She was bashful, tormented with agony, dejected with a withered look. She appeared like the star Rohini oppressed by planet Mars.

w: with her face filled with tears
5.15.23.t:
अश्रुपूर्णमुखीं दीनां कृशामनशनेन च ।
शोकध्यानपरां दीनां नित्यं दुःखपरायणाम्
5.15.23.e: Her face was filled with tears. She looked dejected and emaciated due to fasting. Always plunged in grief, she looked like one meditating in tears.

w: surrounded by a group of hounds
5.15.24.t:
प्रियं जनमपश्यन्तीं पश्यन्तीं राक्षसीगणम् ।
स्वगणेन मृगीं हीनां श्वगणाभिवृतामिव
5.15.24.e: Unable to see her dear kith and kin, she sat guarded by ogresses. She appeared like a doe separated from the herd and encircled by a pack of hounds.

w: which looked like a black serpent
at the close of rainy season
5.15.25.t:
नीलनागाभया वेण्या जघनं गतयैकया ।
नीलया नीरदापाये वनराज्या महीमिव सुखार्हां दुःखसन्तप्तां व्यसनानामकोविदाम् ।
5.15.25.e: She (from behind) appeared like the earth covered with a range of trees at the end of rainy season with her single long black braid touching her hips looking like a black serpent. She who deserved to be happy and had not experienced worries was burning in grief. (एकवेणी is a trait of a प्रोषितभर्तृका Sita who was forced to stay in Lanka was a प्रोषितभर्तृका नायिका.)

5.15.26.t: तां समीक्ष्य विशालाक्षीमधिकं मलिनां कृशाम् तर्कयामास सीतेति कारणैरुपपादिभिः ।
5.15.26.e: After seeing the largeeyed lady worn out and dressed in soiled clothes, Hanuman started deliberating in himself and guessed it was Sita for strong reasons.

5.15.28.t:
पूर्णचन्द्राननां सुभ्रूं चारुवृत्तपयोधराम् कुर्वतीं प्रभयादेवीं सर्वा वितिमिरा दिशः ।
तां नीलकेशीं बिम्बोष्ठीं सुमध्यां सुप्रतिष्ठिताम् सीतां पद्मपलाशाक्षीं मन्मथस्य रतिं यथा ।
5.15.28.e: Her face resembled the fullmoon which dispelled the encircling gloom by its radiance. She had a slender waist, beautiful round breasts, shapely eyebrows, red lips, dark hair, and eyes like lotus petals with attractive limbs. She was comparable to Rati, consort of Cupid.

5.15.30.t: इष्टां सर्वस्य जगतः पूर्णचन्द्रप्रभामिव भूमौ सुतनुमासीनां नियतामिव तापसीम् ।
5.15.30.e: Just as the radiance of the full moon is cherished by all, this lady was liked by every one in this world. With her lovely figure she was seated on the ground like an austere ascetic.

w: like the consort of the serpent lord
5.15.31.t: निःश्वासबहुलां भीरुं भुजगेन्द्रवधूमिव शोकजालेन महता विततेन न राजतीम् ।
5.15.31.e: The timid lady was hissing (sighing) like the consort of the serpent king, who being caught in a widespread cobweb of grief was looking gloomy.

w: was pained by the obstruction to meet Rama
5.15.34.e: She appeared like fame besmirched by false allegation. She was pained by the obstruction to meet Rama and emaciated by  abduction.

w: with her dark and curved eyelashes
5.15.35.t:
अबलां मृगशाबाक्षीं वीक्षमाणां ततस्ततः बाष्पाम्बुपरिपूर्णेन कृष्णवक्राक्षिपक्ष्मणा ।
वदनेनाप्रसन्नेन निःश्वसन्तीं पुनः पुनः
5.15.35.e: The fawneyed lady was looking here and there with her dark, curved eyelashes. Her unhappy face was streaming with tears.

w: one who deserved to be adorned
5.15.37.t:
मलपङ्कधरां दीनां मण्डनार्हाममण्डिताम् ।
प्रभां नक्षत्रराजस्य कालमेघैरिवावृताम्
5.15.37.e: Covered with dirt and mud and shorn of adornments even though she deserved them, she looked wretched like the radiance of the Moon muffled by dark clouds.

w: after seeing carefuly again and again
5.15.38.t:
तस्य संदिदिहे बुद्धिर्मुहुः सीतां निरीक्ष्य तु ।
आम्नायानामयोगेन विद्यां प्रशिथिलामिव
5.15.38.e: Hanuman did recognise Sita after looking at her carefully again and again even as one is able to make out knowledge of shastriclore forgotten with lapse of time and lack of practice.

5.15.39.t:
दुःखेन बुबुधे सीतां हनुमाननलङ्कृताम् ।
संस्कारेण यथा हीनां वाचमर्थान्तरं गताम्
5.15.39.e: Just as an unclear expression which has undergone certain changes in meaning due to lack of usage over a long period is understood by virtue of previous practice so also Hanuman had difficulty in recognising Sita who was devoid of any decoration.

w: ornaments that add beauty to the limbs
wonderfully variegated with corals and other gems
by being used for a long time
with marks of the ornaments formed on the body.
5.15.41.t:
वैदेह्या यानि चाङ्गेषु तदा रामोऽन्वकीर्तयत् ।
तान्याभरणजालानि गात्रशोभीन्यलक्षयत् सुकृतौ कर्णवेष्टौ च श्वदंष्ट्रौ च सुसंस्थितौ ।
मणिविद्रुमचित्राणि हस्तेष्वाभरणानि च श्यामानि चिरयुक्तत्वात्तथा संस्थानवन्ति च ।
5.15.41.e: Hanuman observed the ornaments worn by Vaidehi adding grace to her limbs which Rama had described.They were wellcrafted earrings and wellfit Savdamshtras. He noticed wonderful, variegated ornaments of corals and gems as well as those worn on hands. They were blackened for long wear and Sita had marks of wearing them on her body. (Note: This is a pair ornaments shaped like dog's teeth. It is not known on which part of the body they were worn).

5.15.43.t:
तान्यैवेतानि मन्येऽहं यानि रामोऽन्वकीर्तयत् तत्र यान्यवहीनानि तान्यहं नोपलक्षये ।
यान्यस्या नावहीनानि तानीमानि न संशयः
5.15.43.e: "I think these ornaments are the same that were described by Rama. Those dropped (by Sita) are not found on her body. These were not dropped.There is no doubt."

5.15.45.t:
पीतं कनकपट्टाभं स्रस्तं तद्वसनं शुभम् ।
उत्तरीयं नगासक्तं तदा दृष्टं प्लवङ्गमैः
5.15.45.e: "The shining yellow upper garment like a golden cloth was torn. Flung down, it stuck to a tree which the monkeys noticed.

5.15.46.t:
भूषणानि च मुख्यानि दृष्टानि धरणीतले ।
अनयैवापविद्धानि स्वनवन्ति महान्ति च
5.15.46.e: "The jingling, choice ornaments were thrown down on the ground.

5.15.47.t:
इदं चिरगृहीतत्वाद्वसनं क्लिष्टवत्तरम् ।
तथाऽपि नूनं तद्वर्णं तथा श्रीमद्यथेतरत्
5.15.47.e: "This cloth worn long is crumpled. Even then it has retained its shine and looks fresh.

w: even though lost (whereabouts not known till then)
5.15.48.t:
इयं कनकवर्णाङ्गी रामस्य महिषी प्रिया ।
प्रणष्टापि सती याऽस्य मनसो न प्रणश्यति
5.15.48.e: "This lady of golden complexion is Rama's beloved queen who does not disappear from his mind, although away.

5.15.49.t:
इयं सा यत्कृते रामश्चतुर्भिः परितप्यते ।
कारुण्येनानृशंस्येन शोकेन मदनेन च स्त्री प्रणष्टेति कारुण्यादाश्रितेत्यानृशंस्यतः ।
पत्नी नष्टेति शोकेन प्रियेति मदनेन च
5.15.49.e: "She is that same lady for whom Rama has been passing through compassion, benevolence, grief and passion. He is compassionate considering her a woman, kind and benevolent since she is his dependent, stricken with grief for losing a wife and passionate since she is his beloved.

w: charming body with perfectly symmetrical limbs
5.15.51.t:
अस्या देव्या यथा रूपमङ्गप्रत्यङ्गसौष्ठवम् ।
रामस्य च यथा रूपं तस्येयमसितेक्षणा
5.15.51.e: "This blackeyed Sita and her divine,  charming body with perfect limbs are a match for Rama's figure.

5.15.54.t:
दुष्करं कुरुते रामो य इमां मत्तकाशिनीम् ।
सीतां विना महाबाहुर्मुहूर्तमपि जीवति
5.15.54.e: "Rama, the strongarmed hero has accomplished a difficult task by surviving even for a moment without this Sita who has intoxicating lustre".

5.16.1.t:
प्रशस्य तु प्रशस्तव्यां सीतां तां हरिपुङ्गवः ।
गुणाभिरामं रामं च पुनश्चिन्तापरोऽभवत्
5.16.1.e: Hanuman, the bull among monkeys, admired the laudable Sita and the virtuous Rama and once again began to lament.

w: perfect match in character age and behaviour
perfect match in in birth and auspicious marks
5.16.5.t:
तुल्यशीलवयोवृत्तां तुल्याभिजनलक्षणाम् ।
राघवोऽऽर्हति वैदेहीं तं चेयमसितेक्षणा
5.16.5.e: "Sri Rama matches Vaidehi perfectly in character, age, behaviour, birth and auspicious signs. She is aware that he is the right person for her. Rama deserves Vaidehi and this blackeyed lady deserves him."

5.16.7.t:
अस्या हेतोर्विशालाक्ष्या हतो वाली महाबलः ।
रावणप्रतिमो वीर्ये कबन्धश्च निपातितः
5.16.7.e: "It was for the sake of this largeeyed Sita that the powerful Vali and the heroic Kabandha who was equal to Ravana in heroism were killed.

5.16.9.t:
चतुर्दश सहस्राणि रक्षसां भीमकर्मणाम् ।
निहतानि जनस्थाने शरैरग्निशिखोपमैः
5.16.9.e: At Janasthana fourteen thousand demons, warriors of fierce valour, were slain with arrows like flames of fire.

w: by one who knows the self
5.16.10.t:
खरश्च निहतसङ्ख्ये त्रिशिराश्च निपातितः ।
दूषणश्च महातेजा रामेण विदितात्मना
5.16.10.e: "Ogres like Khara and Trisira and the powerful Dooshana were kileed in battle by Rama endowed with selfknowledge.

5.16.11.t:
ऐश्वर्यं वानराणां च दुर्लभं वालिपालितम् ।
अस्या निमित्ते सुग्रीवः प्राप्तवान् लोकसत्कृतम्
5.16.11.e: On her account Sugriva obtained the coveted kingdom ruled by Vali which was a difficult proposition, and retained supremacy in the world.

5.16.14.t:
राज्यं वा त्रिषु लोकेषु सीता वा जनकात्मजा ।
त्रैलोक्यराज्यं सकलं सीताया नाप्नुयात्कलाम्
5.16.14.e: "The sovereignty over the three worlds will weigh less than one sixteenth part of Janaka's daughter, Sita.

w: resembling the pollen dust of lotus
a lady of unswerving devotion to her husband
5.16.15.t:
इयं सा धर्मशीलस्य मैथिलस्य महात्मनः ।
सुता जनकराजस्य सीता भर्तृदृढव्रता उत्थिता मेदिनीं भित्त्वा क्षेत्रे हलमुखक्षते ।
पद्मरेणुनिभैः कीर्णा शुभैः केदारपाम्सुभिः
5.16.15.e: She had risen from the land when tilled by the plough and was covered with auspicious paddy dust resembling the pollen grains of lotuses, this daughter of Janaka, the great righteous ruler of Mithila, This lady with unswerving devotion to her husband.

w: of a man of noble conduct
of a person who never returned
5.16.17.t:
विक्रान्तस्यार्यशीलस्य संयुगेष्न्विवर्तिनः ।
स्नुषा दशरथस्यैषा ज्येष्ठा राज्ञो यशस्विनी
5.16.17.e: "This celebrated lady is the eldest daughterinlaw of the noble, valiant king Dasaratha who never returned from the battleground without being victorious.

w: inspired by immense love towards her husband
as if she lived in the palace
a lady who had not experienced earlier
5.16.19.t:
सर्वान् भोगान्परित्यज्य भर्तृस्नेहबलात्कृता ।
अचिन्तयित्वा दुःखानि प्रविष्टा निर्जनं वनम् संतुष्टा फलमूलेन भर्तृशुश्रूषणे रता ।
या परां भजते प्रीतिं वनेऽऽपि भवने यथा सेयं कनकवर्णाङ्गी नित्यं सुस्मितभाषिणी ।
सहते यातनामेतामनर्थानामभागिनी
5.16.19.e: "On account of her immense love towards her husband she has given up all kinds of luxuries, not caring for suffering. She was satisfied with fruits and roots in the desolate forest. Engaged in serving her husband, she experienced utmost joy as in her own palace. A lady of golden complexion who had not experienced suffering earlier is subjected to sorrow and is tolerating calamities in this way

5.16.22.t:
इमां तु शीलसम्पन्नां द्रष्टुमर्हति राघवः ।
रावणेन प्रमथितां प्रपामिव पिपासितः
