5.16.22.e: "Rama deserves to see her.Just as a thirsty man longs for the source of water, Rama pines for this highly virtuous lady who is tormented by Ravana.

5.16.23.t:
अस्या नूनं पुनर्लाभाद्राघवः प्रीतिमेष्यति ।
राजा राज्यपरिभ्रष्टः पुनः प्राप्येव मेदिनीम्
5.16.23.e: "Just as a king who had lost his kingdom feels happy on regaining it, surely Raghava will feel exhilarated when he gets her back.

w: one who is eagerly waiting to meet them
5.16.24.t:
कामभोगैः परित्यक्ता हीना बन्धुजनेन च ।
धारयत्यात्मनो देहं तत्समागमकाङ्क्षिणी
5.16.24.e: Deprived of all sensual pleasures, and separated from her relatives, she is surviving with the hope of meeting them.

w: trees full of flowers and fruits
5.16.25.t:
नैषा पश्यति राक्षस्यो नेमान्पुष्पफलद्रुमान् ।
एकस्थहृदया नूनं राममेवानुपश्यति
5.16.25.e: She is looking at neither the shedemons nor these trees full of flowers and fruits. She is surely thinking of Rama with a singleminded  attention.

5.16.26.t:
भर्ता नाम परं नार्या भूषणं भूषणादपि ।
एषा तु रहिता तेन भूषणार्हा न शोभते
5.16.26.e: "Indeed, the husband is the greatest ornament for a married woman. Hence though deserving adornment she does not like it, bereft of her husband who is her only ornament.

w: endowed with eyes resembling a hundredpetalled lotus
5.16.28.t:
इमामसितकेशान्तां शतपत्रनिभेक्षणाम् ।
सुखार्हां दुःखितां दृष्ट्वा ममापि व्यथितं मनः
5.16.28.e: Sita who is endowed with beautiful dark hair and eyes like a hundredpetalled lotus, who deserves to be happy is in sorrow. I grieve to see her in this state.

w: by women who have hideous appearance
5.16.29.t:
क्षतिक्षमा पुष्करसन्निभाक्षी या रक्षिता राघवलक्ष्मणाभ्याम् ।
सा राक्षसीभिर्विकृतेक्षणाभिः संरक्ष्यते सम्प्रति वृक्षमूले
5.16.29.e: She who has beautiful eyes like lotus petals, was protected by the arms of both Rama and Lakshmna, who is tolerant like the earth and is guarded by the female demons of hideous appearance under a tree.

w: like the lotus afflicted by snow
5.16.30.t:
हिमहतनलिनीव नष्टशोभा व्यसनपरम्परया निपीड्यमाना ।
सहचररहितेव चक्रवाकी जनकसुता कृपणां दशां प्रपन्ना
5.16.30.e: "Deprived of her charm, she resembles a lotuscreeper blasted by frost. This daughter of Janaka has reached a pitiable condition afflicted by series of calamities. She resembles a famale Chakravaka separated from her mate.

w: with topmost branches bent down by the heaviness of blossoms
5.16.31.t:
अस्या हि पुष्पावनताग्रशाखाः शोकं दृढं वै जनयन्त्यशोकाः ।
हिमव्यपायेन च शीतरश्मि रभ्युत्थितो नैकसहस्ररश्मि:
5.16.31.e: "The top branches of Ashoka trees bent down with blossoms and the Moon rising with thousands of cool rays at the end of winter (when spring sets in) beholding which she should be delighted intensfy her sorrow."

5.16.32.t:
इत्येवमर्थं कपिरन्ववेक्ष्य सीतेयमित्येव निविष्टबुद्धि: ।
संश्रित्य तस्मिन्निषसाद वृक्षे बली हरीणामृषभस्तरस्वी
5.16.32.e: Hanuman, the swiftfooted bull among monkeys, on his part waiting on the Simsupa  tree thus reflecting concluded in his mind that she was Sita. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये सुन्दरकाण्डे षोडशस्सर्गः। Thus ends the sixteenth sarga of Sundarakanda of the holy Ramayana, the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

w: shining like a bed of lilies
5.17.1.t:
ततः कमुदषण्डाभो निर्मलं निर्मलोदयः ।
प्रजगाम नभश्चन्द्रो हंसो नीलमिवोदकम्
5.17.1.e: Then the Moon shining like a bed of lilies rose stainless, ascended the clear sky and looked like a swan swimming through blue water.

w: like one who wished to render
5.17.2.t:
साचिव्यमिव कुर्वन् स प्रभया निर्मलप्रभः ।
चन्द्रमा रश्मिभिश्शीतैस्सिषेवे पवनात्मजम्
5.17.2.e: The Moon shed clear lightas if with his brightness and his cool rays he wished to refresh the son of the Windgod.

w: whose face was like the fullmoon
5.17.3.t:
स ददर्श ततः सीतां पूर्णचन्द्रनिभाननाम् ।
शोकभारैरिव न्यस्तां भारैर्नावमिवाम्भसि
5.17.3.e: Then he saw Sita whose face shone like the fullmoon. But she was as though sinking under the burden of sorrow, like a boat with heavy load sinking in water.

w: one was breathing through the nose on head
one having thin and long neck
another who had hair covering like a blanket
with ears hanging on the forehead
one with lips extending up to chin
one with long knees sticking out
5.17.4.t:
दिदृक्षमाणो वैदेहीं हनुमान्मारुतात्मजः ।
स ददर्शाविदूरस्था राक्षसीर्घोरदर्शनाः एकाक्षीमेककर्णां च कर्णप्रावरणां तथा ।
अकर्णां शङ्कुकर्णां च मस्तकोच्छ्वासनासिकाम् अतिकायोत्तमाङ्गीं च तनुदीर्घशिरोधराम् ।
ध्वस्तकेशीं तथाऽकेशीं केशकम्बलधारिणीम् लम्बकर्णललाटां च लम्बोदरपयोधराम् ।
लम्बोष्ठीं चुबुकोष्ठीं च लम्बास्यां लम्बजानुकाम् ह्रस्वां दीर्घां तथा कुब्जां विकटां वामनां तथा ।
करालां भुग्नवक्त्रां च पिङ्गाक्षीं विकृताननाम्
5.17.4.e: While Hanuman was eager to observe Sita he saw many shedemons in ugly appearance close by her. One of them was oneeyed, another with a single ear, a third had ears covering the body, yet another had pointed (spikelike) ears, one was breathing through the nose on the head, one had long thin neck, one was hairless another had hair covering like a blanket. One of them had hanging ears on the forehead, another had big hanging lips, still another had long lips hanging  up to the chin. So also one had protruding knees, one stunted, one tall, another had lips extending up to her chin, yet another was longfaced and another had long knees. There was one pigmy, one tall, one was humpbacked and another a dwarf.Similarly an ugly looking one, another with gaping mouth, still another with a distorted face, one with yellow eyes and one of deformed face were seen.

w: holding spears mallets and warhammers of black iron
having faces like boar deer tiger buffalo goat jackal
with feet like those of elephants camels and horses
some having one hand and one leg
some having ears of a donkey or horse
having ears like that of monkeys
with the nose of an elephant
having large and uneven mouths and eyes
women with faces of a pig
like the face of a horse a camel or a donkey
armed with iron crowbars and tridents
women fond of meat and drinks
whose bodies were smeared with blood and flesh
who feed on flesh and blood
5.17.9.t:
विकृताः पिङ्गलाः कालीः क्रोधनाः कलहप्रियाः ।
कालायसमहाशूलकूटमुद्गरधारिणीः वराहमृगशार्दूलमहिषाजशिवामुखीः ।
गजोष्ट्रहयपादीश्च निखातशिरसोऽपराः एकहस्तैकपादाश्च खरकर्ण्यश्वकर्णिकाः ।
गोकर्णीर्हस्तिकर्णीश्च हरिकर्णीस्तथापराः अनासा अतिनासाश्च तिर्यङ्नासा विनासिकाः ।
गजसन्निभनासाश्च ललाटोच्छवासनासिकाः हस्तिपादा महापादा गोपादाः पादचूलिकाः ।
अतिमात्रशिरोग्रीवा अतिमात्रकुचोदरीः अतिमात्रास्यनेत्राश्च दीर्घजिह्वानखास्तथा ।
अजामुखीर्हस्तिमुखीर्गोमुखीस्सूकरीमुखीः हयोष्ट्रखरवक्त्राश्च राक्षसीर्घोरदर्शनाः ।
शूलमुद्गरहस्ताश्च क्रोधनाः कलहप्रियाः कराला धूम्रकेशीश्च राक्षसीर्विकृताननाः ।
पिबन्ती: सततं पानं सदा मांससुराप्रियाः मांसशोणितदिग्धाङ्गीर्मांसशोणितभोजनाः ।
ता ददर्श कपिश्रेष्ठो रोमहर्षणदर्शनाः स्कन्धवन्तमुपासीनाः परिवार्य वनस्पतिम् ।
5.17.9.e: Hanuman, the leader of the monkeys saw there shedemons of several distorted forms. Some were brown in colour and some black and some quarrelsome some holding spears, mallets and hammers of black iron, some with faces like boars, deer, tigers, goats and jackals feet like those of elephants, camels and horses, some had their head sunk into the trunk, others having one hand or one leg likewise some having ears like that of a donkey or a horse or a cow some with elephant ears and some with monkey ears some with big nose, without nose,with crooked nose and some without nostrils breathing through their forehead and some with the trunk of an elephant. Some with elephantfeet, with huge feet, and feet like that of cows and some with hair on their feet. There were some with huge heads and necks, some having large breasts, bellies, some with hanging breasts, and some with long nails and tongues. Similarly there were some having faces of goats, mouths of horses, camels or donkeys. They were terrifying, armed with iron crowbars and tridents. Some were wrathful, some with uneven gaping mouth, and some with smoky hair and distorted faces. They were always found drinking, smeared with flesh and blood and feeding on flesh and blood. Their appearance was horripilating. All of them were seated around the trunk of massive tree.

5.17.19.t: निष्प्रभां शोकसन्तप्तां मलसङ्कुलमूर्धजाम् क्षीणपुण्यां च्युतां भूमौ तारां निपतितामिव ।
5.17.19.e: Shorn of lustre, unkempt hair filled with dust, she appeared like a meteor slipped and fallen on land, merits exhausted.

w: having high reputation for her chastity
distressed yearning to see her husband
5.17.20.e: She was rich by  her reputation for chastity but poor as she yearned to see her husband. Though devoid of all excellent ornaments, she looked adorned with love for her husband.

5.17.21.t: राक्षसाधिपसंरुद्धां बन्धुभिश्च विना कृताम् वियूथां सिंहसंरुद्धां बद्धां गजवधूमिव ।
5.17.21.e: Besieged by the demon king, deprived of her near and dear ones, Sita was looking like a fettered female elephant separated from its herd and besieged by lions.

w: under the hold of the husband
fallen under the sway of shedemons
in the midst of Ashoka grove
5.17.23.t:
सीतां भर्तृवशे युक्तामयुक्तां राक्षसीवशे अशोकवनिकामथ्ये शोकसागरमाप्लुताम् ।
ताभिः परिवृतां तत्र सग्रहामिव रोहिणीम् ददर्श हनुमान् देवीं लतामकुसुमामिव ।
5.17.23.e: She deserves to be with Rama, but had fallen under the sway of shedemons. Sitting in the midst of Ashoka grove she was like a creeper without blossoms. Immersed in the ocean of sorrow the noble lady was like the star Rohini surrounded by unpropitious planets.

w: a lady with a pathetic face
5.17.26.t:
मलिनेन तु वस्त्रेण परिक्लिष्टेन भामिनीम् संवृतां मृगशाबाक्षीं ददर्श हनुमान् कपिः ।
तां देवीं दीनवदनामदीनां भर्तृतेजसा रक्षितां स्वेन शीलेन सीतामसितलोचनाम् ।
5.17.26.e: Hanuman saw the fawneyed lady clad in crushed and soiled clothes with a pathetic face. She felt no dejection when she thought of her husband's prowess. The blackeyed beauty was protected by her own chastity.

5.17.28.t:
तां दृष्ट्वा हनुमान् सीतां मृगशाबनिभेक्षणाम् ।
मृगकन्यामिव त्रस्तां वीक्षमाणां समन्ततः दहन्तीमिव निःश्वासैर्वृक्षान् पल्लवधारिणः ।
संघातमिव शोकानां दुःखस्योर्मिमिवोत्थिताम्
5.17.28.e: Seeing the fawneyed Sita, a frightened female deer  looking all around (as if for some help) sighing hot breath, was as though burning the trees having tender leaves with her hot sighs. She looked like a collective mass of all sorrows, a high tide of suffering.

w: shining even though she did not wear (many) ornaments
5.17.30.t: तां क्षमां सुविभक्ताङ्गी विनाभरणशोभिनीम् प्रहर्षमतुलं लेभे मारुतिः प्रेक्ष्य मैथिलीम् ।
5.17.30.e: She was a tolerant lady. She had beautiful limbs which looked splendid even though she was not wearing ornaments. Hanuman experienced immeasurable joy on seeing Mythili.

5.17.32.t:
नमस्कृत्वा च रामाय लक्ष्मणाय च वीर्यवान् ।
सीतादर्शनसंहृष्टो हनुमान् संवृतोऽभवत्
5.17.32.e: Heroic Hanuman felt happy when he saw Sita. He offered salutations to Rama and Lakshmana at heart and covered himself (with the leaves of the Simsupa tree) and waited. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये सुन्दरकाण्डे सप्तदशस्सर्गः। Thus ends the seventeenth sarga of Sundarakanda of the holy Ramayana, the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

5.18.1.t:
तथा विप्रेक्ष्यमाणस्य वनं पुष्पितपादपम् ।
विचिन्वतश्च वैदेहीं किंचिच्छेषा निशाऽभवत्
5.18.1.e: The night came to a close while Hanuman went searching and looking for Sita at Ashoka grove full of flowering trees.

w: at the end of the night
of those who were knowledgeable of Vedas and its six auxillary branches of sciences
those who were experts in performing exalted sacrificial ceremonies
5.18.2.t:
षडङ्गवेदविदुषां क्रतुप्रवरयाजिनाम् ।
शुश्राव ब्रह्मघोषांश्च स विरात्रे ब्रह्मरक्षसाम्
5.18.2.e: At dawn sounds of recitation of Vedas and the six auxillary sciences, (i.e .grammar, prosody, etymology, phonetics, astronomy and the science of rituals) by the brahmins among demons wellversed in performing exalted sacrificial ceremonies were heard.

5.18.4.t:
विबुध्यतु यथाकालं राक्षसेन्द्रः प्रतापवान् ।
स्रस्तमाल्याम्बरधरो वैदेहीमन्वचिन्तयत्
5.18.4.e: The chivalrous lord of demons woke up as usual.His raiment and garland were still in disarray and he thought of Vaidehi.

5.18.5.t:
भृशं नियुक्तस्तस्यां च मदनेन मदोत्कटः ।
न स तं राक्षसः कामं शशाकात्मनि गूहितुम्
5.18.5.e: The demon king who was unable to hide his great passion and control his senses was drawn towards Sita, in his state of intoxication.

w: filled with all kinds of flowers and fruits
5.18.6.t:
स सर्वाभरणैर्युक्तो बिभ्रच्छ्रियमनुत्तमाम् ।
तां नगैर्बहुभिर्जुष्टां सर्वपुष्पफलोपगैः
5.18.6.e: Adorned with all ornaments and glowing with excellent splendour he went through the path filled with trees flourishing with all kinds of flowers and fruits.

w: beautiful with different kinds of flowers
5.18.7.t:
वृतां पुष्करिणीभिश्च नानापुष्पोपशोभिताम् ।
सदा मदैश्च विहगैर्विचित्रां परमाद्भुताम्
5.18.7.e: Ponds covered with a variety of beautiful flowers and colourful birds always cheerful looked very wonderful.

w: gateways ornamented with gold and gems
filled with several kinds of animals herds
filled with a long stretch trees
5.18.8.t:
ईहामृगैश्च विविधैर्जुष्टां दृष्टिमनोहरैः ।
वीधीः संप्रेक्षमाणश्च मणिकाञ्चनतोरणाः नानामृगगणाकीर्णां फलैः प्रपतितैर्वृताम् ।
अशोकवनिकामेव प्राविशत्संततद्रुमाम्
5.18.8.e: Watching the garden filled with trees, gateways ornamented with gold and gems, he entered through the pleasant pathways in the Ashoka garden. There were wonderful wolves and several herds of animals in the garden. Fruits dropped from trees were strewn all over.

5.18.10.t:
अङ्गनाशतमात्रं तु तं व्रजन्तमनुव्रजत् ।
महेन्द्रमिव पौलस्त्यं देवगन्धर्वयोषितः
5.18.10.e: Ravana, son of sage Paulasti, was followed by a hundred women, just as Indra is trailed by the females of gods and gandharvas.

w: couches (rolls of twisted grass used as seats)
5.18.12.t:
काञ्चनैरपि भृङ्गारैर्जह्रुः सलिलमग्रतः ।
मण्डलाग्रान् बृसीश्चापि गृह्यान्याः पृष्ठतो ययुः
5.18.12.e: Some moved ahead of him carrying water in golden pitchers. Others followed him carrying circular couches (to be used as seats).

5.18.13.t:
काचिद्रत्नमयीं स्थालीं पूर्णां पानस्य भामिनी ।
दक्षिणा दक्षिणेनैव तदा जग्राह पाणिना
5.18.13.e: One glorious and compassionate lady carried in her right hand a gemstudded jar filled with wine.

5.18.14.t:
राजहंसप्रतीकाशं छत्रं पूर्णशशिप्रभम् ।
सौवर्णदण्डमपरा गृहीत्वा पृष्ठतो ययौ
5.18.14.e: Another shedemon moved behind him holding an umbrella with a golden handle which was white like a royal swan and bright like the fullmoon.

w: with eyes dizzy with sleep and intoxication
5.18.15.t:
निद्रामदपरीताक्ष्यो रावणस्योत्तमाः स्त्रियः ।
अनुजग्मुः पतिं वीरं घनं विद्युल्लता इव
5.18.15.e: The chief wives of Ravana with eyes dizzy with sleep and drinking followed their heroic husband like streaks of lightning follow a thunder cloud. (Ravana who was dark looked like a cloud and the women with dazzling golden complexion appeared like lightning.)

w: with smudged sandal paste and other unguents on the body
due to wilting of flowers by the sweat on their limbs
adorned with beautiful flowers in their hair
5.18.16.t:
व्याविद्धहारकेयूराः समामृदितवर्णकाः ।
समागळितकेशान्तास्सस्वेदवदनास्तथा घूर्णन्त्यो मदशेषेण निद्रया च शुभाननाः ।
स्वेदक्लिष्टाङ्गकुसुमास्सुमाल्याकुलमूर्धजाः प्रयान्तं नैऋतपतिं नार्यो मदिरलोचनाः ।
बहुमानाच्च कामाच्च प्रिया भार्यास्तमन्वयुः
5.18.16.e: The necklaces and armlets (of the wives) disarrayed, the sandal paste and other unguents on the body smudged, hair hanging down their faces, the sweating damsels followed Ravana. They were dizzy with leftover intoxication and sleep and were swaying from side to side. Their dishevelled hair was loose and faces filled with sweat, their flower garlands on the body had wilted due to sweat on their limbs. The drunken wives of Ravana, actuated by their high regard and passion for him followed as he advanced with drunken eyes.

w: absorbed in the thoughts of Sita
5.18.19.t:
स च कामपराधीन: पतिस्तासां महाबलः ।
सीतासक्तमना मन्दो मन्दाञ्चितगतिर्बभौ
5.18.19.e: Their husband, powerful Ravana under the control of passion looking dull, absorbed in the  thoughts of Sita walked slowly as though counting his steps.

5.18.22.e: Hanuman saw him in the glow of lamps wet with fragrant oil carried by many shedemons all over.

w: possesed of long curved bloodshot eyes
5.18.23.e: Hanuman saw him, who was possessed of lust, arrogance and intoxication. He appeared like Cupid setting aside his quiver and arrows with his curved, big, red eyes.

5.18.26.t:
अवेक्षमाणस्तु ततो ददर्श कपिकुञ्जरः ।
रूपयौवनसम्पन्ना रावणस्य वरस्त्रियः
5.18.26.e: The leader of the monkeys started gazing at the chief wives of Ravana endowed with youth and beauty৷৷

w: echoed with sounds of beasts and birds
5.18.27.t:
ताभिः परिवृतो राजा सुरूपाभिर्महायशाः ।
तन्मृगद्विजसङ्घुष्टं प्रविष्टः प्रमदावनम्
5.18.27.e: Surrounded by beauties, the glorious king entered the grove meant for women, reverberating with the sounds of beasts and birds.

5.18.28.t:
क्षीबो विचित्राभरणः शङ्कुकर्णो महाबलः ।
तेन विश्रवसः पुत्रः स दृष्टो राक्षसाधिपः वृतः परमनारीभिस्ताराभिरिव चन्द्रमाः ।
तं ददर्श महातेजास्तेजोवन्तं महाकपिः
5.18.28.e: The brilliant vanara looked at the son of Visravas (Ravana), the demon king  adorned with wonderful ornaments. He had long tapering ears. He was intoxicated with drink. Encircled by damsels, he was looking like the Moon surrounded by stars.

5.18.30.t:
रावणोऽयं महाबाहुरिति सञ्चिन्त्य वानरः ।
अवप्लुतो महातेजा हनुमान्मारुतात्मजः
5.18.30.e: The brilliant vanara (Hanuman), son of the Windgod recognising the strongarmed Ravana got down a little, saying 'This is truly the strongarmed Ravana.'

5.18.31.t:
स तथाप्युग्रतेजाः सन्निर्धूतस्तस्य तेजसा ।
पत्रगुह्यान्तरे सक्तो हनुमान् संवृतोऽभवत्
5.18.31.e: Hanuman, possessed of extraordinary energy, was taken aback at the might of Ravana. He remained hiding covered over with leaves.

5.18.32.t:
स तामसितकेशान्तां सुश्रोणीं संहतस्त्नीम् ।
दिदृक्षुरसितापाङ्गामुपावर्तत रावणः
5.18.32.e: With the desire to see Sita endowed with black hair, beautiful hips, plump breasts and dark sideglances, Ravana returned (to Ashokavana). इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये सुन्दरकाण्डे अष्टादशस्सर्गः। Thus ends the eighteenth sarga of Sundarakanda of the holy Ramayana, the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

5.19.1.t:
तस्मिन्नेव ततः काले राजपुत्री त्वनिन्दिता ।
रूपयौवनसम्पन्नं भूषणोत्तमभूषितम् ततो दृष्ट्वैव वैदेही रावणं राक्षसाधिपम् ।
प्रावेपत वरारोहा प्रवाते कदली यथा
5.19.1.e: On just seeing Ravana, the lord of demons from a distance, adorned with the best of ornaments the charming, young, blameles princess Vaidehi of beautiful waist trembled like a banana plant shaken by a strong wind.

w: even the tennecked Ravana on his part
5.19.4.t:
दशग्रीवस्तु वैदेहीं रक्षितां राक्षसीगणैः ।
ददर्श सीतां दुःखार्तां नावं सन्नामिवार्णवे
5.19.4.e: The tennecked Ravana, too, on his part saw Sita, tormented with grief, guarded by the shedemons like a boat sunk in the sea.

5.19.5.t:
असंवृतायामासीनां धरण्यां संशितव्रताम् ।
छिन्नां प्रपतितां भूमौ शाखामिव वनस्पतेः
5.19.5.e: She looked woeful seated on the bare earth like the broken branch of a tree cut and fallen down on the ground.

w: yoked to horses of her determination
with the chariot of her mind
5.19.7.t:
समीपं राजसिंहस्य रामस्य विदितात्मनः ।
सङ्कल्पहयसंयुक्सैर्यान्तीमिव मनोरथैः
5.19.7.e: She was as though moving towards the knower of the self, the supreme king, Rama with the horses of her resolution yoked to the chariot of her mind.

5.19.14.t:
पद्मिनीमिव विध्वस्तां हतशूरां चमूमिव ।
प्रभामिव तमोध्वस्तामुपक्षीणामिवापगाम्
5.19.14.e: She was like a lotuscreeper blighted, an army with its gallant warriors killed, radiance of light blocked by darkness and a stream run dry.

w: destroyed by the trunks of elephants
5.19.16.e: (She appeared) like a lotuspond the excellent leaves of whose lotuses surrounded by frightened birds are destroyed by the trunks of elephants.

w: stricken with grief caused by separation from her husband
like the night during the dark fortnight.
5.19.17.t:
पतिशोकातुरां शुष्कां नदीं विस्रावितामिव ।
परया मृजया हीनां कृष्णपक्षनिशामिव
5.19.17.e: Stricken with grief caused by separation from her husband, she appeared like a river gone thin and dry, not fit for ablution, like a night during dark fortnight of the month deprived of all its glow.

w: who deserves to be in a gemcrusted house
5.19.18.e: A delicate lady with beautiful limbs who deserved to be in a gemcrusted house was (now) like a lotus stem just plucked out and  scorched by the Sun's heat.

w: separated from her lord the leader of the herd
5.19.19.t:
गृहीतामालितां स्तम्भे यूथपेन विनाकृताम् ।
निःश्वसन्तीं सुदुःखार्तां गजराजवधूमिव
5.19.19.e: She was sighing heavily in intense grief like a royal female elephant tied to a pillar and separated from her lord, the leader of the herd.

5.19.21.t:
उपवासेन शोकेन ध्यानेन च भयेन च ।
परिक्षीणां कृशां दीनामल्पाहारां तपोधनाम्
5.19.21.e: She was wasted and emaciated through fasting and grief, depressed due to brooding and threatenings. She ate very little but was rich with  austerities.

w: to the foremost of the Raghu family Rama
5.19.22.t:
आयाचमानां दुःखार्तां प्राञ्जलिं देवतामिव ।
भावेन रघुमुख्यस्य दशग्रीवपराभवम्
5.19.22.e: Tormented with grief, Sita looked like a goddess begging Rama, the foremost of the Raghu family with folded hands in her mind to destroy Ravana, the tennecked demon.

w: with attractive eyelashes and broad bright eyes
5.19.23.t:
समीक्षमाणां रुदतीमनिन्दितां सुपक्ष्मताम्रायतशुक्ललोचनाम् ।
अनुव्रतां राममतीव मैथिलीं प्रलोभयामास वधाय रावणः
5.19.23.e: Blameless Mythili with clear, large eyes and beautiful eyelashes with a reddish tint at the corners was looking around, crying. Ravana tried to allure Sita who was deeply faithful to Rama and threatened to kill her (when he found her unflinching). इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये सुन्दरकाण्डे एकोनविंशस्सर्गः। Thus ends the nineteenth sarga of Sundarakanda of the holy Ramayana, the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

5.20.1.t:
स तां परिवृतां दीनां निरानन्दां तपस्विनीम् ।
साकारैर्मधुरैर्वाक्यैर्न्यदर्शयत रावणः
5.20.1.e: Ravana expressed his intention in sweet words to the depressed and griefstricken ascetic Sita surrounded by demon guards:

w: richly endowed with beauty in all limbs
5.20.3.t:
कामये त्वां विशालाक्षि बहुमन्यस्व मां प्रिये ।
सर्वाङ्गगुणसम्पन्ने सर्वलोकमनोहरे
5.20.3.e: "O largeeyed one  you are endowed with beauty in all limbs. You are the delight of all worlds. I desire you, dear  Oblige me.

w: those who can change their form at their will
5.20.4.t:
नेह केचिन्मनुष्या वा राक्षसाः कामरूपिणः ।
व्यपसर्पतु ते सीते भयं मत्तः समुत्थितम्
5.20.4.e: "O Sita no human or demon. who can take any form at their will can relieve your fear born of me.

5.20.5.t:
स्वधर्मो रक्षसां भीरु सर्वथैव न संशयः ।
गमनं वा परस्त्रीणां हरणं सम्प्रमथ्य वा
5.20.5.e: "O timid lady having an unrighteous approach to wives of others or their abduction by force is natural to demons, There is no doubt.

w: not force to accept my desire
5.20.6.t:
एवं चैतदकामां तु न त्वां स्प्रक्ष्यामि मैथिलि ।
कामं कामः शरीरे मे यथाकामं प्रवर्तताम्
5.20.6.e: "Mythili  let passion hold its sway over my body as it will. But I shall not force you or touch you since you do not love me.

5.20.9.t:
विचित्राणि च माल्यानि चन्दनान्यगरूणि च ।
विविधानि च वासांसि दिव्यान्याभरणानि च महार्हाणि च पानानि शयनान्यासनानि च ।
गीतं नृत्तं च वाद्यं च लभ मां प्राप्य मैथिलि
5.20.9.e: "O Mythili having secured me, you get all these comforts wonderful garlands, sandal, incense, garments and beautiful ornaments, rich drinks, beds and seats.You can enjoy songs, dances accompanied by musical instruments.

5.20.12.t:
इदं ते चारु सञ्जातं यौवनं व्यतिवर्तते ।
यदतीतं पुनर्नैति स्रोतः शीघ्रमपामिव
5.20.12.e: "Your charming youth should not pass away (uselessly). A past event does not come back like a current of stream.

5.20.14.t:
त्वां समासाद्य वैदेहि रूपयौवनशालिनीम् ।
कः पुमानतिवर्तेत साक्षादपि पितामहः
5.20.14.e: "O Vaidehi you have (extraordinary) beauty  and (exuberant) youth. Who would not lose his balance of mind even if he were Brahma the grandsire himself after getting you?

w: with face like the cool fullmoon
5.20.15.t:
यद्यत्पश्यामि ते गात्रं शीतांशुसदृशानने ।
तस्मिंस्तस्मिन् पृथुश्रोणि चक्षुर्मम निबध्यते
5.20.15.e: "O one with a face like the cool fullmoon, with heavy hips. I am unable to extricate my eyes from any limb (of your body) I see.

5.20.16.t:
भव मैथिलि भार्या मे मोहमेनं विसर्जय ।
बह्वीनामुत्तमस्त्रीणामाहृतानामितस्ततः सर्वासामेव भद्रं ते ममाग्रमहिषी भव ।
5.20.16.e: "O Mythili  be my wife. Give up this (folly due to) delusion. Be my chief consort among the several excellent women I have picked up here and there. Be blessed.

5.20.17.t: लोकेभ्यो यानि रत्नानि सम्प्रमथ्याहृतानि वै तानि मे भीरु सर्वाणि राज्यं चैतदहं च ते ।
5.20.17.e: "O timid lady, gems brought forcibly from all the worlds, this kingdom as well as myself are yours.

5.20.18.t: विजित्य पृथिवीं सर्वां नानानगरमालिनीम् जनकाय प्रदास्यामि तव हेतोर्विलासिनि ।
5.20.18.e: "O lovely lady I will win all the cities and lands and give them to Janaka for your sake.

5.20.20.t: असकृत्संयुगे भग्ना मया विमृदितध्वजाः अशक्ताः प्रत्यनीकेषु स्थातुं मम सुरासुराः ।
5.20.20.e: "The gods and demons were unable to withstand my power in wars fought against me. They were often shattered and defeated with their flags crushed in war.

5.20.21.t:
इच्छ मां क्रियतामद्य प्रतिकर्म तवोत्तमम् सप्रभाण्यवसज्यन्तां तवाङ्गे भूषणानि च ।
साधु पश्यामि ते रूपं संयुक्तं प्रतिकर्मणा
5.20.21.e: "Offer your love to me. Get yourself decorated in an excellent way. Wear glowing ornaments on your limbs. Let me see you in pleasingly decorated form.

5.20.23.t:
प्रतिकर्माभिसंयुक्ता दाक्षिण्येन वरानने ।
भुंक्ष्व भोगान्यथाकामं पिब भीरु रमस्व च
5.20.23.e: "O charming lady decorate yourself liberally. Enjoy these pleasures as you please. Drink and make merry.

5.20.24.t:
यथेष्टं च प्रयच्छ त्वं पृथिवीं वा धनानि च ।
ललस्व मयि विस्रब्धा धृष्टमाज्ञापयस्व च
5.20.24.e: "Give away land and wealth as you wish. Enjoy with me freely and command me boldly. I will obey you by all means.

5.20.25.t:
मत्प्रसादाल्ललन्त्याश्च ललन्तां बान्धवास्तव ।
ऋद्धिं ममानुपश्य त्वं श्रियं भद्रे यशश्च मे
5.20.25.e: "O blessed lady, see my affluence and my fame. Seeing you enjoy (life) by my grace all your kinsmen will follow.

5.20.26.t:
किं करिष्यसि रामेण सुभगे चीरवाससा ।
निक्षिप्तविजयो रामो गतश्रीर्वनगोचरः व्रती स्थण्डिलशायी च शङ्के जीवति वा न वा ।
5.20.26.e: "O beautiful lady Rama has renounced victory, he has lost his fortune. Clad in bark, he is wandering in the forest following asceticism and sleeping on the ground. What can he do  for you? I am in doubt if he is alive or not.

5.20.27.t:
न हि वैदेहि रामस्त्वां द्रष्टुं वा प्युपलप्स्यते ।
पुरोबलाकैरसितैर्मेघैर्ज्योत्स्नामिवावृताम्
5.20.27.e: "O Vaidehi I wonder if Rama can see you at all. You are like moonlight veiled by dark clouds and  cannot  be seen even by the flying cranes.

w: even when you are not decorated
5.20.30.t: क्लिष्टकौशेयवसनां तन्वीमप्यनलङ्कृताम् त्वां दृष्ट्वा स्वेषु दारेषु रतिं नोपलभाम्यहम् ।
5.20.30.e: "Even when you are attired in soiled silk and are bereft of ornaments, I find no interest in my own wives.

w: best among the women in the three worlds
5.20.32.t: मम ह्यसितकेशान्ते त्रैलोक्यप्रवराः स्त्रियः तास्त्वां परिचरिष्यन्ति श्रियमप्सरसो यथा ।
5.20.32.e: "Lady of dark tresses, let those women of mine, the best among women in the three worlds, apsaras, wait upon you as they would upon the goddess Lakshmi."

5.20.34.t: न रामस्तपसा देवि न बलेन न विक्रमैः न धनेन मया तुल्यस्तेजसा यशसापि वा ।
5.20.34.e: "O queen Rama is not equal to me  either in penance or prowess or valour or wealth or brilliance or even in fame.

5.20.35.t:
पिब विहर रमस्व भुङ्क्ष्व भोगान् धननिचयं प्रदिशामि मेदिनीं च ।
मयि लल ललने यथासुखं त्वं त्वयि च समेत्य ललन्तु बान्धवास्ते
5.20.35.e: "O delightful one I will bestow you with heaps of riches and land. Therefore, enjoy with me drinking, sporting, and revelling. Accept me and be happy to sport with me.Let your elatives join you and enjoy all my wealth.

5.21.1.t:
तस्य तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा सीता रौद्रस्य रक्षसः ।
आर्ता दीनस्वरा दीनं प्रत्युवाच शनैर्वचः
5.21.1.e: On hearing the demon's haughty words, oppressed, pitiable Sita replied slowly in a sorrowful tone.

5.21.3.t: निवर्तय मनो मत्तः स्वजने क्रियतां मनः न मां प्रार्थयितुं युक्तं सुसिद्धिमिव पापकृत् ।
5.21.3.e: "Turn your mind away from me and fix it on your wives. You should not expect to seek me just as a sinner cannot hope to seek blessedness.

w: a woman devoted to a single husband
5.21.4.t: अकार्यं न मया कार्यमेकपत्न्या विगर्हितम् कुलं सम्प्राप्तया पुण्यं कुले महति जातया ।
5.21.4.e: "I was born of high lineage and joined a meritorious family by virtue of my marriage. I am devoted only to my husband. I should not commit this contemptible, forbidden act."

5.21.5.t: एवमुक्त्वा तु वैदेही रावणं तं यशस्विनी राक्षसं पृष्ठतः कृत्वा भूयो वचनमब्रवीत् ।
5.21.5.e: Glorious Vaidehi having thus spoken to the demon turned her back and continued:

5.21.6.t: नाहमौपयिकी भार्या परभार्या सती तव साधु धर्ममवेक्षस्व साधु साधुव्रतं चर ।
5.21.6.e: "I cannot be your lawful wife obtainable by your personal efforts. I am a chaste woman married to another man. (Being a king) examine the dharma honestly and adopt a pious way of life.

5.21.7.t: यथा तव तथान्येषां दारा रक्ष्या निशाचर आत्मानमुपमां कृत्वा स्वेषु दारेषु रम्यताम् ।
5.21.7.e: "O nightranger Enjoy your wives. Take care of them. Taking your example, others' wives also deserve to be protected.

w: one with no control over the senses
5.21.8.t: अतुष्टं स्वेषु दारेषु चपलं चलितेन्द्रियम् नयन्ति निकृतिप्रज्ञं परदाराः पराभवम् ।
5.21.8.e: "The wives of others will insult an evilminded man who is not satisfied with his own wives, is fickleminded and has no control over his senses.

w: that which is a forbidden act
5.21.9.t: इह सन्तो न वा सन्ति सतो वा नानुवर्तसे तथाहि विपरीता ते बुद्धिराचारवर्जिता ।
5.21.9.e: "Are there no pious men around or are you not heeding their words? Your mind is perverted and inclined to commit a forbidden act.

5.21.13.t: स्वकृतैर्हन्यमानस्य रावणादीर्घदर्शिनः अभिनन्दन्ति भूतानि विनाशे पापकर्मणः ।
5.21.13.e: "O Ravana living beings will welcome and enjoy the destruction of a shortsighted sinner killed by his own vile act.

5.21.14.t: एवं त्वां पापकर्माणं वक्ष्यन्ति निकृता जनाः दिष्ट्यैतद्व्यसनं प्राप्तो रौद्र इत्येव हर्षिताः ।
5.21.14.e: "Seeing you, getting ruined this way for your sin, those who were angry with you for their humiliation in your hands will feel glad and say 'Luckily this terrible fellow has met with his doom' .

w: of the lord of the people
5.21.16.t: उपधाय भुजं तस्य लोकनाथस्य सत्कृतम् कथं नामोपधास्यामि भुजमन्यस्य कस्य चित् ।
5.21.16.e: "How can I pillow on somebody's arm after resting on the honourable arm of the great lord of the worlds ?

5.21.18.t: साधु रावण रामेण मां समानय दुःखिताम् वने वाशितया सार्धं करेण्वेव गजाधिपम् ।
5.21.18.e: "O Ravana it is proper for you to unite me in distress with Rama as one would unite a female elephant with the lordly elephant from which it is separated in the wilderness.

5.21.19.t: मित्रमौपयिकं कर्तुं रामः स्थानं परीप्सता वधं चानिच्छता घोरं त्वयासौ पुरुषर्षभः ।
5.21.19.e: "I wish you to build friendship with Rama, the bull among men. Surely it is the right thing for you to do, if you are desirous of avoiding a dreadful death.

5.21.22.t: एवं हि ते भवेत्स्वस्ति सम्प्रदाय रघूत्तमे अन्यथा त्वं हि कुर्वाणो वधं प्राप्स्यसि रावण ।
5.21.22.e: "It is good for you to give me back to Rama, the foremost in the Raghu dynasty. Otherwise you will face death.

w: released by Indra who has performed a hundred yajnas
5.21.24.t: रामस्य धनुषः शब्दं श्रोष्यसि त्वं महास्वनम् शतक्रतुविसृष्टस्य निर्घोषमशनेरिव ।
5.21.24.e: "You will hear the terrible twang of Rama's bow resembling the rumble of the thunderbolt released by Indra who performed a hundred yajnas.

w: the shafts with feathers of Kanka bird
5.21.26.t: रक्षांसि परिनिघ्नन्तः पुर्यामस्यां समन्ततः असंपातं करिष्यन्ति पतन्तः कङ्कवाससः ।
5.21.26.e: "The shafts bound with feathers of Kanka birds (released by Rama and Lakshmana) will be killing the demons all over this Lanka. They will not give a chance for any other weapon to fall.

w: great serpents (in the form of demon chiefs)
5.21.27.t: राक्षसेन्द्रमहासर्पान् स रामगरुडो महान् उद्धरिष्यति वेगेन वैनतेय इवोरगान् ।
5.21.27.e: "Just as Garuda swiftly extirpates the serpents, Rama will exterminate the demon leaders.

5.21.28.t: अपनेष्यति मां भर्ता त्वत्तः शीघ्रमरिन्दमः असुरेभ्यः श्रियं दीप्तां विष्णुस्त्रिभिरिव क्रमैः ।
5.21.28.e: "My husband, the subduer of enemies, will soon take me away just as Lord Visnu in the form of Vamana took away the glowing prosperity from the demons with three strides.

5.21.29.t: जनस्थाने हतस्थाने निहते रक्षसां बले अशक्तेन त्वया रक्षः कृतमेतदसाधु वै ।
5.21.29.e: "When the army of demons as killed you had no capacity to protect and was destroyed at Janasthana, the place of death. You acted in this dishonest way.

5.21.30.t: आश्रमं तु तयोः शून्यं प्रविश्य नरसिंहयोः गोचरं गतयोर्भ्रात्रोरपनीता त्वयाधम ।
5.21.30.e: "You are a mean creature. Finding me in the vacant hut, when the two brothers, lions among men, were away, you  abducted me.

5.21.31.t: न हि गन्धमुपाघ्राय रामलक्ष्मणयोस्त्वया शक्यं संदर्शने स्थातुं शुना शार्दूलयोरिव ।
5.21.31.e: "Had you smelt the presence of Rama and Lakshmna, it would not have been possible for you to stand there, like a dog under the gaze of a pair of tigers.

5.21.32.t: तस्य ते विग्रहे ताभ्यां युगग्रहणमस्थिरम् वृत्रस्येवेन्द्रबाहुभ्यां बाहोरेकस्य विग्रहे ।
5.21.32.e: "You will not be able to withstand them in a battle. You will meet the same fate as the onearmed Vritra in a battle with the twoarmed Indra.

5.21.33.t: क्षिप्रं तव स नाथो मे रामः सौमित्रिणा सह तोयमल्पमिवादित्यः प्राणानादास्यते शरैः ।
5.21.33.e: "My lord Rama accompanied by Saumitri will draw out your life by his arrows swiftly as Aditya sucks up shallow water at once by his radiance.

5.21.34.t:
गिरिं कुबेरस्य गतोऽथ वालयं सभां गतो वा वरुणस्य राज्ञः ।
असंशयं दाशरथेर्न मोक्ष्यसे महाद्रुमः कालहतोऽशनेरिव
5.21.34.e: "Even if you fly to Kubera's mountain (Kailasa) or the residence of king Varuna (ocean) you will not escape Rama's arrows like a mighty tree cannot evade lightning. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये सुन्दरकाण्डे एकविंशस्सर्गः। Thus ends the twentyfirst sarga of Sundarakanda of the holy Ramayana, the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

5.22.1.t:
सीताया वचनं श्रुत्वा परुषं राक्षसाधिपः ।
प्रत्युवाच ततः सीतां विप्रियं प्रियदर्शनाम्
5.22.1.e: Hearing the sharp words of pleasing Sita, the lord of demons replied in unpleasant terms:

5.22.2.t:
यथा यथा सान्त्वयिता वश्यः स्त्रीणां तथा तथा ।
यथा यथा प्रियं वक्ता परिभूतस्तथा तथा
5.22.2.e: "The more the lover is courteous and loving and pleasing to women the more he is humiliated by them.

5.22.3.t:
सन्नियच्छति मे क्रोधं त्वयि कामः समुत्थितः ।
द्रवतोऽमार्गमासाद्य हयानिव सुसारथिः
5.22.3.e: "My love for you has restrained my anger, just as a good charioteer controls the horses galloping on a wrong path.

5.22.4.t:
वामः कामो मनुष्याणां यस्मिन् किल निबध्यते ।
जने तस्मिंस्त्वनुक्रोशः स्नेहश्च किल जायते
5.22.4.e: "Love is partial. It gets bound to those in whomsoever compassion and friendship is generated, even though they are punishable.

5.22.6.t:
परुषाणीह वाक्यानि यानि यानि ब्रवीषि माम् ।
तेषु तेषु वधो युक्तस्तव मैथिलि दारुणः
5.22.6.e: "O Mythili for each of the piercing statements made you deserve dreadful death."

5.22.9.t:
ऊर्ध्वं द्वाभ्यां तु मासाभ्यां भर्तारं मामनिच्छतीम् ।
मम त्वां प्रातराशार्थमालभन्ते महानसे
5.22.9.e: "If you are still reluctant to accept me as your husband after two months you will be sent to kitchen to be cooked as morning breakfast for me".

5.22.10.t:
तां तर्ज्यमानां सम्प्रेक्ष्य राक्षसेन्द्रेण जानकीम् ।
देवगन्धर्वकन्यास्ता विषेदुर्विकृतेक्षणाः
5.22.10.e: Observing Janaki, threatened by the demon king the daughters of gods and gandharvas shed tears with distressful eyes.

w: with movement of eyes and faces
5.22.11.e: When Sita was threatened by the demon king, the daughters of gods and gandharvas there consoled her through gestures of their lips and eyes.

w: proud of the power of her virtues
5.22.12.t:
ताभिराश्वासिता सीता रावणं राक्षसाधिपम् ।
उवाचात्महितं वाक्यं वृत्तशौण्डीर्यगर्वितम्
5.22.12.e: Having thus been consoled, Sita, proud of the power of her virtues, said this to Ravana in selfdefence:

5.22.14.t:
मां हि धर्मात्मनः पत्नीं शचीमिव शचीपतेः ।
त्वदन्यस्त्रिषु लोकेषु प्रार्थयेन्मनसापि कः
5.22.14.e: "Who in all the three worlds other than you would, even in mind, seek this consort of the righteous self (Sri Rama) like  Sachi to Indra? .

5.22.15.t:
राक्षसाधम रामस्य भार्याममिततेजसः ।
उक्तवानसि यत्पापं क्व गतस्तस्य मोक्ष्यसे
5.22.15.e: "O stupid demon where can you go to escape the consequences of your sinful words spoken against Rama's consort of undimmed brilliance?

5.22.21.t:
नापहर्तुमहं शक्या त्वया रामस्य धीमतः ।
विधिस्तव वधार्थाय विहितो नात्र संशयः
5.22.21.e: "When I was with wise Rama, it was not possible for you to abduct me. No doubt Providence has ordained this to bring about your death.

5.22.22.t:
शूरेण धनदभ्रात्रा बलैः समुदितेन च ।
अपोह्य रामं कस्माद्धि दारचौर्यं त्वया कृतम्
5.22.22.e: "You are a (great) warrior and a brother of Kubera. You possess an army. Then why did you abduct Rama's wife bypassing him?"

w: looked like a mass of dark cloud
who had strong arms and neck
5.22.24.t:
नीलजीमूतसङ्काशो महाभुजशिरोधरः ।
सिंहसत्त्वगतिः श्रीमान् दीप्त जिह्वाग्रलोचनः
5.22.24.e: Prosperous Ravana looked like a mass of dark cloud, with strong arms, stout neck, gait of a lion, a blazing tongue and burning eyes

w: with wonderful garlands and smeared with unguents
adorned with red flower garlands and clothes
5.22.25.e: He appeared taller with an unsteady crown. He was wearing wonderful red flower garlands and clothes and was smeared with unguents, shining in ornamental armlets.

w: of the colour of the rising Sun
5.22.28.e: He stood like a mountain with two Ashoka trees clothed with red leaves and flowers in the form of earrings of the colour of the rising Sun.

w: resembling the wishyielding tree in heaven
resembled a memorial structure built on the cremation ground
5.22.29.t:
स कल्पवृक्षप्रतिमो वसन्त इव मूर्तिमान् ।
श्मशानचैत्यप्रतिमो भूषितोऽपि भयङ्करः
5.22.29.e: He was comparable to the wishfulfilling tree grown in heaven, a personified spring season and a memorial structure raised on the cremation ground. He looked frightening even though  welladorned.

5.22.30.t:
अवेक्षमाणो वैदेहीं कोपसंरक्तलोचनः ।
उवाच रावणः सीतां भुजङ्ग इव निःश्वसन्
5.22.30.e: Looking at Vaidehi, eyes red with anger, and breathing heavily like a histing snake, Ravana replied:

w: a lady following a vow of chastity
5.22.31.e: "O Sita you are following a vow of chastity and treading a meaningless, wrong path. I will destroy you as the Sun dispels the morning twilight with his lustre".

w: who torments enemies with his terrific voice
5.22.32.t:
इत्युक्त्वा मैथिलीं राजा रावणः शत्रुरावणः ।
सन्दिदेश ततः सर्वा राक्षसीर्घोरदर्शनाः
5.22.32.e: King Ravana, a tormentor of enemies, having thus threatened Mythili commanded the shedemons women of fiecrceful appearance as follows:

w: who had ears like those of an elephant
one with the feet of an elephant and another with the hoofs of the horse
with a huge neck and head
with the face of a cow
5.22.33.t:
एकाक्षीमेककर्णां च कर्णप्रावरणां तथा ।
गोकर्णीं हस्तिकर्णीं च लम्बकर्णीमकर्णिकाम् हस्तिपाद्यश्वपाद्यौ च गोपादीं पादचूलिकाम् ।
एकाक्षीमेकपादीं च पृथुपादीमपादिकाम् अतिमात्रशिरोग्रीवामतिमात्रकुचोदरीम् ।
अतिमात्रास्यनेत्रां च दीर्घजिह्वामजिह्विकाम् अनासिकां सिंहमुखीं गोमुखीं सूकरीमुखीम् ।
5.22.33.e: Of them one had one eye, the other one ear, another with ears covered, one had the ear of a cow, another had ears of an elephant and yet another, long, hanging ears. One had the feet of an elephant, another, hoofs of a horse and still another of a cow. While one had a single foot, another had broad feet and yet another no feet at all. One had a long neck and a large head. One had large breasts and belly. One had a big face and eyes, another had a long tongue and yet another no tongue at all. One had no nose and still another had a lion face and yet another the face of a cow.

5.22.36.t: यथा मद्वशगा सीता क्षिप्रं भवति जानकी तथा कुरुत राक्षस्यः सर्वाः क्षिप्रं समेत्य च ।
5.22.36.e: "O demonesses, all of you jointly dispose Janaki towards me. See that she submits to me at once.

w: threatened by pointing his finger at her
5.22.38.t: इति प्रतिसमादिश्य राक्षसेन्द्रः पुनः पुनः काममन्युपरीतात्मा जानकीं पर्यतर्जयत् ।
5.22.38.e: The demon king repeatedly commanded the ogresses burning in anger and passion and threatened Sita again and again, pointing his finger at her.

5.22.39.t: उपगम्य ततः शीघ्रं राक्षसी धान्यमालिनी परिष्वज्य दशग्रीवमिदं वचनमब्रवीत् ।
5.22.39.e: An ogress called Dhanyamalini at once approached the tenheaded Ravana and embracing him, said:.

5.22.40.t: मया क्रीड महाराज सीतया किं तवानया विवर्णया कृपणया मानुष्या राक्षसेश्वर ।
5.22.40.e: "O king of demons, sport with me, my lord. What purpose will be served with this pale wretched Sita, a human being after all?

5.22.42.t: अकामां कामयानस्य शरीरमुपतप्यते इच्छन्तीं कामयानस्य प्रीतिर्भवति शोभना ।
5.22.42.e: "Only the body of a man is tormented who desires a woman devoid of desire; but a lady who herself desires is enjoyable to one who desires her."

w: blazing like the glow of the midday sun
5.22.44.t: प्रस्थितः स दशग्रीवः कम्पयन्निव मेदिनीम् ज्वलद्भास्करवर्णाभं प्रविवेश निवेशनम् ।
5.22.44.e: Thereupon the tennecked demon departed, as if he was shaking the earth and entered his residence which was shining like the blazing midday Sun.

5.23.1.t:
इत्युक्त्वा मैथिलीं राजा रावणः शत्रुरावणः ।
सन्दिश्य च ततः सर्वा राक्षसीर्निर्जगाम ह
5.23.1.e: King Ravana, tormentor of enemies, having thus spoken to Mythili commanded the demonesses and departed.

5.23.2.t:
निष्क्रान्ते राक्षसेन्द्रे तु पुनरन्तःपुरं गते ।
राक्षस्यो भीमरूपास्ताः सीतां समभिदुद्रुवुः
5.23.2.e: As the demon king left for his abode all the demonesses of hideous looks rushed towards Sita and crowded around her.

5.23.3.t:
ततः सीतामुपागम्य राक्षस्यः क्रोधमूर्छिताः ।
परं परुषया वाचा वैदेहीमिदमब्रुवन्
5.23.3.e: The demonesses, overcome with anger, approached Sita and harshly said:

w: with a belly of the size of the palm
5.23.5.t:
ततस्त्वेकजटा नाम राक्षसी वाक्यमब्रवीत् ।
आमन्त्य्र क्रोधाताम्राक्षी सीतां करतलोदरीम्
5.23.5.e: Then Ekajata, a shedemon of hideous looks, eyes red with anger and a belly of the size of the palm said to Sita:

5.23.6.t:
प्रजापतीनां षण्णां तु चतुर्थो यः प्रजापतिः ।
मानसो ब्रह्मणः पुत्रः पुलस्त्य इति विश्रुतः
5.23.6.e: 'The mindborn son of Brahma is well known as Paulastya. He was the fourth  among the six Prajapatis (Maricha, Atri, Angira, Pulastya, Plaha, Kratu).

5.23.8.t:
तस्य पुत्रो विशालाक्षि रावणः शत्रुरावणः ।
तस्य त्वं राक्षसेन्द्रस्य भार्या भवितुमर्हसि मयोक्तं चारुसर्वाङ्गिः वाक्यं किं नानुमन्यसे ।
5.23.8.e: 'O largeeyes lady to become the wife of the lord of demons is a stroke of good luck. You deserve to be one. O lady of beautiful limbs why don't you accept his proposal?'

5.23.10.t: येन देवास्त्रयस्त्रिंशद्देवराजश्च निर्जिताः तस्य त्वं राक्षसेन्द्रस्य भार्या भवितुमर्हसि ।
5.23.10.e: 'You ought to be the wife of the lord of ogres who has vanquished thirty three crores of gods including Indra, their king.'

5.23.12.t: वीर्योत्सिक्तस्य शूरस्य सङ्ग्रामेषु निवर्तिनः बलिनो वीर्ययुक्तस्य भार्यात्वं किं न लप्स्यसे ।
5.23.12.e: 'Why don't you wish to be the wife of such a mighty and powerful king, a valiant hero who has never beaten a retreat in war?

5.23.13.t: प्रियां बहुमतां भार्यां त्यक्त्वा राजा महाबलः सर्वासां च महाभागां त्वामुपैष्यति रावणः ।
5.23.13.e: 'Even renouncing his highly respectable,  favourite wife among all, mighty Ravana is prepared to accept you.

5.23.14.t: समृद्धं स्त्रीसहस्रेण नानारत्नोपशोभितम् अन्तःपुरं समुत्सृज्य त्वामुपैष्यति रावणः ।
5.23.14.e: 'Ravana is prepared to abandon a thousand wives in his prosperous harem  decorated with all kinds of gems in order to accept you.'

5.23.15.t:
अन्या तु विकटा नाम राक्षसी वाक्यमब्रवीत् असकृद्देवता युद्धे नागगन्धर्वदानवाः ।
निर्जिताः समरे येन स ते पार्श्वमुपागतः
5.23.15.e: Another ogress called Vikata said, ' Know that he who has often defeated gods in war and has vanquished nagas, gandharvas and demons has come to you (seeking your favour)'.

5.23.18.t:
ततस्तु दुर्मुखी नाम राक्षसी वाक्यमब्रवीत् ।
यस्य सूर्यो न तपति भीतो यस्य च मारुतः न वाति स्मायतापाङ्गे किं त्वं तस्य न तिष्ठसि ।
5.23.18.e: Then an ogress called Durmukhi said, 'O lady of long sideglances why don't you yield to him, afraid of whom the Sun scorches not and strong winds blow not?

w: for the king of the southwest Ravana
5.23.19.t:
पुष्पवृष्टिं च तरवो मुमुचुर्यस्य वै भयात् शैलाश्च सुभ्रु पानीयं जलदाश्च यदेच्छति ।
तस्य नैरृतराजस्य राजराजस्य भामिनि किं त्वं न कुरुषे बुद्धिं भार्यार्थे रावणस्य हि ।
5.23.19.e: 'O lady of beautiful brows why don't you make up your mind to accept the king of kings, afraid of whom the trees rain flowers, the mountains and clouds release water at his will? Ravana is the king of the southwest, direction Why don't you wish to be his wife?

5.23.20.t:
साधु ते तत्त्वतो देवि कथितं साधु भामिनि ।
गृहाण सुस्मिते वाक्यमन्यथा न भविष्यसि
5.23.20.e: "Well have you spoken the truth, lady, well indeed, O radiant one. Take our word, sweet-smiling one, or otherwise you shall not live."

5.24.1.t:
ततः सीतामुपागम्य राक्षस्यो विकृताननाः ।
परुषं परुषा नार्य ऊचुस्तां वाक्यमप्रियम्
5.24.1.e: Then the hideous ogresses approached Sita and spoke these harsh words in an unbecoming manner:

w: you are holding this in high esteem
5.24.3.t:
मानुषी मानुषस्यैव भार्यात्वं बहुमन्यसे ।
प्रत्याहर मनो रामान्न त्वं जातु भविष्यसि
5.24.3.e: 'You are  a woman, wife of Rama, an ordinary mortal you are holding in high esteem. Withdraw your mind from Rama or else you will not survive.

w: enjoy the wealth of the three worlds
5.24.4.t:
त्रैलोक्यवसुभोक्तारं रावणं राक्षसेश्वरम् ।
भर्तारमुपसङ्गम्य विहरस्व यथासुखम्
5.24.4.e: "Accept Ravana as your husband and after uniting with him enjoy all the pleasures of the three worlds.

5.24.5.t:
मानुषी मानुषं तं तु राममिच्छसि शोभने ।
राज्याद्भ्र्रष्टमसिद्धार्थं विक्लबं त्वमनिन्दिते
5.24.5.e: 'O charming lady you have an irreproachable beauty and grace. Why do you think of human Rama only who has been dethroned from the kingdom. He is only a human being who is unsuccessful and distressful.'

w: a lady with eyes like lotus petals
5.24.6.t:
राक्षसीनां वचः श्रुत्वा सीता पद्मनिभेक्षणा ।
नेत्राभ्यामश्रुपूर्णाभ्यामिदं वचनमब्रवीत्
5.24.6.e: Hearing the words of the ogresses, Sita with eyes like lotus petals full of tears replied this way:

5.24.7.t:
यदिदं लोकविद्विष्टमुदाहरथ सङ्गताः ।
नैतन्मनसि वाक्यं मे किल्बिषं प्रतिभाति वः
5.24.7.e: "All of you joined together and spoke such words that are not acceptable to the world. Your sinful words of advice do not appeal to me.

5.24.8.t:
न मानुषी राक्षसस्य भार्या भवितुमर्हति ।
कामं खादत मां सर्वा न करिष्यामि वो वचः
5.24.8.e: ' A human being ought not to become wife of a demon. Devour me if you want. I refuse to accept your advice.'

5.24.10.t:
यथा शची महाभागा शक्रं समुपतिष्ठति ।
अरुन्धती वसिष्ठं च रोहिणी शशिनं यथा लोपामुद्रा यथागस्त्यं सुकन्या च्यवनं यथा ।
सावित्री सत्यवन्तं च कपिलं श्रीमती यथा सौदासं मदयन्तीव केशिनी सगरं यथा ।
नैषधं दमयन्तीव भैमी पतिमनुव्रता तथाऽहमिक्ष्वाकुवरं रामं पतिमनुव्रता ।
5.24.10.e: 'I am steadfast (in love) to my husband Rama, the foremost of the Ikshvaku family in the same manner as noble Sachi to Indra, Arundhati to Vasistha, Rohini to the Moon, Lopamudra to Agastya, Sukanya to sage Chyavana, Savitri to Satyavan, Srimati to Kapilamuni Madayanti to Soudasu, Kesini to king Sagara and Bhima's daughter Damayanti to her lord Nala, (the king of Nishadas)'.

5.24.13.t: सीताया वचनं श्रुत्वा राक्षस्यः क्रोधमूर्छिताः भर्त्सयन्ति स्म परुषैर्वाक्यै रावणचोदिताः ।
5.24.13.e: Hearing the reply of Sita, the ogresses ordered by Ravana and overtaken by anger again began to threaten Sita using harsh words.

5.24.14.t: अवलीनः स निर्वाक्यो हनूमान् शिंशुपाद्रुमे यसीतां सन्तर्जयन्तीस्ता राक्षसीरशृणोत् कपिः ।
5.24.14.e: Hanuman who kept himself concealed on the simsupa tree speechlessly listened to the ogresses threatening Sita.

5.24.15.t: तामभिक्रम्य सङ्कृद्धा वेपमानां समन्ततः भृशं संलिलिहुर्दीप्तान् प्रलम्बान् दशनच्छदान् ।
5.24.15.e: Sita was trembling in fear. The  enraged ogresses went on licking their lips hanging, again and again.

5.24.16.t: ऊचुश्च परमक्रुद्धाः प्रगृह्याशु परश्वधान् नेयमर्हति भर्तारं रावणं राक्षसाधिपम् ।
5.24.16.e: The enraged ogresses immediately picked up the axes and rose up saying, 'she is unfit to have the demon king, Ravana as her husband'.

5.24.19.t: तां कृशां दीनवदनां मलिनाम्बरधारिणीम् भर्त्सयाञ्चक्रिरे सीतां राक्षस्यस्तां समन्ततः ।
5.24.19.e: The ogresses started intimidating Sita who was dressed in soiled clothes and emaciated with a dejected look on her face.

5.24.21.t: सीते पर्याप्तमेतावद्भर्तुः स्नेहो निदर्शितः सर्वात्रातिकृतं भद्रे व्यसनायोपकल्पते
5.24.21.e: 'O Sita you have shown your love for your husband to this extent. It is enough. O auspicious lady anything carried to excess leads to adversity.

5.24.22.t: परितुष्टास्मि भद्रं ते मानुषस्ते कृतो विधिः ममापि तु वचः पथ्यं ब्रुवन्त्याः कुरु मैथिलि ।
5.24.22.e: "O Mythili I beseech you (to oblige Ravana). You have discharged your duty as a human being. Be happy. But you should also heed my advice which is, after all, salutary.

5.24.23.t:
रावणं भज भर्तारं भर्तारं सर्वरक्षसाम् विक्रान्तं रूपवन्तं च सुरेशमिव वासवम् ।
दक्षिणं त्यागशीलं च सर्वस्य प्रियदर्शनम्
5.24.23.e: 'Accept as your husband the demon king Ravana, courageous and handsome like Indra, king of the gods generous, sacrificing and pleasing.

5.24.25.t:
मानुषं कृपणं रामं त्यक्त्वा, रावणमाश्रय ।
दिव्याङ्गरागा वैदेहि दिव्याभरणभूषिता अद्यप्रभृति सर्वेषां लोकानामीश्वरी भव ।
5.24.25.e: 'Leave the helpless human Rama and seek Ravana's refuge. O Vaidehi, using the heavenly unguents and adorned with imposing ornaments from now on, be the queen of all people.

5.24.27.t: एतदुक्तं च मे वाक्यं यदि त्वं न करिष्यसि अस्मिन्मुहूर्ते सर्वास्त्वां भक्षयिष्यामहे वयम् ।
5.24.27.e: 'If you do not heed our words of advice, all of us will eat you at this very moment.'

5.24.29.t: बहून्यप्रियरूपाणि वचनानि सुदुर्मते अनुक्रोशान्मृदुत्वाच्च सोढानि तव मैथिलि ।
5.24.29.e: O wicked Mythili! we have tolerated many unpleasant words uttered by you due to our kindness and mildness..

5.24.30.t:
न च नः कुरुषे वाक्यं हितं कालपुरस्कृतम् आनीतासि समुद्रस्य पारमन्यैर्दुरासदम् ।
रावणान्तःपुरं घोरं प्रविष्टा चासि मैथिलि
5.24.30.e: 'O Mythili you have heeded not our good and timely advice tendered in your interest. You have been brought to the other shore of the ocean and to the inner chambers of Ravana which is very difficult for others to access.

5.24.33.t:
कुरुष्व हितवादिन्या वचनं मम मैथिलि ।
अलमश्रुप्रपातेन त्यज शोकमनर्थकम्
5.24.33.e: 'Mythili, act according to our advice. I am your wellwisher. Give up sorrow and stop shedding useless tears.

5.24.36.t:
उद्यानानि च रम्याणि पर्वतोपवनानि च ।
सह राक्षसराजेन चर त्वं मदिरेक्षणे
5.24.36.e: 'O lady of intoxicating eyes range in the company of the demon king, the delightful gardens and mountain ranges filled with gardens.

5.24.38.t:
उत्पाट्य वा ते हृदयं भक्षयिष्यामि मैथिलि ।
यदि मे व्याहृतं वाक्यं न यथावत्करिष्यसि
5.24.38.e: 'O Mythili if you heed not my words of advice, I will pluck out your heart and eat it up'.

5.24.40.t:
इमां हरिणलोलाक्षीं त्रासोत्कम्पिपयोधराम् ।
रावणेन हृतां दृष्टवा दौहृदो मे महानभूत्
5.24.40.e: 'I have developed a morbid desire to feast upon this woman with eyes flashing like doe's, whose breasts heave with stress and fear after she was abducted by Ravana.

5.24.47.t:
सुरा चानीयतां क्षिप्रं सर्वशोकविनाशिनी ।
मानुषं मांसमास्वाद्य नृत्यामोऽथ निकुम्भिलाम्
5.24.47.e: 'Get the wine quickly, destroyer of all sorrows. After relishing the human flesh we will start Nikumbhila dance.'

w: like the daughter of a god
5.24.48.t:
एवं संभर्त्स्यमाना सा सीता सुरसुतोपमा ।
राक्षसीभिः सुघोराभिर्दैर्यमुत्सृज्य रोदिति
5.24.48.e: Threatened by the ogresses in that manner, Sita who was like the daughter of a god, cried aloud. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये सुन्दरकाण्डे चतुर्विंशस्सर्गः। Thus ends the twentyfourth sarga of Sundarakanda of the holy Ramayana, the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

5.25.1.t:
अथ तासां वदन्तीनां परुषं दारुणं बहु ।
राक्षसीनामासौम्यानां रुरोद जनकात्मजा
5.25.1.e: On hearing the many harsh words of dire threat by the ugly ogresses, the daughter of Janaka wept.

5.25.2.t:
एवमुक्ता तु वैदेही राक्षसीभिर्मनस्विनी ।
उवाच परमत्रस्ता भाष्पग्द्गदया गिरा
5.25.2.e: In reply to the ogresses who thus spoke, noble Vaidehi, terribly frightened, said in a voice choked with tears.

5.25.6.t:
सा त्वशोकस्य विपुलां शाखामालम्ब्य पुष्पिताम् ।
चिन्तयामास शोकेन भर्तारं भग्नमानसा
5.25.6.e: Laying hold on a large blossoming branch of the Ashoka tree, Sita thought of her husband with a broken heart.

5.25.8.t:
सा वेपमाना पतिता प्रवाते कदली यथा ।
राक्षसीनां भयत्रस्ता विवर्णवदनाभवत्
5.25.8.e: Trembling like a banana tree uprooted by the stormy wind, Sita who was seized with fear of the ogresses looked pale and desperate.

5.25.9.t:
तस्याः सा दीर्घविपुला वेपन्त्या सीतया तदा ।
ददृशे कम्पिनी वेणी व्यालीव परिसर्पती
5.25.9.e: The long, luxuriant braid of hair of the trembling Sita waving (in the wind), appeared like a crawling female serpent.

5.25.10.t:
सा निःश्वसन्ती दुःखार्ता शोकोपहतचेतना ।
आर्ता व्यसृजदश्रूणि मैथिली विललाप च
5.25.10.e: The distressed Mythili, her consciousness drowned in grief, sighing, shed streams of tears.

w: by the speed of the wind
5.25.14.t:
एषाल्पपुण्या कृपणा विनशिष्याम्यनाथवत् ।
समुद्रमध्ये नौः पूर्णा वायुवेगैरिवाहता
5.25.14.e: 'I am a woman of low merit, a wretched woman, an orphan. I will be ruined like the loaded boat that gets hit in the midst of the ocean by the stormy wind.

w: one who has eyes like lotus petals
one who walks majestically like a lion
5.25.16.t:
तं पद्मदलपत्राक्षं सिंहविक्रान्तगामिनम् ।
धन्याः पश्यन्ति मे नाथं कृतज्ञं प्रियवादिनम्
5.25.16.e: 'Blessed are those who are in touch with my husband with eyes like lotus petals, whose walk is majestic like a lion's, who has a sense of gratitude and is pleasing in words.

5.25.17.t:
सर्वथा तेन हीनाया रामेण विदितात्मना ।
तीक्ष्णं विषमिवास्वाद्य दुर्लभं मम जीवितम्
5.25.17.e: 'Separated from Rama endowed with selfknowledge, it is impossible for me to live like one who has drunk venom.

5.25.18.t:
कीदृशं तु महापापं मया जन्मान्तरे कृतम् ।
यनेदं प्राप्यते दुःखं मया घोरं सुदारुणम्
5.25.18.e: 'I do not know what great sin I have committed in my past life for which I experience this terrific, cruel affliction?

5.26.5.t:
न हि मे जीवितेनार्थो नैवार्थेर्न च भूषणैः ।
वसन्त्या राक्षसीमध्ये विना रामं महारथम्
5.26.5.e: "In the absence of the great charioteer Rama, of what use is my living in the midst of ogresses? I need no wealth, no ornaments.

5.26.6.t:
अश्मसारमिदं नूनमथवाप्यजरामरम् ।
हृदयं मम येनेदं न दुःखेनावशीर्यते
5.26.6.e: "It may be, that my heart is made of stone or it has no age or death since it does not riven even with grief.

5.26.7.t:
धिङ्मामनार्यामसतीं याहं तेना विना कृता ।
मुहूर्तमपि रक्षामि जीवितं पापजीविता
5.26.7.e: "I am preserving this sinful life like this though separated from Rama. Fie on me, for this wretched, infidel life

5.26.8.t:
का च मे जीविते श्रद्धा सुखे वा तं प्रियं विना ।
भर्तारं सागरान्ताया वसुधायाः प्रियंवदम्
5.26.8.e: "How can I have interest in any kind of pleasure without my sweettongued husband, the lord of the whole earth extending up to the ocean.

5.26.9.t:
भिद्यतां भक्ष्यतां वापि शरीरं विसृजाम्यहम् ।
न चाप्यहं चिरं दुःखं सहेयं प्रियवर्जिता
5.26.9.e: "I will give up my body. Break me  into pieces or eat me up. I cannot bear the sorrow of separation from my dear Rama any longer.

5.26.10.t:
चरणेनापि सव्येन न स्पृशेयं निशाचरम् ।
रावणं किं पुनरहं काममेयं विगर्हितम्
5.26.10.e: "I will not even touch that vile nightranger Ravana with my left foot. What to speak of loving him.

5.26.12.t:
छिन्ना भिन्ना विभक्ता वा दीप्तेवाग्नौ प्रदीपिता ।
रावणं नोपतिष्ठेयं किं प्रलापेन वश्चिरम्
5.26.12.e: "Even if I am cut, broken to pieces or burnt in glowing fire, I will not accept Ravana. Why do you shout for so long?

5.26.14.t:
राक्षसानां सहस्राणि जनस्थाने चतुर्दश ।
येनैकेन निरस्तानि स मां किं नाभिपद्यते
5.26.14.e: "He who destroyed fourteen thousand demons singlehanded has not come to protect me. I do not know why.

5.26.17.t:
कामं मध्ये समुद्रस्य लङ्केयं दुष्प्रधर्षणा ।
न तु राघवबाणानां गतिरोधो भविष्यति
5.26.17.e: "This Lanka in the middle of the ocean is unassailable. But there is nothing which can resist the arrows of Rama.

5.26.18.t:
किन्नु तत्कारणं येन रामो दृढपराक्रमः ।
रक्षसापहृतां भार्यामिष्टां नाभ्यवपद्यते
5.26.18.e: "What may be the reason that my loving husband, Rama who is highly powerful has not reached this place to which I was abducted by the demon.

5.26.19.t:
इहस्थां मां न जानीते शङ्के लक्ष्मणपूर्वजः ।
जानन्नपि हि तेजस्वी धर्षणं मर्षयिष्यति
5.26.19.e: "The elder brother of Lakshamana does not know that I am here. Or, I'm afraid, the glorious Rama knows and yet tolerates such an outrageous act.

5.26.22.t:
यदि मामिह जानीयाद्वर्तमानां स राघवः ।
अद्य बाणैरभिक्रुद्धः कुर्याल्लोकमराक्षसम्
5.26.22.e: "Had only Raghava known that I was here he would have freed this world of demons with his anger.

w: of those women who lost husbands
5.26.24.t:
ततो निहतनाथानां राक्षसीनां गृहे गृहे ।
यथाहमेवं रुदती तथा भूयो न संशयः
5.26.24.e: "Like me weeping, the cry of ogresses with lost husbands will be heard in every house in Lanka. There is no doubt.

5.26.25.t:
अन्विष्य रक्षसां लङ्कां कुर्याद्रामस्सलक्ष्मणः ।
न हि ताभ्यां रिपुर्दृष्टो मुहूर्तमपि जीवति
5.26.25.e: "If only Lakshmana and Rama in their quest for Lanka reach here, it is  not possible within their sight for the enemy to survive  even a moment.

5.26.28.t:
यादृशानीह दृश्यन्ते लङ्कायामशुभानि वै ।
अचिरेणैव कालेन भविष्यति हतप्रभा
5.26.28.e: "Inauspicious signs are seen here in Lanka. In a short time this city will lose its splendour.

5.26.29.t:
नूनं लङ्का हते पापे रावणे राक्षसाधमे ।
शोषं यास्यति दुर्धर्षा प्रमदा विधवा यथा
5.26.29.e: "Surely this impregnable Lanka will wither up (lose its splendour) and appear like a widow when this sinful Ravana, a mean demon is killed.

5.26.31.t:
नूनं राक्षसकन्यानां रुदन्तीनां गृहे गृहे ।
श्रोष्यामि नचिरादेव दुःखार्तानामिह ध्वनिम्
5.26.31.e: "I shall surely hear very soon sounds of distressful cry of young ogresses in every household.

5.26.33.t:
यदि नाम स शूरो मां रामो रक्तान्तलोचनः ।
जानीयाद्वर्तमानां हि रावणस्य निवेशने अनेन तु नृशंसेन रावणेनाधमेन मे ।
समयो यस्तु निर्दिष्टस्तस्य कालोऽयमागतः स च मे विहितो मृत्युरस्मिन् दुष्टे न वर्तते ।
5.26.33.e: "If the heroic Rama of bloodshot eyes comes to know that I am here at Ravana's, the expiry of time limit fixed by this cruel, lowly, foolish Ravana has arrived, this wicked fellow's death is inevitable.

5.26.35.t:
अकार्यं ये न जानन्ति नैर्ऋताः पापकारिणः अधर्मात्तु महोत्पातो भविष्यति हि सांप्रतम् ।
नैते धर्मं विजानन्ति राक्षसाः पिशिताशनाः
5.26.35.e: Nothing is forbidden for sinful demons. A calamity will befall now due to this adharma. The flesheating ogres are aware of neither dharma nor adharma.

w: one whose eyes have a reddish tinge in the corners
5.26.37.t:
ध्रुवं मां प्रातराशार्थे राक्षसः कल्पयिष्यति ।
साहं कथं करिष्यामि तं विना प्रियदर्शनम् रामं रक्तान्तनयनमपश्यन्ती सुदुःखिता ।
5.26.37.e: "This demon is determined to make me his morning meal. How can I do anything in the absence of my lord of pleasing countenance. I am distressed very much by not seeing Rama, possessed of eyes with a reddish tinge in the corners.

5.26.38.t: यदि कश्चित् प्रदाता मे विषस्याद्य भवेदिह क्षिप्रं वैवस्वतं देवं पश्येयं पतिना विना ।
5.26.38.e: "If I can find some one who can give me poison now I shall soon see the lord of death without my lord.

5.26.40.t: नूनं ममैव शोकेन स वीरो लक्ष्मणाग्रजः देवलोकमितो यातस्त्यक्त्वा देहं महीतले ।
5.26.40.e: "Would it be that the heroic elder brother of Lakshmana has gone to the abode of gods unable to find me on this earth?

5.26.41.t: धन्या देवास्सगन्धर्वाः सिद्धाश्च परमर्षयः मम पश्यन्ति ये नाथं रामं राजीवलोचनम् ।
5.26.41.e: "Blessed are the gods, gandharvas, and siddhas and great sages who are able to see my lotuseyed lord Rama.

w: one who is ever seeking dharma
5.26.42.t: अथवा न हि तस्यार्थो धर्मकामस्य धीमतः मया रामस्य राजर्षेर्भार्यया परमात्मनः ।
5.26.42.e: Or that royal sage, wise Rama who always seeks dharma having become one with the supreme spirit has no longer any interest in me?

5.26.43.t: दृश्यमाने भवेत्प्रीति स्सौहृदं नास्त्यपश्यतः नाशयन्ति कृतघ्नास्तु न रामो नाशयिष्यति ।
5.26.43.e: "Love attaches itself to one who remains before one's eyes.Friendship fades with separation. The ungrateful destroy love and friendship (as their love is conditioned by frequent meetings). But it cannot happen in case of Rama.

5.26.44.t: किं नु मे न गुणाः केचित्किं वा भाग्यक्षयो मम याहं सीदामि रामेण हीना मुख्येन भामिनी ।
5.26.44.e: "Do I, a charming lady, not have any good fortune because of my past deeds? I wonder how a foremost woman like me seperated from my husband is sinking in grief without Rama. Has my fortune diminished?

5.26.45.e: Instead of living separated from noble and brave Rama, a blemishless character and a destroyer of enemies, it is better for me to die.

5.26.48.t: साऽहमेवङ्गते काले मर्तुमिच्छामि सर्वथा न च मे विहितो मृत्युरस्मिन् दुःखेऽपि वर्तते ।
5.26.48.e: "By all means I wish to die in these circumstances. However, death is not ordained for me even in this sorrowful state.

w: who have given up all sins
5.26.49.t: धन्याः खलु महात्मानो मुनयस्त्यक्तकिल्बिषाः जितात्मनो महाभागा येषां न स्तः प्रियाप्रिये ।
5.26.49.e: Blessed are the exhalted sages who have not committed any sin. They have self control and have subdued their senses. There is no pleasure or displeasure for them.

5.26.50.t: प्रियान्न संभवेद्दुःखमप्रियादधिकं भयम् ताभ्यां हि ये वियुज्यन्ते नमस्तेषां महात्मनाम् ।
5.26.50.e: "Salutations to those exalted souls who have distanced themselves from pleasure and displeasure. Pleasures may not lead to suffering or displeasure to excessive, meaningless fear for such great souls.

5.27.1.t:
इत्युक्तास्सीतया घोरं राक्षस्यः क्रोधमूर्छिताः ।
काश्चिज्जग्मुस्तदाख्यातुं रावणस्य तरस्विनः
5.27.1.e: Hearing Sita's words, some terrifying demonesses, overwhelmed with anger, went to inform Ravana, who was quick to act.

w: O woman determined in evil ways
5.27.3.t:
अद्येदानीं तवानार्ये सीते पापविनिश्चये ।
राक्षस्यो भक्षयिष्यन्ति मांसमेतद्यथासुखम्
5.27.3.e: "O vile one you are determined in your evil ways. Today these shedemons will eat away your flesh to their heart's content ".

5.27.4.t:
सीतां ताभिरनार्याभिर्दृष्टवा सन्तर्जितां तदा ।
राक्षसी त्रिजटा वृद्धा शयाना वाक्यमब्रवीत्
5.27.4.e: Then seeing the ignoble shedemons threatening Sita, an old demoness called Trijata, who was lying down there, said:

5.27.7.t:
एवमुक्तास्त्रिजटया राक्षस्यः क्रोधमूर्छिताः ।
सर्वा एवाब्रुवन्भीतास्त्रिजटां तामिदं वचः
5.27.7.e: Seized with fear, the shedemons, overcome with wrath on hearing Trijata's words said to her.

5.27.8.t:
कथयस्व त्वया दृष्टः स्वप्नोऽयं कीदृशो निशि ।
तासां श्रुत्वा तु वचनं राक्षसीनां मुखाच्युतम् उवच वचनं काले त्रिजटा स्वप्नसंश्रितम् ।
5.27.8.e: "O Trijata, tell us the kind of dream you dreamt last night", they insisted. Hearing the words from the mouth of the shedemons, Trijata told them all about her dream.

w: wearing a garland of white flowers and clad in white attire
5.27.9.t:
गजदन्तमयीं दिव्यां शिबिकामन्तरिक्षगाम् युक्तां हंससहस्रेण स्वयमास्थाय राघवः ।
शुक्लमाल्याम्बरधरो लक्ष्मणेन सहागतः
5.27.9.e: "Rama, in white attire, wearing a garland of white flowers, ascending a palanquin made of ivory drawn by a thousand swans and coursing through the sky with Lakshmana arrived.

5.27.11.t:
स्वप्ने चाद्य मया दृष्टा सीता शुक्लाम्बरावृता ।
सागरेण परिक्षिप्तं श्वेतं पर्वतमास्थिता
5.27.11.e: "I also saw Sita in my dream wearing white robes and perched on a white mountain surrounded by the ocean.

5.27.12.t:
रामेण सङ्गता सीता भास्करेण प्रभा यथा ।
राघवश्च मया दृष्टश्चतुर्दष्ट्रं महागजम् आरूढ श्शैलसङ्काशं चचार सहलक्ष्मणः ।
5.27.12.e: "Just as light is united with the Sun, I saw Sita united with Rama. I saw Rama with Lakshmana riding a huge, mountainlike elephant having four tusks.

5.27.13.t: ततस्तौ नरशार्दूलौ दीप्यमानौ स्वतेजसा शुक्लमाल्याम्बरधरौ जानकीं पर्युपस्थितौ ।
5.27.13.e: "Dressed in white garlands and clothes, the two brothers, tigers among men, glowing in their effulgence approached Janaki.

5.27.14.t: ततस्तस्य नगस्याग्रे ह्याकाशस्थस्य दन्तिनः भर्त्रा परिगृहीतस्य जानकी स्कन्धमाश्रिता ।
5.27.14.e: "Then from the front of the mountain Janaki shifted to the back of the elephant held by her husband waiting in the sky.

5.27.16.t: ततस्ताभ्यां कुमाराभ्यामास्थित: स गजोत्तमः सीतया च विशालाक्ष्या लङ्काया उपरिस्थितः ।
5.27.16.e: "Then the excellent elephant was seen halted in the city of Lanka with both princes and the largeeyed Sita mounted on the elephant.

5.27.17.t: पाण्डुरर्षभयुक्तेन रथेनाष्टयुजा स्वयम् इहोपयातः काकुत्स्थ स्सीतया सह भार्यया ।
5.27.17.e: "Rama accompanied by his wife Sita came on a chariot yoked to eight white oxen.

5.27.20.t:
एवं स्वप्ने मया दृष्टो रामो विष्णुपराक्रमः ।
लक्ष्मणेन सह भ्रात्रा सीतया सह राघवः
5.27.20.e: "In this way I saw in my dream Rama as valiant as Lord Visnu accompanied by his brother Lakshmana and his wife Sita.

5.27.21.t:
न हि रामो महातेजाश्शक्यो जेतुं सुरासुरैः ।
राक्षसैर्वापि चान्यैर्वा स्वर्गः पापजनैरिव
5.27.21.e: "Just as a sinner cannot attain heaven Rama cannot be won by gods or demons, even rakshasas and others.

5.27.25.t:
गर्दभेन ययौ शीघ्रं दक्षिणां दिशमास्थितः ।
पुनरेव मया दृष्टो रावणो राक्षसेश्वरः पतितोऽ वाक्चिरा रा भूमौ गर्दभाद्भयमोहितः ।
5.27.25.e: "I saw the demon king Ravana running behind the chariot driven by donkeys in the southerly direction. He was falling with his head bent down and deluded by the fear of the donkey.

5.27.26.t:
सहसोत्थाय संभ्रान्तो भयार्तो मदविह्वलः उन्मत्त इव दिग्वासा दुर्वाक्यं प्रलपन्बहु ।
दुर्गन्धं दुस्सहं घोरं तिमिरं नरकोपमम् मलपङ्कं प्रविश्याशु मग्नस्तत्र स रावणः ।
5.27.26.e: "I saw Ravana, getting up quickly, in a bewildered state, terrorstricken, totally confused in intoxication. He had gone almost insane, naked uttering words of abuse. Plunged into a pool of filth and emitting foul smell he disappeared into a helllike dark chamber.

w: a woman clad in red clothes
a woman smeared with wet mud
towards the abode of Yama in the southerly direction
5.27.28.t: कण्ठे बद्ध्वा दशग्रीवं प्रमदा रक्तवासिनी काली कर्दमलिप्ताङ्गी दिशं याम्यां प्रकर्षति ।
5.27.28.e: A dark woman clad in red, body smeared with wet mud was seen dragging the ten-necked Ravana by his neck towards the abode of Yama in the southerly direction.

5.27.29.t: एवं तत्र मया दृष्टः कुम्भकर्णो निशाचरः रावणस्य सुतास्सर्वे दृष्टास्तैलसमुक्षिताः ।
5.27.29.e: "There I saw the nightranger, Kumbhakarna and also Ravana's sons, their bodies smeared with oil.

5.27.31.t: एकस्तत्र मया दृष्टः श्वेतच्छत्रो विभीषणः शुक्लमाल्याम्बरधरः शुक्लगन्धानुलेपनः ।
5.27.31.e: "Only Vibhishana was under a white umbrella clad in white, with white garlands and white sandal paste.

w: with sounds of conches and drums
5.27.32.t:
शङ्खदुन्धुभिनिर्घोषैर्नृत्तगीतैरलङ्कृतः आरुह्य शैलसङ्काशं मेघस्तनितनिस्स्वनम् ।
चतुर्दन्तं गजं दिव्यमास्ते तत्र विभीषणः चतुर्भिस्सचिवैः सार्थं वैहायसमुपस्थितः ।
5.27.32.e: "(Hailed by) the sounds of conches and drums, and of musicians and dancers, Vibhishana was seen ascending on to a decorated fourtust elephant which was huge like a mountain and trumpting like a thundering cloud. He stood there along with four ministers and reached the aerial region.

w: of those putting on flower garlands
sound of singing and playing musical instruments
5.27.34.t: समाजश्च मया दृष्टो गीतवादित्रनिःस्वनः पिबतां रक्तमाल्यानां रक्षसां रक्तवाससाम् ।
5.27.34.e: " A large group of demons was seen collected together, drinking, wearing red garlands and red clothes, singing and playing musical instruments.

5.27.36.t: लङ्का दृष्टा मया स्वप्ने रावणेनाभिरक्षिता दग्धा रामस्य दूतेन वानरेण तरस्विना ।
5.27.36.e: In my dream I saw this city of Lanka protected by Ravana burnt down by a powerful vanara , a messenger of Rama.

w: in a dry place turned into ashes
5.27.37.t: पीत्वा तैलं प्रनृत्ताश्च प्रहसन्त्यो महास्वनाः लङ्कायां भस्मरूक्षायां सर्वा राक्षसस्त्रियः ।
5.27.37.e: "All the demonesses in the city of Lanka which had turned dry, reduced to ashes, were dancing, laughing and shouting loudly drunk with oil..

5.27.38.t: कुम्भकर्णादयश्चेमे सर्वे राक्षसपुङ्गवाः रक्तं निवसनं गृह्य प्रविष्टा गोमयह्रदे ।
5.27.38.e: "Kumbhakarna and other demon leaders wearing red clothes entered into a pool of cow dung.

5.27.42.t: यस्यामेवंविधः स्वप्नो दुःखितायां प्रदृश्यते सा दुःखैर्विविधैर्मुक्ता प्रियं प्राप्नोत्यनुत्तमम् ।
5.27.42.e: "When any demoness in a sorrowful state dreams this kind of dream, she will be relieved of sorrow and will obtain supreme joy.

w: even if she is threatened this way
where is the need to say something
5.27.43.t: भर्त्सितामपि याचध्वं राक्षस्यः किं विवक्षया राघवाद्धि भयं घोरं राक्षसानामुपस्थितम् ।
5.27.43.e: "O demonesses beg her (pardon) now even though you had threatened her earlier. Where is the need to hesitate? There is cause for concern for demons from Rama.

5.27.48.t: निमित्तभूतमेतत्तु श्रोतुमस्या महत्प्रियम् दृश्यते च स्फुरच्चक्षुः पद्मपत्रमिवायतम् ।
5.27.48.e: "This dream indeed served as an augery for good news about her. Look, her (left) eye which is large like a lotus petal is throbbing.

w: comparable to a female elephant's trunk
5.27.50.t: करेणुहस्तप्रतिम स्सव्यश्चोरुरनुत्तमः वेपमानः सूचयति राघवं पुरतः स्थितम् ।
5.27.50.e: "Her excellent left thigh, comparable to a female elephant's trunk is trembling, as though indicating that Rama is standing in her presence.

w: the bird which utters excellent sweet notes
5.27.51.t:
पक्षी च शाखानिलयं प्रविष्टः पुनः पुनश्चोत्तमसान्त्ववादी ।
सुस्वागतां वाचमुदीरयानः पुनः पुनश्चोदयतीव हृष्टः
5.27.51.e: "One can see the bird which utters excellent sweet notes indicating happy tidings, entering again and again the foliage of the tree, a delightful bird, as if prompting Sita again and again to rejoice. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये सुन्दरकाण्डे सप्तविंशस्सर्गः। Thus ends the twentyseventh sarga of Sundarakanda of the holy Ramayana, the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

5.27.52.t:
ततः सा ह्रीमती बाला भर्तुर्विजयहर्षिता ।
अवोचद् यदि तत् तथ्यं भवेयं शरणं हि वः
5.27.52.e: Then that modest young girl, gladdened by her lord's victory, said: "If that be true, may I be a refuge to you."

5.28.3.t:
सत्यं बतेदं प्रवदन्ति लोके नाकालमृत्युर्भवतीति सन्तः ।
यत्राहमेवं परिभर्त्स्यमाना जीवामि दीना क्षणमप्यपुण्या
5.28.3.e: "Even though I am threatened like this, I am living pitiably because of lack of merit. Indeed I regret my survival due to my bad luck. Elders say that death will not ocurr before its time. It seems to be true.

5.28.4.t:
सुखाद्विहीनं बहुदुःखपूर्ण मिदं तु नूनं हृदयं स्थिरं मे ।
विशीर्यते यन्न सहस्रधाऽद्य वज्राहतं शृङ्गमिवाचलस्य
5.28.4.e: "Even though I am devoid of joy, and living in deep agony, my heart bursts not into a thousand pieces like the summit of a mountain hit by thunderbolt (lightning).

5.28.5.t:
नैवास्ति दोषो मम नूनमत्र वध्याहमस्याप्रियदर्शनस्य ।
भावं न चास्याहमनुप्रदातु मलं द्विजो मन्त्रमिवाद्विजाय
5.28.5.e: "I will not be blamed if I commit suicide now.I stand condemned to death in the hands of this ugly Ravana. I cannot bestow my affection on him or surender to his desire like a brahmin would not like to impart Vedic knowledge to a nonbrahmin. (Better die of my own accord than be killed by a sinful ogre).

5.28.7.t:
दुःखं बतेदं मम दुःखिताया मासौ चिरायाधिगमिष्यतो द्वौ ।
बद्धस्य वध्यस्य तथा निशान्ते राजापराधादिव तस्करस्य
5.28.7.e: "Alas, two months is too long a time to wait in grief. I am like a thief captured for offending a king and waiting overnight for execution at day-break.

5.28.9.t:
तरस्विनौ धारयता मृगस्य सत्त्वेन रूपं मनुजेन्द्रपुत्रौ ।
नूनं विशस्तौ मम कारणात्तौ सिंहर्षभौ द्वाविव वैद्युतेन
5.28.9.e: "Just like two mighty lions are killed by a bolt of lightning, the two princes must have been killed by a creature in the guise of a deer on my account.

w: in the guise of a deer
5.28.10.t:
नूनं स कालो मृगरूपधारी मामल्पभाग्यां लुलुभे तदानीम् ।
यत्रार्यपुत्रं विससर्ज मूढा रामानुजं लक्ष्मणपूर्वजं च
5.28.10.e: "Verily, it is the spirit of the time that assumed the form of deer and tempted this unfortunate soul. It was foolish of me to send away, the sons of a noble king, Lakshmana and his elder brother.

5.28.12.t:
अनन्य दैवत्वमियं क्षमा च भूमौ च शय्या नियमश्च धर्मे ।
पतिव्रतात्वं विफलं ममेदं कृतं कृतघ्नेष्विव मानुषाणाम्
5.28.12.e: "I am devoted to you and to no other god. My hardship in sleeping on the ground, my righteousness, my discipline and chastity have all proved futile like the devotion of an ungrateful person.

w: after the completion of the pledge
5.28.14.t:
पितुर्निदेशं नियमेन कृत्वा वनान्निवृत्तश्चरितव्रतश्च ।
स्त्रीभिस्तु मन्ये विपुलेक्षणाभिस्त्वं रंस्यसे वीतभयः कृतार्थः
5.28.14.e: "Having truly fulfilled your pledge given to your father, you will return from the forest to Ayodhya, rid of all fear, as an accomplished person, will and revel in the company of largeeyed damsels, I think.

w: with my feeling of love fixed on you
5.28.15.t:
अहं तु राम त्वयि जातकामा चिरं विनाशाय निबद्धभावा ।
मोघं चरित्वाथ तपो व्रतञ्च त्यक्ष्यामि धिग्जीवितमल्पभाग्याम्
5.28.15.e: "O RamaI loved you and concentrated all my love on you for a long time only for my doom. I have observed vows and austerities in vain. I cannot continue it for long. Here I am giving up my life. Fie upon this luckless one (me).

5.28.16.t:
सा जीवितं क्षिप्रमहं त्यजेयं विषेण शस्त्रेण शितेन वापि ।
विषस्य दाता न हि मेऽस्ति कश्चि च्छस्त्रस्य वा वेश्मनि राक्षसस्य
5.28.16.e: "I will end my life at once by taking poison or else by a sharp weapon. Alas There is none to give get me poison or a weapon at this demon's residence".

5.28.19.t:
उपस्थिता सा मृदुसर्वगात्री शाखां गृहत्वाऽध नगस्य तस्य ।
तस्यास्तु रामं प्रविचिन्तयन्त्या रामानुजं स्वं च कुलं शुभाङ्ग्या: शेकानिमित्तानि तथा बहूनि धैर्यार्जितानि प्रवराणि लोके ।
प्रादुर्निमित्तानि तदा बभूवुः पुरापि सिद्धान्युपलक्षितानि
5.28.19.e: Sita of delicate limbs approached the Simsupa tree and held on to a branch and stood. While she was thinking of Rama and Lakshmana and their noble family many  omens of proven results appeared on her auspicious charming body. These omens were dispellers of grief, and harbingers of courage in the world as declared from ancient times. (Now) they manifested themselves. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये सुन्दरकाण्डे अष्टाविंशस्सर्गः।। Thus ends the twentyeigth sarga of Sundarakanda of the holy Ramayana, the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

5.29.1.t:
तथागतां तां व्यथितामनिन्दितां व्यपेतहर्षां परिदीनमानसाम् ।
शुभां निमित्तानि शुभानि भेजिरे नरं श्रिया जुष्टमिवोपजीविनः
5.29.1.e: Like wellwishers flocking round a person on whom fortune is smiling, omens foretelling auspicious happenings in near future appeared to Sita. She was unimpeachable. She was in agony, distressed in mind, bereft of all joy (now) standing under that Simsupa tree.

w: of the lady with beautiful hair
surrounded by a row of curved eye lashes
5.29.2.t:
तस्याः शुभं वाममरालपक्ष्म राजीवृतं कृष्णविशालशुक्लम् ।
प्रास्पन्दतैकं नयनं सुकेश्या मीनाहतं पद्ममिवाभिताम्रम्
5.29.2.e: Her left eye with a row of curved eyelashes, the black pupils of the eye in white throbbed in an auspicious manner. The lady  with her long tresses, and throbbing eye appeared like a red lotus gently struck by a fish.

w: deserving the application of excellent black agaru and sandal paste
5.29.3.t:
भुजश्च चार्वञ्चितपीनवृत्तः परार्थ्यकालागरुचन्दनार्हः ।
अनुत्तमेनाध्युषितः प्रियेण चिरेण वामः समवेपताऽशु
5.29.3.e: Her stout left arm curved beautifully, fit for excellent agaru and sandal paste once the pillow by her beloved lord for long, throbbed suddenly.

5.29.4.t:
गजेन्द्रहस्तप्रतिमश्च पीन स्तयोर्द्वयोः सम्हतयोः सुजातः ।
प्रस्पन्दमानः पुनरूरुरस्या रामं पुरस्तात् स्थितमाचचक्षे
5.29.4.e: Again her roundshaped left thigh resembling an elephant's trunk started throbbing, presaging union with Rama.

w: of the lady of beautiful limbs
slightly dull on account of dust
5.29.5.t:
शुभं पुनर्हेमसमानवर्ण मीषद्रजोध्वस्तमिवामलाक्ष्याः ।
वास स्स्थिताया श्शिखराग्रदन्त्याः किञ्चित्परिस्रंसत चारुगात्य्राः
5.29.5.e: Her eyes were pristine, teeth wellshaped. The goldhued auspicious sari on her charming limbs was now a little soiled on account of dust. It slipped slightly as she stood up. This augured well for her.

5.29.6.t:
एतैर्निमित्तैरपरैश्च सुभ्रूः सम्बोधिता प्रागपि साधु सिद्धैः ।
वातातपक्लान्तमिव प्रणष्टं वर्षेण बीजं प्रतिसंजहर्ष
5.29.6.e: Reassured by such omens which augured well as tested by time, Sita, with beautiful eyebrows, and deep foresight experienced great joy, like a seed blighted by the wind and the Sun comes back to joyful life through a pleasing shower. (A foreteller is addressed as siddha in sanskrit dramas)

w: curved eyelashes extending up to her hair
5.29.7.t:
तस्याः पुनर्बिम्बफलाधरोष्ठं स्वक्षिभ्रुकेशान्तमरालपक्ष्म ।
वक्त्रं बभासे सितशुक्लदंष्ट्रं राहोर्मुखाच्चन्द्र इव प्रमुक्तः
5.29.7.e: Her face shining with beautiful red lips like bimba fruit, sparkling teeth, and curved eyelashes with lovely brows extending up to her hair, she appeared like a Moon released from the mouth of Rahu.

w: a lady with her mind illumined by joy
5.29.8.t:
सा वीतशोका व्यपनीततन्द्री शान्तज्वरा हर्षविबुद्धसत्त्वा ।
अशोभतार्या वदनेन शुक्ले शीतांशुना रात्रिरिवोदितेन
5.29.8.e: Revered Sita, completely relieved of grief, exhaustion gone, fears allayed, mind illumined with joy, looked charming with her countenance as a night with the Moon fully risen during the bright fortnight. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये सुन्दरकाण्डे एकोनत्रिंशस्सर्गः।। Thus ends the twentyninth sarga of Sundarakanda of the holy Ramayana, the first epic compsed by sage Valmiki.

5.30.1.t:
हनुमानपि विक्रान्तः सर्वं शुश्राव तत्त्वतः ।
सीतायास्त्रिजटायाश्च राक्षसीनां च तर्जनम्
5.30.1.e: The valiant hero Hanuman heard everything including the lamentation of Sita and the dream of Trijata and the threats of the demonesses.

5.30.3.t:
यां कपीनां सहस्राणि सुबहून्ययुतानि च ।
दिक्षु सर्वासु मार्गन्ते सेयमासादिता मया
5.30.3.e: "This is Sita whom thousands of vanaras are searching in all directions.

5.30.5.t:
राक्षसानां विशेषश्च पुरी चेयमवेक्षिता ।
राक्षसाधिपतेरस्य प्रभावो रावणस्य च
5.30.5.e: "I have seen the ability of the demons and the citadel of Lanka. I have seen the power of Ravana the demon king.

5.30.6.t:
युक्तं तस्याप्रमेयस्य सर्वसत्त्वदयावतः ।
समाश्वासयितुं भार्यां पतिदर्शनकाङ्क्षिणीम्
5.30.6.e: "It is the opportune time for me to comfort Sita eagerly waiting to see her husband who is of immeasurable prowess and who is compassionate to all beings.

w: who has the countenance of a fullmoon
5.30.7.e: "The moonfaced Sita had never experienced sorrow before. She sees no end to her sorrow and suffering. I will console her.

w: whose mind is overwhelmed with grief
5.30.8.t:
यद्यप्यहमिमां देवीं शोकोपहतचेतनाम् ।
अनाश्वास्य गमिष्यामि दोषवद्गमनं भवेत्
5.30.8.e: "If I should return to Kishkindha without reassuring Sita, whose understanding has been clouded in grief I would be blamed.

5.30.9.t:
गते हि मयि तत्रेयं राजपुत्री यशस्विनी ।
परित्राणमविन्दन्ती जानकी जीवितं त्यजेत्
5.30.9.e: "If I so back, this illustrious princess, Janaki will give up her life, finding no means of deliverance (from this tragic situation).

5.30.10.t:
मया च स महाबाहुः पूर्णचन्द्रनिभाननः ।
समाश्यासयितुं न्याय्यस्सीतादर्शनलालसः
5.30.10.e: "I should provide some comfort to the strongarmed Rama with a face like the fullmoon yearning to see Sita.

5.30.14.t:
सीतासन्देशरहितं मामितस्त्वरयाऽगतम् ।
निर्दहेदपि काकुत्स्य क्रुद्धस्तीव्रेण चक्षुषा
5.30.14.e: "If I leave this place without any message from Sita, Rama will burn me with his eyes full of great anger.

w: of him along with his army
5.30.15.t:
यदि चोद्योजयिष्यामि भर्तारं रामकारणात् ।
