व्यर्थमागमनं तस्य ससैन्यस्य भविष्यति
5.30.15.e: "If I get the lord of vanaras and his army for the cause of Rama (without talking to Sita), their arrival will be useless (if Sita would have given up her life by then).

5.30.16.t:
अन्तरं त्वहमासाद्य राक्षसीनामिह स्थितः ।
शनैराश्वासयिष्यामि सन्तापबहुळामिमाम्
5.30.16.e: "I shall wait and speak to her slowly and console this deeply distressed lady when I get a chance to speak to her (when  these ogresses are asleep).

5.30.18.t:
यदि वाचं प्रदास्यामि द्विजातिरिव संस्कृताम् ।
रावणं मन्यमाना मां सीता भीता भविष्यति वानरस्य विशेषेण कथं स्यादभिभाषणम् ।
5.30.18.e: "If I speak like a brahmin in sanskrit language she would be frightened thinking that I am Ravana and how would a vanara speak?

5.30.19.t: अवश्यमेव वक्तव्यं मानुषं वाक्यमर्थवत् मया सान्त्वयितुं शक्या नान्यथेयमनिन्दिता ।
5.30.19.e: "I will certainly speak to her meaningfully in the language of the people. Otherwise it is not possible to pacify the sinless Sita.

5.30.20.t: सेयमालोक्य मे रूपं जानकी भाषितं तथा रक्षोभिस्त्रासिता पूर्वं भूयस्त्रासं गमिष्यति ।
5.30.20.e: "Since Janaki has already been frightened by the demons, she will be even more terrified seeing me in this form and hearing me speaking this way.

w: who can change form at will
5.30.21.t: ततो जातपरित्रासा शब्दं कुर्यान्मनस्विनी जानमाना विशालाक्षी रावणं कामरूपिणम् ।
5.30.21.e: By seeing me in this form, sensitive largeeyed Sita will scream loudly thinking that I am Ravana who can assume any form at his free will.

5.30.23.t: ततो मां सम्परिक्षिप्य सर्वतो विकृताननाः वधे च ग्रहणे चैव कुर्युर्यत्नं यथाबलम् ।
5.30.23.e: "Then all these hideous ogresses will swarm round me and make efforts to capture me with all their strength and kill me.

5.30.24.t: गृह्य शाखाः प्रशाखाश्च स्कन्धांश्चोत्तमशाखिनाम् दृष्ट्वा विपरिधावन्तं भवेयुर्भयशङ्किताः ।
5.30.24.e: "Seeing me holding big and small branches of large trees and leaping from one place to the other, the ogresses will get scared.

5.30.25.t: मम रूपं च सम्प्रेक्ष्य वने विचरतो महत् राक्षस्यो भयवित्रस्ता भवेयुर्विकृताननाः ।
5.30.25.e: "These ogresses with their hideous faces will be frightened on looking at my huge form moving in this grove.

w: in the residence of the king of demons
engaged by the demon king to guard
5.30.26.t: ततः कुर्युस्समाह्वानं राक्षस्यो रक्षसामपि राक्षसेन्द्रनियुक्तानां राक्षसेन्द्रनिवेशने ।
5.30.26.e: "Thereafter the ogresses will draw the attention of demon guards engaged by the king of demons at his residence towards me.

w: holding different kinds of weapons such as spears tridents and swords
5.30.27.e: "Those ogresses due to fear will come speedily, armed with spears, tridents, swords and different kinds of weapons for a combat.

5.30.28.t: समृद्धस्तैस्तु परितो विधमन् रक्षसां बलम् शक्नुयां न तु संप्राप्तुं परं पारं महोदधेः ।
5.30.28.e: "With them around me, I may not be able to  reach the other end of the ocean (my strength spent in the combat.)

5.30.30.t: हिंसाभिरुचयो हिंस्युरिमां वा जनकात्मजाम् विपन्नं स्यात्ततः कार्यं रामसुग्रीवयोरिदम् ।
5.30.30.e: "These demons who are keen on indulging in violence will harm Janaka's daughter. Then the mission of Rama and Sugriva will also fail.

5.30.32.t: विशस्ते वा गृहीते वा रक्षोभिर्मयि संयुगे नान्यं पश्यामि रामस्य सहायं कार्यसाधने ।
5.30.32.e: "If I am killed in the combat or captured by the demons, I do not see another person who can help in accomplishing this task.

w: extended over a distance of hundred yojanas
5.30.33.t: विमृशंश्च न पश्यामि यो हते मयि वानरः शतयोजनविस्तीर्णं लङ्घयेत महोदधिम् ।
5.30.33.e: "When I am killed here, I cannot see any other vanara who can leap over a hundred yojanas of the ocean (to reach this place).

5.30.35.t: असत्यानि च युद्धानि संशयो मे न रोचते कश्च निस्संशयं कार्यं कुर्यात्प्राज्ञः ससंशयम् ।
5.30.35.e: "Battles, no doubt, are unpredictable. Which wise man with a sound intellect will take up a doubtful work unhesitatingly?

5.30.36.t: प्राणत्यागश्च वैदेह्या भवेदनभिभाषणे एष दोषो महान्हि स्यान्मम सीताभिभाषणे ।
5.30.36.e: "If I talk to Vaidehi it will be a great mistake on my part.If I do not speak to Vaidehi she may give up her life.

w: of the knower of the self
5.30.42.t:
इक्ष्वाकूणां वरिष्ठस्य रामस्य विदितात्मनः शुभानि धर्मयुक्तानि वचनानि समर्पयन् ।
श्रावयिष्यामि सर्वाणि मधुरां प्रब्रुवन् गिरम् श्रद्धास्यति यथाहीयं तथा सर्वं समादधे ।
5.30.42.e: "I shall present in auspicious words the esteemed Rama of Ikshvaku family who is a knower of self and make her listen to everything in such a sweet manner that she will trust me.

w: behind the branch of the tree
of the lord of the universe
5.30.44.t:
इति स बहुविधं महानुभावो जगतिपतेः प्रमदामवेक्षमाणः ।
मधुरमवितथं जगाद वाक्यं द्रुमविटपान्तरमास्थितो हनूमान्
5.30.44.e: Highsouled Hanuman seated on the branch of the tree without being seen began to speak faithfully in praise of the lord of the universe in many ways while looking at her. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये सुन्दरकाण्डे त्रिंशस्सर्गः।। Thus ends the thirtieth sarga of Sundarakanda of the holy Ramayana, the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

5.31.1.t:
एवं बहुविधां चिन्तां चिन्तयित्वा महाकपिः ।
संश्रवे मधुरं वाक्यं वैदेह्या व्याजहार ह
5.31.1.e: After deliberating in several ways the great Hanuman spoke these sweet words to Vaidehi:

5.31.2.t:
राजा दशरथो नाम रथकुञ्जरवाजिमान् ।
पुण्यशीलो महाकीर्तिरिक्ष्वाकूणां महायशाः
5.31.2.e: "There was an illustrious king called Dasaratha in Ikshvaku race, a master of chariots, elephants and horses. He was highly meritorious and renowned.

5.31.3.t:
राजर्षीणां गुणश्रेष्ठस्तपसा चर्षिभि स्समः ।
चक्रवर्तिकुले जातः पुरन्दरसमो बले
5.31.3.e: "He was the most virtuous among royal sages, equal to sages in austerity, born in the race of emperors and equal to Indra in might.

5.31.4.t:
अहिंसारतिरक्षुद्रो घृणी सत्यपराक्रमः ।
मुख्यश्चेक्ष्वाकुवंशस्य लक्ष्मीवान् लक्ष्मिवर्धनः
5.31.4.e: "He was committed to nonviolence, magnanimous, compassionate and one whose strength was truth. He was not only a prosperous king of Ikshvaku family but also a promoter of prosperity of others too.

5.31.5.t:
पार्थिवव्यञ्जनैर्युक्तः पृथुश्रीः पार्थिवर्षभः ।
पृथिव्यां चतुरन्तायां विश्रुतस्सुखदस्सुखी
5.31.5.e: "Endowed with signs of kingship and vast wealth, he was a bull among rulers of the vast earth, surrounded by the sea. A happy king himself, he was wellknown as a provider of happiness.

5.31.8.t:
तस्य सत्याभिसन्धस्य वृद्धस्य वचनात्पितुः ।
सभार्यस्सह च भ्रात्रा वीरः प्रव्राजितो वनम्
5.31.8.e: "Honouring the word of his aged father who was ever steadfast in truth, Rama left for the forest along with his wife and brother.

w: those who can assume any form at their will
5.31.9.t:
तेन तत्र महारण्ये मृगयां परिधावता ।
राक्षसा निहताश्शूरा बहवः कामरूपिणः
5.31.9.e: "In the deep forest he went round hunting animals and killing the demon warriors who assumed any form at their free will.

w: in the form of a deer
5.31.10.t:
जनस्थानवधं श्रुत्वा हतौ च खरदूषणौ ।
ततस्त्वमर्षापहृता जानकी रावणेन तु वञ्चयित्वा वने रामं मृगरूपेण मायया ।
5.31.10.e: "Ravana having heard about the killing of all demons at Janasthana including Khara and Dooshana in the forest, deceived Rama in the guise of a deer and abducted Janaki in anger.

w: one who can win over enemy forts
5.31.12.t: तत स्स वालिनं हत्वा रामः परपुरञ्जयः प्रायच्छत्कपिराज्यं तत्सुग्रीवाय महाबलः ।
5.31.12.e: "Rama, a powerful king, who can win enemy forts killed Vali and offered the monkey kingdom to Sugriva.

5.31.14.t: अहं सम्पातिवचनाच्छतयोजनमायतम् अस्या हेतोर्विशालाक्ष्याः सागरं वेगवान्प्लुतः ।
5.31.14.e: "On hearing the words of Sampati I leaped the wide ocean swiftly crossing a hundred yojanas in quest of the largeeyed Sita.

5.31.15.t: यथारूपां यथावर्णां यथालक्ष्मीवतीं च निश्चिताम् अश्रौषं राघवस्याहं सेयमासादिता मया ।
5.31.15.e: "Surely I have seen here a lady of similar body, of similar complexion, of similar glow and beauty as described by Rama".

5.31.16.t: विररामैवमुक्त्वासौ वाचं वानरपुङ्गवः जानकी चापि तच्छ्रुत्वा परं विस्मयमागता ।
5.31.16.e: Having spoken thus, the great vanara stopped speaking after that. Janaki was wonderstruck by the words of the vanara.

5.31.18.t:
निशम्य सीता वचनं कपेश्च दिशश्च सर्वाः प्रदिशश्च वीक्ष्य ।
स्वयं प्रहर्षं परमं जगाम सर्वात्मना राममनुस्मरन्ती
5.31.18.e: On hearing Hanuman's words Sita looked at all directions and quarters while quietly contemplating on Rama, the self of all and experienced supreme joy.

5.31.19.t:
सा तिर्यगूर्ध्वं च तथाप्यधस्तान्निरीक्षमाणा तमचिन्त्यबुद्धिम् ।
ददर्श पिङ्गाधिपतेरमात्यं वातात्मजं सूर्यमिवोदयस्थम्
5.31.19.e: She looked obliquely, up, and down and saw Hanuman of unimaginable intelligence, the minister of the monkey lord, son of the Windgod, who looked like the rising Sun. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये सुन्दरकाण्डे एकत्रिंशस्सर्गः।। Thus ends the thirtyfirst sarga of Sundarakanda of the holy Ramayana, the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

w: of tawny complexion like a cluster of lightnings
5.32.1.t:
ततश्शाखान्तरे लीनं दृष्ट्वा चलितमानसा ।
वेष्टितार्जुनवस्त्रं तं विद्युत्सङ्घातपिङ्गलम्
5.32.1.e: Sita got perplexed on seeing him (Hanuman), who was tawny in complexion and looked like a cluster of lightnings, clad in white  and hidden in between the branches.

w: whose eyes are bright like molten gold
one who spoke softly and pleasingly
5.32.2.t:
सा ददर्श कपिं तत्र प्रश्रितं प्रियवादिनम् ।
फुल्लाशोकोत्कराभासं तप्तचामीकरेक्षणम्
5.32.2.e: There (on the tree) she noticed a monkey like a cluster of fully blossomed Ashoka flower, shining bright, whose eyes were glowing like pure molten gold, speaking softly and pleasingly.

5.32.3.t:
मैथिली चिन्तयामास विस्मयं परमं गता ।
अहो भीममिदं रूपं वानरस्य दुरासदम् दुर्निरीक्षमिति ज्ञात्वा पुनरेव मुमोह सा ।
5.32.3.e: Astonisted Mythili began thinking. 'Oh this vanara's appearance is frightening. He is terrible to look at. He is inaccessible'. Thinking over this again and again, she fainted.

5.32.4.t:
विललाप भृशं सीता करुणं भयमोहिता रामरामेति दुःखार्ता लक्ष्मणेति च भामिनी ।
रुरोद बहुधा सीता मन्दं मन्दस्वरा सती
5.32.4.e: Overcome with sorrow and fear, noble Sita sobbed pitiably muttering repeatedly. 'O Rama, O Rama, O Lakshmana'.

5.32.6.t:
सा तं दृष्ट्वा हरिश्रेष्ठं विनीतवदुपस्थितम् ।
मैथिली चिन्तयामास स्वप्नोऽयमिति भामिनी
5.32.6.e: Noble Sita, seeing the best of vanaras who stood near humbly, began reflecting 'Is this a dream'?

5.32.7.t:
सा वीक्षमाणा पृथुभुग्नवक्त्रं शाखामृगेन्द्रस्य यथोक्तकारम् ।
ददर्श पिङ्गाधिपते रमात्यं वातात्मजं बुद्धिमतां वरिष्ठम्
5.32.7.e: Looking here and there, she saw a monkey with a large, curved face, an obedient servant and a minister of the monkeylord, the foremost among the intelligentia and the son of the Windgod.

w: as if she was almost dead
5.32.8.t:
सा तं समीक्ष्यैव भृशं विसंज्ञा गतासुकल्पेन बभूव सीता ।
चिरेण संज्ञां प्रतिलभ्य भूयो विचिन्तयामास विशालनेत्रा
5.32.8.e: The largeeyed Sita lost her senses looking at him. She got back her senses after a long time and started thinking again:

5.32.9.t:
स्वप्ने मयाऽयं विकृतोऽद्य दृष्टश्शाखामृगश्शास्त्रगणैर्निषिद्धः ।
स्वस्त्यस्तु रामाय स लक्ष्मणाय तथा पितुर्मे जनकस्य राज्ञः
5.32.9.e: 'Today I saw an ugly monkey in my dream. Its sight in a dream is inauspicious according to sastras. Let it be auspicious for Lakshmana and Rama for the sake of my father Janaka.

5.32.11.t:
रामेति रामेति सदैव बुद्ध्या विचिन्त्य वाचा ब्रुवती तमेव ।
तस्यानुरूपां च कथां तदर्थमेवं प्रपश्यामि तथा शृणोमि
5.32.11.e: "I am always meditating upon Rama and thinking of him alone. I am talking about things related to him. Because of that I see him and hear him.

w: all my thoughts immersed in him
5.32.12.t:
अहं हि तस्याद्य मनोभवेन सम्पीडिता तद्गतसर्वभावा ।
विचिन्तयन्ती सततं तमेव तथैव पश्यामि तथा शृणोमि
5.32.12.e: "I am tormented by intense love for Rama, with all my thoughts immersed in him. Since I am constantly thinking of him I see him and hear words about him. (She thinks it is all hallucination.)

5.32.13.t:
मनोरथस्स्यादिति चिन्तयामि तथापि बुद्ध्या च वितर्कयामि ।
किं कारणं तस्य हि नास्ति रूपं सुव्यक्तरूपश्च वदत्ययं माम्
5.32.13.e: "I feel it is only the desire in my mind. Desire has no form. But the one who is addressing me has a form. I cannot understand this.

w: by the resident of the forest
5.32.14.t:
नमोऽस्तु वाचस्पतये सवज्रिणे स्वयंभुवे चैव हुताशनाय च ।
अनेन चोक्तं यदिदं ममाग्रतो वनौकसा तच्छ तथास्तु नान्यथा
5.32.14.e: "My salutations to Indra, Brihaspati, Brahma the creator and also to the firegod. Let all those words spoken by the vanara here in front of me be true and not other than that." इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये सुन्दरकाण्डे द्वात्रिंशस्सर्गः।। Thus ends the thirtysecond sarga of Sundarakanda of the holy Ramayana, the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

w: whose face was like the colour of a coral
5.33.1.t:
सोऽवतीर्य द्रुमात्तस्माद्विद्रुमप्रतिमाननः ।
विनीतवेषः कृपणः प्रणिपत्योपसृत्य च तामब्रवीन्महातेजा हनूमान्मारुतात्मजः ।
शिरस्यञ्जलिमाधाय सीतां मधुरया गिरा
5.33.1.e: Hanuman, son of the Windgod whose face shone like coral, dressed in a sober manner climbed down the tree, went close to Sita, offered salutations with his palms on his head and spoke in sweet words:

w: from two petals of white lotus
5.33.4.t:
किमर्थम् तव नेत्राभ्यां वारि स्रवति शोकजम् ।
पुण्डरीकपलाशाभ्यां विप्रकीर्णमिवोदकम्
5.33.4.e: "Why are tears of grief flowing from your eyes like water trickling down a pair of petals of white lotuses?

5.33.5.t:
सुराणामसुराणां वा नागगन्धर्वरक्षसाम् ।
यक्षाणां किन्नराणां वा का त्वं भवसि शोभने
5.33.5.e: "O noble lady, are you a goddess or a demoness, a naga, a gandharva, a rakshasa, a yaksha or a kinnera?

w: from the abode of the gods
5.33.7.t:
कि नु चन्द्रमसा हीना पतिता विबुधालयात् ।
रोहिणी ज्योतिषां श्रेष्ठा श्रेष्ठसर्वगुणान्विता
5.33.7.e: "are you Rohini, embellished with best virtues among the constellations? Have you come down from the abode of the luminaries separated from the Moon, her lord?

w: O lady of lovely black eyes
5.33.8.t:
का त्वं भवसि कल्याणि त्वमनिन्दितलोचने ।
कोपाद्वा यदि वा मोहाद्भर्तारमसितेक्षणे वसिष्ठं कोपयित्वा त्वं नासि कल्याण्यरुन्धती ।
5.33.8.e: "O lady of lovely black eyes who are you? Have you by any chance offended your husband out of anger or out of delusion? Are you the auspicious Arundhati dislodged for making your lord Vasistha angry?

5.33.12.t: रावणेन जनस्थानाद्बलादपदहृता यदि सीता त्वमसि भद्रं ते तन्ममाचक्ष्व पृच्छतः ।
5.33.12.e: "If you are Sita, who was forcefully borne away by Ravana from Janasthana you may kindly reveal to me freely. May god bless you.

5.33.13.t: यथा हि तव वै दैन्यं रूपं चाप्यतिमानुषम् तपसा चान्वितो वेषस्त्वं राममहिषी ध्रुवम् ।
5.33.13.e: "Indeed your plight, the superhuman beauty and your robes marked with asceticism, surely tell me that you are Rama's queen."

w: happy to hear words of praise of Rama
5.33.14.t: सा तस्य वचनं श्रुत्वा रामकीर्तनहर्षिता उवाच वाक्यं वैदेही हनुमन्तं द्रुमाश्रितम् ।
5.33.14.e: Happy to have heard words of praise of Rama, Vaidehi spoke this to Hanuman, who got up the tree:

w: of the slayer of enemy army
5.33.15.t: पृथिव्यां राजसिंहानां मुख्यस्य विदितात्मनः स्नुषा दशरथस्याहं शत्रुसैन्यप्रतापिनः ।
5.33.15.e: "I am daughterinlaw of king Dasaratha, knower of the self, the foremost among kings on earth and a slayer of enemy army.

5.33.18.t: तत्र त्रयोदशे वर्षे राज्येनेक्ष्वाकुनन्दनम् अभिषेचयितुं राजा सोपाध्यायः प्रचक्रमे ।
5.33.18.e: "Then in the thirteenth year king Dasaratha along with the royal preceptor arranged to  coronate Rama, delight of the Ikshvaku family, in the kingdom.

5.33.19.t: तस्मिन्सम्भ्रियमाणे तु राघवस्याभिषेचने कैकयी नाम भर्तारं देवी वचनमब्रवीत् ।
5.33.19.e: "While preparations for the coronation were on, queen Kaikeyi said to her husband:

5.33.20.t: न पिबेयं न खादेयं प्रत्यहं मम भोजनम् एष मे जीवितस्यान्तो रामो यद्यभिषिच्यते ।
5.33.20.e: 'I shall not drink or eat food, if Rama is coronated. I shall end my life this moment.

5.33.21.t: यत्तदुक्तं त्वया वाक्यं प्रीत्या नृपतिसत्तम तच्छेन्न वितथं कार्यं वनं गच्छतु राघवः ।
5.33.21.e: 'O Dasaratha, the foremost among kings if the promise lovingly made by you earlier is not going to be false, Rama should go to the forest'.

5.33.22.t: स राजा सत्यवाग्देव्या वरदानमनुस्मरन् मुमोह वचनं श्रुत्वा कैकेय्याः क्रूरमप्रियम् ।
5.33.22.e: "Remembering the boons the ever truthful king had granted to Kaikeyi, he fainted after hearing her cruel and harsh words.

5.33.23.t: ततस्तु स्थविरो राजा सत्ये धर्मे व्यवस्थितः ज्येष्ठं यशस्विनं पुत्रं रुदन्राज्यमयाचत ।
5.33.23.e: "The aged king who held on to truthfulness and righteousness begged his famed eldest son Rama to return the kingdom.

5.33.24.t: स पितुर्वचनं श्रीमानभिषेकात्परं प्रियम् मनसा पूर्वमासाद्य वाचा प्रतिगृहीतवान् ।
5.33.24.e: "The illustrious Rama who valued his father's word more than sovereignty, bowed to the command of the father.

w: one whose truthfulness was his strength
5.33.25.t: दद्यान्न प्रतिगृह्णीयान्न ब्रूयात्किञ्चिदप्रियम् अपि जीवितहेतोर्वा रामस्सत्यपराक्रमः ।
5.33.25.e: "Rama, whose strength was his truthfulness, gave whatever others sought but would not accept anything in return. He would not speak a harsh word.

5.33.26.t: स विहायोत्तरीयाणि महार्हाणि महायशाः विसृज्य मनसा राज्यं जनन्यै मां समादिशत् ।
5.33.26.e: "Having given up the kingdom  voluntarily, Rama, a highly renowned king cast off his luxurious upper garments and asked me to take care of his mother.

5.33.27.t: साहं तस्याग्रतस्तूर्णं प्रस्थिता वनचारिणी न हि मे तेन हीनाया वासस्स्वर्गेऽपि रोचते ।
5.33.27.e: "I, however resolved to live in the forest, marched ahead of him quickly as I did not prefer even heaven without him.

5.33.28.e: The noble Saumitri, a delight to his friends, had already dressed himself in bark to follow his eldest brother.

5.33.29.t: ते वयं भर्तुरादेशं बहुमान्य दृढव्रताः प्रविष्टास्स्म पुरादृष्टं वनं गम्भीरदर्शनम् ।
5.33.29.e: "Respecting the king's order and determined firmly, we entered the impenetrable forest.

5.34.1.e: Hearing the words of Sita who was overwhelmed with grief, the monkey leader Hanuman felt sad and thus spoke comforting her:

5.34.2.t:
अहं रामस्य सन्देशाद्देवि दूतस्तवागतः ।
वैदेहि कुशली रामस्त्वां च कौशलमब्रवीत्
5.34.2.e: "By the command of Rama I am here as a messenger. He is keeping well. He is well and wishes you well.

5.34.3.t:
यो ब्रह्ममस्त्रं वेदांश्च वेद वेदविदांवरः ।
स त्वां दाशरथी रामो देवि कौशलमब्रवीत्
5.34.3.e: "O godlike lady Rama, son of Dasaratha, master of the Vedas, wielder of Brahmastra wishes you well.

5.34.6.t:
कल्याणी बत गाथेयं लौकिकी प्रतिभाति मा ।
एति जीवन्तमानन्दो नरं वर्षशतादपि
5.34.6.e: "The adage that 'joy comes to a living being even though it be at the end of  a hundred years' is popular. It appears true in my case".

5.34.11.t:
तामशोकस्य शाखां सा विमुक्त्वा शोककर्शिता ।
तस्यामेवानवद्याङ्गी धरण्यां समुपाविशत्
5.34.11.e: So saying Sita of flawless limbs, emaciated with grief, left the branch of Ashoka tree held by her and squatted on the ground.

5.34.13.t: तं दृष्ट्वा वन्दमानं तु सीता शशिनिभानना अब्रवीद्धीर्घमुच्छवस्य वानरं मधुरस्वरा ।
5.34.13.e: On seeing the vanara prostrated, the moonfaced lady, sighed deeply and spoke to him in a sweet voice:

5.34.14.t: मायां प्रविष्टो मायावी यदि त्वं रावणस्स्वयम् उत्पादयसि मे भूयस्सन्तापं तन्न शोभनम् ।
5.34.14.e: "If you are that trickster Ravana who appears incognito before me, it is not good for you. You are causing grief again.

w: one who can assume any form
5.34.16.t:
उपवासकृशां दीनां कामरूप निशाचर ।
सन्तापयसि मां भूयस्सन्तप्तां तन्न शोभनम्
5.34.16.e: "Oh you are one who can assume any form at will. You are a nightstalker. It is not good for you to cause pain to me who is already emaciated through fasting, who is pitiable and who is already afflicted.

5.34.18.t: यदि रामस्य दूतस्त्वमागतो भद्रमस्तु ते पृच्छामि त्वां हरिश्रेष्ठ प्रिया रामकथा हि मे ।
5.34.18.e: "O great vanara, If on the other hand you have come here as Rama's messenger I wish you well. I love Rama's story. Tell me.

5.34.19.t: गुणान्रामस्य कथय प्रियस्य मम वानर चित्तं हरसि मे सौम्य नदीकूलं यथा रयः ।
5.34.19.e: "O vanara Rama's virtues are dear to me to hear. O gentle one just as the current of the river wears away its banks, my mind is lured by your presence.

5.34.21.t: स्वप्नेऽपि यद्यहं वीरं राघवं सहलक्ष्मणम् पश्येयं नावसीदेयं स्वप्नोऽपि मम मत्सरी ।
5.34.21.e: "Even if I can see the heroic Rama together with Lakshmana in my dream my pain will be gone. Even the dream is inimical to me (I cannot sleep and thus cannot dream.)

w: or else is it a change?
5.34.23.t: किन्नु स्याचित्तमोहोऽयं भवेद्वातगतिस्त्वियम् उन्मादजो विकारो वा स्यादियं मृगतृष्णिका ।
5.34.23.e: "Can this be a delusion of my mind or a mental imbalance (resulting in movement of the mind in the body). Is it a malady born of  my madness? Or is it a mirage?

5.34.24.t: अथवा नायमुन्मादो मोहोऽप्युन्मादलक्षणः सम्बुध्ये चाहमात्मानमियं चापि वनौकसम् ।
5.34.24.e: "No, this cannot be insanity. nor even delusion. But I recognise this vanara well"

5.34.25.t: इत्येवं बहुधा सीता सम्प्रधार्य बलाबलम् रक्षसां कामरूपत्वान्मेने तं राक्षसाधिपम् ।
5.34.25.e: Considering the strength and weakness of demons in that manner Sita thought that Hanuman was none other than the king of demons who can asume any form at will.

5.34.26.t: एतां बुद्धिं तदा कृत्वा सीता सा तनुमध्यमा न प्रतिव्याजहाराथ वानरं जनकात्मजा ।
5.34.26.e: Having entertained such thoughts, Sita, the lady with a fairwaist, daughter of Janaka,  did not respond to the vanara.

5.34.27.t: सीतायाश्चिन्तितं बुद्ध्वा हनुमान्मारुतात्मजः श्रोत्रानुकूलैर्वचनैस्तदा तां संप्रहर्षयत् ।
5.34.27.e: Hanuman, son of the Windgod understood what was going on in Sita's mind and spoke pleasing words that brought joy in her.

w: brings delight to the whole world
5.34.28.t:
आदित्य इव तेजस्वी लोककान्तश्शशी यथा राजा सर्वस्य लोकस्य देवो वैश्रवणो यथा ।
विक्रमेणोपपन्नश्च यथा विष्णुर्महायशाः
5.34.28.e: "Rama is glorious as the Sun, brings delight to the whole world like the Moon, is the king of kings like Vaisravana,  and renowned like Visnu endowed with valour.

5.34.30.t:
सत्यवादी मधुरवाग्देवो वाचस्पतिर्यथा ।
रूपवान्सुभग श्रीमान् कन्दर्प इव मूर्तिमान्
5.34.30.e: "He is truthful in speech like Brihaspati, prosperous (like Kubera), sweettongued, handsome, graceful like Kamadeva.

5.34.33.t:
न चिराद्रावणं संख्ये यो वधिष्यति वीर्यवान् ।
रोषप्रमुक्तैरिषुभिर्ज्वलद्भिरिव पावकैः तेनाहं प्रेषितो दूत स्त्वत्सकाशमिहागतः ।
त्वद्वियोगेन दुःखार्त स्स त्वां कौशलमब्रवीत्
5.34.33.e: "Heroic Rama will soon release many scorching, fiery arrows in anger and kill Ravana. I seek your permission as an envoy of Rama. Filled with grief by your separation, he has made inquiries about your welfare.

5.34.37.t:
नित्यं स्मरति रामस्त्वां ससुग्रीव स्सलक्ष्मणः ।
दिष्ट्या जीवसि वैदेहि राक्षसीवशमागता
5.34.37.e: "O Vaidehi Rama, Lakshmana and Sugriva always remember you. Luckily you are alive even though you are under the clutches of shedemons.

w: of a hero of unlimited prowess
5.34.38.t:
नचिराद्द्रक्ष्यसे रामं लक्ष्मणं च महाबलम् ।
मध्ये वानरकोटीनां सुग्रीवं चामितौजसम्
5.34.38.e: "Very soon you will see mighty Rama, Lakshmana and Sugriva of unlimited prowess surrounded by crores of vanaras.

5.34.39.t:
अहं सुग्रीवसचिवो हनुमान्नाम वानरः ।
प्रविष्टो नगरीं लङ्कां लङ्घयित्वा महोदधिम्
5.34.39.e: "I am Sugriva's minister known as Hanuman, a vanara who entered the city of Lanka after leaping over the great ocean.

5.34.40.t:
कृत्वा मूर्ध्नि पदन्यासं रावणस्य दुरात्मनः ।
त्वां द्रष्टुमुपयातोऽहं समाश्रित्य पराक्रमम्
5.34.40.e: "Setting my foot with my valour on the head of the cruelminded Ravana, using my valour,  I came here to see you.

5.35.1.t:
तां तु रामकथां श्रुत्वा वैदेही वानरर्षभात् ।
उवाच वचनं सान्त्वमिदं मधुरया गिरा
5.35.1.e: On hearing about Rama from the bull among vanaras, thus spoke Vaidehi politely in a sweet voice:

5.35.2.t:
क्व ते रामेण संसर्गः कथं जानासि लक्ष्मणम् ।
वानराणां नराणां च कथमासीत्समागमः
5.35.2.e: "Where did you come in contact with Rama? How did you assess Lakshmana? How did an alliance of vanaras and humans take place?

5.35.3.t:
यानि रामस्य लिङ्गानि लक्ष्मणस्य च वानर ।
तानि भूयस्समाचक्ष्व न मां शोकस्समाविशेत्
5.35.3.e: "O vanara tell me all about the identification marks of Rama and Lakshmana again so that grief does not enter my mind.

5.35.4.t:
कीदृशं तस्य संस्थानं रूपं रामस्य कीदृशम् ।
कथमूरू कथं बाहू लक्ष्मणस्य च शंस मे
5.35.4.e: "What does Rama look like? And Laksmana? How are his thighs, arms? Tell me".

5.35.9.t:
तेजसाऽदित्य सङ्काशः क्षमया पृथिवीसमः ।
बृहस्पतिसमो बुद्ध्या यशसा वासवोपमः
5.35.9.e: "He vies with the Sun in effulgence, with earth in forbearance, with Brihaspati in intelligence, and in fame with Indra.

w: of the world of living beings
5.35.10.t:
रक्षिता जीवलोकस्य स्वजनस्याभिरक्षिता ।
रक्षिता स्वस्य वृत्तस्य धर्मस्य च परन्तपः
5.35.10.e: "Rama is a protector of the entire world of living beings not to speak of his own people. He is a protector of his own race. He guards righteousness. He is a scorcher of enemies.

w: by the knowers of the Vedas
5.35.14.t:
यजुर्वेदविनीतश्च वेदविद्भिस्सुपूजितः ।
धनुर्वेदे च वेदेषु वेदाङ्गेषु च निष्ठितः
5.35.14.e: "He is versed in Yajurveda and is respected by Vedic scholars. He has mastered Dhanurveda and other Vedas and auxillary Vedas as well.

5.35.15.t:
विपुलांसो महाबाहुः कम्बुग्रीवश्शुभाननः ।
गूढजत्रुस्सुताम्राक्षो रामो देवि जनै श्श्रुतः
5.35.15.e: "O godlike lady Rama has broad shoulders, strong arms, conchshaped neck and an auspicious countenance. With his fleshy round arms and copperyred eyes, he is renowned in all the worlds.

w: his tone is resonant like the drums
5.35.16.t:
दुन्दुभिस्वननिर्घोष स्स्निग्धवर्णः प्रतापवान् ।
सम स्समविभक्ताङ्गो वर्णं श्यामं समाश्रितः
5.35.16.e: "His tone is resonant like drums, he has a beautiful, dark, shining complexion. He has symmetrical, well proportioned limbs. He is neither too tall nor too short.

w: has the three stiff limbs (chest fist and wrists)
long in three (arms eyebrows and scrotum)
has three even parts (locks of hair knees and testicles)
elevated in three parts (abdomen navel and chest)
all the three parts (soles nails and eyes)
in the three parts (the underlines of feet the hair and the reproductive  organs)
5.35.17.t:
त्रिस्थिरस्त्रिप्रलम्बश्च त्रिसमस्त्रिषु चोन्नतः ।
त्रिताम्रस्त्रिषु च स्निग्धो गम्भीरस्त्रिषु नित्यशः
5.35.17.e: "He has three stiff parts, three long parts, three even parts, three shining parts, elevated in three parts, has three raised parts, his body has lines in three parts and is  of coppery reddish colour in three parts. He has a majestic look.

w: has three folds on his neck
his nipples and middle of his soles are depressed
four parts of his body are depressedneck penis shanks and back
has three spirals in the head
has four lines under his thumb
has four lines on the forehead
he is four cubits in height
he has arms knees cheeks and thighs well proportioned
5.35.18.e: "He has three folds in the skin of his neck and belly, is depressed in the middle of his soles and the nipples, undersized at four placesthe neck, penis, shanks and back, has three spirals on his head, has four lines under his thumb, has four lines on his forehead, he is a person with four cubits in height and symmetrical arms, cheeks and thighs.

w: ten lotuslike limbs (eyes face mouth tongue lips cheeks nipples nails feet and hands)
he is one with ten wellproportioned limbs (head forehead ears neck chest heart belly hands legs buttocks)
covered with three aspects (splendour fame and glory)
two white limbs teeth and eyes
he has six elevated  limbs (nose shoulders forehead chest and arm pits)
has nine fine features (moustache nails knuckles beard skin hair penis acumen perception)
he pursues spiritual merit worldly comforts and sensual delight in three periodsforenoon middday and evening of the day
5.35.20.t:
दशपद्मो दशबृहत्त्रिभिर्व्याप्तो द्विशुक्लवान् ।
षडुन्नतो नवतनुस्त्रिभिर्व्याप्नोति राघवः
5.35.20.e: "Ten limbs of the body resemble lotuses. He has proportionate limbs. He is known by the virtue of his spledour, fame and glory. Both his teeth and eyes are fair. Six parts of his body are elevated, nine parts of his body are fine and sharp. He pursues spiritual merit, worldly comfort and sensual delight in three periods of the dayforenoon, midday and evening. He always adopts the righteous way of life.

w: he is involved in both accumulation and favourable disposition towards others
who discharges his duties at proper time and place
who is loved by all for his endearing words.
5.35.21.e: "He is ever established in truth and righteousness. He is prosperous and desires to accumulate wealth in order to shower favour on others. He knows the right use of time and place in discharging his duties. He has endeared himself to all by his words.

w: one who has never been defeated
5.35.22.t:
भ्राता तस्य च द्वैमात्रस्सौमित्रिरपराजितः ।
अनुरागेण रूपेण गुणैश्चैव तथाविधः
5.35.22.e: "His invincible brother Saumitri born of a different mother is a replica of Rama in affection, charm and virtues.

w: one who has been thrown out
one who is pleasing to see
5.35.24.t:
त्वामेव मार्गमाणौ तौ विचरन्तौ वसुन्धराम् ।
ददर्शतुर्मृगपतिं पूर्वजेनावरोपितम् ऋश्यमूकस्य पृष्ठे तु बहुपादपसङ्कुले ।
भ्रातुर्भयार्तमासीनं सुग्रीवं प्रियदर्शनम्
5.35.24.e: "While both of them were wandering, searching for you all over the earth they saw Sugriva, the lord of animals who had been thrown out of kingship by his elder brother and was living on the mountain Rshyamuka frightened of him.

w: one who is committed to truth
5.35.26.t:
वयं तु हरिराजं तं सुग्रीवं सत्यसङ्गरम् ।
परिचर्यामहे राज्यात्पूर्वजेनावरोपितम्
5.35.26.e: "Sugriva, king of vanaras who is committed to defend truth has been deposed from the kingdom by his elder brother. We keep attending on him.

5.35.28.t:
स तौ दृष्ट्वा नरव्याघ्रौ धन्विनौ वानरर्षभः ।
अवप्लुतो गिरेस्तस्य शिखरं भयमोहितः
5.35.28.e: "On seeing the tigers among men armed with bows, Sugriva, the bull among vanaras jumped from the mountain deluded with fear and reached the peak.

5.35.29.t:
ततस्स शिखरे तस्मिन्वानरेन्द्रो व्यवस्थितः ।
तयोस्समीपं मामेव प्रेषयामास सत्वरम्
5.35.29.e: "Thereafter the lord of vanaras staying on the mountain top quickly sent me to meet both of them.

w: according to the instruction of Sugriva
both endowed with charming appearance and auspicious marks
5.35.30.e: "According to the instruction of Sugriva I came upon those two tigers among men, the two lords endowed with charming appearance and auspicious marks."

w: got to know each other through conversation
5.35.32.t:
निवेदितौ च तत्त्वेन सुग्रीवाय महात्मने ।
तयोरन्योन्यसल्लापाद्भृशं प्रीतिरजायत
5.35.32.e: "I reported faithfully about both the highsouled men to Sugriva. As they got to know each other through conversation a fast friendship developed between them.

5.35.34.t:
ततस्स सान्त्वयामास सुग्रीवं लक्ष्मणाग्रजः ।
स्त्रीहेतोर्वालिना भ्रात्रा निरस्तमुरुतेजसा
5.35.34.e: "Then Rama, consoled Sugriva who was dethroned and abandoned on acount of a woman by his brother Vali, endowed with great prowess.

w: one who is adept in accomplishing tasks with ease
5.35.35.t:
ततस्त्वन्नाशजं शोकं रामस्याक्लिष्टकर्मणः ।
लक्ष्मणो वानरेन्द्राय सुग्रीवाय न्यवेदयत्
5.35.35.e: "Then Lakshmana spoke to the lord of vanaras, Sugriva about your loss and the grief caused to Rama, who is adept in accomplishing difficult deeds with ease.

5.35.37.t:
ततस्त्वद्गात्रशोभीनि रक्षसा ह्रियमाणया ।
यान्याभरणजालानि पातितानि महीतले तानि सर्वाणि रामाय आनीय हरियूथपाः ।
संहृष्टा दर्शयामासुर्गतिं तु न विदुस्तव
5.35.37.e: "At that time, when you were being borne away by the demon, those bundles of ornaments that had adorned your limbs dropped down —

5.35.39.t:
तानि रामाय दत्तानि मयैवोपहृतानि च ।
स्वनवन्त्यवकीर्णानि तस्मिन्विगतचेतसि
5.35.39.e: "I collected the ornaments and gave them to Rama. He lost his senses on seeing the jingling ornaments scattered.

w: by an effulgent one looking like the divine
5.35.40.t:
तान्यङ्के दर्शनीयानि कृत्वा बहुविधं तव ।
तेन देवप्रकाशेन देवेन परिदेवितम्
5.35.40.e: "The divine self who is effulgent like god wailed in many ways placing the beautiful ornaments on his lap.

w: fire in the form of grief
5.35.41.t:
पश्यतस्तानि रुदतस्ताम्यतश्च पुनः पुनः ।
प्रादीपयन्दाशरथेस्तानि शोकहुताशनम्
5.35.41.e: "Rama looked at them and wept clasping them again and again in grief which inflamed like fire.

5.35.42.t:
शयितं च चिरं तेन दुःखार्तेन महात्मना ।
मयापि विविधैर्वाक्यैः कृच्छ्रादुत्थापितः पुनः
5.35.42.e: "Rama, the great self, immersed in sorrow lay down on the ground. I also consoled him with great difficulty and helped him to get up.

5.35.43.t:
तानि दृष्ट्वा महाबाहुर्दर्शयित्वा मुहुर्मुहुः ।
राघवस्सह सौमित्रिस्सुग्रीवे स न्यवेदयत्
5.35.43.e: "Longarmed Rama along with Lakshmana looked at them again and again and gave them to the care of Sugriva.

w: by the sorrow of not being able to see you
5.35.46.t:
तवादर्शनशोकेन राघवः प्रविचाल्यते ।
महता भूमिकम्पेन महानिव शिलोच्चयः
5.35.46.e: "On account of sorrow caused by not being able to see you, Rama of Raghu dynasty is shaken up like a lofty mountain is shaken by earthquake.

w: along with his friends and relatives
5.35.48.t:
स त्वां मनुजशार्दूलः क्षिप्रं प्राप्स्यति राघवः ।
समित्रबान्धवं हत्वा रावणं जनकात्मजे
5.35.48.e: "Oh daughter of Janaka after killing Ravana, along with his friends and relatives Rama, the tiger among men, will meet you.

5.35.49.t:
सहितौ रामसुग्रीवावुभावकुरुतां तदा ।
समयं वालिनं हन्तुं तव चान्वेषणं तथा
5.35.49.e: "(Having become friends) Rama and Sugriva together reached an agreement to kill Vali and search for you.

5.35.50.t:
ततस्ताभ्यां कुमाराभ्यां वीराभ्यां स हरीश्वरः ।
किष्किन्धां समुपागम्य वाली युद्धे निपातितः
5.35.50.e: "Thereafter both the princes together arrived at Kishkinda and killed Vali, king of vanaras in a combat.

5.35.52.t:
रामसुग्रीवयोरैक्यं देव्येवं समजायत ।
हनुमन्तं च मां विद्धि तयोर्दूतमिहागतम्
5.35.52.e: "Oh Illustrious lady In that manner alliance was established between Rama and Sugriva. Know me to be Hanuman, arrived here as their messenger.

5.35.53.t:
स्वराज्यं प्राप्य सुग्रीवस्समानीय हरीश्वरान् ।
त्वदर्थं प्रेषयामास दिशो दश महाबलान्
5.35.53.e: "Having obtained his kingdom Sugriva despatched the vanara leaders to all ten directions (to search for you).

w: huge as the Himalayas king of mountains
5.35.54.t:
आदिष्टा वानरेन्द्रेण सुग्रीवेण महौजसा ।
अद्रिराजप्रतीकाशास्सर्वतः प्रस्थितौ महीम्
5.35.54.e: "Following Sugriva's orders, the powerful monkey leaders huge as the Himalayas, king of mountains went all over the earth (searching).

w: eager to carry out Sugriva's order
5.35.55.t:
ततस्ते मार्गमाणा वै सुग्रीववचनातुराः ।
चरन्ति वसुधां कृत्स्नां वयमन्ये च वानराः
5.35.55.e: "Following Sugriva's orders, we, the monkeys, since then are moving about searching the entire earth eager to find you or to carry out Sugriva's orders.

w: together with one third of the army
5.35.56.e: "The prosperous and mighty son of Vali, called Angada, a tiger among vanaras, set out with a third part of the army."

5.35.57.t:
तेषां नो विप्रणष्टानां विन्ध्ये पर्वतसत्तमे ।
भृशं शोकपरीतानामहोरात्रगणा गताः
5.35.57.e: "We wasted many nights and days immersed in disappointment (for not being able to find you) and we missed our path in the great Vindhya mountain.

5.35.58.t:
ते वयं कार्यनैराश्यात्कालस्यातिक्रमेण च ।
भयाच्च कपिराजस्य प्राणांस्त्यक्तुं व्यवस्थिताः
5.35.58.e: "We decided to give up our lives due to disappointment, transgression of the time limit  fixed for us and fear of the monkey lord (fear of facing the king without finding you).

5.35.59.t:
विचित्य वनदुर्गाणि गिरिप्रस्रवणानि च ।
अनासाद्य पदं देव्याः प्राणांस्त्यक्तुं समुद्यताः
5.35.59.e: "We decided to give up our lives since we were unable to see the feet of the queen (Sita) even after searching the forest fortresses and the (banks of) mountain streams.

5.35.60.t:
दृष्ट्वा प्रायोपविष्टांश्च सर्वान्वानरपुङ्गवान् ।
भृशं शोकार्णवे मग्नः पर्यदेवयदङ्गदः तव नाशं च वैदेहि वालिनश्च वधं तथा ।
प्रायोपवेशमस्माकं मरणं च जटायुषः
5.35.60.e: "Vaidehi, when Angada saw all those vanara leaders resolved to die, he was plunged intensely into a sea of sorrow —

w: according to the king's cmmand (that who ever overstays would be killed)
when we were desiring to die
as if to fulfil the task
5.35.62.e: "When we were disappointed (in tracing you) and were at the point of death having been commanded by the king (that whosoever overstays would be killed) a gigantic powerful bird appeared to fulfil our task.

5.35.63.t:
गृध्रराजस्य सोदर्यः सम्पातिर्नाम गृध्रराट् ।
श्रुत्वा भ्रातृवधं कोपादिदं वचनमब्रवीत्
5.35.63.e: "That king of vultures, Sampati was the brother of king of birds Jatayu. Hearing about the death of his younger brother Sampati felt distresed and spoke in anger:

5.35.64.t:
यवीयान्केन मे भ्राता हतः क्व च निपातितः ।
एतदाख्यातुमिच्छामि भवद्भिर्वानरोत्तमाः
5.35.64.e: 'O best of vanaras by whom was my younger brother killed? Where was he dropped down? I wish you to tell me all about that.

5.35.66.t:
जटायुषो वधं श्रुत्वा दुःखितस्सोऽरुणात्मजः ।
त्वां शशंस वरारोहे वसन्तीं रावणालये
5.35.66.e: "Having heard about the death of Jatayu, O charming lady that Sampati Aruna's son felt sad and told us that you are at Ravana's palace.

5.35.67.t:
तस्य तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा सम्पातेः प्रीतिवर्धनम् ।
अङ्गदप्रमुखास्तूर्णं ततस्सम्प्रस्थिता वयम्
5.35.67.e: "Having heard Sampati's encouraging words all of us led by Angada departed immediately.

w: the limit of the northern direction
5.35.68.t:
विन्ध्यादुत्थाय सम्प्राप्ता स्सागरस्यान्तमुत्तरम् ।
त्वद्धर्शनकृतोत्साहा हृष्टास्तुष्टाः प्लवङ्गमाः
5.35.68.e: "The happy monkeys were satisfied. Enthusiastic about seeing you, they rose from the Vindhya mountain and reached the limit of the sea  shore in the north.

5.35.69.e: "All of them headed by Angada, eager to see you, reached the sea shore; and being frightened, they again fell into anxiety."

5.35.70.t:
अथाहं हरिसैन्यस्य सागरं प्रेक्ष्य सीदतः ।
व्यवधूय भयं तीव्रं योजनानां शतं प्लुतः
5.35.70.e: "When the vanara army was feeling despondent at the sight of the ocean, I leaped across the sea, a hundred yojanas, pushing aside  all my fear.

5.35.72.t:
एतत्ते सर्वमाख्यातं यथावृत्तमनन्दिते ।
अभिभाषस्व मां देवि दूतो दाशरथेरहम्
5.35.72.e: "O sinless lady I have given you a faithful account. I am a messenger of Dasaratha's son. And you may speak now, O divine lady

5.35.73.t:
तं मां रामकृतोद्योगं त्वन्निमित्तमिहागतम् ।
सुग्रीवसचिवं देवि बुद्ध्यस्व पवनात्मजम्
5.35.73.e: "O divine lady Know that I have come here for your cause carrying out the mission of Rama. I am Sugriva'a minister and son of the Windgod.

5.35.74.t:
कुशली तव काकुत्स्थस्सर्वशस्त्रभृतां वरः ।
गुरोराराधने युक्तो लक्ष्मणश्च सुलक्षणः
5.35.74.e: "Your lord Rama of Kakutstha race, supreme among wielders of weapons is doing well. So is venerable Lakshmana endowed with auspicious signs engaged in serving him.

5.35.75.t:
तस्य वीर्यवतो देवि भर्तुस्तव हिते रतः ।
अहमेकस्तु सम्प्राप्त स्सुग्रीववचनादिह
5.35.75.e: "O queen seeking the welfare of your Valiant husband I came here at the behest of Sugriva all alone.

5.35.77.t:
दिष्ट्याहं हरिसैन्यानां त्वन्नाशमनुशोचताम् ।
अपनेष्यामि सन्तापं तवाभिगमशंसनात्
5.35.77.e: "Fortunately for me I can finally dispel the fear of the vanara chiefs who are regretting your loss, by letting them know that you have been found.

w: by the act of seeing you
5.35.78.t:
दिष्ट्या हि मम न व्यर्थं देवि सागरलङ्घनम् ।
प्राप्स्याम्यहमिदं दिष्ट्या त्वद्दर्शनकृतं यशः
5.35.78.e: "Oh queen luckily for me, crossing the ocean has not gone in vain. I am fortunate because I will attain fame of finding you.

5.35.80.t:
माल्यवान्नाम वैदेहि गिरीणामुत्तमो गिरिः ।
ततो गच्छति गोकर्णं पर्वतं केसरी हरिः
5.35.80.e: "Oh Vaidehi there is a famous mountain called Malyavan. From there a monkey called Kesari went to mount Gokarna.

5.35.81.t:
स च देवर्षिभिर्दिष्टः पिता मम महाकपिः ।
तीर्थे नदीपतेः पुण्ये शम्बसादनमुद्धरत्
5.35.81.e: "He (Kesari) is said to be my father by the divine sages. He retrieved a piece of land in a holy spot of that sea shore and killed Sambasadana, a demon who was oppressing righteous people.

5.35.84.t:
एवं विश्वासिता सीता हेतुभिश्शोककर्शिता ।
उपपन्नैरभिज्ञानैर्दूतं तमवगच्छति
5.35.84.e: The griefstricken Sita trusted him by his logical presentation of reasons as well as identifications. She believed that he was a messenger (of Rama).

5.35.85.t:
अतुलं च गता हर्षं प्रहर्षेण च जानकी ।
नेत्राभ्यां वक्रपक्ष्माभ्यां मुमोचानन्दजं जलम्
5.35.85.e: Janaki experienced immeasurable happiness and shed tears of joy through her curved eyes.

w: having wide white eyes with tinge of red corners
5.35.86.t:
चारु तद्वदनं तस्यास्ताम्रशुक्लायतेक्षणम् ।
अशोभत विशालाक्ष्या राहुमुक्त इवोडुराट्
5.35.86.e: Her face with large eyes with a tinge of red corners shone like the Moon released from Rahu.

5.35.87.t:
हनुमन्तं कपिं व्यक्तं मन्यते नान्यथेति सा ।
अथोवाच हनूमांस्तामुत्तरं प्रियदर्शनाम्
5.35.87.e: She realised that the monkey was none other than Hanuman. Then he looked at her who was pleasing to see and spoke again:

5.35.88.t:
एतत्ते सर्वमाख्यातं समाश्वसिहि मैथिलि ।
किं करोमि कथं वा ते रोचते प्रतियाम्यहम्
5.35.88.e: "Mythili, everything I intended to say has been narrated to you. Calm yourself down. What shall I do? Or else, tell me what pleases you. I shall go back.

w: in order to inspire trust in Sita
5.36.1.t:
भूय एव महातेजा हनूमान्पवनात्मजः ।
अब्रवीत्प्रश्रितं वाक्यं सीताप्रत्ययकारणात्
5.36.1.e: Mighty Hanuman, the son of the Windgod again spoke to Sita humbly to inspire confidence in her.

5.36.3.t:
प्रत्ययार्थं तवाऽनीतं तेन दत्तं महात्मना ।
समाश्वसिहि भद्रं ते क्षीणदुःखफला ह्यसि
5.36.3.e: "Be calm. Be blessed. Your sorrows have come to an end. This (the ring) is given by the great self, Rama, to make you trust me.

w: delighted at the news of her husband
5.36.6.t:
ततस्सा ह्रीमती बाला भर्तृसन्देशहर्षिता ।
परितुष्टा प्रियं कृत्वा प्रशशंस महाकपिम्
5.36.6.e: Young Sita felt delighted about her husband's news and blushed. By praising him for his action, she pleased the great monkey.

5.36.7.t:
विक्रान्तस्त्वं समर्थस्त्वं प्राज्ञस्त्वं वानरोत्तम ।
येनेदं राक्षसपदं त्वयैकेन प्रधर्षितम्
5.36.7.e: "O foremost among the vanaras you have trespassed the abodes of demons all alone. You are mighty and capable and wise.

5.36.9.t:
न हि त्वां प्राकृतं मन्ये वानरं वानरर्षभ ।
यस्य ते नास्ति सन्त्रासो रावणान्नापि सम्भ्रमः
5.36.9.e: "I do not think you are an ordinary monkey. You have no fear or excitement about Ravana. You are a bull among vanaras.

5.36.10.t:
अर्हसे च कपिश्रेष्ठ मया समभिभाषितुम् ।
यद्यसि प्रेषितस्तेन रामेण विदितात्मना
5.36.10.e: "O best of monkeys As you have been sent by Rama, the knower of the self, it is proper for me to converse with you.

5.36.11.t:
प्रेषयिष्यति दुर्धर्षो रामो न ह्यपरीक्षितम् ।
पराक्रममविज्ञाय मत्सकाशं विशेषतः
5.36.11.e: "The formidable Rama will not send any one specially to me without testing him or knowing his valour.

5.36.12.t:
दिष्ट्या च कुशली रामो धर्मात्मा सत्यसङ्गरः ।
लक्ष्मणश्च महातेजास्सुमित्रानन्दवर्धनः
5.36.12.e: "To my luck, righteous Rama who abides in truth and glorious Lakshmana who enhances the joy of Sumitra are keeping well.

w: at the time of dissolution of the era
5.36.13.t:
कुशली यदि काकुत्स्थः किं नु सागरमेखलाम् ।
महीं दहति कोपेन युगान्ताग्निरिवोत्थितः
5.36.13.e: "Indeed if Kakutstha is well wherefore does he not burn the oceangirdled earth in his rage as (the earth is burnt) at the time of dissolution of the era?

5.36.19.t:
कच्चिदाशास्ति देवानां प्रसादं पार्थिवात्मजः ।
कच्चित्पुरुषकारं च दैवं च प्रतिपद्यते
5.36.19.e: "Does the prince ever seek the blessings of gods or fall back upon personal effort as well as providence?

5.36.22.t:
कौसल्यायास्तथा कच्चित्सुमित्रायास्तथैव च ।
अभीक्ष्णं श्रूयते कच्चित्कुशलं भरतस्य च
5.36.22.e: "I hope he regularly receives news about the welfare of Kausalya, Sumitra and Bharata.

5.36.24.t:
कच्चिदक्षौहिणीं भीमां भरतो भ्रातृवत्सलः ।
ध्वजिनीं मन्त्रिभिर्गुप्तां प्रेषयिष्यति मत्कृते
5.36.24.e: "Will Bharata, the devoted brother, send his formidable army of one akshavhini protected by ministers for my cause? I trust he will. (Akshauhini  109350 foot soldiers  65610 horse soldiers  21860 elephants soldiers on chariot)

5.36.26.e: "Hope heroic Lakshmana, enhancer of the joy of Sumitra, who has mastered the use of weapons will blow away the demons through a network of arrows.

5.36.27.t:
रौद्रेण कच्चिदस्त्रेण ज्वलता निहतं रणे ।
द्रक्ष्याम्यल्पेन कालेन रावणं ससुहृज्जनम्
5.36.27.e: "Can I hope to see Ravana and his relatives slain in the battle by fiery weapons in a short time?

5.36.28.t:
कच्चिन्न तद्धेमसमानवर्णं तस्याननं पद्मसमानगन्धि ।
मया विना शुष्यति शोकदीनं जलक्षये पद्ममिवातपेन
5.36.28.e: "Hope, Rama's moonlike face without me with its golden complexion and lotus fragrance must not have been pale and withered with tears like the lotus in a pond scorched by the heat.

w: for the cause of establishing righteousness
5.36.29.t:
धर्मापदेशात्त्यजतश्च राज्यं मां चाप्यरण्यं नयतः पदातिम् ।
नासीद्व्यथा यस्य न भीर्न शोकः कच्चित्स धैर्यं हृदये करोति
5.36.29.e: "Rama has given up sovereignty for the sake of establishing righteousness and led me into the forest on foot.He had not then felt any fear, anxiety or grief at heart.Rama showed patience, instead. Hope he retains them.

5.36.30.t:
न चास्य माता न पिता च नान्यः स्नेहाद्विशिष्टोऽस्ति मया समो वा ।
तावत्त्वहं दूत जिजीविषेयं यावत्प्रवृत्तिं शृणुयां प्रियस्य
5.36.30.e: "His love for me is superior to his love for his father, mother or any one else. O messenger, I wish to survive till I hear any  news from my dear lord."

5.36.31.t:
इतीव देवी वचनं महार्थं तं वानरेन्द्रं मधुरार्थमुक्त्वा ।
श्रोतुं पुनस्तस्य वचोऽभिरामं रामार्थयुक्तं विरराम रामा
5.36.31.e: The godlike lady, having spoken to the vanara leader in a very meaningful and sweet manner about her beloved Rama, she remained silent, waiting to hear Hanuman's attractive words of description of Rama once again.

5.36.32.t:
सीताया वचनं श्रुत्वा मारुतिर्भीमविक्रमः ।
शिरस्यञ्जलिमाधाय वाक्यमुत्तरमब्रवीत्
5.36.32.e: Having heard Sita, Hanuman endowed with fearsome power placed his folded hands on his head and said this:

5.36.33.t:
न त्वामिहस्थां जानीते रामः कमललोचने ।
तेन त्वां नानयत्याशु शचीमिव पुरन्दरः
5.36.33.e: "O lotuseyed one Rama knows not that you are here. Therefore he has not taken you away immediately as did Indra to rescue his wife Sachi.

5.36.34.t:
श्रुत्वैव तु वचो मह्यं क्षिप्रमेष्यति राघवः ।
चमूं प्रकर्षन्महतीं हर्यृक्षगणसङ्कुलाम्
5.36.34.e: "As soon as he hears your words from me, Rama will reach (here), leading a huge army of powerful troops of vanaras and bears.

5.36.35.t:
विष्टम्भयित्वा बाणौघैरक्षोभ्यं वरुणालयम् ।
करिष्यति पुरीं लङ्कां काकुत्स्थः शान्तराक्षसाम्
5.36.35.e: "Kakutstha Rama will still the imperturbable abode of Varuna (ocean) by the torrent of his arrows and rid the city of Lanka of all the demons.

5.36.36.t:
तत्र यद्यन्तरा मृत्युर्यदि देवास्सहासुराः ।
स्थास्यन्ति पथि रामस्य स तानपि वधिष्यति
5.36.36.e: "Thereafter, whoever comes Rama's way,  be it  gods or demons or even death or any one else he will destroy them.

5.36.38.t:
मलयेन च विन्ध्येन मेरुणा मन्दरेण च ।
दर्दुरेण च ते देवि शपे मूलफलेन च यथा सुनयनं वल्गु बिम्बोष्ठं चारु कुण्डलम् ।
मुखं द्रक्ष्यसि रामस्य पूर्णचन्द्रमिवोदितम्
5.36.38.e: "O Sita I swear in the name of mountains like Malaya, Vindhya, Meru, and Dardura (the abodes of monkeys and bears) and  by the roots and fruits as well (which are the food of vanaras). you will soon behold Rama with beautiful eyes, red lips like bimba fruit, lovely earrings and a countenance resembling the full moon.

w: like Indra who has performed a hundred sacrifices
5.36.40.t:
क्षिप्रं द्रक्ष्यसि वैदेहि रामं प्रस्रवणे गिरौ ।
शतक्रतुमिवासीनं नागराजस्य मूर्धनि
5.36.40.e: "O Vaidehi, you will soon see Rama seated on the Prasravana mountain just as Indra (who performed a hundred sacrifices) seated on the back of the king of elephants.

5.36.41.t:
न मांसं राघवो भुङक्ते न चाऽपि मधु सेवते ।
वन्यं सुविहितं नित्यं भक्तमश्नाति पञ्चमम्
5.36.41.e: "Rama is not eating meat, nor drinking wine. He takes only the one fifth of a meal (sanctioned for an ascetic) available in the forest.

5.36.42.t:
नैव दंशान्न मशकान्न कीटान्न सरीसृपान् ।
राघवोऽपनयेद्गात्रात्त्वद्गतेनान्तरात्मना
5.36.42.e: "Since you left, Rama has been always thinking sincerely of you, no longer drives away flies or mosquitoes nor insects or serpents from his body (his mind entirely fixed on you).

5.36.43.t:
नित्यं ध्यानपरो रामो नित्यं शोकपरायणः ।
नान्यच्चिन्तयते किञ्चित्स तु कामवशं गतः
5.36.43.e: "Rama is always lost in thought. He is totally given to grief. Absorbed in love for you, he thinks of none else৷৷

5.36.44.t:
अनिद्रस्सततं रामस्सुप्तोऽपि च नरोत्तमः ।
सीतेति मधुरां वाणीं व्याहरन्प्रतिबुध्यते
5.36.44.e: "Rama, the best of men never goes to sleep and even if he drops off to sleep he mutters 'Sita, Sita' in a sweet voice in his sleep.

5.36.46.t:
स देवि नित्यं परितप्यमान स्त्वामेव सीतेत्यभिभाषमाणः ।
धृतव्रतो राजसुतो महात्मा तवैव लाभाय कृतप्रयत्नः
5.36.46.e: "O divine lady prince Rama is ceaselessly suffering. He keeps talking to you in air. The determined Rama is only thinking of your recovery ".

5.37.1.t:
सीता तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा पूर्णचन्द्रनिभानना ।
हनूमन्तमुवाचेदं धर्मार्थसहितं वचः
5.37.1.e: To the righteous words (about Rama's grief) of Hanuman, Sita with a face like the full moon replied.

5.37.2.t:
अमृतं विषसंसृष्टं त्वया वानर भाषितम् ।
यच्च नान्यमना रामो यच्च शोकपरायणः
5.37.2.e: "O vanara you have told me that Rama has his mind always fixed on me, not on others and you have also said that he is sad. It is like offering me poison mixed with nectar.

5.37.4.t:
विधिर्नूनमसंहार्यः प्राणिनां प्लवगोत्तम ।
सौमित्रिं मां च रामं च व्यसनै: पश्य मोहितान्
5.37.4.e: "O best of vanaras surely it is not possible for living beings to overcome destiny. You see how Sri Rama, Saumitri, and my own self are all   afflicted with grief.

5.37.6.t:
राक्षसानां वधं कृत्वा सूदयित्वा च रावणम् ।
लङ्कामुन्मूलितां कृत्वा कदा द्रक्ष्यति मां पतिः
5.37.6.e: "When will my husband see me after killing the demons including Ravana and uprooting Lanka?

5.37.7.t:
स वाच्यस्संत्वरस्वेति यावदेव न पूर्यते ।
अयं संवत्सरः कालस्तावद्धि मम जीवितम्
5.37.7.e: "One year's time has been given (by Ravana) to me.  Rama should be informed to be quick in reaching before the completion of the time limit and that I will survive till then only.

w: fallen into the trap of time
5.37.10.t:
मम प्रतिप्रदानं हि रावणस्य न रोचते ।
रावणं मार्गते संख्ये मृत्युः कालवशं गतम्
5.37.10.e: "Ravana did not like to return me having fallen into the death trap. Death lies in wait for him in battle.

5.37.12.t:
असंशयं हरिश्रेष्ठ क्षिप्रं मां प्राप्स्यते पतिः ।
अन्तरात्मा च मे शुद्धस्तस्मिंश्च बहवो गुणाः
5.37.12.e: "O eminent vanara no doubt my lord will soon reach this place. My pure conscience tells me that Rama has many virtues.

5.37.14.t:
चतुर्दशसहस्राणि राक्षसानां जघान यः ।
जनस्थाने विना भ्रात्रा शत्रुः कस्तस्य नोद्विजेत्
5.37.14.e: "At Janasthana without the help of his brother also he slew fourteen thousand demons. Which enemy will not tremble before him?

5.37.15.t:
न स शक्यस्तुलयितुं व्यसनैः पुरुषर्षभः ।
अहं तस्य प्रभावज्ञा शक्रस्येव पुलोमजा
5.37.15.e: "O bull among men he will not be shaken by calamities. Just as Sachi, the daughter of Puloma knows Indra's might I know Rama's.

5.37.20.t:
त्वां हि पृष्ठगतां कृत्वा सन्तरिष्यामि सागरम् ।
शक्तिरस्ति हि मे वोढुं लङ्कामपि सरावणाम्
5.37.20.e: "Placing you on my back I shall cross the ocean. Indeed, I have the capacity to carry the entire city of Lanka along with Ravana.

w: to a person staying on Prasravan mountain
I will take you today itself.
5.37.21.t:
अहं प्रस्रवणस्थाय राघवायाद्य मैथिलि ।
प्रापयिष्यामि शक्राय हव्यं हुतमिवानलः
5.37.21.e: "O Mythili Just as oblations offered to the sacred fire goes to Indra, I shall offer you today to Rama waiting on the Prasravana mountain.

w: of the king of elephants Airavatam
5.37.23.e: Mighty Rama staying in asram ill be enthused to see you seated on my back like Lord Purandara (Indra) seated on the back of the lord of elephants (Airavata)

5.37.25.t:
कथयन्तीव चन्द्रेण सूर्येण च महार्चिषा ।
मत्पृष्ठमधिरुह्य त्वं तराकाशमहार्णवौ
5.37.25.e: "Climb on my back and cross the ocean through space in the flaming light, conversing with Moon and Sun.

5.37.26.t:
न हि मे सम्प्रयातस्य त्वामितो नयतोऽङ्गने ।
अनुगन्तुं गतिं शक्तास्सर्वे लङ्कानिवासिनः
5.37.26.e: "O beautiful lady it is not possible for all the inhabitants of Lanka together to follow me while I carry you from this place.

5.37.29.t:
हनुमन्दूरमध्वानं कथं मां वोढुमिच्छसि ।
तदेव खलु ते मन्ये कपित्वं हरियूथप
5.37.29.e: "Hanuman how do you intend to carry me to such a distant place? Indeed, it is your monkey nature, I suppose.

5.37.30.t:
कथं वाल्पशरीरस्त्वं मामितो नेतुमिच्छसि ।
सकाशं मानवेन्द्रस्य भर्तुर्मे प्लवगर्षभ
5.37.30.e: "O bull among monkeys you have  such a small body. How can you intend to carry me from here to my husband, the lord of men"?

5.37.32.t:
न मे जानाति सत्त्वं वा प्रभावं वाऽसितेक्षणा ।
तस्मात्पश्यतु वैदेही यद्रूपं मम कामतः
5.37.32.e: 'Blackeyed Sita is not aware of my strength or my power. Therefore let her see the real (huge) form that I can assume at my free will'.

5.37.35.t:
मेरुमन्दरसङ्काशो बभौ दीप्तानलप्रभः ।
अग्रतो व्यवतस्थे च सीताया वानरोत्तमः
5.37.35.e: Hanuman, the foremost of the vanaras resembling mount Meru or Mandara stood there glowing like blazing fire in front of Sita.

w: one who has a red face
teeth and nails as strong as diamonds
5.37.36.t:
हरिः पर्वतसङ्काशस्ताम्रवक्त्रो महाबलः ।
वज्रदंष्ट्रनखो भीमो वैदेहीमिदमब्रवीत्
5.37.36.e: Resembling a mountain in size, with a red face, with teeth and nails strong like  diamond, the vanara in dreadful form said to Vaidehi:

5.37.37.t:
सपर्वतवनोद्देशां साट्टप्राकारतोरणाम् ।
लङ्कामिमां सनाथां वा नयितुं शक्तिरस्ति मे
5.37.37.e: "I have the capacity to carry away this entire Lanka uprooted with its mountains, gardens, forts, ramparts and gateways along with the king.

5.37.38.t:
तदवस्थाप्यतां बुद्धिरलं देवि विकाङ्क्षया ।
विशोकं कुरु वैदेहि राघवं सहलक्ष्मणम्
5.37.38.e: "O queen it is enough. Give up this unworthy attitude. Be stable. O Vaidehi, rid Lakshmana and Rama of grief".

5.37.41.t:
प्राकृतोऽन्यः कथं चेमां भूमिमागन्तुमर्हति ।
उदधेरप्रमेयस्य पारं वानरपुङ्गव
5.37.41.e: "O chief of vanaras how could an ordinary person be capable of reaching this land on far off shore of the immeasurable ocean?

5.37.42.t:
जानामि गमने शक्तिं नयने चापि ते मम ।
अवश्यं सम्प्रधार्याशु कार्यसिद्धिर्महात्मनः
5.37.42.e: "I know you are capable of carrying me on your journey. I am sure about the quick success of your mission which has been carried out after careful planning.

5.37.46.t:
न च शक्ष्ये त्वया सार्धं गन्तुं शत्रुविनाशन ।
कलत्रवति सन्देहस्त्वय्यपि स्यादसंशयः
5.37.46.e: "O destroyer of foes, it is not possible for me to go with you. Further, when you are burdened with a woman you will also fall into danger (because of me), no doubt.

5.37.47.t:
ह्रियमाणां तु मां दृष्ट्वा राक्षसा भीमविक्रमाः ।
अनुगच्छेयुरादिष्टा रावणेन दुरात्मना
5.37.47.e: "When I am seen (while being carried away) by the demons of fearsome valour they will pursue you, ordered by the wicked Ravana.

w: by those wielding spears and mace
5.37.48.t:
तैस्त्वं परिवृतश्शूरैश्शूलमुद्गरपाणिभिः ।
भवेस्त्वं संशयं प्राप्तो मया वीर कलत्रवान्
5.37.48.e: "O heroic monkey as the warriors armed with spears and maces surround you and attack, your life will be in danger, because of me.

5.37.49.t:
सायुधा बहवो व्योम्नि राक्षसास्त्वं निरायुधः ।
कथं शक्ष्यसि संयातुं मां चैव परिरक्षितुम्
5.37.49.e: "The demons are in large number and they will be armed with weapons. You are unarmed. How can you fight and protect me?

w: for you while engaged in fighting
5.37.50.t:
युध्यमानस्य रक्षोभिस्तव तैः क्रूरकर्मभिः ।
प्रपतेयं हि ते पृष्ठाद्भयार्ता कपिसत्तम
5.37.50.e: "O noble monkey while you are engaged in fighting with those demons of wicked deeds, I may drop down out of fear.

5.37.51.t:
अथ रक्षांसि भीमानि महान्ति बलवन्ति च ।
कथञ्चित्सांपराये त्वां जयेयुः कपिसत्तम
5.37.51.e: "O noble monkey the massive, fearsome and powerful demons may defeat you in the fight in any way.

5.37.54.t:
अहं वापि विपद्येयं रक्षोभिरभितर्जिता ।
त्वत्प्रयत्नो हरिश्रेष्ठ भवेन्निष्फल एव तु
5.37.54.e: "In such a case, caught and intimidated by the demons I may die. Then your efforts will be wasted.

w: it may be you can do the task
5.37.55.t:
कामं त्वमसि पर्याप्तो निहन्तुं सर्वराक्षसान् ।
राघवस्य यशो हीयेत्त्वया शस्तैस्तु राक्षसैः
5.37.55.e: "It may be that you can kill  all the demons but by such an act the fame of Rama will be diminished. (He cannot give his strength a trial)

5.37.57.t:
आरम्भस्तु मदर्थोऽयं ततस्तव निरर्थकः ।
त्वया हि सह रामस्य महानागमने गुणः
5.37.57.e: "All your effort for my sake would be futile. Hence Rama's arrival along with you will be of great benefit.

5.37.60.t:
भर्तुर्भक्तिं पुरस्कृत्य रामादन्यस्य वानर ।
न स्पृशामि शरीरं तु पुंसो वानरपुङ्गव
5.37.60.e: "O chief of vanaras I cherish my devotion towards Rama alone and not touch the body of any other man.

w: having no control over my self
5.37.61.t:
यदहं गात्रसंस्पर्शं रावणस्य बलाद्गता ।
अनीशा किं करिष्यामि विनाथा विवशा सती
5.37.61.e: "I had no control over myself. I was helpless and my husband was not present when I had to bear the touch of Ravana's limbs. What can I do?

5.37.62.t:
यदि रामो दशग्रीवमिह हत्त्वा सबान्धवम् ।
मामितो गृह्य गच्छेत तत्तस्य सदृशं भवेत्
5.37.62.e: "It will be proper if Rama comes here, kills Ravana along with all his relations and takes me away.

w: whether gods gandharvas nagas or demons
5.37.63.t:
श्रुता हि दृष्टाश्च मया पराक्रमा महात्मनस्तस्य रणावमर्दिनः ।
न देवगन्धर्वभुजङ्गराक्षसा भवन्ति रामेण समा हि संयुगे
5.37.63.e: "I have seen and heard about Rama's conquest of enemies and his valiant deeds in war. Indeed, gods gandharvas, nagas or even demons cannot match him in war.

5.37.64.t:
समीक्ष्य तं संयति चित्रकार्मुकम् महाबलं वासवतुल्यविक्रमम् ।
सलक्ष्मणं को विषहेत राघवं हुताशनं दीप्तमिवानिलेरितम्
5.37.64.e: "After seeing Rama who is equal to lord Indra in valour. He is like blazing fire whipped by wind, wielding a wonderful bow, who can withstand the power of strong Rama accompanied by Lakshmana in war?

w: like the elephant supporting quarter of the earth
resembling the Sun at the at the time of the deluge
5.37.65.t:
सलक्ष्मणं राघवमाजिमर्दनं दिशागजं मत्तमिव व्यवस्थितम् ।
सहेत को वानरमुख्य संयुगे युगान्तसूर्यप्रतिमं शरार्चिषम्
5.37.65.e: "O chief of vanaras who can withstand Rama accompanied by Lakshmana, the conqueror of enemies? His arrows resemble the rays of the Sun at the time of the deluge, steady like the elephants who support the quarters of the earth.

w: is in accordance with your nature
5.38.2.t:
युक्तरूपं त्वया देवि भाषितं शुभदर्शने ।
सदृशं स्त्रीस्वभावस्य साध्वीनां विनयस्य च
5.38.2.e: "O queen O lady of auspicious appearance your words are most appropriate to and characteristic of a modest virtuous woman.

5.38.3.t:
स्त्रीत्वं न तु समर्थं हि सागरं व्यतिवर्तितुम् ।
मामधिष्ठाय विस्तीर्णं शतयोजनमायतम्
5.38.3.e: "It may not be possible for a woman to cross on my back the vast ocean stretching over a hundred yojanas. It is not possible for a woman.

5.38.4.t:
द्वितीयं कारणं यच्च ब्रवीषि विनयान्विते ।
रामादन्यस्य नार्हामि संस्पर्शमिति जानकि एतत्ते सदृशं देवि पत्न्यास्तस्य महात्मनः ।
का ह्यन्या त्वामृते देवि ब्रूयाद्वचनमीदृशम्
5.38.4.e: "O humble lady the second reason given by you, 'I ought not to touch a person other than Rama' is well said and worthy of you, being the wife of the great soul. Who else can speak such words?

5.38.7.e: "O queen my heart is drenched with love for Rama and desires to please him for many reasons. Therefore these words have been spoken by me.

w: you may give me a token of identity.
5.38.10.t:
यदि नोत्सहसे यातुं मया सार्थमनिन्दिते ।
अभिज्ञानं प्रयच्छ त्वं जानीयाद्राघवो हि यत्
5.38.10.e: "O blameless lady If you wish not to accompany me you may give me a token of identification to let Rama know about my coming here and seeing you".

5.38.11.t:
एवमुक्ता हनुमता सीता सुरसुतोपमा ।
उवाच वचनं मन्दं बाष्पप्रग्रथिताक्षरम् इदं श्रेष्ठमभिज्ञानं ब्रूयास्त्वं तु मम प्रियम् ।
5.38.11.e: Having heard Hanuman, Sita, a child of god, said these words in a low tone. Choked with tears, 'Carry this token of identity to my dear husband':

w: with abundant roots fruits and water
5.38.12.t:
शैलस्य चित्रकूटस्य पादे पूर्वोत्तरे पुरा तापसाश्रमवासिन्याः प्राज्यमूलफलोदके ।
तस्मिन्सिद्धाश्रमे देशे मन्दाकिन्या विदूरतः तस्योपवनषण्डेषु नानापुष्पसुगन्धिषु ।
विहृत्य सलिले क्लिन्ना ममाङ्के समुपाविशमः
5.38.12.e: 'Long ago we were staying at Siddhasrama. This hermitage was situated to the northeast at the foot of Chitrakuta mountain which was not far from the river Mandakini. It had abundant roots, fruits and water. You sported with me in the gardens which were fragrant with many types of flowers and ponds. You sat down on my lap with wet clothes in the hermitage'.

w: went round with its beak and pecked
5.38.15.t:
ततो मांससमायुक्तो वायसः पर्यतुण्डयत् ।
तमहं लोष्टमुद्यम्य वारयामिस्म वायसम्
5.38.15.e: 'Then a crow greedy of flesh began to peck my bossom with its beak. I took a clod of earth and warded him off.

5.38.16.t:
दारयन्स च मां काकस्तत्त्रैव परिलीयते ।
न चाप्युपारमन्मांसाद्भक्षार्थि बलिभोजनः
5.38.16.e: 'The crow was an eater of offerings, hungry for food began to peck me again and again for flesh.He did not stop.

5.38.17.t:
उत्कर्षन्त्यां च रशनां क्रुद्धायां मयि पक्षिणि ।
स्रस्यमाने च वसने ततो दृष्टा त्वया ह्यहम्
5.38.17.e: 'My upper cloth was slipping. I was trying to pull up my waist string angrily when you saw me.

5.38.20.t:
बाष्पपूर्णमुखी मन्दं चक्षुषी परिमार्जती ।
लक्षिताऽहं त्वया नाथ वायसेन प्रकोपिता
5.38.20.e: 'O lord when I was angered by the crow and my face was filled with tears, you marked me wiping my eyes.

5.38.22.t:
स तत्र पुनरेवाथ वायसस्समुपागमत् ।
ततस्सुप्तप्रबुद्धां मां रामस्याङ्कात्समुत्थिताम् वायसस्सहसागम्य विददार स्तनान्तरे ।
पुनः पुनरथोत्पत्य विददार स मां भृशम्
5.38.22.e: 'The crow came back again and clawed me in the space between my breasts even after I woke up after slumber from Rama's lap. Flying, it tore my bosom again and again.

5.38.25.t: स मां दृष्ट्वा महाबाहुर्वितुन्नां स्तनयोस्तदा आशीविष इव क्रुद्धश्वसन्वाक्यमभाषत ।
5.38.25.e: 'O strongarmed Rama, seeing my torn breasts, you became angry like a hissing serpent  and hissing said :

5.38.27.t: वीक्षमाणस्ततस्तं वै वायसं समुदैक्षत नखैस्सरुधिरैस्तीक्ष्णैर्मामेवाभिमुखं स्थितम् ।
5.38.27.e: 'Then looking around, you saw the crow facing me with sharp, bloodstained claws.

w: it is said that he is the son
5.38.28.t: पुत्त्रः किल स शक्रस्य वायसः पततां वरः धरान्तरगतश्शीघ्रं पवनस्य गतौ समः ।
5.38.28.e: 'This crow was the best of birds. He was surely Indra's son who had covered a long distance with great speed and his speed was like the Windgod's.

w: invoked the weapon of Brahma into it by reciting the mantra
5.38.30.t: स दर्भं संस्तराद्गृह्य ब्राह्मेणास्त्रेण योजयत् स दीप्त इव कालाग्निर्जज्वालाभिमुखो द्विजम् ।
5.38.30.e: 'Taking out a blade of darbha grass from your mat, you invoked the weapon of Brahma by reciting the mantra. Then you discharged it which blazed like the fire of death and went spearheading towards the crow.

5.38.31.t: स तं प्रदीप्तं चिक्षेप दर्भं तं वायसं प्रति ततस्तं वायसं दर्भस्सोम्बरेऽनुजगाम ह ।
5.38.31.e: 'Then you threw the burning darbha grass at the crow and it chased him in the sky.

5.38.32.t: अनुसृष्टस्तदा काको जगाम विविधां गतिम् लोककाम इमं लोकं सर्वं वै विचचार ह ।
5.38.32.e: 'Then that crow flew to many places seeking asylum all over the universe chased by the blade of grass.

5.38.33.t: स पित्रा च परित्यक्तस्सुरैश्च समहर्षिभिः त्रीन्लोकान्सम्परिक्रम्य तमेव शरणं गतः ।
5.38.33.e: 'Then the crow went round all the three worlds, having been rejected by his father Indra, including all the sages and gods. Refused by all he came back to Rama seeking shelter.

w: even though deserves to be killed
5.38.34.t: स तं निपतितं भूमौ शरण्यश्शरणागतम् वधार्हमपि काकुत्स्थ: कृपया पर्यपालयत् ।
5.38.34.e: 'Seeing the crow fallen on the ground, O Kakutstha, you who are a saviour of those who seek refuge saved him out of compassion, even though he deserved to be killed.

5.38.35.t: परिद्यूनं विषण्णं च स तमायान्तमब्रवीत् मोघं कर्तुं न शक्यं तु ब्राह्ममस्त्रं तदुच्यताम् ।
5.38.35.e: 'Rama, you saw the crow in pain and despondency who returned to you and said that it is not possible to make Brahma's weapon ineffectual.You may tell now. (what should be done.)

5.38.38.t:
स रामाय नमस्कृत्य राज्ञे दशरथाय च ।
विसृष्टस्तेन वीरेण प्रतिपेदे स्वमालयम्
5.38.38.e: 'That crow offered salutations to you Rama and king Dasaratha, thereafter took permission and went to his own dwelling.

5.38.39.t:
मत्कृते काकमात्रे तु ब्रह्मास्त्रं समुदीरितम् ।
कस्माद्यो मां हरेत्त्वत्तः क्षमसे तं महीपते
5.38.39.e: '(Addressing Rama as though he was present before her, Sita said) 'O lord of the earth for my sake you released the weapon of Brahma on a crow. What makes you excuse him who has abducted me?

5.38.40.t:
स कुरुष्व महोत्साहः कृपां मयि नरर्षभ ।
त्वया नाथवती नाथ ह्यनाथा इव दृश्यते
5.38.40.e: 'O bull among men you are so loving to me. I am like an orphan. Be kind to me. She who has found her lord in you stays without a protector.

5.38.41.t:
आनृशंस्यं परो धर्मस्तवत्त्त ऐव मया श्रुतः ।
जानामि त्वां महावीर्यं महोत्साहं महाबलम् अपारपारमक्षोभ्यं गाम्भीर्यात्सागरोपमम् ।
भर्तारं ससमुद्राया धरण्या वासवोपमम्
5.38.41.e: 'O my supreme lord I know you are kind, righteous, valiant, vigroous, mighty. You are boundless, calm and deep like the ocean. You are lord of earth and the seas and compeer of Vasava. I have heard from you that motiveless compassion is the best way to make one righteous.

5.38.48.t:
ममैव दुष्कृतं किञ्चिन्महदस्ति न संशयः ।
समर्थावपि तौ यन्मां नावेक्षेते परन्तपौ
5.38.48.e: "Perhaps I must have committed an atrocious sin. There is no doubt. For although both of them are scorchers of enemies, they deliver me not."

5.38.51.t:
कथञ्चिद्भवती दृष्टा न कालः परिदेवितुम् ।
इमं मुहूर्तं दुःखानां द्रक्ष्यस्यन्तमनिन्दिते
5.38.51.e: "I could find you with difficulty. This is not the time to wail. O blameless lady take it, your sorrow has come to an end at this moment.

5.38.52.t:
तावुभौ पुरुषव्याघ्रौ राजपुत्रौ महाबलौ ।
त्वद्दर्शनकृतोत्साहौ लङ्कां भस्मीकरिष्यतः
5.38.52.e: "Both the mighty brothers, tigers among men, are eager to see you. Both the princes will reduce this Lanka  into ashes.

5.38.53.t:
हत्त्वा च समरे क्रूरं रावणं सहबान्धवम् ।
राघवस्त्वां विशालाक्षि नेष्यति स्वां पुरीं प्रति
5.38.53.e: "O largeeyed lady cruel Ravana along with his relatives will be killed by Rama in war and Rama will return to his city with you.

5.38.55.t:
इत्युक्तवति तस्मिंस्तु सीता सुरसुतोपमा ।
उवाच शोकसन्तप्ता हनुमन्तं प्लवङ्गमम्
5.38.55.e: "Hanuman having spoken this way, Sita, resembling a god's daughter, grieving, thus addressed Hanuman:

5.38.56.t:
कौसल्या लोकभर्तारं सुषुवे यं मनस्विनी ।
तं ममार्थे सुखं पृच्छ शिरसा चाभिवादय
5.38.56.e: "Bow to Rama and offer salutations on my behalf. Inquiries concerning his welfare should be addressed to Rama, whom virtuous Kausalya bore as a son.

w: has attained the title of blessed mother
pleased by adopting the life of an ascetic
5.38.57.t:
स्रजश्च सर्वरत्नानि प्रिया याश्च वराङ्गनाः ।
ऐश्वर्यं च विशालायां पृथिव्यामपि दुर्लभम् पितरं मातरं चैव सम्मान्याभिप्रसाद्य च ।
अनुप्रव्रजितो रामं सुमित्रा येन सुप्रजाः
5.38.57.e: "He by whom Sumitra attained the title of blessed mother — garlands and all jewels, and those dear best of women in the wide city —

5.38.59.t:
आनुकूल्येन धर्मात्मा त्यक्त्वा सुखमनुत्तमम् ।
अनुगच्छति काकुत्स्थं भ्रातरं पालयन्वने
5.38.59.e: "Great, righteous Lakshmana had given up his pleasures and followed his brother Rama in his favour into the forest to be able to serve him.

5.38.60.t:
सिंहस्कन्धो महाबाहुर्मनस्वी प्रियदर्शिनः ।
पितृवद्वर्तते रामे मातृवन्मां समाचरन्
5.38.60.e: "Lakshmana, who has lionshoulders and strong arms, who is handsome, who takes Rama as his father and treats me as his own mother.

5.38.61.t:
ह्रियमाणां तदा वीरो न तु मां वेद लक्ष्मणः ।
वृद्धोपसेवी लक्ष्मीवान् शक्तो न बहुभाषिता राजपुत्रः प्रियः श्रेष्ठः सदृशः श्वशुरस्य मे ।
5.38.61.e: "Heroic Lakshmana, did not know while I was borne away. He is prosperous, foremost in serving elders. He is energetic and reserved in his speech like my fatherinlaw. He is a prince dear (to his brother).

5.38.62.t: ममः प्रियतरो नित्यं भ्राता रामस्य लक्ष्मणः नियुक्तो धुरि यस्यां तु तामुद्वहति वीर्यवान् ।
5.38.62.e: "Rama's brother Lakshmana is always dear to me. Heroic Lakshmana will discharge whichever responsibility is entrusted to him.

5.38.64.t:
मृदुर्नित्यं शुचिर्दक्षः प्रियो रामस्य लक्ष्मणः यथा हि वानरश्रेष्ठ दुःखक्षयकरो भवेत् ।
त्वमस्मिन्कार्यनिर्योगे प्रमाणं हरिसत्तमः
5.38.64.e: "Lakshmana is soft, pure, competent and dear to Rama. O great vanara, act in such a manner that Lakshmana can mitigate my suffering. O great monkey, the best of vanaras you are competent in accomplishing this task.

5.38.66.t:
राघवस्त्वत्समारम्भान्मयि यत्नपरो भवेत् ।
इदं ब्रूयाश्च मे नाथं शूरं रामं पुनः पुनः
5.38.66.e: "By your efforts alone my husband will try for my release. You may tell these words to my heroic husband, Rama, again and again.

5.38.67.t:
जीवितं धारयिष्यामि मासं दशरथात्मज ।
ऊर्ध्वं मासान्न जीवेयं सत्येनाहं ब्रवीमि ते
5.38.67.e: "I will hold on to life  only for a month. Beyond, I will not survive. I swear by truth. You may tell this to Rama.

w: Chudamani an ornament worn on the head
5.38.69.t:
ततो वस्त्रगतं मुक्त्वा दिव्यं चूडामणिं शुभम् ।
प्रदेयो राघवायेति सीता हनुमते ददौ
5.38.69.e: Then Sita took out the exquisite and auspicious Chudamani worn on the head, untied from her clothes and gave it to Hanuman to be presented to Rama.

5.38.71.t:
मणिरत्नं कपिवरः प्रतिगृह्याभिवाद्य च ।
सीतां प्रदक्षिणं कृत्वा प्रणतः पार्व्शतः स्थितः
5.38.71.e: Having recieved the jewel from Sita and circumambulated her, Hanuman offered salutations to  her and stood by her.

5.38.73.t:
मणिवरमुपगृह्य तं महार्हं जनकनृपात्मजया धृतं प्रभावात् ।
गिरिरिव पवनावधूतमुक्तः सुखितमनाः प्रतिसङ्क्रमं प्रपेदे
5.38.73.e: Having received the most precious jewel from the daughter of Janaka, Hanuman prepared to return like a mountain released from the impact of the wind. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये सुन्दरकाण्डे अष्टत्रिंशस्सर्गः।। Thus ends the thirtyeighth sarga of Sundarakanda of the holy Ramayana, the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

5.39.2.t:
मणिं तु दृष्ट्वा रामो वै त्रयाणां संस्मरिष्यति ।
वीरो जनन्या मम च राज्ञो दशरथस्य च
5.39.2.e: "Seeing this jewel,Rama will recall three of us, my mother, myself and the king Dasaratha" (as this was given by her mother at her marriage.)

5.39.4.t:
त्वमस्मिन्कार्यनिर्योगे प्रमाणं हरिसत्तम ।
हनुमन्यत्नमास्थाय दुःखक्षयकरो भव तस्य चिन्तयतो यत्नो दुःखक्षयकरो भवेत् ।
5.39.4.e: "O best of monkeys it is your  responsibility to carry out this task. O Hanuman think carefully of that. Take the initiative to reduce my suffering. I am confident that you can do it."

5.39.5.t: स तथेति प्रतिज्ञाय मारुतिर्भीमविक्रमः शिरसा वन्ध्य वैदेहीं गमनायोपचक्रमे ।
5.39.5.e: Hanuman possessed with fierce valour said to Vaidehi, 'so be it' and bowed his head, and offered salutations before he departed.

5.39.6.t: ज्ञात्वा सम्प्रस्थितं देवी वानरं मारुतात्मजम् बाष्पगद्गदया वाचा मैथिली वाक्यमब्रवीत् ।
5.39.6.e: The noble lady, Sita, having been fully convinced about Hanuman and realising that he is about to start, her voice was choked with tears. She said these words:

5.39.7.t:
कुशलं हनुमन्ब्रूयाः सहितौ रामलक्ष्मणौ सुग्रीवं च सहामात्यं वृद्धान् सर्वांश्च वानरान् ।
ब्रूयास्त्वं वानरश्रेष्ठ कुशलं धर्मसंहितम्
5.39.7.e: "O Hanuman the great communicate my welfare  to both Rama and Lakshmana, to Sugriva, his ministers, elderly vanaras in righteous order.

5.39.10.t:
जीवन्तीं मां यथा रामः सम्भावयति कीर्तिमान् ।
तत्तथा हनुमन्वाच्यं वाचा धर्ममवाप्नुहि
5.39.10.e: "Let the illustrious Rama take me alive. Help me with your (persuasive) words and you will acquire merit.

5.39.11.t:
नित्यमुत्साहयुक्ताश्च वाचश्रुत्वा त्वयेरिताः ।
वर्धिष्यते दाशरथेः पौरुषं मदवाप्तये
5.39.11.e: "On hearing your ever spirited words his manliness to get me back will be charged.

5.39.14.t:
क्षिप्रमेष्यति काकुत्स्थो हार्यृक्षप्रवरैर्वृतः ।
यस्ते युधि विजित्यारीन्शोकं व्यपनयिष्यति
5.39.14.e: "Kakutstha Rama, accompanied by vanaras and bears will reach here soon and conquer the enemies in war and relieve your grief.

5.39.16.t:
अप्यर्कमपि पर्जन्यमपि वैवस्वतं यमम् ।
स हि सोढुं रणे शक्तस्तव हेतोर्विशेषतः
5.39.16.e: "Indeed, Rama is capable of conquering even the Sungod, or the raingod or Yama (the son of the Sun) specially for your sake.

5.39.17.t:
स हि सागरपर्यन्तां महीं शासितुमीहति ।
त्वन्निमित्तो हि रामस्य जयो जनकनन्दिनि
5.39.17.e: "Rama is fit to rule the entire earth surrounded by the ocean. O delight of Janaka he will succeed in serving your cause."

5.39.18.t:
तस्य तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा सम्यक्सत्यं सुभाषितम् ।
जानकी बहुमेनेऽथ वचनं चेदमब्रवीत्
5.39.18.e: On hearing the truthful, proper, pleasing words by Hanuman whom she held in great esteem, Sita said this:

5.39.19.t:
ततस्तं प्रस्थितं सीता वीक्षमाणा पुनः पुनः ।
भर्तृस्नेहान्वितं वाक्यं सौहार्दादनुमानयत्
5.39.19.e: Sita again and again looked at Hanuman who was about to start. She made him understand her words conveying her love for Rama.

5.39.21.t:
मम चेदल्पभाग्याया सान्निध्यात्तव वानर ।
अस्य शोकस्य महतो मुहूर्तं मोक्षणं भवेत्
5.39.21.e: "Your presence will relieve me of my suffering, if you stay here for a while.

5.39.23.t:
तवादर्शनजः शोको भूयो मां परितापयेत् ।
दुःखाद्धुःखपरामृष्टां दीपयन्निव वानर
5.39.23.e: "My agony would be increased further by not seeing you. It would be inflamming my agony and I would be even more pained.

5.39.24.t:
अयं च वीर सन्देहस्तिष्ठतीव ममाग्रतः ।
सुमहांस्त्वत्सहायेषु हर्यृक्षेषु हरीश्वरः
5.39.24.e: "O heroic chief of vanaras I am doubtful as to whether vanaras and bears can extend help?

5.39.25.t:
कथं नु खलु दुष्पारं तरिष्यन्ति महोदधिम् ।
तानि हर्यृक्षसैन्यानि तौ वा नरवरात्मजौ
5.39.25.e: "How can the army of vanaras and bears, for that matter, princes Rama and Lakshmana negotiate the ocean, which is difficult to cross?

5.39.27.t:
तदस्मिन्कार्यनिर्योगे वीरैवं दुरतिक्रमे ।
किं पश्यसि समाधानं त्वं हि कार्यविदां वरः
5.39.27.e: "What means do you, being the foremost hero among the three who are capable performing this difficult task, foresee?

5.39.29.t:
बलैस्समग्रैर्यदि मां रावणं जित्य संयुगे ।
विजयी स्वपुरं यायात्तत्तस्य सदृशं भवेत्
5.39.29.e: "It would be worthy of Rama if he with his entire army emerges victorious over Ravana in a battle and takes me to his city.

5.39.30.t:
शरैस्तु सङ्कुलां कृत्वा लङ्कां परबलार्दनः ।
मां नयेद्यदि काकुत्स्थः तत्तस्य सदृशं भवेत्
5.39.30.e: "If Kakutstha (Rama), slayer of the enemy army fills the entire Lanka with his arrows and takes me, then his action will be worthy of him.

5.39.31.t:
तद्यथा तस्य विक्रान्तमनुरूपं महात्मनः ।
भवेदाहवशूरस्य तथा त्वमुपपादय
5.39.31.e: "You may make arrangement in such a manner that, that great self, the hero in war makes his victorious march which is worthy of him."

5.39.32.t:
तदर्थोपहितं वाक्यं प्रश्रितं हेतुसंहितम् ।
निशम्य हनुमान्शेषं वाक्यमुत्तरमब्रवीत्
5.39.32.e: Having heard the meaningful, courteous and logical words of Sita, Hanuman replied:

5.39.34.t:
स वानरसहस्राणां कोटीभिरभिसंवृतः ।
क्षिप्रमेष्यति वैदेहि राक्षसानां निबर्हणः
5.39.34.e: "O Vaidehi Sugriva will reach this place with thousands of crores of vanaras very soon and would kill all the ogres.

w: who can leap with the speed of mind
5.39.35.t:
तस्य विक्रमसम्पन्नास्सत्त्ववन्तो महाबलाः ।
मनस्सङ्कल्पसम्पाता निदेशे हरयः स्थिताः
5.39.35.e: "Valiant, virtuous and powerful vanaras who can leap with the speed of mind are awaiting orders (of Sugriva).

5.39.36.t:
येषां नोपरि नाधस्तान्न तिर्यक्सज्जते गतिः ।
न च कर्मसु सीदन्ति महत्स्वमिततेजसः
5.39.36.e: "Their course cannot be impeded either upward, or downward or right or left. They  are indeed very brilliant and would never fail in any task.

5.39.37.e: "They have often circumambulated the earth including its oceans and mountains through the aerial path with great enthusiasm.

5.39.41.t:
मम पृष्ठगतौ तौ च चन्द्रसूर्याविवोदितौ ।
त्वत्सकाशं महासत्त्वौ नृसिंहावागमिष्यतः
5.39.41.e: "Both the valiant Rama and Lakshmana, lions among men, looking brilliant like Sun and Moon will come to you riding on my back.

5.39.42.t:
ततो वीरौ नरवरौ सहितौ रामलक्ष्मणौ ।
आगम्य नगरीं लङ्कां सायकैर्विधमिष्यतः
5.39.42.e: "Both the heroes, Rama and Lakshmana will come and blow up the city of Lanka with their unfailing arrows.

w: the delight of the Raghu race
5.39.43.t:
सगणं रावणं हत्त्वा राघवो रघुनन्दनः ।
त्वामादाय वरारोहे स्वपुरीं प्रतियास्यति
5.39.43.e: "O beautiful lady Raghava, the delight of the Raghu race would kill Ravana and his kins and return with you to his city৷৷

w: let it be auspicious to you
5.39.44.t:
तदाश्वसिहि भद्रं ते भव त्वं कालकाङ्क्षिणी ।
नचिराद्द्रक्ष्यसे रामं प्रज्वलन्तमिवानलम्
5.39.44.e: "Therefore, count the days and rest assured. Let it be auspicious to you. You will shortly see Rama burning like fire.

5.39.46.t:
क्षिप्रं त्वं देवि शोकस्य पारं यास्यसि मैथिलि ।
रावणं चैव रामेण निहतं द्रक्ष्यसेऽचिरात्
5.39.46.e: "O queen Mythili you come to the end of your sorrow and will soon see Ravana killed by Rama".

5.39.47.t:
एवमाश्वास्य वैदेहीं हनुमान्मारुतात्मजः ।
गमनाय मतिं कृत्वा वैदेहीं पुनरब्रवीत्
5.39.47.e: Having thus consoled Vaidehi, Hanuman, son of the Windgod resolved to depart. Once again he spoke to Vadehi:

5.39.48.t:
तमरिघ्नं कृतात्मानं क्षिप्रं द्रक्ष्यसि राघवम् ।
लक्ष्मणं च धनुष्पाणिं लङ्काद्वारमुपागतम्
5.39.48.e: "Very soon you would see the slayer of foes, who is an accomplished wielder of the bow (Rama) along with Lakshmana at the entrance of Lanka.

w: whose body is like clouds on mountain
5.39.50.e: "O respectable lady you would see many troops of vanara chiefs who resemble clouds hovering on the mountain peaks of Lankaroaring.

5.39.53.t:
रामाद्विशिष्टः कोऽन्योऽस्ति कश्चित्सौमित्रिणा समः ।
अग्निमारुतकल्पौ तौ भ्रातरौ तव संश्रयौ
5.39.53.e: "Who is superior to Rama? Who is equal to Lakshmana? Both the brothers are like Fire and Wind. They are your refuge.

5.40.1.t:
श्रुत्वा तु वचनं तस्य वायुसूनोर्महात्मनः ।
उवाचात्महितं वाक्यं सीता सुरसुतोपमा
5.40.1.e: Sita who was like the daughter of the gods heard the son of the Windgod for her benefit and replied:

w: who has been speaking pleasing words
5.40.2.t:
त्वां दृष्ट्वा प्रियवक्तारं सम्प्रहृष्यामि वानरः ।
अर्धसञ्जातसस्येव वृष्टिं प्राप्य वसुन्धरा
5.40.2.e: "O vanara just as the earth feels happy when the half grown crops receive rain, I feel happy after seeing you. You have been speaking pleasing words

5.40.3.t:
यथा तं पुरुषव्याघ्रं गात्रैश्शोकाभिकर्शितैः ।
संस्पृशेयं सकामाहं तथा कुरु दयां मयि
5.40.3.e: "Be kind to me and act in such a manner that I may embrace my lord passionately with my body emaciated with grief.

5.40.4.t:
अभिज्ञानं च रामस्य दद्या हरिगणोत्तम ।
क्षिप्तामिषीकां काकस्य कोपादेकाक्षिशातनीम्
5.40.4.e: "O best leader of vanaras remind Rama about the incident of the release of a blade of grass in anger blinding one of the eyes of the crow narrated to you.

5.40.6.t:
स वीर्यवान्कथं सीतां हृतां समनुमन्यसे ।
वसन्तीं रक्षसां मध्ये महेन्द्रवरुणोपमः
5.40.6.e: 'Rama you are like Indra and Varuna in valiance. How are you tolerating Sita seized, dwelling among the demons?

5.40.7.t:
एष चूडामणिर्दिव्यो मया सुपरिरक्षितः ।
एतं दृष्ट्वा प्रहृष्यामि व्यसने त्वामिवानघ
5.40.7.e: "O sinless Rama this wonderful Chudamani of mine has been carefully safeguarded. Seeing this is like seeing you when I am in distress.

w: it is not possible for me.
5.40.8.t:
एष निर्यातितश्श्रीमान्मया ते वारिसम्भवः ।
अतः परं न शक्ष्यामि जीवितुं शोकलालसा
5.40.8.e: "I am sending you this (Chudamani) born of the sea. O glorious Rama and now engrossed in grief it is not possible for me to live.

5.40.9.t:
असह्यानि च दुःखानि वाचश्च हृदयच्छिदः ।
राक्षसीनां सुघोराणां त्वत्कृते मर्षयाम्यहम्
5.40.9.e: "I am tolerating this unbearable grief, and the words of the dreadful ogresses piercing my heart. Only for you.

5.40.10.t:
धारयिष्यामि मासं तु जीवितं शत्रुसूदन ।
ऊर्ध्वं मासान्न जीविष्ये त्वया हीना नृपात्मज
5.40.10.e: "O subduer of enemies O prince I will hold on to life only for a month. I will not survive beyond a month in your absence.

5.40.12.t:
वैदेह्या वचनं श्रुत्वा करुणं साश्रु भाषितम् ।
अथाब्रवीन्महातेजा हनुमान्मारुतात्मजः
