5.40.12.e: Hearing the words of Sita who was weeping piteously, brilliant Hanuman said this:

w: that which makes him more happy
5.40.17.t:
यत्तु रामो विजानीयादभिज्ञानमनिन्दिते ।
प्रीतिसञ्जननं तस्य भूयस्त्वं दातुमर्हसि
5.40.17.e: "O unimpeachable lady give one more identification which would make him more happy".

5.40.18.t:
साब्रवीद्दत्तमेवेति मयाभिज्ञानमुत्तमम् ।
एतदेव हि रामस्य दृष्ट्वा मत्केशभूषणम् श्रद्धेयं हनुमन्वाक्यं तव वीर भविष्यति ।
5.40.18.e: "I have already given the best identification. When you hand this jewel used on my hair to him,  he will believe what you tell him".

5.40.19.t: स तं मणिवरं गृह्य श्रीमान्प्लवगसत्तमः प्रणम्य शिरसा देवीं गमनायोपचक्रमे ।
5.40.19.e: The illustrious vanara held the ornament, prostrated to Sita and prepared to depart.

5.40.22.t:
हनुमन्सिंहसङ्काशौ भ्रातरौ रामलक्ष्मणौ ।
सुग्रीवं च सहामात्यं सर्वान् ब्रूयाह्यनामयम्
5.40.22.e: "O Hanuman to the lionlike brothers Rama and Lakshmana, to Sugriva  including his ministers and to every one convey my good wishes.

5.40.24.t:
इमं च तीव्रं मम शोकवेगं रक्षोभिरेभिः परिभर्त्सनं च ।
ब्रूयास्तु रामस्य गतस्समीपम् शिवश्च तेऽध्वाऽस्तु हरिप्रवीर
5.40.24.e: "Foremost vanara tell Rama about my intense grief as well as the threats of the demons. May your journey be happy.

5.40.25.t:
स राजपुत्र्य्राप्रतिवेदितार्थः कपिः कृतार्थः परिहृष्टचेताः ।
अल्पावशेषं प्रसमीक्ष्य कार्यं दिशं ह्युदीचीं मनसा जगाम
5.40.25.e: Hanuman understood the message of princess Sita and felt delighted at heart at his accomplishment. Considering the small task yet to be accomplished he reached the northern shore mentally (He thought of Rama who waited in Kishkinda which is in the northern direction). इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये सुन्दरकाण्डे चत्वारिंशस्सर्गः।। Thus ends the fortieth sarga of Sundarakanda of the holy Ramayana, the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

5.41.1.t:
स च वाग्भिः प्रशस्ताभिर्गमिष्यन्पूजितस्तया ।
तस्माद्देशादपक्रम्य चिन्तयामास वानरः
5.41.1.e: Having been honoured and praised by Sita's words, Hanuman prepared to depart from Sita's presence.

w: will not yield by sowing seeds of dissension
5.41.3.t:
न साम रक्षस्सु गुणाय कल्पते न दानमर्थोपचितेषु युज्यते ।
न भेदसाध्या बलदर्पिता जनाः पराक्रमस्त्वेव ममेह रोचते
5.41.3.e: 'With demons, negotiation is of no use. They are wealthy, they need no gifts. Proud of their stregth, the demons will not yield to dissension. I think only by using power it can be done.

5.41.8.t:
कथं नु खल्वद्य भवेत्सुखागतं प्रसह्य युद्धं मम राक्षसैः सह ।
तथैव खल्वात्मबलं च सारवत्सम्मानयेन्मां च रणे दशाननः
5.41.8.e: 'How can I have enduring war with the ogres today? How will my visit to this place end in happy return? Only in a combat this tenheaded Ravana will guage his strength and mine

5.41.9.t:
ततस्समासाद्य रणे दशाननं समन्त्रिवर्गं सबलप्रयायिनम् ।
हृदि स्थितं तस्य मतं बलं च वै सुखेन मत्त्वाऽहमितः पुनर्व्रजे
5.41.9.e: 'I can return happily only after I gauge the tenheaded Ravana's army in war, his strength, his companions including the ministers and his mind.

w: feast to the eyes and mind
filled with different kinds of trees and creepers
like the Nandana garden of Indra.
5.41.10.t:
इदमस्य नृशंसस्य नन्दनोपममुत्तमम् ।
वनं नेत्रमनःकान्तं नानाद्रुमलतायुतम्
5.41.10.e: 'This Ashoka garden of Ravana filled with different kinds of trees and creepers is a feast to the eyes and mind. It is an excellent garden like the Nandana  garden of Indra.

5.41.11.t:
इदं विध्वंसयिष्यामि शुष्कं वनमिवानलः ।
अस्मिन्भग्ने ततः कोपं करिष्यति दशाननः
5.41.11.e: 'I will devastate this garden, just as fire destroys a dried up forest. This will enrage Ravana.

w: armed with tridents black iron spears
5.41.12.t:
ततो महत्साश्वमहारथद्विपं बलं समादेक्ष्यति राक्षसाधिपः ।
त्रिशूलकालायसपट्टिसायुधं ततो महद्युद्धमिदं भविष्यति
5.41.12.e: 'Then the demon king will order the horses, chariots and elephants and army equipped with tridents and spears to march against me. A great war will take place.

w: with those endowed with fierce strength
5.41.13.t:
अहं तु तैः संयति चण्डविक्रमै स्समेत्य रक्षोभिरसह्य विक्रमः ।
निहत्य तद्रावणचोदितं बलं सुखं गमिष्यामि कपीश्वरालयम्
5.41.13.e: 'I will fight with the ogres sent by Ravana, endowed with fierce strength and irresistible valour. After destroying their army I will go to the abode of vanaras happily'.

w: with variety of trees and vines
5.41.15.t:
ततस्तु हनुमान्वीरो बभञ्ज प्रमदावनम् ।
मत्तद्विजसमाघुष्टं नानाद्रुमलतायुतम्
5.41.15.e: Then Hanuman felled a variety of trees and vines inhabited by intoxicated birds in the beautiful garden meant for womenfolk.

5.41.16.t:
तद्वनं मथितैर्वृक्षैर्भिन्नैश्च सलिलाशयैः ।
चूर्णितैः पर्वताग्रैश्च बभूवाप्रियदर्शनम्
5.41.16.e: That garden looked ugly with uprooted trees, breached ponds and powdered mountain peaks.

w: with birds shrieking with different kinds of sounds
like women with their robes disarrayed
5.41.17.t:
नानाशकुन्तविरुतैः प्रभिन्नैस्सलिलाशयैः ।
ताम्रैः किसलयैः क्लान्तै: क्लान्तद्रुमलतायुतम् न बभौ तद्वनं तत्र दावानलहतं यथा ।
व्याकुलावरणा रेजुर्विह्वला इव ता लताः
5.41.17.e: Vines and trees wilted, birds shrieking, the embankments of ponds destroyed, its tender coppery red shoots withered, the garden looked as though it is burnt by forest fire and the climbers looked like women shivering in fear with their robes disarrayed.

5.41.19.t:
लतागृहैश्चित्रगृहैश्च नाशितैर्महोरगैर्व्यालमृगैश्च निर्धुतैः ।
शिलागृहैरुन्मथितैस्तथा गृहैः प्रणष्टरूपं तदभून्महद्वनम्
5.41.19.e: The great garden lay disfigured, with the arbours and the picture galleries ruined, huge serpents and wild animals scattered, with stone houses and sheds destroyed.

5.41.21.t:
स तस्य कृत्वार्थपतेर्महाकपिर्महद्व्यलीकं मनसो महात्मनः ।
युयुत्सुरेको बहुभिर्महाबलैश्शिया ज्वलंस्तोरणमास्थितः कपिः
5.41.21.e: The great vanara having perpetrated mischief, rousing anger in the mind of the great lord of wealth, stood at the exit doorway ready to combat singlehanded with many warriors in that  mighty army blazing in glory. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये सुन्दरकाण्डे एकचत्वारिंशस्सर्गः।। Thus ends the fortyfirst sarga of Sundarakanda of the holy Ramayana, the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

w: by the cracking sound of trees
5.42.1.t:
ततः पक्षिनिनादेन वृक्षभङ्गस्वनेन च ।
बभूवुस्त्राससम्भ्रान्तास्सर्वे लङ्कानिवासिनः
5.42.1.e: The residents of Lanka panicked at the shrieking sounds of birds and cracking sounds of trees.

5.42.2.t:
विद्रुताश्च भयत्रस्ता विनेदुर्मृगपक्षिणः ।
रक्षसां च निमित्तानि क्रूराणि प्रतिपेदिरे
5.42.2.e: The frightened beasts and birds ran and flew, screeching in all directions. Fierce portents appeared to the demons.

5.42.3.t:
ततो गतायां निद्रायां राक्षस्यो विकृताननाः ।
तद्वनं ददृशुर्भग्नं तं च वीरं महाकपिम्
5.42.3.e: Hideouslooking ogresses, awakened from sleep, saw the garden devastated by the heroic Vanara.

5.42.4.t:
स ता दृष्ट्वा महाबाहुर्महासत्त्वो महाबलः ।
चकार सुमहद्रूपं राक्षसीनां भयावहम्
5.42.4.e: When the powerful, mighty and strongarmed Hanuman saw the ogresses he assumed a very huge form in order to strike terror in them.

5.42.5.t:
ततस्तं गिरिसङ्काशमतिकायं महाबलम् ।
राक्षस्यो वानरं दृष्ट्वा पप्रच्छुर्जनकात्मजाम्
5.42.5.e: Then, seeing the huge body of the mighty vanara resembling a mountain the ogresses questioned Janaki about him.

5.42.8.t:
अथाब्रवीन्महासाध्वी सीता सर्वाङ्गसुन्दरी ।
रक्षसां भीमरूपाणां विज्ञाने मम का गतिः
5.42.8.e: Chaste and beautiful Sita said, "How do I know about the ogresses who assume many fierce forms?"

5.42.9.t:
यूयमेवाभिजानीत योऽयं यद्वा करिष्यति ।
अहिरेव ह्यहेः पादान्विजानाति न संशयः
5.42.9.e: "You alone can know about who he is and what he is about. A serpent alone knows the movement (footprints) of another serpent. There is no doubt about it.

w: who has assumed his desired form in various ways
5.42.10.t:
अहमप्यस्य भीतास्मि नैनं जानामि को न्वयं ।
वेद्मि राक्षसमेवैनं कामरूपिणमागतम्
5.42.10.e: "I am also scared of him. I do not know who he is. I think he is a demon, who came here assuming a form of his choice.

5.42.11.t:
वैदेह्या वचनं श्रुत्वा राक्षस्यो विद्रुता दिशः ।
स्थिताः काश्चिद्गताः काश्चिद्रावणाय निवेदितुम्
5.42.11.e: LIstening to Vaidehi's words the ogresses divided themselves and fled in all directions. While some stood there, others went to report to Ravana.

5.42.12.t:
रावणस्य समीपे तु राक्षस्यो विकृताननाः ।
विरूपं वानरं भीममाख्यातुमुपचक्रमुः
5.42.12.e: The uglyfaced ogresses went to the presence of Ravana and reported about the frightening form of the vanara.

w: in the midst of Ashoka garden
5.42.13.e: "Your majesty an extremely powerful and frightening Vanara had a dialogue with Sita. He is stationed in the midst of Ashoka garden.

w: by a person of wonderful form
filled with various kinds of animals
5.42.16.t:
तेन त्वद्भुतरूपेण यत्तत्तव मनोहरम् ।
नानामृगगणाकीर्णं प्रमृष्टं प्रमदावनम्
5.42.16.e: "Your beautiful pleasure garden filled with a variety of beasts has been ruined by this wonderful figure.

w: or is it because he was tired
we are not able to understand
5.42.18.t:
जानकीरक्षणार्थं वा श्रमाद्वा नोपलभ्यते ।
अथवा कश्श्रमस्तस्य सैव तेनाभिरक्षिता
5.42.18.e: "It is not clear whether he spared that place for protecting Janakai or he stopped due to exhaustion. What is fatigue for him? It must be to save her that she is spared by him.

w: a tree with lovely tender leaves and flowers
5.42.19.t:
चारुपल्लवपुष्पाढ्यं यं सीता स्वयमास्थिता ।
प्रवृद्धश्शिंशुपावृक्ष स्स च तेनाभिरक्षितः
5.42.19.e: "He has spared the simsupa tree with lovely, tender leaves and flowers which is a chosen  resort by Sita.

5.42.23.t:
तस्य क्रुद्धस्य नेत्राभ्यां प्रापतन्नास्रबिन्दवः ।
दीप्ताभ्यामिव दीपाभ्यां सार्चिष स्स्नेहबिन्दवः
5.42.23.e: From his angry eyes fell down drops of tears just as burning drops of oil drip from two burning lamps.

5.42.24.t:
आत्मनस्सदृशान्शूरान्किङ्करान्नाम राक्षसान् ।
व्यादिदेश महातेजा निग्रहार्थं हनूमतः
5.42.24.e: Then powerful Ravana commanded heroic demons called kinkaras who vied in strength to catch Hanuman.

5.42.25.t:
तेषामशीतिसाहस्रं किङ्कराणां तरस्विनाम् ।
निर्ययुर्भवनात्तस्मात्कूटमुद्गरपाणयः महोदरा महादंष्ट्रा घोररूपा महाबलाः ।
युद्धाभिमनसस्सर्वे हनुमद्ग्रहणोद्यताः
5.42.25.e: Eighty thousand powerful  kinkaras (a clan of demons), largebellied, with large teeth and of dreadful appearance, swift in action, armed with hammers and clubs marched from there, resolved to capture Hanuman.

5.42.27.t:
ते कपीन्द्रं समासाद्य तोरणस्थमवस्थितम् ।
अभिपेतुर्महावेगाः पतङ्गा इव पावकम्
5.42.27.e: The kinkaras rushed towards the leader of vanaras who stood near the archway like the moths rushing towards the flame.

5.42.28.t:
ते गदाभिर्विचित्राभिः परिघैः काञ्चनाङ्गदैः ।
आजघ्नुर्वानरश्रेष्ठं शरैश्चादित्यसन्निभैः
5.42.28.e: They assailed Hanuman with iron maces, crowbars edged with gold and shining arrows resembling the Sun.

w: with barbed missiles and powerful javelins
5.42.29.t:
मुद्गरैः पट्टिशैश्शूलैः प्रासतोमरशक्तिभिः ।
परिवार्य हनूमन्तं सहसा तस्थुरग्रतः
5.42.29.e: They quickly surrounded Hanuman and stood with hammers, sharpedged spears, tridents, barbed missiles and powerful javelins.

5.42.31.t:
स भूत्वा सुमहाकायो हनुमान्मारुतात्मजः ।
धृष्टमास्फोटयामास लङ्कां शब्देन पूरयन्
5.42.31.e: Hanuman, son of Maruti, enlarged his body to a huge size and patted himself wildly  making loud noise that echoed the entire Lanka.

w: by the sound of the patting
5.42.32.e: By the highly frightening sound caused by Hanuman patting, the birds from the sky fell down making a loud noise and Hanuman proclaimed in a loud voice as follows:

5.42.33.t:
जयत्यतिबलो रामो लक्ष्मणश्च महाबलः ।
राजा जयति सुग्रीवो राघवेणाभिपालितः
5.42.33.e: "Victory to Rama, the mighty and powerful, Victory to Lakshmana. Victory to king Sugriva who is ruled by Rama."

w: of the lord of Kosala kingdom
5.42.34.t:
दासोऽहं कोसलेन्द्रस्य रामस्याक्लिष्टकर्मणः ।
हनुमान्शत्रुसैन्यानां निहन्ता मारुतात्मजः
5.42.34.e: "I, son of the Windgod, destroyer of hostile armies, am a servant of Rama, the lord of Kosala kingdom, a man of unwearied action.

5.42.35.t:
न रावणसहस्रं मे युद्धे प्रतिबलं भवेत् ।
शिलाभिस्तु प्रहरतः पादपैश्च सहस्रशः
5.42.35.e: Even a thousand Ravanas will not match me in strength when I pound stones and trees in a thousand ways.

5.42.36.t:
अर्दयित्वा पुरीं लङ्कामभिवाद्य च मैथिलीम् ।
समृद्धार्थो गमिष्यामि मिषतां सर्वरक्षसाम्
5.42.36.e: "I shall destroy the city of Lanka and pay my respects to Mythili right under the nose of all demons. I will return with my purpose accomplished.

5.42.37.t:
तस्य सन्नादशब्देन तेऽभवन्भयशङ्किताः ।
ददृशुश्च हनूमन्तं सन्ध्यामेघमिवोन्नतम्
5.42.37.e: Terrified on hearing the roar, the kinkaras looked at the towering Hanuman who seemed like a cloud in twilight (red in colour).

5.42.39.t:
स तैः परिवृतश्शूरैस्सर्वतस्सुमहाबलः ।
आससादाऽयसं भीमं परिघं तोरणाश्रितम्
5.42.39.e: Extremely powerful Hanuman surrounded by heroes all over, on his part went to the archway and picked up a terrific iron beam.

5.42.40.t:
स तं परिघमादाय जघान रजनीचरान् ।
स पन्नगमिवादाय स्फुरन्तं विनतासुतः विचचाराम्बरे वीरः परिगृह्य च मारुतिः ।
5.42.40.e: Hanuman, the mighty hero, seized the iron beam and struck the kinkaras, just as Garuda, the son of Vinata shoots up a struggling serpent and starts taking strides in the sky with the weapon in his hand (like Indra with his thunderbolt did with demons).

5.42.41.t: स हत्वा राक्षसान्वीरान्किङ्करान्मारुतात्मजः युद्धाकाङ्क्षी पुनर्वीरस्तोरणं समुपाश्रितः ।
5.42.41.e: The great Windgod's son killed the kinkaras, and returned to the archway desiring further combat.

5.42.43.t:
स राक्षसानां निहतं महद्बलं निशम्य राजा परिवृत्तलोचनः ।
समादिदेशाप्रतिमं पराक्रमे प्रहस्तपुत्रं समरे सुदुर्जयम्
5.42.43.e: The mighty demon king having heard about the killing of the formidable army of ogres, his eyes rolling in rage, commanded the son of Prahasta, who is difficult to conquer and matchless in war. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये सुन्दरकाण्डे द्विचत्वारिंशस्सर्गः।। Thus ends the fortysecond sarga of Sundarakanda of the holy Ramayana, the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

w: like the peak of mount Meru
5.43.1.t:
ततस्स किङ्करान्हत्वा हनुमान्ध्यानमास्थितः ।
वनं भग्नं मया चैत्यप्रासादो न विनाशितः तस्मात्प्रासादमप्येवं भीमं विध्वंसयाम्यहं ।
इति सञ्चिन्त्य मनसा हनुमान्दर्शयन्बलम् चैत्यप्रासादमाप्लुत्य मेरुशृङ्गमिवोन्नतम् ।
आरुरोह कपिश्रेष्ठो हनुमान्मारुतात्मजः
5.43.1.e: Having slain the kinkaras, Hanuman stood and reflected, ' I have ruined the garden and not the palatial buildings that are like temples (Chaityas)'. Then Hanuman, son of the Windgod, decided in his mind to show his strength and jumped on to the top of the palatial building that appeared like the peak of mount Meru.

5.43.4.t:
आरुह्य गिरिसङ्काशं प्रासादं हरियूथपः ।
बभौ स सुमहातेजाः प्रतिसूर्य इवोदितः
5.43.4.e: The powerful vanara leader climbed the tall, palatial building which resembled a mountain. He looked like another Sun, just risen.

5.43.7.t:
तस्यास्फोटितशब्देन महता श्रोत्रघातिना ।
पेतुर्विहङ्गमास्तत्र चैत्यपालाश्च मोहिताः
5.43.7.e: By the deafening sound caused by the patting, the birds fell down and the guards of the palace lost consciousness.

5.43.12.t:
एवमुक्त्वा विमानस्थश्चैत्यस्थान्हरियूथपः ।
ननाद भीमनिर्ह्रादो रक्षसां जनयन्भयम्
5.43.12.e: Having made proclamations that way from the top of the Vimana (palace) the monkey leader roared making terrific sound frightening the ogres.

5.43.13.t:
तेन शब्देन महता चैत्यपालाश्शतं ययुः ।
गृहीत्वा विविधानस्त्रान्प्रासान्खङ्गान्परश्वथान् विसृजन्तो महाकाया मारुतिं पर्यवारयन् ।
5.43.13.e: Hearing the terrific sound, a hundred gigantic guards of the palace set forth, holding different kinds of weapons like darts, swords and axes and hurled at Maruti surrounding him.

5.43.14.t:
ते गदाभिर्विचित्राभिः परिघैः काञ्चनाङ्गदैः ।
आजघ्नुर्वानरश्रेष्ठं बाणैश्चादित्यसन्निभैः
5.43.14.e: Holding astonishing maces decorated with gold, iron crowbars and sharp arrows resembling the rays of the Sun the ogres hit Hanuman, the foremost of vanaras.

5.43.15.t:
आवर्त इव गङ्गायास्तोयस्य विपुलो महान् ।
परिक्षिप्य हरिश्रेष्ठं स बभौ रक्षसां गणः
5.43.15.e: The demons surrounding the great monkey looked like a big whirlpool of the water of the river Ganga.

5.43.16.t:
ततो वातात्मजः क्रुद्धो भीम रूपं समास्थितः प्रासादस्य महन्तस्य स्तम्बं हेमपरिष्कृतम् ।
उत्पाटयित्वा वेगेन हनुमान्पवनात्मजः ततस्तं भ्रामयामास शतधारं महाबलः ।
5.43.16.e: Thereupon the infuriated son of the Windgod, assumed a fearsome form, uprooted a pillar of the palace decked with gold and holding that hundred edged pillar whirled it round swiftly.

5.43.18.t:
तत्र चाग्निस्समभवत्प्रासादश्चाप्यदह्यत दह्यमानं ततो दृष्ट्वा प्रासादं हरियूथपः ।
स राक्षसशतं हत्त्वा वज्रेणेन्द्र इवासुरान् अन्तरिक्षे स्थितश्श्तीमानिदं वचनमब्रवीत् ।
5.43.18.e: Thereafter fire was generated (through friction) and with if the palace blazed. Hanuman saw the palace burning. He killed a hundred demons there as Indra killed demons with his thunderbolt. (The whirling pillar that generated fire apeared like a thunderbolt) Later he stood in the air and proclaimed this:

w: of the best of  vanara leaders
5.43.20.t:
मादृशानां सहस्राणि विसृष्टानि महात्मनाम् बलिनां वानरेन्द्राणां सुग्रीववशवर्तिनाम् ।
अटन्ति वसुधां कृत्स्नां वयमन्ये च वानराः
5.43.20.e: "Thousands of huge and mighty monkeys, equal to me, loyal to king Sugriva, are coming under the orders and have been recruited from the entire earth. They  are the best among monkeys.

5.43.22.e: "Of them some have the strength equal to ten elephants, others are ten times stronger, and still others have a thousand elephants' strength.

5.43.23.e: "Some have the strength of flood waters, some are powerful as wind and yet others have strength beyond measure.

w: with the lord of Ikshvaku dynasty
5.43.25.t:
नेयमस्ति पुरी लङ्का न यूयं न च रावणः ।
.. ।
 ।
यस्मादिक्ष्वाकुनाथेन बद्धं वैरं महात्मना ।
5.43.25.e: "You have established great enmity with the noble lord of Ikshvaku dynasty. Neither this Lanka will endure nor you, nor even Ravana will be traced. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये सुन्दरकाण्डे त्रिचत्वारिशस्सर्गः।। Thus ends the fortythird sarga of Sundarakanda of the holy Ramayana, the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

w: adorned with a garland of red flowers and red clothes
5.44.1.t:
सन्दिष्टो राक्षसेन्द्रेण प्रहस्तस्य सुतो बली ।
जम्बुमाली महादंष्ट्रो निर्जगाम धनुर्धरः रक्तमाल्याम्बरधरस्स्रग्वी रुचिरकुण्डलः ।
महान्विवृत्तनयनश्चण्डस्समरदुर्जयः धनुश्शक्रधनुः प्रख्यं महद्रुचिरसायकम् ।
विष्फारयाणो वेगेन वज्राशनिसमस्वनम्
5.44.1.e: Commanded  by the demon king, Jambumali the invincible son of Prahasta, who had large teeth in front, big rolling eyes, red flower garland, red robes and a chaplet with beautiful earrings. He went round twanging his producing thunderous sound. His arrows were huge, shining and beautiful.

w: who stood on top of the exit archway
5.44.6.t:
तं तोरणविटङ्कस्थं हनुमन्तं महाकपिम् ।
जम्बुमाली महाबाहुर्विव्याध निशितैश्शरैः
5.44.6.e: Strongarmed Jambumali with his sharp arrows hit great Hanuman who stood on top of the exit archway.

5.44.7.t:
अर्धचन्द्रेण वदने शिरस्येकेन कर्णिना ।
बाह्वोर्विव्याध नाराचैर्दशभिस्तं कपीश्वरम्
5.44.7.e: Jambumali released a crescentshaped arrow on the face, one earshaped (barbed) arrow on the head and ten iron arrows into the arms of the lord of monkeys.

5.44.8.t:
तस्य तच्छुशुभे ताम्रं शरेणाभिहतं मुखम् ।
शरदीवाम्बुजं फुल्लं विद्धं भास्कररश्मिना
5.44.8.e: His red face struck by an arrow appeared like a fullblown lotus in autumn season hit  by  the rays of the Sun.

5.44.9.t:
तत्तस्य रक्तं रक्तेन रञ्जितं शुशुभे मुखम् ।
यथाकाशे महापद्मं सिक्तं चन्दनबिन्दुभिः
5.44.9.e: His red face  stained with blood was glowing bright like red lotus in the sky sprinkled with drops of red sandal.

5.44.10.t:
चुकोप बाणाभिहतो राक्षसस्य महाकपिः ।
ततः पार्श्वेऽतिविपुलां ददर्श महतीं शिलाम्
5.44.10.e: Struck by the shafts of the ogre, the great monkey was enraged and happened to see a huge,  heavy rock lying beside him on the ground.

5.44.11.t:
तरसा तां समुत्पाट्य चिक्षेप बलवद्भली ।
तां शरैर्दशभिः क्रुद्धस्ताडयामास राक्षसः
5.44.11.e: Powerful Hanuman with all vehemence lifted the rock and hurled it at the giant which he angrily smashed with ten arrows.

5.44.12.t:
विपन्नं कर्म तद्दृष्ट्वा हनुमांश्चण्डविक्रमः ।
सालं विपुलमुत्पाट्य भ्रामयामास वीर्यवान्
5.44.12.e: Hanuman, a strong, powerful and fierce warrior pulled out a sala tree and whirled it. Seeing that his attempt has failed.

5.44.13.t:
भ्रामयन्तं कपिं दृष्ट्वा सालवृक्षं महाबलम् ।
चिक्षेप सुबहून्बाणान्जम्बुमाली महाबलः
5.44.13.e: Gigantic Jambumali seeing the mighty Hanuman whirling the sala tree fired many arrows at him.

w: in the hollow of the chest
5.44.14.t:
सालं चतुर्भिश्चिच्छेद वानरं पञ्चभिर्भुजे ।
उरस्येकेन बाणेन दशभिस्तु स्तनान्तरे
5.44.14.e: He struck the sala tree with four arows, the arm of Hanuman with five arrows, chest with one, the hollow of the chest with ten more arrows.

5.44.16.t:
अतिवेगोऽतिवेगेन भ्रामयित्वा बलोत्कटः ।
परिघं पातयामास जम्बुमालेर्महोरसि
5.44.16.e: Hanuman of immeasurable strength hurled the iron spear after turning it round and round at high speed on the broad chest of Jambumali.

w: with his ornaments reduced to powder
5.44.18.t:
स हतस्सहसा तेन जम्बुमाली महाबलः ।
पपात निहतो भूमौ चूर्णिताङ्गविभूषणः
5.44.18.e: Mighty Jambumali killed  by that blow dropped down dead at once with his ornaments reduced to powder.

5.44.19.t:
जम्बुमालिं च निहतं किङ्करांश्च महाबलान् ।
चुक्रोध रावणश्शुत्वा कोपसंरक्तलोचनः
5.44.19.e: Ravana's eyes became bloodshot in anger when he heard about the death of Jambumali and of the strong army of kinkaras.

w: his eyes red and rolling in anger
5.44.20.t:
स रोषसंवर्तितताम्रलोचनः प्रहस्तपुत्त्रे निहते महाबले ।
अमात्यपुत्त्रानतिवीर्यविक्रमान् समादिदेशाशु निशाचरेश्वरः
5.44.20.e: When the mighty son of Prahasta was killed, infuriated Ravana, his eyes red and rolling, commanded the highly valiant sons of ministers. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये सुन्दरकाण्डे चतुश्चत्वारिंशस्सर्गः।। Thus ends the fortyfourth sarga of Sundarakanda of the holy Ramayana, the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

5.45.1.t:
ततस्ते राक्षसेन्द्रेण चोदिता मन्त्रिणस्सुताः ।
निर्ययुर्भवनात्तस्मात्सप्तसप्तार्चिवर्चसः महाबलपरीवारा धनुष्मन्तो महाबलाः ।
कृतास्त्रास्त्रविदां श्रेष्ठाः परस्परजयैषिणः हेमजालपरिक्षिप्तैर्ध्वजवद्भिः पताकिभिः ।
तोयदस्वननिर्घोषैर्वाजियुक्तैर्महारथैः तप्तकाञ्चनचित्राणि चापान्यमितविक्रमाः ।
विस्फारयन्तस्संहृष्टास्तटित्वन्त इवाम्बुदाः
5.45.1.e: Commanded by Ravana, the seven sons of minister blazing like fire followed by large army of experts in archery, possessing great valour, armed with weapons, being distinguished wielders of weapons, skilled in the use of weapons, who were equally capable of conquering each other sallied forth gladly to fight with Hanuman. They drove chariots yoked with horses which were decked with golden mesh, holding totem staffs (a figure engraved to identify a hero) and flags, neighing like clouds. The valiant heroes were sporting and making sounds like stormy  clouds wielding wonderful bows glittering like molten gold, shining like lightning. As they marched from the palace they looked like  stormy clouds accompanied by lightning.

5.45.5.e: Their mothers and relatives and their friends were struck with grief when they learnt about the kinkaras killed.

5.45.6.e: The barnished golden ornaments worn by them were shining as they brushed shoulders with one another (eager to fight first) to attack Hanuman who stood waiting at the main archway.

w: the rattling of the chariots mixed with the roaring of the warriors
5.45.7.t:
सृजन्तो बाणवृष्टिं ते रथगर्जितनिस्स्वनाः ।
वृष्टिमन्त इवांभोदा विचेरुर्नैऋताम्बुदाः
5.45.7.e: They went roaring with their chariots rattling, sending forth torrents of arrows like the stormy clouds thundering.

w: with those bows in their hands
5.45.10.t:
स तैः क्रीडन्धनुष्मद्भिर्व्योम्नि वीरः प्रकाशते ।
धनुष्मद्भिर्यथा मेघैर्मारुतः प्रभुरम्बरे
5.45.10.e: Sporting in the sky with the giants who held bows in their hands, Hanuman shone like the powerful Windgod sporting in the sky surrrounded by rambling dark clouds.

5.45.11.t:
स कृत्वा निनदं घोरं त्रासयंस्तां महाचमूम् ।
चकार हनुमान्वेगं तेषु रक्षस्सु वीर्यवान्
5.45.11.e: Valiant Hanuman making terrific sound and frightening the army of ogres marched swiftly.

5.45.12.e: The scorcher of enemies, Hanuman hit some ogres with his palm, some with his feet and some with his fist and pierced some with his nails.

5.45.13.t:
प्रममाथोरसा कांश्चिदूरुभ्यामपरान्कपिः ।
केचित्तस्य निनादेन तत्रैव पतिता भुवि
5.45.13.e: The monkey strangled some with his chest and some between his thighs. A few fell down dead on the ground hearing his roaring noise.

w: with broken seats parasols flag staffs
5.45.15.t:
विनेदुर्विस्वरं नागा निपेतुर्भुवि वाजिनः ।
भग्ननीडध्वजच्छत्रैर्भूश्च कीर्णाऽभवद्रथैः
5.45.15.e: The elephants trumpeted discordantly out of fear, the horses fell down on the ground and even the chariots with seats, parasols and flag staffs broken were strewn all over the ground.

5.45.16.t:
स्रवता रुधिरेणाथ स्रवन्त्यो दर्शिताः पथि ।
विविधैश्च स्वरैर्लङ्का ननाद विकृतं तदा
5.45.16.e: Streams of blood flowed and Lanka was filled with many kinds of horrifying sounds of cries.

w: the ogres who were old and grew stronger
5.45.17.t:
स तान्प्रवृद्धान्विनिहत्य राक्षसान् महाबलश्चण्डपराक्रमः कपिः ।
युयुत्सुरन्यैः पुनरेव राक्षसै स्तमेव वीरोऽभिजगाम तोरणम्
5.45.17.e: Having killed the ogres who were old and strong, the valiant and mighty Hanuman, wishing to slay the other ogres advanced towards the archway. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये सुन्दरकाण्डे पञ्चचत्वारिंशस्सर्गः।। Thus ends the fortyfifth sarga of Sundarakanda of the holy Ramayana, the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

w: along with horses chariots and elphants
5.46.4.e: "O Army generals march with a large, strong army with horses, chariots and elephants and punish the vanara.

w: that which is not against time and space
5.46.5.t:
यत्नैश्च खलु भाव्यं स्यात्तमासाद्य वनालयम् ।
कर्म चापि समाधेयं देशकालाविरोधिनम्
5.46.5.e: "Go to that forestdweller and make all efforts to impose on him punishment appropriate to time and place (keeping in view the harm he has done).

5.46.6.t:
न ह्यहं तं कपिं मन्ये कर्मणा प्रतितर्कयन् ।
सर्वथा तन्महद्भूतं महाबलपरिग्रहम्
5.46.6.e: "Judging again and again from all actions, I do not think he is an ordinary monkey. He is a being endowed with great strength.

5.46.7.t:
भवेदिन्द्रेण वा सृष्टमस्मदर्थं तपोबलात् ।
सनागयक्षगन्धर्वा देवासुरमहर्षयः युष्माभिस्सहितैस्सर्वैर्मया सह विनिर्जिताः ।
तैरवश्यं विधातव्यं व्यलीकं किञ्चिदेव नः तदेव नात्र सन्देहः प्रसह्य परिगृह्यताम् ।
नावमान्यो भवद्भिश्च हरिर्धीरपराक्रमः
5.46.7.e: "To me it appears he is created by Indra with his ascetic power (for punishing us). I have subdued nagas, yakshas, gandharvas and even gods, asuras and ascetics with your help. So you should certainly bring him here without doing any harm. Capture the monkey forcibly. Do not insult that mighty monkey.

w: ability to change form at will.
5.46.10.t:
दृष्टा हि हरयः पूर्वं मया विपुलविक्रमाः ।
वाली च सहसुग्रीवो जाम्बवांश्च महाबलः नीलस्सेनापतिश्चैव ये चान्ये द्विविदादयः ।
नैवं तेषां गतिर्भीमा न तेजो न पराक्रमः न मतिर्न बलोत्साहौ न रूपपरिकल्पनम् ।
5.46.10.e: "Earlier I have seen monkeys of immense prowess, like Vali and Sugriva as well as Jambavan, the bear. Also I have seen the army general, Nila, Dvivida and others. They do not have such tremendous splendour or movement valour, intellect and strength and energy. They did not have such ability to change form at their will.

5.46.12.t: महत्सत्त्वमिदं ज्ञेयं कपिरूपं व्यवस्थितम् प्रयत्नं महदास्थाय क्रियतामस्य निग्रहः ।
5.46.12.e: "It should be understood that he has taken the form of a monkey. You have to put in extraordinary effort to capture him by acting in a suitable manner.

5.46.13.t: कामं लोकास्त्रयस्सेन्द्रास्ससुरासुरमानवाः भवतामग्रतः स्थातुं न पर्याप्ता रणाजिरे ।
5.46.13.e: "Even Indra, suras, asuras and humans and the three worlds together are incompetent to stand before you in a battlefield.

5.46.15.t:
ते स्वामिवचनं सर्वे प्रतिगृह्य महौजसः समुत्पेतुर्महावेगा हुताशसमतेजसः ।
रथैर्मत्तैश्च मातङ्गैर्वाजिभिश्च महाजवैः शस्त्रैश्च विविधैस्तीक्ष्णैस्सर्वैश्चोपचिता बलैः ।
5.46.15.e: Taking King's order, the strong and swift warriors, resplendent as the flame of sacrificial fire sallied forth with their army on chariots, on the back of rutting elephants,  some on swift horses equipped with sharp weapons of many kinds.

w: shining like the Sungod with his own effulgence
5.46.17.t:
ततस्तं ददृशुर्वीरा दीप्यमानं महाकपिम् रश्मिमन्तमिवोद्यन्तं स्वतेजोरश्मिमालिनम् ।
तोरणस्थं महोत्साहं महासत्त्वं महाबलम्
5.46.17.e: The heroic giants caught sight of the vanara, who was blazing  encircled as though he was by the rays of his own glory, looking like the rising Sun. He was endowed with extraordinary agility, intelligence, and tremendous strength standing, waiting at the archway.

5.46.19.t:
महामतिं महावेगं महाकायं महाबलम् ।
तं समीक्ष्यैव ते सर्वे दिक्षु सर्वास्ववस्थिताः तै स्तै: प्रहरणैर्भीमैरभिपेतुस्ततस्ततः ।
5.46.19.e: Having observed the tremendous strength, intelligence and swiftness in action of Hanuman, the generals of the army positioned at all directions and assailed him with dreadful weapons.

w: steel shafts with polished yellow tips (of gold)
5.46.20.t: तस्य पञ्चायसास्तीक्ष्णाश्शिताः पीतमुखाश्शराः शिरस्युत्पलपत्राभा दुर्धरेण निपातिताः ।
5.46.20.e: Durdhara pierced into the head of Hanuman with five sharp arrows and polished steel shafts with yellow tips (gold) shining like red lotus petals. They were like petals of lilies thrown on the head of Hanuman (causing no pain).

5.46.22.t: ततस्तु दुर्धरो वीरस्सरथस्सज्यकार्मुकः किरन् शरशतैस्तीक्ष्णैरभिपेदे महाबलः ।
5.46.22.e: Then the powerful, hero, Durdhara, mounted on his chariot, fastened his bowstring and hit Hanuman with hundreds of sharp arrows.

w: at the end of the rainy season
5.46.23.t: स कपिर्वारयामास तं व्योम्नि शरवर्षिणम् वृष्टिमन्तं पयोदान्ते पयोदमिव मारुतः ।
5.46.23.e: The great monkey kept away the showering arrows like the wind prevents raincloud from showering rain drops at the end of monsoon.

5.46.24.t: अर्ध्यमानस्ततस्तेन दुर्धरेणानिलात्मजः चकार कदनं भूयो व्यवर्धत च वेगवान् ।
5.46.24.e: When the son of the Windgod was attacked by Durdhara, he again grew in size

5.46.25.t: स दूरं सहसोत्पत्य दुर्धरस्य रथे हरिः निपपात महावेगो विद्युद्राशिर्गिराविव ।
5.46.25.e: Hanuman suddenly leaped far off into the air at high speed and fell on Durdhara's chariot just like a thunderous lightning falls on a mountain.

w: with its axle and wooden frame (to which the yoke is fixed) broken
5.46.26.t: ततस्स मथिताष्टाश्वं रथं भग्नाक्षकूबरम् विहाय न्यपतद्भूमौ दुर्धरस्त्यक्तजीवितः ।
5.46.26.e: Having lost his chariot, the horses yoked to it killed, its axle and pole broken to pieces, Durdhara fell down dead from the chariot.

5.46.27.t: तं विरूपाक्षयूपाक्षौ दृष्ट्वा निपतितं भुवि सञ्जातरोषौ दुर्धर्षावुत्पेतुररिन्दमौ ।
5.46.27.e: Seeing the body of Durdhara fallen on the ground, enraged Virupaksha and Yupaksha, the unassailable crushers of enemies leaped towards him.

5.46.28.t: स ताभ्यां सहसोत्पत्य विष्ठितो विमलेऽम्बरे मुद्गराभ्यां महाबाहुर्वक्षस्यभिहतः कपिः ।
5.46.28.e: As the strongarmed vanara stood stationed in the clear white sky both the generals leaped into the sky and hit him all of a sudden with two iron hammers.

w: of those two who were swift in action
5.46.29.t: तयोर्वेगवतोर्वेगं विनिहत्य महाबलः निपपात पुनर्भूमौ सुपर्णसमविक्रमः ।
5.46.29.e: Powerful Hanuman, an equal to Garuda in valour fell down while resisting the swift generals.

w: was shining like the rising Sun
5.46.34.t: स ताभ्यां विक्षतैर्गात्रैरसृग्दिग्धतनूरुहः अभवद्वानरः क्रुद्धो बालसूर्यसमप्रभः ।
5.46.34.e: Attacked by both the generals, the fur on the vanara's body was smeared with blood from his wounded limbs, shining like the rising Sun smeared with blood became furious.

5.46.36.t: ततस्तेष्ववसन्नेषु सेनापतिषु पञ्चसु बलं तदवशेषं च नाशयामास वानरः ।
5.46.36.e: When the five army chiefs were killed, Hanuman began to destoy the remaining army force.

5.46.37.t: अश्वैरश्वान् गजैर्नागान् योधैर्योधान् रथैरथान् स कपिर्नाशयामास सहस्राक्ष इवासुरान् ।
5.46.37.e: The vanara pitted horses against horses, elephants against elephants, warriors against warriors and chariots against chariots as Indra destroyed demons.

5.46.39.t:
ततः कपिस्तान्ध्वजिनीपतीन् रणे निहत्य वीरान्सबलान्सवाहनान् ।
समीक्ष्य वीरः परिगृह्य तोरणं कृतक्षणः काल इव प्रजाक्षये
5.46.39.e: Then the heroic monkey having killed the army generals and their army and destroyed their vehicles in war came back to the archway after reviewing and stood like the timespirit bent upon the destruction of humanity. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये सुन्दरकाण्डे षट्चत्वारिंशस्सर्गः।। Thus ends the fortysixth sarga of Sundarakanda of the holy Ramayana, the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

5.47.1.t:
सेनापतीन्पञ्च स तु प्रमापितान् हनूमता सानुचरान्सवाहनान् ।
समीक्ष्य राजा समरोद्धतोन्मुखं कुमारमक्षं प्रसमैक्षताग्रतः
5.47.1.e: Hearing the sad news of death of the five army generals including their followers and destruction of their vehicles, King (Ravana) gave a suggestive look at prince Aksha who was inclined to fight the war.

w: spurred by the glance of the king
holding a marvellous bow inlaid with gold
5.47.2.t:
स तस्य दृष्ट्यर्पणसम्प्रचोदितः प्रतापवान्काञ्चनचित्रकार्मुकः ।
समुत्पपाताथ सदस्युदीरितो द्विजातिमुख्यैर्हविषेव पावकः
5.47.2.e: Spurred by the mere glance of Ravana, the glorious Aksha with his wonderful bow inlaid with gold sprang up from the royal assembly just as flame rises from firesanctuary when oblations are poured in by reputed brahmins.

w: glittering like the stretch of pure gold
5.47.3.t:
ततो महद्बालदिवाकरप्रभं प्रतप्तजाम्बूनदजालसन्ततम् ।
रथं समास्थाय ययौ स वीर्यवान्महाहरिं तं प्रति नैरृतर्षभः
5.47.3.e: Ascending a glittering chariot inlaid with pure gold Aksha, the courageous bull among giants looking splendid like the rising Sun, marched forth towards the great vanara.

w: gained by the austerities of high order
overlaid with the pure gold armour
with flag staff studded with precious gems
with eight choice horses endowed with the speed of mind
5.47.4.t:
ततस्तपस्सङ्ग्रहसञ्चयार्जितं प्रतप्तजाम्बूनदजालशोभितम् ।
पताकिनं रत्नविभूषितध्वजं मनोजवाष्टाश्ववरैः सुयोजितम्
5.47.4.e: The chariot was (strong as it was) gained by his austerities of high order. It was overlaid with pure gold armour, fixed with flags, and staff, studded with precious gems, yoked to the best of eight horses and endowed with the speed of mind.

w: that which can fly in air
javelins and clubs placed in right place in order.
5.47.5.t:
सुरासुराधृष्यमसङ्गचारिणं रविप्रभं व्योमचरं समाहितम् ।
सतूणमष्टासिनिबद्धबन्धुरं यथाक्रमावेशितशक्तितोमरम्
5.47.5.e: (The chariot) was unassailable to suras or asuras.It moved without touching the ground, it could fly in air and had the splendour of the Sun. It was equipped readily with quivers, eight swords, javelins and clubs placed in right order.

w: equipped with all weapons bows and shields etc
5.47.6.t:
विराजमानं प्रतिपूर्णवस्तुना सहेमदाम्ना शशिसूर्यवर्चसा ।
दिवाकराभं रथमास्थितस्ततस्स निर्जगामामरतुल्यविक्रमः
5.47.6.e: Prince Aksha, whose courage was equal to that of gods, shone like the Sun. He ascended the splendid chariot decked with golden garlands shining like Sun and Moon, equipped with all weapons, bows and shields etc, he went out.

w: with the sounds of horses elephants and chariot
5.47.7.t:
स पूरयन्खं च महीं च साचलां तुरङ्गमातङ्गमहारथस्वनैः ।
बलैस्समेतैस्सहि तोरणस्थितं समर्थमासीनमुपागमत्कपिम्
5.47.7.e: Seated on the chariot he (Aksha) sallied forth along with the army filling the entire earth and mountains with the sounds of horses, elephants and rumblings of big chariots and reached the portal where the great vanara stood.

w: who had eyes like that of a lion
at the time of destruction of the universe
like the cosmic fire at the time of dissolution
5.47.8.t:
स तं समासाद्य हरिं हरीक्षणो युगान्तकालाग्निमिव प्रजाक्षये ।
अवस्थितं विस्मितजातसम्भ्रम स्समैक्षताक्षो बहुमानचक्षुषा
5.47.8.e: The lioneyed Aksha saw the vanara who appeared like the cosmic fire at the time of dissolution of the universe. The prince was astonished and struck with awe (at the majestic form of the Vanara) and looked at him with great  respect.

5.47.10.t:
स जातमन्युः प्रसमीक्ष्य विक्रमं स्थिरं स्थिरस्सम्यति दुर्निवारणम् ।
समाहितात्मा हनुमन्तमाहवे प्रचोदयामास शरैस्त्रिभि श्शितैः
5.47.10.e: Knowing that it is difficult to win Hanuman who was steady and of irresistible valour Aksha was angry. Remaining steady, with full attention, he provoked the vanara to fight and released three sharp arrows.

w: who was intent to conquer the enemy
with bow and arrows in hand
5.47.11.t:
ततः कपिं तं प्रसमीक्ष्य गर्वितं जितश्रमं शत्रुपराजयोर्जितम् ।
अवैक्षताक्षस्समुदीर्णमानसस्सबाणपाणिः प्रगृहीतकार्मुकः
5.47.11.e: Then Aksha contempuously looked at Hanuman who had conquered his fatigue and was determined to defeat the enemy. Holding in his hands his bow and arrows proudly, he reflected.

5.47.13.t:
ररास भूमिर्न तताप भानुमा न्वनौ न वायुः प्रचाचल चाचलः ।
कपेः कुमारस्य च वीक्ष्य संयुगं ननाद च द्यौरुदधिश्च चुक्षुभे
5.47.13.e: Witnessing the fight between Hanuman and Prince Aksha, even the earth shrieked in agony, the Sun became dim, the wind stopped blowing, mountains were shaken, the sky thundered and even the ocean was agitated.

w: good at targeting and releasing with due concentration
on the head of the vanara
5.47.14.e: Heroic Aksha, who was good at targeting correctly, with due  concentration struck the vanara on his head with three goldenshafted, winged arrows with feathers smeared with poison which resembled serpents.

w: eyes wetted with red blood flowing down
5.47.15.t:
स तै श्शरैर्मूर्ध्नि समं निपातितैः क्षरन्नसृग्दिग्धविवृत्तलोचनः ।
नवोदितादित्यनिभ श्शरांशुमान् व्यराजतादित्य इवांशुमालिकः
5.47.15.e: With the three arrows shot on his forehead simultaneously his eyes were drenched with flowing blood and with arrows shining like rays he appeared like the rising Sun, garlanded by glowing rays.

w: esteemed minister of the copperyeyed Sugriva
5.47.16.t:
ततस्स पिङ्गाधिपमन्त्रिसत्तमः समीक्ष्य तं राजवरात्मजं रणे ।
उदग्रचित्रायुधचित्रकार्मुकं जहर्ष चापूर्यत चाहवोन्मुखः
5.47.16.e: Hanuman, the esteemed minister of the copperyeyed Sugriva observed the prince holding manifold splendid weapons. He rejoiced, grew in size ready to fight, making the necessary prepararions (taking the required position).

w: Sun shining on the peak of mount Mandara
with the fiery rays emerging from the fiery eyes
5.47.17.t:
स मन्दराग्रस्थ इवांशुमालिको विवृद्धकोपो बलवीर्यसंयुतः ।
कुमारमक्षं सबलं सवाहनं ददाह नेत्राग्निमरीचिभिस्तदा
5.47.17.e: Huge Hanuman, endowed with strength and valour looked  like the rising Sun on the peak of mount Mandara. He looked at prince Aksha and his army as well as his vehicles as though he was burning them with the rays emerging from his fiery eyes.

w: endowed with a quiver and a wonderful bow
5.47.18.t:
ततस्स बाणासनचित्रकार्मुक श्शरप्रवर्षो युधि राक्षसाम्बुदः ।
शरान्मुमोचाशु हरीश्वराचले वलाहको वृष्टिमिवाचलोत्तमे
5.47.18.e: Aksha, with his wonderful quiver and bow, began to rain rapidly a shower of arrows in the battle, on the mountainlike monkeylord just as a cloud rains on a mountain.

w: endowed with excessive splendour power and energy
who had valour equal to a cloud
5.47.19.t:
ततः कपिस्तं रणचण्डविक्रमं विवृद्धतेजोबलवीर्यसंयुतम् ।
कुमारमक्षं प्रसमीक्ष्य संयुगे ननाद हर्षाद् घनतुल्यविक्रमम्
5.47.19.e: Then Hanuman saw prince Aksha, endowed with excessive splendour, power and energy advancing in a fierce manner like a cloud in the battle. Then Hanuman happy (to see the heroic prince) roared like a clap of thunder.

w: puffed with the pride of his valour
5.47.20.t:
स बालभावाद्युधि वीर्यदर्पितः प्रवृद्धमन्युः क्षतजोपमेक्षणः ।
समाससादाप्रतिमं कपिं रणे गजो महाकूपमिवावृतं तृणैः
5.47.20.e: Young Aksha, proud of his valour with eyes bloodshot in anger rushed towards the matchless Hanuman, just as an elephant would approach a huge pitfall covered with grass.

w: looking dreadful stretching his arms and thighs
5.47.21.t:
स तेन बाणैः प्रसभं निपातितैश्चकार नादं घननादनिस्स्वनः ।
समुत्पपाताशु नभस्स मारुतिर्भुजोरुविक्षेपणघोरदर्शनः
5.47.21.e: Struck by the arrows released by prince Aksha, Hanuman roared violently like a thundering cloud and leaped into the sky  putting up a fierce appearance, stretching his arms and thighs.

w: formost among the best warriors fighting on a chariot
5.47.22.t:
समुत्पतन्तं समभिद्रवद्बली स राक्षसानां प्रवरः प्रतापवान् ।
रथी रथिश्रेष्ठतमः किरन्शरैः पयोधरश्शैलमिवाश्मवृष्टिभिः
5.47.22.e: That mighty and brave leader of the ogres, foremost among the best of chariot-warriors, poured down a rain of stones as a cloud pours rain.

w: one who had speed of mind
while allowing them to be released
5.47.23.t:
स तान्शरांस्तस्य हरिर्विमोक्षयंश्चचार वीरः पथि वायुसेविते ।
शरान्तरे मारुतवद्विनिष्पतन्मनोजवस्संयति चण्डविक्रमः
5.47.23.e: Dodging like the wind  between the arrows and also escaping the arrows Hanuman, who was swift in movement like the mind, was seen exhibiting his terrific valour in the battle while he moved in the sky.

w: of the hero who knows all means of fighting
5.47.26.t:
अबालवद्बालदिवाकरप्रभः करोत्ययं कर्म महन्महाबलः ।
न चास्य सर्वाहवकर्मशोभिनः प्रमापणे मे मतिरत्र जायते
5.47.26.e: 'He (Aksha) is like the radiant, rising Sun with extraordinary might. He is accomplishing great deeds unlike young warriors of his age and is exhibiting a magnificent feat. He knows all means of fighting. I do not feel like cutting him to size. My mind does not allow me to kill this boy.

w: on account of his excellent actions
5.47.27.t:
अयं महात्मा च महांश्च वीर्यत स्समाहितश्चातिसहश्च संयुगे ।
असंशयं कर्मगुणोदयादयं सनागयक्षैर्मुनिभिश्च पूजितः
5.47.27.e: 'He is a great self. His valour is also admirable. He is focused in battle and highly tolerant. There is no doubt that on account of his excellence  even nagas, yakshas and sages offer salutations to him.

5.47.29.t:
न खल्वयं नाभिभवेदुपेक्षितः पराक्रमो ह्यस्य रणे विवर्धते ।
प्रमापणं त्वेव ममाद्य रोचते न वर्धमानोऽग्निरुपेक्षितुं क्षमः
5.47.29.e: If I ignore him now, he would get the better of me (I have to consider his challenge seriously). His valour in the battle is growing. It is proper to subdue him now. A spreading fire cannot be neglected.

w: and his own course of action
5.47.30.t:
इति प्रवेगं तु परस्य चिन्तयन्स्वकर्मयोगं च विधाय वीर्यवान् ।
चकार वेगं तु महाबलस्तदा मतिं च चक्रेऽस्य वधे महाकपिः
5.47.30.e: Reflecting on the power of the enemy, the mighty and valiant vanara thought of his own course of action. Hanuman made up his mind to kill the enemy and increased his speed.

w: minister of the copperyeyed monkeylord destroyed
wooden frame (to which the yoke is fixed) disjointed
5.47.32.t:
ततस्तलेनाभिहतो महारथ स्स तस्य पिङ्गाधिपमन्त्रिनिर्जितः ।
प्रभग्ननीडः परिमुक्तकूबरः पपात भूमौ हतवाजिरम्बरात्
5.47.32.e: Then hit by Hanuman with his palm, the minister of the copperyeyed Sugriva, the huge chariot seat of Aksha was broken, the wooden frame of the yoke was disjointed, horses were  slain and the great chariot fell down from the sky.

5.47.33.t:
स तं परित्यज्य महारथो रथं सकार्मुकः खङ्गधरः खमुत्पतन् ।
तपोऽभियोगादृषिरुग्रवीर्यवान्विहाय देहं मरुतामिवालयम्
5.47.33.e: (Aksha) the great charioteer abandoned the chariot, held a sword and a bow, and flew up to the region of the sky with his fierce power just as a sage with his fearsome ascetic power ascends to heaven, leaving his body.

w: in the flying abode of Garuda Wind and the Siddhas
5.47.34.t:
ततः कपिस्तं विचरन्तमम्बरे पतत्रिराजानिलसिद्धसेविते ।
समेत्य तं मारुततुल्यविक्रमः क्रमेण जग्राह स पादयोर्दृढम्
5.47.34.e: Thereupon Hanuman with the prowess that was equal to wind, approaching the sky firmly caught hold of the legs of Aksha flying into the abode of Garuda, the Windgod and the Siddhas.

w: one who had the valour of  his father
5.47.35.t:
स तं समाविध्य सहस्रशः कपिर्महोरगं गृह्य इवाण्डजेश्वरः ।
मुमोच वेगात्पितृतुल्यविक्रमो महीतले संयति वानरोत्तमः
5.47.35.e: Hanuman, the foremost of the vanaras who was equal to his father in valour, seized him just as Garuda, the lord of birds, would seize a great serpent. And spinning him round speedily a thousand times and hitting him, dropped him on the earth.

w: with arms thighs hips and neck mangled
with his bones and eyes protruded
by the son of the Windgod
5.47.36.t:
स भग्नबाहूरुकटीशिरोधरः क्षरन्नसृङिनर्मथितास्थिलोचनः ।
सम्भग्नसन्धि: प्रविकीर्णबन्धनो हतः क्षितौ वायुसुतेन राक्षसः
5.47.36.e: Hit by Hanuman, the ogre's arms, thighs, hips and neck broken, bones rendered to fragments, eyes protruded, joints disjointed, tendons strewn he was thrown down on the earth dripping blood.

w: by those observants of great vows
5.47.37.t:
महाकपिर्भूमितले निपीड्य तं चकार रक्षोधिपतेर्महद्भयम् ।
महर्षिभिश्चक्रचरैर्महाव्रतै स्समेत्य भूतैश्च सयक्षपन्नगैः सुरैश्च सेन्द्रैर्भृशजातविस्मयै र्हते कुमारे स कपिर्निरीक्षितः ।
5.47.37.e: When the great vanara dashed Aksha down on to the earth, the king of demons was struck with terror. The great sages who go round the planets, great seers who were observants of vows, yakshas, panagas, suras including Indra all beings collected together and looked at the vanara with awe.

5.48.1.t:
ततस्तु रक्षोधिपतिर्महात्मा हनूमताक्षे निहते कुमारे ।
मनस्समाधाय सदेवकल्पं समादिदेशेन्द्रजितं सरोषः
5.48.1.e: Thereafter the great demon king, mighty angry at the death of Aksha in the hands of Hanuman, controlled his feeling and ordered Indrajit who was like a godhead.

w: among the experts in the use of weapons
propitiating grand father Brahma acquired many missiles.
5.48.2.t:
त्वमस्त्रविच्छस्त्रविदां वरिष्ठस्सुरासुराणामपि शोकदाता ।
सुरेषु सेन्द्रेषु च दृष्टकर्मा पितामहाराधनसञ्चितास्त्रः
5.48.2.e: "You are an expert in wielding astras (missiles) and foremost among the wielders of weapons. You are highly efficient. You have brought grief even to suras and asuras. You are a warrior of proven ability demonstrated in your war against the gods including Indra. By propitiating, (through penance), grandfather Brahma you have acquired many missiles.

5.48.3.t:
तवास्त्रबलमासाद्य ससुराः समरुद्गणाः ।
न शेकुस्समरे स्थातुं सुरेश्वरसमाश्रिताः
5.48.3.e: "None could face you in war including Indra, Maruts and gods because of your skill and the power of your astras.

w: protected by the strength of your arms
aware of the proper place and time of action.
5.48.4.t:
न कश्चित्त्रिषु लोकेषु संयुगेन गतश्रमः ।
भुजवीर्याभिगुप्तश्च तपसा चाभिरक्षितः देशकालविभागज्ञस्त्वमेव मतिसत्तमः ।
5.48.4.e: "Excepting you there is none who has not experienced fatigue in war in the three worlds. You alone are intelligent in fighting. You are protected by the strength of your arms and power of austerity. You are aware of the proper place and time of action.

5.48.7.t:
निहताः किङ्करास्सर्वे जम्बुमाली च राक्षसः ।
अमात्यपुत्रा वीराश्च पञ्च सेनाग्रयायिनः बलानि सुसमृद्धानि साश्वनागरथानि च ।
5.48.7.e: "All the kinkaras , Jambumali, the heroic demons, sons of the ministers and five army generals were slain. Battalions of well-equipped army including horses, elephants and chariots were also destroyed.

5.48.8.t: सहोदरस्ते दयितः कुमारोऽक्षश्च सूदितः न हि तेष्वेव मे सारो यस्त्वय्यरिनिषूदन ।
5.48.8.e: "Your dear young brother Aksha is killed. O scourage of enemies I do not have the faith in them as I have in you.

w: in keeping with your own strength
5.48.9.t:
इदं हि दृष्ट्वा मतिमन्महद्बलं कपेः प्रभावं च पराक्रमं च ।
त्वमात्मनश्चापि समीक्ष्य सारं कुरुष्व वेगं स्वबलानुरूपम्
5.48.9.e: "O intelligent warrior measure the  strength, power and valour of the monkey and  your own strength carefully. Exercise your own strength and speed accordingly.

5.48.10.t:
बलावमर्थस्तयि सन्निकृष्टे यथा गते शाम्यति शान्तशत्रौ ।
तथा समीक्ष्यात्मबलं परं च समारभस्वास्त्रविदां वरिष्ठ
5.48.10.e: "O  warrior of extraordinary merit among the wielders of astras  asses your strength approach the enemy in a manner by which he is subdued without causing further destruction to our army. Carefully measure your own strength and your enemy's  before you start fighting.

w: without being destroyed in the middle
5.48.12.t:
तमेवमर्थं प्रसमीक्ष्य सम्यक् स्वकर्मसाम्याद्धि समाहितात्मा ।
स्मरंश्च दिव्यं धनुषोऽस्त्रवीर्यं व्रजाक्षतं कर्म समारभस्व
5.48.12.e: "Assess the situation properly. You are a person of sound judgement. You are a master in weaponry. Recollect the strength of your bow and divine astras and march forward with a singleminded attention. Act in a manner that does not bring your doom.

5.48.13.t:
न खल्वियं मतिश्श्रेष्ठा यत्त्वां सम्प्रेषयाम्यहम् ।
इयं च राजधर्माणां क्षत्रियस्य मतिर्मता
5.48.13.e: "I am reluctant to send you to war in the circumstances. But you are the best choice for me. However, certainly this is the duty of a kshatriya who follows the science of polity. Hence I am sending you.

w: by his own kith and kin
5.48.16.t:
ततस्तै स्स्वगणैरिष्टैरिन्द्रजित् प्रतिपूजितः ।
युद्धोद्धतः कृतोत्साहस्सङ्ग्रामं प्रत्यपद्यत
5.48.16.e: Having been honoured by his own kith and kin who loved him, Indrajit rushed forth for war with martial vigour.

5.48.19.t:
स रथी धन्विनां श्रेष्ठः शस्त्रज्ञोस्त्रविदां वरः ।
रथेनाभिययौ क्षिप्रं हनुमान्यत्र सोऽभवत्
5.48.19.e: Mounted on the chariot, Indrajit, the best in archery and an expert in weaponry went quickly to the place where that great Hanuman was stationed.

w: those who go round the orbits
5.48.23.t:
समागतास्तत्र तु नागयक्षा महर्षयश्चक्रचराश्च सिद्धाः ।
नभस्समावृत्य च पक्षिसङ्घा विनेदुरुच्चैः परमप्रहृष्टाः
5.48.23.e: (To see the combat) the Nagas, Yakshas, seers and Siddhas who move round the heavenly orbits assembled in the sky. The birds collected  in flocks in the sky and screeched loudly and happily.

5.48.24.t:
आयान्तं सरथं दृष्ट्वा तूर्णमिन्द्रजितं कपिः ।
विननाद महानादं व्यवर्धत च वेगवान्
5.48.24.e: Hanuman of very high speed enlarged his body and roared, perceiving Indrajit's chariot coming swiftly.

5.48.25.e: Indrajit on his part sat in his divine chariot holding a wonderful bow and in a lightning speed twanged it.

5.48.26.t:
ततस्समेतावतितीक्ष्णवेगौ महाबलौ तौ रणनिर्विशङ्कौ ।
कपिश्च रक्षोधिपतेस्तनूजः सुरासुरेन्द्राविव बद्धवैरौ
5.48.26.e: Then the son of the demon king and Hanuman, both very fast in speed, mighty and powerful, fearless in war and like sura and asura closed in upon each other.

5.48.27.t:
स तस्य वीरस्य महारथस्य धनुष्मतः संयति सम्मतस्य ।
शरप्रवेगं व्यहनत्प्रवृद्ध श्चचार मार्गे पितुरप्रमेयः
5.48.27.e: Hanuman of immeasurable strength heaved himself to a huge proprtion and went moving on the path of his father (windgod) rendering useless the extraordinary speed of the arrows of Indrajit, who was great in chariot warfare, and an efficient archer.

w: beating sound of mrudangas bheris and patahas
5.48.29.t:
ततस्तु तत्स्यन्दननिस्स्वनं च मृदङ्गभेरीपटहस्वनं च ।
विकृष्यमाणस्य च कार्मुकस्य निशम्य घोषं पुनरुत्पपात
5.48.29.e: Thereupon, hearing the rumbling of the chariot, the sounds of mrudangas, bheris, and patahas drawing towards him, and percieving the loud twang of the bow (of Indrajit) Hanuman sprang up again.

5.48.30.e: The great tawny monkey moved quickly between spaces of arrows that were aimed at him rendering hosts of Indrajit's targets futile.

w: unable to bear with each other
5.48.33.t:
हनुमतो वेद न राक्षसोऽन्तरं न मारुतिस्तस्य महात्मनोऽन्तरम् ।
परस्परं निर्विषहौ बभूवतुः समेत्य तौ देवसमानविक्रमौ
5.48.33.e: The demon did not find a way to hit Hanuman. Maruti also found no opportunity to hit great Indrajit. Both of them being equal to gods in valour became too much to each other in war. (Both of them moved at meteoric speed making it difficult to aim at the enemy.)

w: the great warrior entered a meditative mood with great concentration
5.48.34.t:
ततस्तु लक्ष्ये स विहन्यमाने शरेष्वमोघेषु च संपतत्सु ।
जगाम चिन्तां महतीं महात्मा समाधिसंयोगसमाहितात्मा
5.48.34.e: Indrajit's infallible arrows missed Hanuman. Then the great warrior became perplexed and started thinking seriously within himself entering into a reflective mood.

5.48.35.t:
ततो मतिं राक्षसराजसूनु श्चकार तस्मिन् हरिवीरमुख्ये ।
अवध्यतां तस्य कपेस्समीक्ष्य कथं निगच्छेदिति निग्रहार्थम्
5.48.35.e: Then Indrajit, son of the demon king, thinking that a vanara should not be killed started considering other means of catching hm.

5.48.36.t:
ततः पैतामहं वीरः सोऽस्त्रमस्त्रविदां वरः ।
संदधे सुमहत्तेजा: तं हरिप्रवरं प्रति
5.48.36.e: Then the heroic master of weapons, an excellent and glorious warrior directed the  Brahmastram towards the foremost of monkeys.

5.48.39.t:
ततोऽथ बुद्ध्वा स तदस्त्रबन्धं प्रभोः प्रभावाद्विगतात्मवेगः ।
पितामहानुग्रहमात्मनश्च विचिन्तयामास हरिप्रवीरः
5.48.39.e: The monkey leader realised that his speed was arrested by the power of the lord Brahma, by the strength of the bond of Brahmastram. He then recalled lord Brahma's boon to him.

5.48.40.e: Hanuman realised that it was by invoking creator Brahma and applying the mantra that he was caught by Brahmastram. On that occasion he started thinking of the boon given to him  by Grandsire Brahma :

w: the power of liberation from bondage
5.48.42.t:
स वीर्यमस्त्रस्य कपिर्विचार्य पितामहानुग्रहमात्मनश्च ।
विमोक्षशक्तिं परिचिन्तयित्वा पितामहाज्ञामनुवर्तते स्म
5.48.42.e: Reflecting within himself about the power of the astra, Hanuman recalled Braham's favour to him. He recalled his own power to liberate himself from the Brahmastra and resolved to abide by the order of Brahma.

w: will have the opportunity to see
5.48.44.t:
ग्रहणे चापि रक्षोभिर्महन्मे गुणदर्शनम् ।
राक्षसेन्द्रेण संवादस्तस्माद्गृह्णन्तु मां परे
5.48.44.e: 'If I am caught by the demon I will have the opportunity to see the demon lord. Therefore, let me be caught by my enemies'.

5.48.46.t:
ततस्तं राक्षसा दृष्ट्वा निर्विचेष्टमरिंदमम् ।
बबन्धुश्शणवल्कैश्च द्रुमचीरैश्च संहतैः
5.48.46.e: Then the ogres had Hanuman, the subduer of enemies, who made no effort to move, bound with hemp rope and bark robes.

5.48.47.t:
स रोचयामास परैश्च बन्धनं प्रसह्य वीरैरभिनिग्रहं च ।
कौतूहलान्मां यदि राक्षसेन्द्रो द्रष्टुं व्यवस्येदिति निश्चितार्थः
5.48.47.e: Bound by the enemy warriors, Hanuman, decided to bear all humiliations, thinking, 'May be the demon king might come to see me out of curiosity if he is so disposed'.

5.48.48.t:
स बद्धस्तेन वल्केन विमुक्तोऽस्त्रेण वीर्यवान् ।
अस्त्रबन्धः स चान्यं हि न बन्धमनुवर्तते
5.48.48.e: On being bound by bark ropes Hanuman was set free from the bond of Brahmastra, since  the bondage of Brahmastra does not tolerate another ordinary bondage.

5.48.49.t:
अथेन्द्रजित्तु द्रुमचीरबद्धं विचार्य वीरः कपिसत्तमं तम् ।
विमुक्तमस्त्रेण जगाम चिन्तां नान्येन बद्धो ह्यनुवर्ततेऽस्त्रम्
5.48.49.e: Then the heroic Indrajit coming to know that the foremost of the monkeys bound by bark ropes was released from the bondage of Brahmastra, thought, 'indeed the divine weapon does not tolerate other bonds, so the vanara is released'.

5.48.52.t:
हन्यमानस्ततः क्रूरै राक्षसैः काष्ठमुष्टिभिः ।
समीपं राक्षसेन्द्रस्य प्राकृष्यत स वानरः
5.48.52.e: The cruel ogres hit Hanuman with sticks and fists and dragged him to the presence of the demon lord.

5.48.53.t:
अथेन्द्रजित्तं प्रसमीक्ष्य मुक्तमस्त्रेण बद्धं द्रुमचीरसूत्रैः ।
न्यदर्शयत्तत्र महाबलं तं हरिप्रवीरं सगणाय राज्ञे
5.48.53.e: Then Indarjit, seeing the powerful Hanuman, the foremost of monkeys who was released from the Brahmastra, still bound by bark ropes, presented him to the ogres and their master in the royal assembly.

5.48.54.t:
तं मत्तमिव मातङ्गं बद्धं कपिवरोत्तमम् ।
राक्षसा राक्षसेन्द्राय रावणाय न्यवेदयन्
5.48.54.e: The ogres presented the best of monkeys, Hanuman looking like an elephant in rut to Ravana, the demon king.

5.48.55.t:
कोऽयं कस्य कुतोवात्र किं कार्यं को व्यपाश्रयः ।
इति राक्षसवीराणां तत्र सञ्जज्ञिरे कथाः
5.48.55.e: "Who is he? Whose son is he? Why has he come here? Where has he come from? What business does he have here?" Thus the heroic demons talked among themselves.

w: near the feet of the king
the aged and experienced ministers of the king
5.48.57.t:
अतीत्य मार्गं सहसा महात्मा स तत्र रक्षोधिपपादमूले ।
ददर्श राज्ञः परिचारवृद्धान् गृहं महारत्नविभूषितं च
5.48.57.e: The great Hanuman moving quickly and crossing the path came near the feet of the king. He saw the aged and experienced ministers of the king and the palace of the king adorned with precious gems.

5.48.58.t:
स ददर्श महातेजा रावणः कपिसत्तमम् ।
रक्षोभिर्विकृताकारैः कृष्यमाणमितस्ततः
5.48.58.e: Resplendent Ravana saw  the ogres of ugly appearance dragging the foremost of the monkeys here and there.

5.49.2.t:
भ्राजमानं महार्हेण काञ्चनेन विराजता ।
मुक्ताजालावृतेनाथ मकुटेन महाद्युतिम्
5.49.2.e: (Hanuman looked at Ravana) of innate splendour, who shone with a glittering crown of gold glowing, encircled with strings of pearls.

5.49.4.e: He was dressed in exquisite silk and smeared with red sandal paste and had many ornamental designs drawn on his body with fragrant unguents.

5.49.5.t:
विचित्रैर्दर्शनीयैश्च रक्ताक्षैर्भीमदर्शनैः ।
दीप्ततीक्ष्णमहादंष्ट्रैः प्रलम्बदशनच्छदैः शिरोभिर्दशभिर्वीरं भ्राजमानं महौजसम् ।
नानाव्यालसमाकीर्णैश्शिखरैरिव मन्दरम्
5.49.5.e: He appeared terrible with bloodred eyes, shining sharp big teeth, drooping lips and ten heads, which looked like ten peaks of mountain Mandara inhabited by various beasts. He was heroic, powerful and splendid.

5.49.9.t:
महतिस्फाटिके चित्रे रत्नसंयोगसंस्कृते ।
उत्तमास्तरणास्तीर्णे सूपविष्टं वरासने
5.49.9.e: (He was) seated on a huge magnificent throne of crystal encrusted with precious stones and overspread with a wonderful carpet.

5.49.10.e: Young and beautiful girls decorated exceedingly well holding whisks all over the vicinity attended on him.

5.49.11.t:
दुर्धरेण प्रहस्तेन महापार्श्वेन रक्षसा ।
मन्त्रिभिर्मन्त्रतत्त्वज्ञैर्निकुम्भेन च मन्त्रिणा सुखोपविष्टं रक्षोभिश्चतुर्भिर्बलदर्पितैः ।
कृत्स्नं परिवृतं लोकं चतुर्भिरिव सागरैः
5.49.11.e: He was attended by Durdhara, Prahasta, Mahaparsva and Nikumbha who were his learned ministers. Seated comfortably and attended by the four arrogant ministers, he was puffed with pride of their strength and appeared like the entire world surrounded by four oceans.

5.49.13.t:
मन्त्रिभिर्मन्त्रतत्त्वज्ञैरन्यैश्च शुभबुद्धिभिः ।
अन्वास्यमानं रक्षोभिः सुरैरिव सुरेश्वरम्
5.49.13.e: He was attended by ogres including ministers who were intellectuals and adept in counselling. He appeared like lord Indra attended by the gods.

w: on the peak of mount Meru
5.49.14.t:
अपश्यद्राक्षसपतिं हनुमानतितेजसम् ।
विष्ठितं मेरुशिखरे सतोयमिव तोयदम्
5.49.14.e: Hanuman saw the highly resplendent giant king (seated on the throne) who appeared like a cloud laden with water appearing on the peak of mount Meru.

5.49.15.t:
स तैस्सम्पीड्यमानोऽपि रक्षोभिर्भीमविक्रमैः ।
विस्मयं परमं गत्वा रक्षोधिपमवैक्षत
5.49.15.e: Hanuman looked at the demon king with great amazement even while he was dealt harshly by the demons of fierce valour.

w: even of the world of gods
5.49.18.t:
यद्यधर्मो न बलवान् स्यादयं राक्षसेश्वरः ।
स्यादयं सुरलोकस्य सशक्रस्यापि रक्षिता
5.49.18.e: 'If only this lord of demons was not unrighteous, he could have become even the lord (protector) of gods including Indra.

5.49.19.t:
अस्य क्रूरैर्नृशंसैश्च कर्मभिर्लोककुत्सितैः ।
सर्वे बिभ्यति खल्वस्माल्लोकास्सामरदानवाः अयं ह्युत्सहते क्रुद्धः कर्तुमेकार्णवं जगत् ।
5.49.19.e: 'This Ravana has done many cruel, fierce and contemptible deeds. That is why even the demons, gods and all the people of this world get scared of him. He will render the entire world into a single ocean when he turns angry'.

5.50.1.t:
तमुद्वीक्ष्य महाबाहुः पिङ्गाक्षं पुरत स्थितम् ।
कोपेन महताऽविष्टो रावणो लोकरावणः शङ्काहृतात्मा दध्यौ स कपीन्द्रं तेजसावृतम् ।
5.50.1.e: The mighty armed Ravana, a tormentor of all worlds, overcome with anger beheld the tawnyeyed brilliant lord of monkeys who stood before him and started thinking in his mind full of apprehensions.

5.50.4.t:
स राजा रोषताम्राक्षः प्रहस्तं मन्त्रिसत्तमम् ।
कालयुक्तमुवाचेदं वचोऽविपुलमर्थवत्
5.50.4.e: The infuriated demon king told the great minister Prahasta, these  profound words in a brief manner appropriate to the hour.

5.50.9.t:
यदि वैश्रवणस्य त्वं यमस्य वरुणस्य च ।
चाररूपमिदं कृत्वा प्रविष्टो नः पुरीमिमाम् विष्णुना प्रेषितो वाऽपि दूतो विजयकाङ्क्षिणा ।
5.50.9.e: "Having assumed this charming appearance you entered this city of ours. Are you a messenger of Vaisravana, of Yama, or of Varuna?"

5.50.10.t: न हि ते वानरं तेजो रूपमात्रं तु वानरम् तत्त्वत: कथयस्वाद्य ततो वानर मोक्ष्यसे ।
5.50.10.e: "Your appearance is only of that of a vanara. But your glow is not of a vanara indeed. Tell the truth today. You will be set free.

5.50.11.t: अनृतं वदतश्चापि दुर्लभं तव जीवितम् अथवा यन्निमित्तस्ते प्रवेशो रावणालये ।
5.50.11.e: "If you tell a lie, it will be difficult for you to live. Or else, tell me for what reason have you entered the abode of Ravana.'

w: to the lord of the demon clan
5.50.12.t:
एवमुक्तो हरिश्रेष्ठस्तदा रक्षोगणेश्वरम् अब्रवीन्नास्मि शक्रस्य यमस्य वरुणस्य वा ।
धनदेन न मे सख्यं विष्णुना नास्मि चोदितः जातिरेव मम त्वेषा वानरोऽहमिहागतः ।
5.50.12.e: The foremost of the vanaras spoke to the lord of ogres in response to the equiries made to him: "I have not come from Indra or Yama or Varuna. I have no friendship with Kubera. I have not been sent by Visnu. By birth I am vanara and I have come here.'

5.50.14.t: दर्शने राक्षसेन्द्रस्य दुर्लभे तदिदं मया वनं राक्षसराजस्य दर्शनार्थे विनाशितम् ।
5.50.14.e: "Since it is difficult to see the lord of ogres, I entered this garden in order that I might see the demon king; and for no other reason."

5.50.15.t:
ततस्ते राक्षसाः प्राप्ता बलिनो युद्धकाङ्क्षिणः ।
रक्षणार्थं तु देहस्य प्रतियुद्धा मया रणे
5.50.15.e: "Desiring to fight with me the powerful ogres came. Then I fought in self defence.

5.50.16.t: अस्त्रपाशैर्न शक्योऽहं बद्धुं देवासुरैरपि पितामहादेष वरो मामाप्येषोऽभ्युपागतः ।
5.50.16.e: "It is not possible to bind me with any bondage of astras even by devas or danavas. Such a boon has been granted to me by Grandfather Brahma.

5.50.17.t:
राजानं द्रष्टुकामेन मयास्त्रमनुवर्तितम् विमुक्तो ह्यहमस्त्रेण राक्षसैस्त्वभिपीडितः ।
केनचिद्राजकार्येण सम्प्राप्तोऽस्मि तवान्तिकम्
5.50.17.e: "Wishing to see the king I honoured this astra and not otherwise. Even though I was tormented by the ogres and released by the astra I submitted to you as I have a small work assigned by the king.

5.50.19.t:
दूतोऽहमिति विज्ञेयो राघवस्यामितौजसः ।
श्रूयतां चापि वचनं मम पथ्यमिदं प्रभो
5.50.19.e: Know that I am a messenger of the highly powerful Rama. O lord please listen to these beneficial words of mine meant for your welfare. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये सुन्दरकाण्डे पञ्चाशस्सर्गः।। Thus ends the fiftieth sarga of Sundarakanda of the holy Ramayana, the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

5.51.2.t:
अहं सुग्रीवसंदेशादिह प्राप्तस्तवालयम् ।
राक्षसेन्द्र हरीशस्त्वां भ्राता कुशलमब्रवीत्
5.51.2.e: "O lord of demons I reached your realm here by the orders of Sugriva, lord of monkeys who is like your brother. He conveys his good wishes to you.

5.51.3.t:
भ्रातुश्शृणु समादेशं सुग्रीवस्य महात्मनः ।
धर्मार्थोपहितं वाक्यमिह चामुत्र च क्षमम्
5.51.3.e: "The great Sugriva who is like your brother sends you a message pertinent to this world and the other world, that which is beneficial and consistent with righteousness and propriety (धर्म and अर्थ). Listen:

5.51.5.t:
ज्येष्ठस्तस्य महाबाहुः पुत्रः प्रियकरः प्रभुः ।
पितुर्निदेशान्निष्क्रान्तः प्रविष्टो दण्डकावनम् लक्ष्मणेन सह भ्रात्रा सीतया चापि भार्यया ।
रामो नाम महातेजा धर्म्यं पन्थानमास्थितः
5.51.5.e: "His eldest son, a highly effulgent one, named Rama who was dear to the king, accepting his father's orders went into exile with brother Lakshmana and wife Sita also accepting a righteous path and entered Dandaka forest.

5.51.9.t:
तस्य तेन प्रतिज्ञातं सीतायाः परिमार्गणम् ।
सुग्रीवस्यापि रामेण हरिराज्यं निवेदितम्
5.51.9.e: "Sugriva promised Rama to undertake search for Sita and Rama assured Sugriva of securing him the kingdom of the monkeys.

5.51.10.t:
ततस्तेन मृधे हत्वा राजपुत्रेण वालिनम् ।
सुग्रीवः स्थापितो राज्ये हर्यृक्षाणां गणेश्वरः
5.51.10.e: "Then prince Rama killed Vali in battle and made Sugriva, king of the vanaras and bears and restored the kingship of Sugriva.

5.51.11.t:
त्वया विज्ञातपूर्वश्च वाली वानरपुङ्गवः ।
रामेण निहतस्सङ्ख्ये शरेणैकेन वानरः
5.51.11.e: "You know of Vali, chief of the vanaras, in the past. Rama killed him with a single arrow in the combat.

w: one who is a faithful warrior
5.51.12.t:
स सीतामार्गणे व्यग्रस्सुग्रीवः सत्यसङ्गरः ।
हरीन् सम्प्रेषयामास दिशस्सर्वा हरीश्वरः
5.51.12.e: "Sugriva, who is true to his word and a faithful warrior, king of monkeys anxiously sent vanaras in all directions for searching Sita.

5.51.13.t:
तां हरीणां सहस्राणि शतानि नियुतानि च ।
दिक्षु सर्वासु मार्गन्ते ह्यधश्चोपरि चाम्बरे
5.51.13.e: "Hundreds, thousands and unlimited number of monkeys are searching (for Sita) in all directions, in the underworld and heavens and the sky.

5.51.14.e: "Some of the very powerful heroes equal to Garuda, equal to the Windgod (in swiftness) have gone (in quest of Sita) without touching the earth.

5.51.15.t:
अहं तु हनुमान्नाम मारुतस्यौरसस्सुतः ।
सीतायास्तु कृते तूर्णं शतयोजनमायतम् समुद्रं लङ्घयित्वैव तां दिदृक्षुरिहागतः ।
5.51.15.e: "I, Maruta's son, Hanuman by name too came swiftly leaping across a hundred yojanas across the ocean searching for Sita.

5.51.18.t:
न हि धर्मविरुद्धेषु बह्वपायेषु कर्मसु ।
मूलघातिषु सज्जन्ते बुद्धिमन्तो भवद्विधाः
5.51.18.e: "Indeed, respectable people and wise men like you should not indulge in actions opposed to righteousness as it will strike at the very root of your existence.

5.51.19.t:
कश्च लक्ष्मणमुक्तानां रामकोपानुवर्तिनाम् ।
शराणामग्रतः स्थातुं शक्तो देवासुरेष्वपि
5.51.19.e: "Who, even among gods and asuras can withstand the arrows released by Lakshmana in obedience to the infuriated Rama's orders?

5.51.20.t:
न चापि त्रिषु लोकेषु राजन्विद्येत कश्चन ।
राघवस्य व्यलीकं यः कृत्वा सुखमवाप्नुयात्
5.51.20.e: "O king  there is none in these three worlds who can enjoy happiness by displeasing Rama.

w: good for all three times past present and future
to the lord of the people
5.51.21.t:
तत् त्रिकालहितं वाक्यं धर्म्यमर्थानुबन्धि च ।
मन्यस्व नरदेवाय जानकी प्रतिदीयताम्
5.51.21.e: "Think that my advice is beneficial to you for you present, past and future. It is righteous. It will provide you material wealth too. Hence return Sita to the lord of the people.

5.51.22.t:
दृष्टा हीयं मया देवी लब्धं यदिह दुर्लभम् ।
उत्तरं कर्म यच्छेषं निमित्तं तत्र राघवः
5.51.22.e: "I have actually spotted the divine lady here which was most difficult. Rama will plan the remaining course of action.

5.51.24.t:
नेयं जरयितुं शक्या सासुरैरमरैरपि ।
विषसंसृष्टमत्यर्थं भुक्तमन्नमिवौजसा
5.51.24.e: "Just as food mixed with venom cannot be digested by the great fire (fire of hunger), it is not possible to keep Sita even by gods and demons. (Sita is like food mixed with poison. Ravana cannot digest her with all his power.)

5.51.26.t:
अवध्यतां तपोभिर्यां भवान् समनुपश्यति ।
आत्मनः सासुरैर्देवैर्हेतुस्तत्राप्ययं महान्
5.51.26.e: "You know you will not be killed by asuras or gods. In that case also this (keeping Sita with you) may be the prime cause of your death.

5.51.27.t:
सुग्रीवो न हि देवोऽयं नासुरो न च राक्षसः ।
न दानवो न गन्धर्वो न यक्षो न च पन्नगः तस्मात्प्राणपरित्राणं कथं राजन्करिष्यसि ।
5.51.27.e: "Sugriva is not an demon, nor a danava nor gandharva, nor a yaksha nor even a pannaga. Therefore how can you save your life from Sugriva?

w: killing of all ogres at Janasthana
alliance of Rama and Sugriva also
know (Judge and adopt suitable course of action.)
5.51.30.t: जनस्थानवधं बुद्ध्वा बुद्ध्वा वालिवधं तथा रामसुग्रीवसख्यं च बुध्यस्व हितमात्मनः ।
5.51.30.e: "You know about the killing of all ogres at Janasthana and of Vali also. You know about the alliance of Rama and Sugriva. You may  decide on a proper course of action for the sake of your own welfare.

5.51.35.t: तदलं कालपाशेन सीताविग्रहरूपिणा स्वयं स्कन्धावसक्तेन क्षेममात्मनि चिन्त्यताम् ।
5.51.35.e: "Stop holding the noose of death in Sita's form whom you yourself have placed on your shoulders. Think of your own welfare.

5.51.36.t: सीतायास्तेजसा दग्धां रामकोपप्रपीडिताम् दह्यमानामिमां पश्य पुरीं साट्टप्रतोलिकाम् ।
5.51.36.e: "Visualize this city of Lanka including its marketplaces and main streets as  burnt by Sita's power of chastity and  Rama's anger.

5.51.38.t: सत्यं राक्षसराजेन्द्र शृणुष्व वचनं मम रामदासस्य दूतस्य वानरस्य विशेषतः ।
5.51.38.e: "O king of demon listen to the words of truth of the servant of Rama, his messenger and specially a vanara.

w: among the kings of gods and asuras
5.51.40.t:
देवासुरनरेन्द्रेषु यक्षरक्षोगणेषु च विद्याधरेषु सर्वेषु गन्धर्वेषूरगेषु च ।
सिद्धेषु किन्नरेन्द्रेषु पतत्रिषु च सर्वतः सर्वभूतेषु सर्वत्र सर्वकालेषु नास्ति सः ।
यो रामं प्रतियुध्येत विष्णुतुल्यपराक्रमम्
5.51.40.e: "He is equal to Visnu in valour. There is none who can dare face his rage, be it among gods, asuras, yakshas, rakshasas, vidyadharas, gandharvas uragas, siddhas, kings of kinnaras, birds and all beings at all places and at all times.

w: deemed to be killed by Rama
5.51.45.t:
ब्रह्मा स्वयम्भूश्चतुराननो वा रुद्रस्त्रिणेत्रस्त्रिपुरान्तको वा ।
इन्द्रो महेन्द्रस्सुरनायको वा त्रातुं न शक्ता युधि रामवध्यम्
5.51.45.e: "Even the selfborn, fourfaced Brahma, the threeeyed Siva who destroyed Tripura, Mahendra, the king of suras do not have the power to save one whom Rama decides to kill".

5.52.1.t:
तस्य तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा वानरस्य महात्मनः ।
आज्ञापयद्वधं तस्य रावणः क्रोधमूर्छितः
5.52.1.e: Hearing the great vanara's speech, Ravana overwhelmed with anger ordered the execution of Hanuman.

w: who had  declared (the purpose of his visit)
5.52.2.t:
वधे तस्य समाज्ञप्ते रावणेन दुरात्मना ।
निवेदितवतो दौत्यं नानुमेने विभीषणः
5.52.2.e: Vibhishana did not approve of the killing of Hanuman, who had declared that he was an envoy (of Sri Rama) when the wicked Ravana ordered his murder.

5.52.3.t:
तं रक्षोधिपतिं क्रुद्धं तच्च कार्यमुपस्थितम् ।
विदित्वा चिन्तयामास कार्यं कार्यविधौ स्थितः
5.52.3.e: Vibhishana who stood by the right course of action, having realised that the lord of demons was angry pondered over his duty.

5.52.4.t:
निश्चितार्थस्ततस्साम्ना पूज्यं शत्रुजिदग्रजम् ।
उवाच हितमत्यर्थं वाक्यं वाक्यविशारदः
5.52.4.e: Then Vibhishana, who was skilled in speech having decided about his duty   addressed his reverential elder brother, a conqueror of enemies in soothing, words in a meaningful, wholesome manner.

w: knower of what is exalted and what is mean (basic values of life)
5.52.5.t:
क्षमस्व रोषं त्यज राक्षसेन्द्र प्रसीद मद्वाक्यमिदं शृणुष्व ।
वधं न कुर्वन्ति परावरज्ञा दूतस्य सन्तो वसुधाधिपेन्द्राः
5.52.5.e: "O king of ogres give up your wrath, forgive and calm down. Please listen to my appeal. You know the basic values of life. Virtuous rulers of the earth do not order killing of an envoy.

5.52.6.t:
राजधर्मविरुद्धं च लोकवृत्तेश्च गर्हितम् ।
तव चासदृशं वीर कपेरस्य प्रमापणम्
5.52.6.e: "Mighty king killing this Hanuman is contrary to righteousness of kings. This is deplorable diplomacy and also unbecoming of you.

w: you have a sense of gratitude
knower of right and wrong practices
5.52.7.t:
धर्मज्ञश्च कृतज्ञश्च राजधर्मविशारदः ।
परावरज्ञो भूतानां त्वमेव परमार्थवित्
5.52.7.e: "You are conversant with  dharma of a king.  You have a sense of gratitude. You are a knower of right and wrong of all beings. the supeme truth.

w: that which is proper and improper
5.52.9.t:
तस्मात्प्रसीद शत्रुघ्न राक्षसेन्द्र दुरासद ।
युक्तायुक्तं विनिश्चित्य दूतदण्डो विधीयताम्
5.52.9.e: "O destroyer of foes, O unassailable king of demon calm down. Only after carefully considering what is proper and improper decide on the punishment to be imposed".

5.52.11.t:
न पापानां वधे पापं विद्यते शत्रुसूदन ।
तस्मादेनं वधिष्यामि वानरं पापचारिणम्
5.52.11.e: "O slayer of foes it is not wrong to kill a sinner. I shall, therefore, kill the sinful vanara."

5.52.12.t:
अधर्ममूलं बहुदोषयुक्तमनार्यजुष्टं वचनं निशम्य ।
उवाच वाक्यं परमार्थतत्त्वं विभीषणो बुद्धिमतां वरिष्ठः
5.52.12.e: On hearing his brother's harsh words spoken in tremendous anger, which were not acceptable to noble souls, wise Vibhishana again spoke these words of supreme truth:

w: which is the essence of  dharma and artha
5.52.13.t:
प्रसीद लङ्केश्वर राक्षसेन्द्र धर्मार्थयुक्तं वचनं शृणुष्व ।
दूतानवध्यान् समयेषु राजन् सर्वेषु सर्वत्र वदन्ति सन्तः
5.52.13.e: "O lord of Lanka O king of demons be pleased to listen to my words which are the essence of dharma and artha. The elders have declared that the emissaries should not be killed by any means.

5.52.14.t:
असंशयं शत्रुरयं प्रवृद्धः कृतं ह्यनेनाप्रियमप्रमेयम् ।
न दूतवध्यां प्रवदन्ति सन्तो दूतस्य दृष्टा बहवो हि दण्डाः
5.52.14.e: This enemy has done a lot of harm, no doubt. Indeed he has done terrible and unpleasant deeds. (Yet) the wise have recommended many alternate punishments, while prohibiting their killing.

5.52.15.t:
वैरूप्यमङ्गेषु कशाभिघातो मौण्ड्यं तथा लक्षणसन्निपातः ।
एतान् हि दूते प्रवदन्ति दण्डान् वधस्तु दूतस्य न नः श्रुतोऽस्ति
5.52.15.e: "Mutilation of limbs, flogging, shaving of the head, and deforming limbs etc. these punishments have been prescribed for an emissary. Never has killing of an emissary been heard.

5.52.18.t:
शूरेण वीरेण निशाचरेन्द्र सुरासुराणामपि दुर्जयेन ।
त्वया प्रगल्भाः सुरदैत्यसङ्घा जिताश्च युद्धेष्वसकृन्नरेन्द्राः
5.52.18.e: "You are the king of demons. Hosts of gods and daityas efficient in wars are conquered by you again and again since you are a brave warrior invincible to gods and demons.

w: of one of such a kind
5.52.18.1.t:
इत्थंविधस्यामरदैत्यशत्रोः शूरस्य वीरस्य तवाजितस्य ।
कुर्वन्ति वीरा मनसाप्यलीकं प्राणैर्विमुक्ता न तु भोः पुरा ते
5.52.18.1.e: "Against one of such a kind, foe of immortals and daityas, valiant, heroic and unconquered as you are, would heroes do anything false even in thought? Only those bereft of their lives, alas, have done so before."

5.52.19.t:
न चाप्यस्य कपेर्घाते कञ्चित्पश्याम्यहं गुणम् ।
तेष्वयं पात्यतां दण्डो यैरयं प्रेषितः कपिः
5.52.19.e: "I do not see any use in killing this monkey. Pronounce  punishment on those who have sent this vanara.

5.52.25.t:
हिताश्च शूराश्च समाहिताश्च कुलेषु जाताश्च महागुणेषु ।
मनस्विनश्शस्त्रभृतां वरिष्ठाः कोट्यग्रतस्ते सुभृताश्च योधाः
5.52.25.e: "You have with you wellwishers, courageous ones, who have good qualities born in a good race, who are noble, sensible people, wielders of weapons and wellpaid warriors in crores.

w: they may march out for war.
5.52.26.t: तदेकदेशेन बलस्य तावत्केचित्तवाऽऽदेशकृतोऽभियान्तु तौ राजपुत्रौ विनिगृह्य मूढौ परेषु ते भावयितुं प्रभावम्
5.52.26.e: By your order let some strong soldiers from one contingency go and capture the two sons of the king, to exhibit your power over the enemy.

w: in keeping with the laws of the land
5.53.1.t:
तस्य तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा दशग्रीवो महात्मनः ।
देशकालहितं वाक्यं भ्रातुरुत्तरमब्रवीत्
5.53.1.e: The tenheaded Ravana heard his brother, the greatsoul Vibhishana's timely advice which was in keeping with the laws of the land and replied.

5.53.2.t:
सम्यगुक्तं हि भवता दूतवध्या विगर्हिता ।
अवश्यं तु वधादन्यः क्रियतामस्य निग्रहः
5.53.2.e: "Indeed, you have spoken very well.Killing of emissary is censured (in sastras). Surely we will impose suitable punishment other than killing.

5.53.3.t:
कपीनां किल लाङ्गूलमिष्टं भवति भूषणम् ।
तदस्य दीप्यतां शीघ्रं तेन दग्धेन गच्छतु
5.53.3.e: "The tail is dear to the monkeys and it is an ornament for them. Set fire to it at once and let him go with his burning tail.

w: disfigured and deformed by such handicap
5.53.4.t:
ततः पश्यन्त्विमं दीनमङ्गवैरूप्यकर्शितम् ।
समित्रज्ञातयस्सर्वे बान्धवाः ससुहृज्जनाः आज्ञापयद्राक्षसेन्द्रः पुरं सर्वं सचत्वरम् ।
लाङ्गूलेन प्रदीप्तेन रक्षोभिः परिणीयताम्
5.53.4.e: "Then all his friends, relatives and his kinsmen will see his disfigured and handicapped form. The demon king having ordered thus, the monkey was taken by the ogres round the junctions of the roads all over the city with his tail on fire.

5.53.6.t:
तस्य तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा राक्षसाः कोपकर्शिताः ।
वेष्टयन्ति स्म लाङ्गूलं जीर्णैः कार्पासकैः पटैः
5.53.6.e: "Obeying the orders of the king, the brutally angry demons wrapped his tail with tatters of cotton.

w: his face looking like the rising Sun
5.53.8.t:
तैलेन परिषिच्याथ तेऽग्निं तत्राभ्यपातयन् ।
लाङ्गूलेन प्रदीप्तेन राक्षसांस्तानपातयत् रोषामर्षपरीतात्मा बालसूर्यसमाननः ।
5.53.8.e: The demons soaked the tail and set fire to it. His face burning in anger shone like the rising Sun and his mind seized with indignation, he struck them with the burning tail.

w: including children women and the old
5.53.9.t: लाङ्गूलं सम्प्रदीप्तं तु द्रष्टुं तस्य हनूमतः सहस्त्रीबालवृद्धाश्च जग्मुः प्रीता निशाचराः ।
5.53.9.e: All the demons including the shedemons and their children and the elders went out joyfully to see the burning tail of Hanuman.

5.53.10.t: स भूयः सङ्गतैः क्रूरैर्राक्षसैर्हरिसत्तमः निबद्धः कृतवान्वीरस्तत्कालसदृशीं मतिम् ।
5.53.10.e: When the cruel demons collected together and bound him once again the heroic Hanuman thought what was appropriate to the moment.

w: by the order of their lord
5.53.12.t: यदि भर्तुर्हितार्थाय चरन्तं भर्तृशासनात् बध्नन्त्येते दुरात्मनो न तु मे निष्कृतिः कृता ।
5.53.12.e: 'These  evilminded demons bind me, ordered by their lord. When I am moving here for the welfare of  my master, I will not let them escape৷৷

5.53.16.t:
कामं बद्धस्य मे भूयः पुच्छस्योद्दीपनेन च ।
पीडां कुर्वन्तु रक्षांसि न मेऽस्ति मनसश्श्रमः
5.53.16.e: 'Let the demons torture me freely by setting fire to my tail. Let them bind me. I am not exhausted.

5.53.17.t:
ततस्ते संवृताकारं सत्त्ववन्तं महाकपिम् ।
परिगृह्य ययुर्हृष्टा राक्षसाः कपिकुञ्जरम्
5.53.17.e: Then the ogres set forth joyfully capturing the very powerful elephant among the monkeys, the great vanara who had contracted his body.

5.53.19.t:
अन्वीयमानो रक्षोभिर्ययौ सुखमरिन्दमः ।
हनुमांश्चारयामास राक्षसानां महापुरीम्
5.53.19.e: Hanuman, the subduer of enemies ranged forth happily while he was followed by the demons in the great city.

5.53.22.t: चत्वरेषु चतुष्केषु राजमार्गे तथैव च घोषयन्ति कपिं सर्वे चारीक इति राक्षसाः ।
5.53.22.e: All the demons went forth through cross roads, altars built on four pillars and royal roads announcing that he (Hanuman) was a spy.

w: that I am longing to unite with him
5.53.30.t: यदि मां वृत्तसम्पन्नां तत्समागमलालसाम् स विजानाति धर्मात्मा शीतो भव हनूमतः ।
5.53.30.e: "O Firegod if Rama is righteous, if I am pure in mind, and if I am longing to unite with him, be cool to Hanuman.

5.53.32.t: ततस्तीक्ष्णार्चिरव्यग्रः प्रदक्षिणशिखोऽनलः जज्वाल मृगशाबाक्ष्या श्शंसन्निव शिवं कपेः ।
5.53.32.e: Then the tips of the intense flame appeared steadily moving to the fawneyed Sita indicating the firegod's auspiciousness and safety to Hanuman.

w: cool like the wind blowing from the snow
5.53.33.t: हनुमज्जनकश्चापि पुच्छानलयुतोऽनिलः ववौ स्वास्थ्यकरो देव्याः प्रालेयानिलशीतलः ।
5.53.33.e: "The Windgod accompanying Hanuman's firelit tail also blew cool like the wind from snow, to calm the mind of the divine lady.

5.53.36.t: अथवा तदिदं व्यक्तं यद्दृष्टं प्लवता मया रामप्रभावादाश्चर्यं पर्वत स्सरितां पतौ ।
5.53.36.e: 'It must be due to the power of Rama, by which I found a wonderful mountain  emerging from the sea to give me protection while I was crossing the ocean. Now evidently this is due to Rama's power (that my tail is not burning me).

5.53.39.1.t:
प्रतिक्रियास्य युक्ता स्यात् सति मह्यं पराक्रमे ।
ततश्छित्त्वा च तान् पाशान् वेगवान् वै महाकपिः
5.53.39.1.e: "While valour is present in me, a requital for this would be fitting." Then the swift great monkey cut through those bonds.

w: like the peak of a mountain
5.53.40.e: Then the illustrious Hanuman reached the entrance of the lofty city, which was  like the peak of a mountain and turned away the demons.

5.53.41.t: स भूत्वा शैलसङ्काशः क्षणेन पुनरात्मवान् ह्रस्वतां परमां प्राप्तो बन्धनान्यवशातयत् ।
5.53.41.e: From his mountainlike form he assumed his original small figure within a moment casting off the bonds.

5.54.1.t: वीक्षमाणस्ततो लङ्कां कपिः कृतमनोरथः वर्धमानसमुत्साहः कार्यशेषमचिन्तयत् ।
5.54.1.e: With his objectives achieved, the monkey gazed at Lanka with growing zeal and pondered over the remaining work.

5.54.2.t: किन्नु खल्ववशिष्टं मे कर्तव्यमिह साम्प्रतम् यदेषां रक्षसां भूयः सन्तापजननं भवेत् ।
5.54.2.e: 'Is there anything still left which can further torment the demons here?

5.54.3.t:
