वनं तावत्प्रमथितं प्रकृष्टा राक्षसा हताः ।
 ।
.. ।
बलैकदेशः क्षपितश्शेषं दुर्गविनाशनम् ।
5.54.3.e: 'All the trees of the garden are broken, powerful demons have been killed, and a contingent of the army is destroyed. Only the destruction of the citadel is left.

5.54.6.t:
ततः प्रदीप्तलाङ्गूलस्सविद्युदिव तोयदः ।
भवनाग्रेषु लङ्काया विचचार महाकपिः
5.54.6.e: The great Hanuman, with his burning tail wandered on tops of the mansions of Lanka, which looked like clouds with lightning.

5.54.7.t:
गृहाद्गृहं राक्षसानामुद्यानानि च वानरः ।
वीक्षमाणो ह्यसन्त्रस्तः प्रासादांश्च चचार सः
5.54.7.e: The vanara moved from one house to the other, looking at the gardens and houses of the demons without fear.

w: like the flame of fire at the hour of dissolution
5.54.8.t:
अवप्लुत्य महावेगः प्रहस्तस्य निवेशनम् ।
अग्निं तत्र स निक्षिप्य श्वसनेन समो बली ततोऽन्यत्पुप्लुवे वेश्म महापार्श्वस्य वीर्यवान् ।
मुमोच हनुमानग्निं कालानलशिखोपमम्
5.54.8.e: Powerful and brave Hanuman who was equal to the Windgod in speed jumped down on the house of Prahasta and set fire to it. From there he jumped on to Mahaparsva's house and set it ablaze. Hanuman appeared like the fireflame at the time of dissolution.

5.54.11.t:
तथा चेन्द्रजितो वेश्म ददाह हरियूथपः ।
जम्बुमाले स्सुमालेश्च ददाह भवनं ततः
5.54.11.e: Thus Hanuman, the chief of the vanaras set fire to Indrajit's residence and then to Jambumali's and Sumali's building.

5.54.22.e: Combined with the wind the fire began to spread, burning the houses with great speed.

w: disappointed thoroughly about their multiplying riches
in the form of a monkey
5.54.24.t:
संजज्ञे तुमुलश्शब्दो राक्षसानां प्रधावताम् ।
स्वगृहस्य परित्राणे भग्नोत्साहोर्जितश्रियाम् नूनमेषोऽग्निरायातः कपिरूपेण हा इति ।
5.54.24.e: Unable to protect their rich houses, and thoroughly disappointed the demons said, 'Alas, the Firegod came in the form of a vanara' A tumultuous sound arose.

5.54.25.t:
क्रन्दन्त्यस्सहसा पेतुः स्तनन्धयधराः स्त्रियः काश्चिदग्निपरीतेभ्यो हर्मेभ्यो मुक्तमूर्धजाः ।
पतन्त्यो रेजिरेऽभ्रेभ्यस्सौदामन्य इवाम्बरात्
5.54.25.e: A few shedemons at once jumped out of their burning mansions surrounded by fire. They held their breastfeeding babies in their arms, their hair let loose shouting as they jumped. As they were alighting, they glowed like lightnings dropping from the clouds.

w: mixed with diamonds corals Vaiduryas pearls and silver
5.54.27.e: Hanuman saw many colourful molten minerals mixed with diamonds, corals vaiduryas, pearls and silver flowing (dropping) from every mansion.

5.54.28.t:
नाग्निस्तृप्यति काष्ठानां तृणानां च यथा तथा ।
हनूमान् राक्षसेन्दाणां विशस्तानां न तृप्यति
5.54.28.e: Just as fire is not satisfied with dry sticks and grass Hanuman was not satisfied with the dead demons.

w: by the vanara of great spped
5.54.30.t:
हनूमता वेगवता वानरेण महात्मना ।
लङ्कापुरं प्रदग्धं तद्रुद्रेण त्रिपुरं यथा
5.54.30.e: Hanuman, endowed with great speed, burnt Lanka just as Tripurari, or Rudra burnt theTripuras (three cities of gold, silver and iron).

w: fat of the demons body adding
spreading fast just as the fire with the end of the universe
5.54.32.t:
युगान्तकालानलतुल्यवेग स्समारुतोऽग्निर्ववृधे दिविस्पृक् ।
विधूमरश्मिर्भवनेषु सक्तो रक्षश्शरीराज्यसमर्पतार्चिः
5.54.32.e: Fanned by the wind, inflamed by the fat from the corpses of the demons, the fire spread in the mansions burning without smoke. It spread with great speed like the fire at the end of the universe.

5.54.33.t:
आदित्यकोटीसदृशस्सुतेजा लङ्कां समस्तां परिवार्य तिष्ठन् ।
शब्दैरनेकैरशनिप्ररूढैर्भिन्दन्निवाण्डं प्रबभौ महाग्निः
5.54.33.e: The highly radiant fire stood like a crore of Suns surrounding the entire Lanka. It was glowing, cracking like Indra's thunderbolt as though the whole universe was collapsing.

w: to kill the clan of demons
5.54.36.t:
किं ब्रह्मणस्सर्वपितामहस्य सर्वस्य धातुश्चतुराननस्य ।
इहाऽऽगतो वानररूपधारी रक्षोपसंहारकरः प्रकोपः
5.54.36.e: 'Or is it Grandfather Brahma, the supreme fourfaced god enraged and arrived in the form of vanara to kill the clan of demons?

5.54.37.t:
किं वैष्णवं वा कपिरूपमेत्य रक्षोविनाशाय परं सुतेजः ।
अनन्तमव्यक्तमचिन्त्यमेकं स्वमायया साम्प्रतमागतं वा
5.54.37.e: 'Can he be the vast boundless energy, the unthinkable and infinite lord Visnu assuming the monkeyform? Is he the peerless, unmanifest form beyond all imagination who has arrived here by virtue of his Maya (illusory power) in order to destroy the demons'?

5.54.38.t:
इत्येवमूचुर्बहवो विशिष्टा रक्षोगणास्तत्र समेत्य सर्वे ।
सप्राणिसङ्घां सगृहां सवृक्षां दग्धां पुरीं तां सहसा समीक्ष्य
5.54.38.e: All eminent demons having collected together, quickly surveyed the situation.Seeing the burnt city, with  all its living creatures, houses and trees consigned to the flames, they spoke to one another.

5.54.39.t:
ततस्तु लङ्का सहसा प्रदग्धा सराक्षसा साश्वरथा सनागा ।
सपक्षिसङ्घा समृगा सवृक्षा रुरोद दीना तुमुलं सशब्दम्
5.54.39.e: Lanka with its chariots horses, elephants, flocks of birds, animals and trees burnt all of a sudden, the ogres cried loudly and piteously.

5.54.40.t:
हा तात हा पुत्रक कान्त मित्र हा जीवितं भोगयुतं सुपुण्यम् ।
रक्षोभिरेवं बहुधा ब्रुवद्भि श्शब्दः कृतो घोरतरस्सुभीमः
5.54.40.e: "O father dear O son O my dear O friend alas, the life which is enjoyable, sacred and prosperous is destroyed in this way". Saying this, the demons cried out dreadfully and loudly.

w: engulfed in the flames spread by the Firegod
5.54.41.t: हुताशनज्वालसमावृता सा हतप्रवीरा परिवृत्तयोधा हनूमतः क्रोधबलाभिभूता बभूव शापोपहतेव लङ्का
5.54.41.e: With the Fire god spreading flames all over, heroes dead, retreating troops shattered by Hanuman's anger, Lanka appeared as though it was cursed.

w: with demons perplexed scared and sorrowful
succumbed to the flames of the burning firegod
hit by the anger of Brahma (at the time of dissolution of the universe)
5.54.42.t:
स सम्भ्रमत्रस्तविषण्णराक्षसां समुज्ज्वलज्ज्वालहुताशनाङ्किताम् ।
ददर्श लङ्कां हनुमान्महामनाः स्वयम्भूकोपोपहतामिवावनिम्
5.54.42.e: Highly sensitive Hanuman saw the city of Lanka filled with perplexed, scared and sorrowful demons, Lanka succumbed to the flames of firegod and looked as if it was  hit by the anger of Brahma, the selfborn god.

w: that which was full of excellent trees
5.54.43.t:
भङ्क्त्वा वनं पादपरत्नसङ्कुलं हत्वा तु रक्षांसि महान्ति संयुगे ।
दग्ध्वा पुरीं तां गृहरत्नमालिनीं तस्थौ हनूमान्पवनात्मजः कपिः
5.54.43.e: Hanuman, son of the Windgod stood at ease having shattered the garden that was full of excellent trees, and killed the demons and burnt down rows of beautiful houses in the city.

w: on the peak of Trikuta mountain
enriched by the flames emerging from his burning tail
5.54.44.t:
त्रिकूटशृङ्गाग्रतले विचित्रे प्रतिष्ठितो वानरराजसिंहः ।
प्रदीप्तलाङ्गूलकृतार्चिमाली व्यराजताऽऽदित्य इवांशुमाली
5.54.44.e: Standing on the peak of Trikuta mountain with his tail burning like the aura of the Sun, the lion among vanaras looked resplendent like the Sun surrounded by his rays.

5.54.45.t:
स राक्षसांस्तान्सुबहूंश्च हत्वा वनं च भङ्क्त्वा बहुपादपं तत् ।
विसृज्य रक्षोभवनेषु चाग्निं जगाम रामं मनसा महात्मा
5.54.45.e: Great Hanuman, sought Rama's presence in his mind after killing many demons, breaking down many trees of the garden, and setting fire to the mansions of demons.

w: who had the speed of wind
5.54.46.t:
ततस्तु तं वानरवीरमुख्यं महाबलं मारुततुल्यवेगम् ।
महामतिं वायुसुतं वरिष्ठं प्रतुष्टुवुर्देवगणाश्च सर्वे
5.54.46.e: All the gods praised the vanara chief, son of the Windgod, who was powerful, wise and efficient and had the speed of the Wind.

5.54.47.t:
भङ्क्त्वा वनं महातेजा हत्वा रक्षांसि संयुगे ।
दग्ध्वा लङ्कापुरीं रम्यां रराज स महाकपिः
5.54.47.e: Hanuman destroyed the garden, killed the demons, burnt the city of Lanka and was shining with delight

5.54.48.t:
तत्र देवास्सगन्धर्वास्सिद्धाश्च परमर्षयः ।
दृष्ट्वा लङ्कां प्रदग्धां तां विस्मयं परमं गताः
5.54.48.e: The gandharvas, gods, siddhas and great sages were amazed at seeing the burning city of Lanka৷৷

5.55.1.t:
लङ्कां समस्तां सन्दीप्य लाङ्गूलाग्निं महाबलः ।
निर्वापयामास तदा समुद्रे हरिसत्तमः ।
 ।
सन्दीप्यमानां विध्वस्तां त्रस्तरक्षोगणां पुरीम् ।
आवेक्ष्य हनुमान् लङ्कां चिन्तयामास वानरः
5.55.1.e: Powerful Hanuman, having burnt the entire city of Lanka, put out the fire on his tail in the ocean. Beholding the burning city, the destroyed gardens and the panic stricken ogres, he began to think:

5.55.2.t:
तस्याभूत्सुमहांस्त्रासः कुत्सा चात्मन्यजायत ।
लङ्कां प्रदहता कर्म किंस्वित्कृतमिदं मया
5.55.2.e: Overtaken by great fear, Hanuman felt a sense of selfreproach seeing Lanka reduced to ashes, and said, ' Lanka is burnt. What a heinous action has been perpetrated by me'.

5.55.3.t:
धन्यास्ते पुरुषश्रेष्ठा ये बुद्ध्या कोपमुत्थितम् ।
निरुन्धन्ति महात्मानो दीप्तमग्निमिवाम्भसा
5.55.3.e: 'Blessed indeed are the highsouled men, who in their wisdom restrain their own anger as one would put off  burning fire with water.

5.55.4.t:
क्रुद्धः पापं न कुर्यात्कः क्रुद्धो हन्याद्गुरूनपि ।
क्रुद्धः परुषया वाचा नरस्साधूनधिक्षिपेत्
5.55.4.e: 'Which sinful act an angry man will not commit? He will even kill his respectable elders or insult sages with his harsh tongue.

5.55.6.t:
यस्समुत्पतितं क्रोधं क्षमयैव निरस्यति ।
यथोरगस्त्वचं जीर्णां स वै पुरुष उच्यते
5.55.6.e: 'A man who drives away his rising anger with tolerance just as a snake casts off its slough is alone called a truly wise man.

5.55.7.t:
धिगस्तु मां सुदुर्बुद्धिं निर्लज्जं पापकृत्तमम् ।
अचिन्तयित्वा तां सीतामग्निदं स्वामिघातुकम्
5.55.7.e: 'Fie upon me, a wicked, shameless person and the greatest sinner for betraying the  master and setting fire to the city without thinking of Sita.

5.55.11.t:
विनष्टा जानकी नूनं न ह्यदग्धः प्रदृश्यते ।
लङ्कायां कश्चिदुद्धेशस्सर्वा भस्मीकृता पुरी
5.55.11.e: 'Surely Janaki has perished in Lanka, for not even a little place is left unburnt. The entire city is reduced to ashes.

5.55.12.t:
यदि तद्विहतं कार्यं मम प्रज्ञाविपर्ययात् ।
इहैव प्राणसंन्यासो ममापि ह्यद्य रोचते
5.55.12.e: 'If my work has been destroyed by my perversity of judgement, I will give up my life now  and here itself'.

w: in the mouth of submarine fire
to those aquatic creatures living in the ocean
5.55.13.t:
किमग्नौ निपताम्यद्य आहोस्विद्बडबामुखे ।
शरीरमाहो सत्त्वानां दद्मि सागरवासिनाम्
5.55.13.e: 'Shall I end my life by jumping into fire just now, or else into the mouth of submarine fire? Should I offer my body to the living creatures of the ocean as their food?

5.55.14.t:
कथं हि जीवता शक्यो मया द्रष्टुं हरीश्वरः ।
तौ वा पुरुषशार्दूलौ कार्यसर्वस्वघातिना
5.55.14.e: 'Having spoilt the entire work how can I show my face to the king of monkeys? How is it possible to see both the tigers among men?

5.55.17.t:
विनष्टायां तु सीतायां तावुभौ विनशिष्यतः ।
तयोर्विनाशे सुग्रीवः सबन्धुर्विनशिष्यति
5.55.17.e: 'If the two princes know about Sita's loss they will die and when they are dead Sugriva would perish along with all his relatives.

5.55.18.t:
एतदेव वचश्श्रुत्वा भरतो भ्रातृवत्सलः ।
धर्मात्मा सहशत्रुघ्नः कथं शक्ष्यति जीवितुम्
5.55.18.e: 'How will the loving righteous brother, Bharata along with Satrughna survive after hearing this?

w: failed to secure dharma and artha
5.55.20.t: तदहं भाग्यरहितो लुप्तधर्मार्थसङ्ग्रहः रोषदोषपरीतात्मा व्यक्तं लोकविनाशनः ।
5.55.20.e: 'I have failed in seeking dharma and artha. It is evident is that I am a destroyer of the world because I was overtaken by anger. How unfortunate I am'

5.55.21.e: When Hanuman was thus bemoaning, good omens as in the past appeared before him. He started reflecting once again:

w: of a man of immeasureable glory
5.55.23.t:
न हि धर्मात्मनस्तस्य भार्याममिततेजसः ।
स्वचारित्राभिगुप्तां तां स्प्रष्टुमर्हति पावकः
5.55.23.e: 'Fire cannot touch that lady who is protected by her own chastity and who is wedded to the righteous man of immasureable glory.

5.55.24.t:
नूनं रामप्रभावेण वैदेह्यास्सुकृतेन च ।
यन्मां दहनकर्मायं नादहद्धव्यवाहनः
5.55.24.e: 'Fire, the consumer of oblations who has the property of burning has not burnt me and this is surely on account of Rama's power and Vaidehi's merits.

5.55.25.t:
त्रयाणां भरतादीनां भ्रात्रूणां देवता च या ।
रामस्य च मन: कान्ता सा कथं विनशिष्यति
5.55.25.e: 'To Bharata, Lakshmana and Satrughna she is a goddess and she is dear to Rama's heart, how would she perish?

5.55.26.t:
यद्वा दहनकर्मायं सर्वत्र प्रभुरव्ययः ।
न मे दहति लाङ्गूलं कथमार्यां प्रधक्ष्यति ।
 ।
.. ।
5.55.26.e: 'If not so, the firegod who never fails in burning has not burnt my tail. How will he burn noble Sita?'

5.55.27.e: Then Hanuman thought of the appearance of mountain Hiranyanabha in the midst of water, a wonderful phenomenon.

w: of charanas (heavenly birds moving in the sky)
5.55.29.t:
स तथा चिन्तयंस्तत्र देव्या धर्मपरिग्रहम् ।
शुश्राव हनुमान्वाक्यं चारणानां महात्मनाम्
5.55.29.e: As Hanuman was thinking so, he heard the words of the great charanas who were praising the queen's power of righteousness.

5.55.30.t:
अहो खलु कृतं कर्म दुष्करं हि हनूमता ।
अग्निं विसृजताऽभीक्ष्णं भीमं राक्षसवेश्मनि
5.55.30.e: 'Oh Hanuman has indeed accomplished the marvellous task of spreading the terrific fire on the demons buildings.

5.55.34.t:
ततः कपिः प्राप्तमनोरथार्थस्तामक्षतां राजसुतां विदित्वा ।
प्रत्यक्षतस्तां पुनरेव दृष्टवा प्रतिप्रयाणाय मतिं चकार
5.55.34.e: Hanuman, having fulfilled his desires and knowing that Sita is not hurt, thought of departing after meeting Sita once again (to testify that she is really safe). इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये सुन्दरकाण्डे पञ्चपञ्चाशस्सर्गः।। Thus ends the fiftyfifth sarga of Sundarakanda  of the holy Ramayana, the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

5.56.1.t:
ततस्तु शिंशुपामूले जानकीं पर्युपस्थिताम् ।
अभिवाद्याब्रवीद्दिष्ट्या पश्यामि त्वामिहाक्षताम्
5.56.1.e: Then Hanuman offered salutations to Janaki, stationed at the foot of the simsupa tree, and said, "Luckily I see you unscathed."

w: who is chivalrous in the battle
5.56.5.t:
तद्यथा तस्य विक्रान्तमनुरूपं महात्मनः ।
भवत्याहवशूरस्य तथा त्वमुपपादय
5.56.5.e: "You should act in such a manner that the exalted Rama, who is chivalrous in the battlefield, exhibits his valour worthy of his stature".

w: with the foremost among vanaras and bears
5.56.7.t:
क्षिप्रमेष्यति काकुत्स्थः हर्यृक्षप्रवरैर्वृतः ।
यस्ते युधि विजित्यारीन् शोकं व्यपनयिष्यति
5.56.7.e: "Rama will come soon with the best of vanaras and bears. He would win the battle and remove your sorrrow.

5.56.8.t:
एवमाश्वास्य वैदेहीं हनुमान् मारुतात्मजः ।
गमनाय मतिं कृत्वा वैदेहीमभ्यवादयत्
5.56.8.e: Hanuman, son of the Windgod having consoled Vaidehi, saluted her respectfully and decided to depart.

5.56.8.1.t:
राक्षसान् प्रवरान् हत्वा नाम विश्राव्य चात्मनः ।
समाश्वास्य च वैदेहीं दर्शयित्वा परं बलम्
5.56.8.1.e: Having slain the foremost rakshasas, proclaimed his own name, comforted Vaidehi and shown his supreme strength —

w: by those choicest tall padmaka trees
hanging down from the spaces between the peaks of mountain
as if covered with an upper garment.
5.56.10.e: Mount Arishta was full of blue forestranges with choicest tall padmaka trees. With clouds hanging on the slopes of mountain peaks, it appeared as though the mountain was wrapped in an upper garment.

w: sounds of gurgling masses of waters
with different kinds of sounds of waterfalls
5.56.12.e: With the loud sounds of masses of gurgling waters, the mountain appeared as though it was standing and reciting (the Vedas) loudly. With murmuring sounds of different waterfalls, it appeared as though the mountain was singing. (The sage differentiates the steadily trickling watersound from the rhythmic musical sounds of waterfalls.)

w: as though meditating controlling all senses.
5.56.15.e: The mountain was as though hissing like a dreadful, poisonous snake. With the caves standing majestically covered with mist, the mountain appeared as if it was meditating.

w: appearing like the feet of clouds
5.56.16.t:
मेघपादनिभैः पादैः प्रक्रान्तमिव सर्वतः ।
जृंम्भमाणमिवाऽकाशे शिखरैरभ्रमालिभिः
5.56.16.e: With the ranges of foothills appearing like the feet of clouds traversing, with its peaks like garlands of clouds traversing over the mountain, it made one feel it was yawning.

w: with Sal palms Aswakarna trees and
5.56.17.t:
कूटैश्च बहुधा कीर्णैश्शोभितं बहुकन्दरैः ।
सालतालाश्वकर्णैश्च वंशैश्च बहुभिर्वृतम्
5.56.17.e: With many kinds of caves and peaks scattered all over, the mountain looked delightful. It was canopied with numerous trees like Sal, palms, Aswakarnas and bamboos.

w: decorated with colourful minerals dropping down.
5.56.18.e: It was spread with creepers filled with beautiful flowers and herds of animals. The colourful minerals flowing down decorated the mountain.

w: with heaps of rocks making (the streams' flow difficult)
attended with sages yakshas gandharvas kinnaras and nagas.
5.56.19.e: There were many streams of water flowing and rocks making it difficult for the streams to flow. The mountain was inhabited by sages, yakshas, gandharvas, kinnaras and nagas, and uragas.

w: with clusters of creepers and trees
herds of tigers scattered all over
full of trees bearing tasty roots and fruits.
5.56.20.e: The clusters of creepers, and trees bearing tasty fruits and roots were uprooted. There were caves inhabited by lions. Herds of tigers were scattered all over (by the impetus of Hanuman's pressure on the mountain).

5.56.21.t:
तमारुरोह हनुमान् पर्वतं पवनात्मजः ।
रामदर्शनशीघ्रेण प्रहर्षेणाभिचोदितः
5.56.21.e: Anxious to see Rama soon, the son of the Windgod ascended the mountain happily.

5.56.22.t:
तेन पादतलाक्रान्ता रम्येषु गिरिसानुषु ।
सघोषास्समशीर्यन्त शिलाश्चूर्णीकृतास्ततः
5.56.22.e: Crushed under Hanuman's feet the rocks making a loud noise on the beautiful mountain ranges rolled down, reduced to powder.

5.56.24.t:
अधिरुह्य ततो वीरः पर्वतं पवनात्मजः ।
ददर्श सागरं भीमं मीनोरगनिषेवितम्
5.56.24.e: Then the heroic son of the Windgod, who had ascended the mountain saw the dreadful ocean inhabited by fishes and snakes.

5.56.25.t:
स मारुत इवाऽकाशं मारुतस्यात्मसम्भवः ।
प्रपेदे हरिशार्दूलो दक्षिणादुत्तरां दिशम्
5.56.25.e: Hanuman, the tiger among monkeys leaped into the sky like the Windgod from the south to the north shore.

w: with the force of his thighs
as if struck by Indra's thunderbolt
5.56.27.t: तस्योरुवेगोन्मथिताः पादपाः पुष्पशालिनः निपेतुर्भूतले रुग्णाश्शक्रायुधहता इव ।
5.56.27.e: Shaken by the violent force of Hanuman's thighs, the blossoming trees fell on the ground like sickmen hit by Indra's thunderbolt.

w: of those residing in mountain caves
5.56.28.t: कन्दरान्तरसंस्थानां पीडितानां महौजसाम् सिंहानां निनदो भीमो नभो भिन्दन् स शुश्रुवे ।
5.56.28.e: The dreadful roar of strong lions, lying in mountaincaves was heard cracking the sky when they were crushed in the turmoil.

w: with their clothes slipped with fear
5.56.29.e: The Vidyadharis with their clothes slipped and ornaments disarrayed in fear, at once flew from the mountain.

w: pressed on their heads and necks
5.56.30.t: अतिप्रमाणा बलिनो दीप्तजिह्वा महाविषाः निपीडितशिरोग्रीवा व्यचेष्टन्त महाहयः ।
5.56.30.e: Highly powerful, huge and poisonous snakes with their glowing tongues protruded, pressed on their heads and necks (by Hanuman).

w: kinnaras uragas gandharvas yakshas and vidyadharas
5.56.31.t: किन्नरोरगन्धर्वयक्षविद्याधरास्तदा पीडितं तं नगवरं त्यक्त्वा गगनमास्थिता: ।
5.56.31.e: Then the kinnaras, uragas, gandhravas, yakshas and vidyadharas left the tortured mountain and occupied the sky.

5.56.33.t: दशयोजनविस्तारस्त्रिंशद्योजनमुच्छ्रितः धरण्यां समतां यातः स बभूव धराधरः ।
5.56.33.e: That mountain of ten yojanas in width and thirty yojanas in height got levelled with the earth.

w: with huge waves dashing towards the shore
5.56.34.t: स लिलङ्घयिषुर्भीमं सलीलं लवणार्णवम् कल्लोलास्फालवेलान्तमुत्पपात नभो हरिः ।
5.56.34.e: Eager to leap the terrific ocean lashed by huge waves hitting the shore Hanuman rose up effortlessly and jumped into the sky. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये सुन्दरकाण्डे षट्पञ्चाशस्सर्गः।। Thus ends the  fiftysixth sarga of Sundarakanda of the holy Ramayana, the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

w: Tishya and Shravana for sweetvoiced swans
clouds for duckweeds and grassy spots on the shores
the planet Mars for a crocodile
waves produced by wind for its billows
nagas yakshas gandharvas together as fully blossomed lotuses
5.57.1.t:
स चन्द्रकुमुदं रम्यं सार्ककारण्डवं शुभम् ।
तिष्यश्रवणकादम्बमभ्रशैवालशाद्वलम् पुनर्वसुमहामीनं लोहिताङ्गमहाग्रहम् ।
ऐरावतमहाद्वीपं स्वातिहंसविलोलितम् वातसङ्घातजातोर्मि चन्द्रांशुशिशिराम्बुमत् ।
भुजङ्गयक्षगन्धर्वप्रबुद्धकमलोत्पलम् हनुमान्मारुतगतिर्महानौरिव सागरम् ।
अपारमपरिश्रान्तः पुप्लुवे गगनार्णवम्
5.57.1.e: Hanuman leaped ike the Windgod, unwearied across the sky, as a huge boat crosses an ocean. The ocean was graced with a swan, the sky with constellation of Swati with fullblown lotuses and water lilies, like the nagas, yakshas, and gandharvas gathered together. The Moon in the sky was like a white lotus, the Sun like a waterfowl, the auspicious Tishya and Shravana like the sweetvoiced swans, and the clouds like duckweeds and green grassy spots on the shore. The Punarvasu star was like a large fish and the planet Mars was like a crocodile. Airavata was like the great island. The waves produced by the wind were like cool moonlight in the cold water.

5.57.5.t:
ग्रसमान इवाकाशं ताराधिपमिवोल्लिखन् ।
हरन्निव सनक्षत्रं गगनं सार्कमण्डलम् मारुतस्यात्मजः श्रीमान्कपिर्व्योमचरो महान् ।
हनुमान्मेघजालानि विकर्षन्निव गच्छति
5.57.5.e: Great Hanuman, son of the Windgod, flew through the abode of the Windgod as if he was swallowing the space, scratching the  Moon, lord of the stars, as if seizing the heavens along with the constellation of Sun and stars and as though he was drawing the clusters of clouds.

w: passing through the clouds clad in white
5.57.9.e: Passing through the clouds, appearing and disappearing, the heroic Hanuman clad in white was like the Moon in the white sky.

5.57.10.t:
तार्क्ष्यायमाणो गगने बभासे वायुनन्दनः ।
दारयन्मेघबृन्दानि निष्पतंश्च पुनः पुनः नदन्नादेन महता मेघस्वनमहास्वनः ।
5.57.10.e: As he made his way through flakes of clouds, again and again appearing and disappearing, Hanuman the delight of the Windgod shone in the sky roaring like a thundering cloud. He looked like Garuda.

5.57.11.t:
प्रवरान्राक्षसान् हत्वा नाम विश्राव्य चात्मनः आकुलां नगरीं कृत्वा व्यथयित्वा च रावणम् ।
अर्दयित्वा बलं घोरं वैदेहीमभिवाद्य च आजगाम महातेजाः पुनर्मध्येन सागरम् ।
5.57.11.e: The glorious Hanuman, having killed eminent ogres and thereby making himself widely known, having caused havoc to the city of Lanka and  terrific sorrow to Ravana by tormenting the army, offered salutations to Vaidehi from midocean and continued his journey.

5.57.14.t: स किञ्चिदनुसम्प्राप्तः समालोक्य महागिरिम् महेन्द्रं मेघसङ्काशं ननाद हरिपुङ्गवः ।
5.57.14.e: The chief of the monkeys arrived near, and beholding the face of the Mahendra mountain, which resembled a mass of clouds, thundered.

5.57.20.t: ते दीनमनसस्सर्वे शुश्रुवुः काननौकसः वानरेन्द्रस्य निर्घोषं पर्जन्यनिनदोपमम् ।
5.57.20.e: All the vanaras who were feeling dejected and waiting anxiously heard the noise of Hanuman that sounded like a thundering cloud.

w: speed of his arms and thighs
5.57.24.t: तस्य बाहूरुवेगं च निनादं च महात्मनः निशम्य हरयो हृष्टाः समुत्पेतुस्ततस्ततः ।
5.57.24.e: Hearing the sound of his dashing movements of arms and thighs the vanaras jumped about in joy, then and there.

w: from the top of a tree
to another peak of a mountain
5.57.25.t: ते नगाग्रान्नगाग्राणि शिखराच्छिखराणि च प्रहृष्टाः समपद्यन्त हनूमन्तं दिदृक्षवः ।
5.57.25.e: The vanaras were very happy. Longing to see Hanuman, they jumped from one tree top to another and from one peak of a mountain to the other.

w: like the wind in the mountain caves
5.57.27.t: गिरिगह्वरसंलीनो यथा गर्जति मारुतः एवं जगर्ज बलवान् हनुमान्मारुतात्मजः ।
5.57.27.e: Hanuman, the powerful son of the Windgod roared like the wind captured in a mountain cave would.

5.57.28.t: तमभ्रघनसङ्काशमापतन्तं महाकपिम् दृष्ट्वा ते वानरास्सर्वे तस्थुः प्राञ्जलयस्तदा ।
5.57.28.e: (On seeing) Hanuman, who was resembling a heavy cloud approaching, the vanaras stood with folded hands.

5.57.29.t: ततस्तु वेगवांस्तस्य गिरेर्गिरिनिभः कपिः निपपात महेन्द्रस्य शिखरे पादपाकुले ।
5.57.29.e: Thereafter the vanara, who resembled a mountain, descended with great speed on the summit of mount Mahendra full of trees.

5.57.31.t:
ततस्ते प्रीतमनसस्सर्वे वानरपुङ्गवाः हनुमन्तं महात्मानं परिवार्योपतस्थिरे ।
परिवार्य च ते सर्वे परां प्रीतिमुपागताः
5.57.31.e: Feeling very happy at heart all the vanara leaders gathered around Hanuman. They  stood motionless with extreme happiness.

5.57.33.1.t:
विनेदुर्मुदिताः केचित् केचित् किलकिलां तथा ।
हृष्टाः पादपशाखाश्च आनिन्युर्वानरर्षभाः
5.57.33.1.e: Some cried out delighted, and some raised a shout of joy; and the bulls among vanaras, thrilled, brought branches of trees.

5.57.35.t: स ताभ्यां पूजितः पूज्यः कपिभिश्च प्रसादितः दृष्टा सीतेति विक्रान्त स्संक्षेपेण न्यवेदयत् ।
5.57.35.e: The valiant Hanuman worthy of worship having been honoured by both Jambavan and Angada was pleased. He responded briefly, saying 'Saw Sita'.

5.57.36.t: निषसाद च हस्तेन गृहीत्वा वालिनस्सुतम् रमणीये वनोद्देशे महेन्द्रस्य गिरेस्तदा ।
5.57.36.e: Then holding the hand of Vali's son he sat down at a beautiful location of the garden of mountain Mahendra.

w: in the groves of Ashoka trees
5.57.37.t:
हनुमानब्रवीद्धृष्टस्तदा तान्वानरर्षभान् अशोकवनिकासंस्था दृष्टा सा जनकात्मजा ।
रक्षमाणा सुघोराभी राक्षसीभिरनिन्दिता एकवेणीधरा बाला रामदर्शनलालसा ।
उपवासपरिश्रान्ता जटिला मलिना कृशा
5.57.37.e: Hanuman felt happy and told Angada, the bull of vanaras, "I saw Sita in the groves of Ashoka guarded by dreadful ogres. She is blameless, eager to see Rama. She is wearing a single braid of hair. She is young and emaciated due to fasting. Her hair is matted and soiled".

5.57.40.t:
ततो दृष्टेति वचनं महार्थममृतोपमम् ।
निशम्य मारुतेस्सर्वे मुदिता वानराभवन्
5.57.40.e: Then hearing Hanuman's meaningful and nectarlike words all the vanaras rejoiced.

5.57.41.t:
क्ष्वेलन्त्यन्ये नदन्त्यन्ये गर्जन्त्यन्ये महाबलाः ।
चक्रुः किलकिलामन्ये प्रतिगर्जन्ति चापरे
5.57.41.e: Some powerful vanaras howled, some chattered, some roared and some screamed, going round and round and others echoed the sounds.

5.57.42.t:
केचिदुच्छ्रितलाङ्गूलाः प्रहृष्टाः कपिकुञ्जराः ।
आयताञ्चितदीर्घाणि लाङ्गूलानि प्रविव्यधुः
5.57.42.e: Some elephantlike vanaras who were excited and felt overjoyed lifted their long and beautiful tails and hit them on the ground.

w: from the top of the mountain
5.57.43.t:
अपरे च हनूमन्तं वानरा वारणोपमम् ।
आप्लुत्य गिरिशृङ्गेभ्यस्संस्पृशन्ति स्म हर्षिताः
5.57.43.e: A few vanaras jumped down from the mountain top and hugged the elephantlike Hanuman.

5.57.44.t:
उक्तवाक्यं हनूमन्तमङ्गदस्तमथाब्रवीत् ।
सर्वेषां हरिवीराणां मध्ये वचनमुत्तमम्
5.57.44.e: And hearing Hanuman's sweetest words, Angada addressed the heroic vanaras

5.57.45.t:
सत्त्वे वीर्ये न ते कश्चित्समो वानर विद्यते ।
यदवप्लुत्य विस्तीर्णं सागरं पुनरागतः
5.57.45.e: "O vanara you have leaped such a wide ocean and have returned. In strength and valour. There is none equal to you.

5.57.46.t:
अहो स्वामिनि ते भक्तिरहो वीर्यमहो धृतिः ।
दिष्ट्या दृष्टा त्वया देवी रामपत्नी यशस्विनी दिष्ट्या त्यक्ष्यति काकुत्स्थ श्शोकं सीतावियोगजम् ।
5.57.46.e: "O your devotion to the king, O your valour, fortitude  and courage is admirable. You could see Rama's wife, an illustrious lady. This is a matter of our good luck. Rama will (now) shed the sorrow due to separation from Sita.

5.57.47.t: ततोऽङ्गदं हनूमन्तं जाम्बवन्तं च वानराः परिवार्य प्रमुदिता भेजिरे विपुलाश्शिलाः ।
5.57.47.e: Then the vanaras went round all the three Angada, Hanuman and Jambavan. Out of joy they lay down on the huge rocks.

5.57.48.t:
श्रोतुकामास्समुद्रस्य लङ्घनं वानरोत्तमाः दर्शनं चापि लङ्कायास्सीताया रावणस्य च ।
तस्थुः प्राञ्जलयस्सर्वे हनुमद्वचनोन्मुखाः
5.57.48.e: All the vanaras longing to listen to Hanuman about his crossing the ocean, seeing Lanka, Sita and Ravana kept looking at the face of Hanuman.

5.57.50.t:
तस्थौ तत्राङ्गदः श्रीमान् वानरैर्बहुभिर्वृतः ।
उपास्यमानो विबुधैर्दिवि देवपतिर्यथा
5.57.50.e: Surrounded by many great vanaras, Angada was shining like Indra, lord of the gods attended by the gods in heaven.

5.57.51.t:
हनूमता कीर्तिमता यशस्विना तथाङ्गदेनाङ्गदबद्धबाहुना ।
मुदा तदाऽध्यासितमुन्नतं महन्महीधराग्रं ज्वलितं श्रियाभवत्
5.57.51.e: The mountain peak graced by famous Hanuman and renowned Angada bedecked with armlets seated on top joyfully, appeared prosperous and splendid. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये सुन्दरकाण्डे सप्तपञ्चाशस्सर्गः।। Thus ends the fiftyseventh sarga of Sundarakanda of the holy Ramayana, the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

5.58.1.t:
ततस्तस्य गिरेः शृङ्गे महेन्द्रस्य महाबलाः ।
हनुमत्प्रमुखाः प्रीतिं हरयो जग्मुरुत्तमाम्
5.58.1.e: Then the mighty Hanuman and other vanaras having assembled on the summit of mountain Mahendra and felt vey much happy.

5.58.2.t:
तं ततः प्रीतिसंहृष्टः प्रीतिमन्तं महाकपिम् ।
जाम्बवान्कार्यवृत्तान्तमपृच्छदनिलात्मजम्
5.58.2.e: Thereafter, very delighted Jambavan inquired Hanuman most affectionately of all that happened.

5.58.3.t:
कथं दृष्टा त्वया देवी कथं वा तत्र वर्तते ।
तस्यां वा स कथंवृत्तः क्रूरकर्मा दशाननः
5.58.3.e: "How did you find the godlike lady? How was she? How was the tenheaded one, cruel in action, behaving with her? You may narrate what she said.

5.58.4.t:
तत्त्वतस्सर्वमेतन्नः प्रब्रूहि त्वं महाकपे ।
श्रुतार्थाश्चिन्तयिष्यामो भूयः कार्यविनिश्चयम्
5.58.4.e: "O Hanuman, tell us in detail  the entire thing. On hearing it, we will think about the next course of action.

5.58.7.t:
प्रत्यक्षमेव भवतां महेन्द्राग्रात्खामाप्लुतः ।
उदधेर्दक्षिणं पारं काङ्क्षमाण स्समाहितः
5.58.7.e: "I rose upwards leaping into the sky, intent on reaching the southern shore from the mountain Mahendra.It has been witnessed directly by all of you.

w: like a form that came to obstruct
5.58.8.t:
गच्छतश्च हि मे घोरं विघ्नरूपमिवाभवत् ।
काञ्चनं शिखरं दिव्यं पश्यामि सुमनोहरम्
5.58.8.e: "Even as I was leaping I saw a terrific and wonderful golden peak which came as if to obstruct me on my path.

5.58.9.t:
स्थितं पन्धानमावृत्य मेने विघ्नं च तं नगम् ।
उपसङ्गम्य तं दिव्यं काञ्चनं नगसत्तमम् कृता मे मनसा बुद्धिर्भेत्तव्योऽयं मयेति च ।
5.58.9.e: "The mountain stood on my way turning towards me in order to obstruct me. Then I resolved in my mind that this great, wonderful, golden mountain has to be smashed.

5.58.10.t: प्रहतं च मया तस्य लाङ्गूलेन महागिरेः शिखरं सूर्यसङ्काशं व्यशीर्यत सहस्रधा ।
5.58.10.e: "Hit by my tail the great mountain peak, which was radiating like the Sun was shattered into a thousand pieces.

5.58.11.t:
व्यवसायं च तं बुद्ध्वा स होवाच महागिरिः ।
 ।
.. ।
पुत्त्रेति मधुरां वाणीं मनः प्रह्लादयन्निव ।
5.58.11.e: "Perceiving that I am going to smash him he spoke to me in a sweet tone delighting my heart, addressing me like a son.

5.58.12.t: पितृव्यं चापि मां विद्धि सखायं मातरिश्वनः मैनाकमिति विख्यातं निवसन्तं महोदधौ ।
5.58.12.e: 'Know me to be a friend of windgod and so I am like your father's brother. I am dwelling in this great ocean and known as Mainaka.

5.58.13.t: पक्षवन्तः पुरा पुत्त्र बभूवुः पर्वतोत्तमाः छन्दतः पृथिवीं चेरुर्बाधमानाः समन्ततः ।
5.58.13.e: 'O son in the past, foremost of the mountains too had wings and they used to range  at will all over the earth tormenting all.

5.58.14.t: श्रुत्वा नगानां चरितं महेन्द्रः पाकशासनः चिच्छेद भगवान् पक्षान्वज्रेणैषां सहस्रशः ।
5.58.14.e: 'Mahendra, the killer of ogre Paka, heard the story (of the cruel deeds) of mountains and cut off their wings into a thousand pieces with his thunderbolt.

5.58.17.t:
एतच्छ्रुत्वा वचस्तस्य मैनाकस्य महात्मनः कार्यमावेद्य तु गिरेरुद्यतं च मनो मम ।
तेन चाहमनुज्ञातो मैनाकेन महात्मना
5.58.17.e: "When I heard Mainaka, I told him about my intention to go up. That great self Mainaka allowed me.

5.58.20.t:
उत्तमं जवमास्थाय शेषं पन्थानमास्थितः ।
ततोऽहं सुचिरं कालं वेगेनाभ्यागमं पथि
5.58.20.e: "Then with great speed I proceeded on my path. It took a long time to cross the ocean.

w: in the midst of the ocean
5.58.21.t:
ततः पश्याम्यहं देवीं सुरसां नागमातरम् ।
समुद्रमध्ये सा देवी वचनं मामभाषत
5.58.21.e: "I saw Surasa, the mother of serpents in the midst of the ocean and she said:

5.58.22.t:
मम भक्षः प्रदिष्टस्त्वममरैर्हरिसत्तम ।
अतस्त्वां भक्षयिष्यामि विहितस्त्वं चिरस्य मे
5.58.22.e: 'O powerful monkey you are destined to be my food provided by the immortals. Therefore, I will eat you as I have I found you after a long time. (of unsatiated hunger).'

5.58.23.t:
एवमुक्त स्सुरसया प्राञ्जलिः प्रणतः स्थितः ।
विवर्णवदनो भूत्वा वाक्यं चेदमुदीरयम्
5.58.23.e: "When addressed thus by Surasa, I bowed low with joined palms, stood before her with my face turned pale, and said:

5.58.26.t:
कर्तुमर्हसि रामस्य साहाय्यं विषये सती ।
अथवा मैथिलीं दृष्ट्वा रामं चाक्लिष्टकारिणम् आगमिष्यामि ते वक्त्रं सत्यं प्रतिशृणोमि ते ।
5.58.26.e: "I told her that it is proper for her (living in the domain of Rama) to help his queen and wife. Or else, I promised after I disclose to Rama, Sita's whereabouts, I will come and enter her mouth.

5.58.29.t:
मत्प्रमाणानुरूपं च व्यादितं च मुखं तया तद्दृष्ट्वा व्यादितं चास्यं ह्रस्वं ह्यकरवं वपुः ।
तस्मिन्मुहूर्ते च पुनर्बभूवाङ्गुष्ठमात्रकः
5.58.29.e: "She too opened her mouth wide enough for my size. Seeing her distending her mouth, in a moment I became small equal to the size of thumb and came out.

5.58.31.t:
अभिपत्याशु तद्वक्त्रं निर्गतोऽहं ततः क्षणात् ।
अब्रवीत्सुरसा देवी स्वेन रूपेण मां पुनः
5.58.31.e: "Then Surasa assumed her natural form again in a moment and said this to me:

5.58.36.t:
ततो मे बुद्धिरुत्पन्ना किन्नाम गगने मम ।
ईदृशो विघ्न उत्पन्नो रूपं यत्र न दृश्यते
5.58.36.e: Then the thought arose in me: "Whose form is this in the sky that cannot be seen? What is her name, and of what kind, that I cannot discern her?"

5.58.37.t:
अधोभागेन मे दृष्टि श्शोचता पातिता मया ।
ततोऽद्राक्षमहं भीमां राक्षसीं सलिलेशयाम्
5.58.37.e: "Thinking so I looked down into the water and there I saw a terrific shedemon.

5.58.39.t:
क्वासि गन्ता महाकाय क्षुधिताया ममेप्सितः ।
भक्षः प्रीणय मे देहं चिरमाहारवर्जितम्
5.58.39.e: 'O huge monkey where are you going? I am hungry since long. I am going without food and must eat you. Make me satisfied'.

5.58.40.t:
बाढमित्येव तां वाणीं प्रत्यगृह्णामहं ततः ।
अस्यप्रमाणादधिकं तस्याः कायमपूरयम्
5.58.40.e: "I said 'well' and enlarged my body more than her mouth could hold.

5.58.41.t:
तस्याश्चास्यं महद्भीमं वर्धते मम भक्षणे ।
न च मां साधु बुबुधे मम वा विकृतं कृतम्
5.58.41.e: "She opened her huge mouth to eat me as she did not know that I had already assumed a huge ugly form on my own.

5.58.42.t:
ततोऽहं विपुलं रूपं संक्षिप्य निमिषान्तरात् ।
तस्या हृदयमादाय प्रपतामि नभ:स्थलम्
5.58.42.e: "In a moment I reduced from a huge form to a small one, entered her heart and sprang into the sky.

5.58.44.t:
शृणोमि खगतानां च सिद्धानां चारणैस्सह ।
राक्षसी सिंहिका भीमा क्षिप्रं हनुमता हता
5.58.44.e: "I heard the charanas and siddhas residing in the sky talking to each other that the fierce ogres Simhika has been killed by Hanuman in a moment.

5.58.46.t: अस्तं दिनकरे याते रक्षसां निलयं पुरम् प्रविष्टोऽहमविज्ञातो रक्षोभिर्भीमविक्रमैः ।
5.58.46.e: After the sun had set, I entered unnoticed the city that was the abode of the demons, guarded by those of fierce valour.

w: like a cloud at the dissolution of the universe
5.58.47.t: तत्र प्रविशतश्चापि कल्पान्तघनसन्निभा अट्टहासं विमुञ्चन्ती नारी काप्युत्थिता पुरः ।
5.58.47.e: As I entered the city there stood a woman, like a cloud at the dissolution of the universe, yelling and letting loose her laughter.

5.58.50.t:
अहं लङ्कापुरी वीर निर्जिता विक्रमेण ते ।
यस्मात्तस्माद्विजेतासि सर्वरक्षांस्यशेषतः
5.58.50.e: 'O hero I am the presiding deity of Lanka whom you have won by your valour. Therefore you will win many demons she foretold.

5.58.53.t:
शोचता च मया दृष्टं प्राकारेण समावृतम् ।
काञ्चनेन विकृष्टेन गृहोपवनमुत्तमम्
5.58.53.e: "While worrying like that I saw a long golden boundary wall surrounding a splendid home garden. (upabana)

w: in the midst of Ashoka garden
5.58.54.t:
स प्राकारमवप्लुत्य पश्यामि बहुपादपम् ।
अशोकवनिकामध्ये शिंशुपापादपो महान् तमारुह्य च पश्यामि काञ्चनं कदलीवनम् ।
5.58.54.e: "I crossed that boundary wall and saw many kinds of trees and in the midst of that Ashoka garden, a huge Simsupa tree. I ascended it and saw rows of banana plants.

w: whose face was emaciated due to fasting
who were fed with flesh and blood
5.58.55.t:
अदूरे शिंशुपावृक्षात्पश्यामि वरवर्णिनीम् श्यामां कमलपत्राक्षीमुपवासकृशाननाम् ।
तदेकवासस्संवीतां रजोध्वस्तशिरोरुहाम् शोकसन्तापदीनाङ्गीं सीतां भर्तृहिते स्थिताम् ।
राक्षसीभिर्विरूपाभिः क्रूराभिरभिसंवृताम् मांसशोणितभक्षाभिर्व्याघ्रीभिर्हरिणीमिव ।
5.58.55.e: "Not far from the Simsupa tree I saw beautiful Sita, of dark complexion, with eyes like lotus petals, whose face was emaciated due to fasting, wearing only a single sari (the same one since her abduction) her locks filled with dust, pathetic looking,  immersed in sorrow, meditating on her husband seated like a doe encircled by tigresses, surrounded by ugly and cruel shedemons fed on flesh and blood.

5.58.61.t:
तां दृष्ट्वा तादृशीं नारीं रामपत्नीं यशस्विनीम् ।
तत्रैव शिंशुपावृक्षे पश्यन्नहमवस्थितः
5.58.61.e: "I remained there looking on that renowned wife of Rama from the Simsupa tree.

w: sound of jingling bells of gold
5.58.62.t:
ततो हलहलाशब्दं काञ्चीनूपुरमिश्रितम् ।
शृणोम्यधिकगम्भीरं रावणस्य निवेशने
5.58.62.e: "Then I heard a deep sound mixed with jingling golden girdles and anklets coming from Ravana's residence.

5.58.64.t:
ततो रावणदाराश्च रावणश्च महाबलः ।
तं देशं समनुप्राप्ता यत्र सीताऽभवत् स्थिता
5.58.64.e: "Then arrived the powerful Ravana with his consorts to that place where Sita was and stood there.

5.58.65.t:
तं दृष्ट्वाथ वरारोहा सीता रक्षोगणेश्वरम् ।
सङ्कुच्योरूस्तनौ पीनौ बाहुभ्यां परिरभ्य च
5.58.65.e: "On seeing Ravana, the king of demons, beautiful Sita, full of fear hid her face and plump breasts between her thighs.

5.58.66.t:
वित्रस्तां परमोद्विग्नां वीक्षमाणां ततस्ततः ।
त्राणं किञ्चिदपश्यन्तीं वेपमानां तपस्विनीम् तामुवाच दशग्रीवस्सीतां परमदुःखिताम् ।
अवाक्चिराः प्रपतितो बहुमन्यस्व मामिति
5.58.66.e: "Sita was full of fear and worry, looked here and there without any protector to pacify. She was trembling in fear. To that Sita, the tenheaded Ravana bent his head down and said, 'trust me and respect me'.

w: if you do not respect me
5.58.68.t:
यदि चेत्त्वं तु दर्पान्मां नाभिनन्दसि गर्विते ।
द्वौ मासावन्तरं सीते पास्यामि रुधिरं तव
5.58.68.e: 'O Sita if in your pride, you do not respect me, I will see (drink) your blood in two months.

5.58.69.t:
एतच्छ्रुत्वा वचस्तस्य रावणस्य दुरात्मनः ।
उवाच परमक्रुद्धा सीता वचनमुत्तमम्
5.58.69.e: "Hearing the words of evilminded Ravana, Sita became very angry and spoke these approprate words:

5.58.71.t: किञ्चिद्वीर्यं तवानार्य यो मां भर्तुरसन्निधौ अपहृत्याऽऽगतः पाप ते नादृष्टो महात्मना ।
5.58.71.e: 'O ignoble one when my husband was away, you came and abducted me unseen by the great Rama. You do not have even a little courage (to win me through a straight fight).

5.58.72.t: न त्वं रामस्य सदृशो दास्येऽप्यस्य न युज्यसे यज्ञीय स्सत्यवादी च रणश्लाघी च राघवः ।
5.58.72.e: 'You are not equal to Rama and not even fit to be his servant. He does yagnas and always abides in truth. He is valiant in war.

5.58.74.t: विवृत्य नयने क्रूरे मुष्टिमुद्यम्य दक्षिणम् मैथिलीं हन्तुमारब्ध: स्त्रीभिर्हाहाकृतं तदा ।
5.58.74.e: "Then the wicked Ravana raised his eyebrows and his right fist to strike at Sita and even the shedemon there raised their voice saying, ' alas, alas '

5.58.76.t: उक्तश्च मधुरां वाणीं तया स मदनार्दितः सीतया तव किं कार्यं महेन्द्रसमविक्रमः ।
5.58.76.e: "She spoke sweetly to Ravana, who was tormented by the god of love saying, 'For what purpose do you desire Sita? You are equal to Mahendra in might'.

w: O you whose valour equals great Indra's
5.58.76.1.t:
सीतया तव किं कार्यं महेन्द्रसमविक्रम ।
मया सह रमस्वाद्य मद्विशिष्टा न जानकी
5.58.76.1.e: "What business have you with Sita, O you whose valour equals great Indra's? Take your pleasure with me today; Janaki is no better than I."

w: even gods and  daughters of gandharvas
5.58.77.t: देवगन्धर्वकन्याभिर्यक्षकन्याभिरेव च सार्धं प्रभो रमस्वेह सीतया किं करिष्यसि ।
5.58.77.e: 'O lord you enjoy with the daughters of gods, gandharvas and even the young ladies of yakshas. Why do you need Sita?'

5.58.79.t: याते तस्मिन् दशग्रीवे राक्षस्यो विकृताननाः सीतां निर्भर्त्सयामासुर्वाक्यैः क्रूरैस्सुदारुणैः ।
5.58.79.e: When that ten-headed one had gone, those ugly-faced demonesses threatened Sita with cruel and frightful words.

5.58.80.t: तृणवद्भाषितं तासां गणयामास जानकी गर्जितं च तदा तासां सीतां प्राप्य निरर्थकम् ।
5.58.80.e: "Janaki did not care for their words of threat, as though they were a blade of grass and of no use to her.

w: since their threatenings were of no use
5.58.81.t: वृथागर्जितनिश्चेष्टा राक्षस्यः पिशिताशनाः रावणाय शशंसुस्ताः सीताध्यवसितं महत् ।
5.58.81.e: "Since the threatenings of the shedemons were of no use the ogresses who live on flesh and blood reported to Ravana about great Sita's formidable determination.

5.58.82.t: ततस्तास्सहितास्सर्वा निहताशा निरुद्यमाः परिक्षिप्य समन्तात्तां निद्रावशमुपागताः ।
5.58.82.e: "Then all of them gave up hope of their efforts and scattered around her, succumbed to sleep.

5.58.83.t: तासु चैव प्रसुप्तासु सीता भर्तृहिते रता विलप्य करुणं दीना प्रशुशोच सुदुःखिता ।
5.58.83.e: When they had fallen asleep, Sita, miserable and well-wisher of her husband, cried pathetically and very sadly.

5.58.84.t:
तासां मध्यात्समुत्थाय त्रिजटा वाक्यमब्रवीत् आत्मानं खादत क्षिप्रं न सीता विनशिष्यति ।
जनकस्यात्मजा साध्वी स्नुषा दशरथस्य च
5.58.84.e: "From the midst of all of them got up Trijata, saying, 'You eat me if you like. Know that Janaka's daughter is a chaste woman and is the daughterinlaw of Dasaratha. She cannot be destroyed'.

5.58.87.t:
अलमस्मात्परित्रातुं राघवाद्राक्षसीगणम् ।
अभियाचाम वैदेहीमेतद्धि मम रोचते
5.58.87.e: 'To protect the demon clan from destruction by Rama, it is enough if we beg her (pardon). Indeed, I think that way.

w: feeling happy that he will succeed
5.58.89.t: ततस्सा ह्रीमती बाला भर्तुर्विजयहर्षिता अवोचद्यदि तत्तथ्यं भवेयं शरणं हि वः ।
5.58.89.e: 'On hearing the words (of Trijata) that 'Rama will succeed', young and bashful Sita felt happy and said that 'If it comes true I will protect thee'.

5.58.90.t:
तां चाहं तादृशीं दृष्ट्वा सीताया दारुणां दशाम् ।
चिन्तयामास विक्रान्तो न च मे निर्वृतं मनः
5.58.90.e: "Seeing Sita's deplorable state, her illluck and her dread, I began  to worry and had no peace of mind.

w: sanctified by the names of royal seers
5.58.92.t: श्रुत्वा तु गदितां वाचं राजर्षिगणपूजिताम् प्रत्यभाषत मां देवी बाष्पैः पिहितलोचना ।
5.58.92.e: "The divine lady heard my enumeration, sanctifying the royal seers. She replied me, with  her eyes blinded by tears:

5.58.93.t: कस्त्वं केन कथं चेह प्राप्तो वानरपुङ्गवः का च रामेण ते प्रीतिस्तन्मे शंसितुमर्हसि ।
5.58.93.e: "O foremost of vanaras who are you? Why and how have you come here? How did you make friendship with Rama? Tell me all that in detail.

5.58.94.t:
तस्यास्तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा ह्यहमप्यब्रुवं वचः देवि रामस्य भर्तुस्ते सहायो भीमविक्रमः ।
सुग्रीवो नाम विक्रान्तो वानरेन्द्रो महाबलः
5.58.94.e: "Hearing her I also said, 'O queen Sugriva, the warrior of fierce valour and king of monkeys developed friendship with your husband'.

5.58.96.t:
तस्य मां विद्धि भृत्यं त्वं हनुमन्तमिहागतम् ।
भर्त्राहं प्रेषितस्तुभ्यं रामेणाक्लिष्टकर्मणा
5.58.96.e: 'I came here as a servant sent by your tireless husband to find you.

5.58.97.t:
इदं च पुरुषव्याघ्रः श्रीमान् दाशरथिः स्वयम् ।
अङ्गुलीयमभिज्ञानमदात्तुभ्यं यशस्विनि
5.58.97.e: 'O glorious lady the tiger among men, the illustrious son of Dasaratha himself sent this ring to you as a taken of identity.

5.58.98.t:
तदिच्छामि त्वयाऽऽज्ञप्तं देवि किं करवाण्यहम् ।
रामलक्ष्मणयोः पार्श्वं नयामि त्वां किमुत्तरम्
5.58.98.e: 'O venerable lady I seek your order. What should I do? Should I take you to  Rama and Lakshmana? What do you say?

5.58.99.t:
एतच्छ्रुत्वा विदित्वा च सीता जनकनन्दिनी ।
आहरावणमुत्साद्य राघवो मां नयत्विति
5.58.99.e: "Having heard all that (Hanuman said) Sita, the delight of Janaka thought over and said, 'Rama should kill Ravana and take me'.

5.58.101.t:
अथ मामब्रवीत्सीता गृह्यतामयमुत्तमः ।
मणिर्येन महाबाहू रामस्त्वां बहुमन्यते
5.58.101.e: "Sita then said to me, 'Take this best of gems and present it to the longarmed Rama as a token'.

5.58.103.t:
ततस्तस्यै प्रणम्याहं राजपुत्र्यै समाहितः ।
प्रदक्षिणं परिक्राममिहाभ्युद्गतमानसः
5.58.103.e: "Reminded by her again (that Rama should turn up soon to take her), I offered reverential salutations by circumambulating her.

5.58.106.t:
यद्यन्यथा भवेदेतद्द्वौ मासौ जीवितं मम ।
न मां द्रक्ष्यति काकुत्स्थो म्रिये साहमनाथवत्
5.58.106.e: 'Otherwise with none to protect me, I will live only  for two months.I will die like an orphan and he will not see me'.

5.58.107.t:
तच्छ्रुत्वा करुणं वाक्यं क्रोधो मामभ्यवर्तत ।
उत्तरं च मया दृष्टं कार्यशेषमनन्तरम्
5.58.107.e: "When I heard her pathetic appeal, I was overtaken by anger. I perceived the task left over for me to do.

5.58.108.t:
ततोऽवर्धत मे कायस्तदा पर्वतसन्निभः ।
युद्धकाङ्क्षी वनं तच्च विनाशयितुमारभे
5.58.108.e: "Thereafter, I increased my body to the size of a mountain, intent on fighting and started destroying the pleasure garden.

5.58.109.t:
तद्भग्नं वनषण्डं तु भ्रान्तत्रस्तमृगद्विजम् ।
प्रतिबुद्धा निरीक्षन्ते राक्षस्यो विकृताननाः
5.58.109.e: "Those uglyfaced ogresses woke up and saw the devastated garden and terrified beasts and birds.

5.58.110.t:
मां च दृष्ट्वा वने तस्मिन् समागम्य ततस्ततः ।
ता स्समभ्यागताः क्षिप्रं रावणायाचचक्षिरे
5.58.110.e: Collecting here and there, they saw me in that garden, and at once understanding, they told Ravana of it.

5.58.111.t:
राजस्वनमिदं दुर्गं तव भग्नं दुरात्मना ।
वानरेण ह्यविज्ञाय तव वीर्यं महाबल
5.58.111.e: 'O powerful king an evilminded vanara has destroyed the inaccessible pleasure garden not knowing your valour.

w: who has done contrary to your interest
5.58.112.t:
दुर्बुद्धेस्तस्य राजेन्द्र तव विप्रियकारिणः ।
वधमाज्ञापय क्षिप्रं यथासौ विलयं व्रजेत्
5.58.112.e: 'O king may orders be issued to kill this wickedminded vanara wandering aimlessly. He has done contrary to your interest.

5.58.113.t:
तच्छ्रुत्वा राक्षसेन्द्रेण विसृष्टा भृशदुर्जयाः ।
राक्षसाः किङ्करा नाम रावणस्य मनोनुगाः
5.58.113.e: "Ravana, lord of the demons having heard (the ogresses) sent invincible ogres called kinkaras who know his mind.

5.58.115.t:
तेषां तु हतशेषा ये ते गत्वा लघुविक्रमाः ।
निहतं च महत्सैन्यं रावणायाचचक्षिरे
5.58.115.e: "Those who were left behind, the less powerful ones went and reported to Ravana that the great army has been killed.

5.58.116.t:
ततो मे बुद्धिरुत्पन्ना चैत्यप्रासादमाक्रमम् ।
तत्रस्थान्राक्षसान् हत्वा शतं स्तम्भेन वै पुनः ललामभूतो लङ्कायास्स वै विध्वंसितो मया ।
5.58.116.e: "Then a thought struck my mind. I took hold of a pillar of the tall, decorated mansion of Lanka and killed with it all the hundred demons stationed there.

5.58.117.t: ततः प्रहस्तस्य सुतं जम्बुमालिनमादिशत् राक्षसैर्बहुभिस्सार्धं घोररूपैर्भयानकैः ।
5.58.117.e: Then he ordered Jambumali, the son of Prahasta, together with many ogres of terrific and frightening appearance.

5.58.122.t:
तानहं सहसैन्यान्वै सर्वानेवाभ्यसूदयम् ।
ततः पुनर्दशग्रीवः पुत्रमक्षं महाबलम् बहुभी राक्षसैस्सार्धं प्रेषयामास रावणः ।
5.58.122.e: "Since I killed all of them along with the army, the tenheaded Ravana sent out his mighty son Aksha together with many demons.

5.58.123.t:
तं तु मन्दोदरीपुत्त्रं कुमारं रणपण्डितम् सहसा खं समुत्क्रान्तं पादयोश्च गृहीतवान् ।
चर्मासिनं शतगुणं भ्रामयित्वा व्यपेषयम्
5.58.123.e: "When Mandodari's son, an expert in war had risen up to the sky I caught his feet and whirled him round a hundred times and smashed him.

5.58.125.t:
तमक्षमागतं भग्नं निशम्य स दशाननः ।
तत इन्द्रजितं नाम द्वितीयं रावणस्सुतम् व्यादिदेश सुसंकृद्धो बलिनम् युद्धदुर्मदम् ।
5.58.125.e: "When Aksha was done to death, the tenfaced Ravana was enraged and gave instruction to the second son, called Indrajit who was thirsting for war.

5.58.126.t: तच्चाप्यहं बलं सर्वं तं च राक्षसपुङ्गवम् नष्टौजसं रणे कृत्वा परं हर्षमुपागमम् ।
5.58.126.e: "When the army and even the Generals were done to death in combat I was very happy.

5.58.130.t: दृष्ट्वा सम्भाषितश्चाहं रावणेन दुरात्मना पृष्टश्च लङ्कागमनं राक्षसानां च तं वधम् ।
5.58.130.e: "The wickedminded Ravana, then enquired me why I came to Lanka and why I killed the demons.

5.58.131.t:
तत्सर्वं च मया तत्र सीतार्थमिति जल्पितम् अस्याहं दर्शनाकाङ्क्षी प्राप्तस्त्वद्भवनं विभो ।
मारुतस्यौरसः पुत्रो वानरो हनुमानहम्
5.58.131.e: 'I have done all this for the sake of Sita, O demon king I came to your mansion desiring to see Sita. I am the legitimate son of Windgod. My name is Hanuman.

5.58.133.t:
रामदूतं च मां विद्धि सुग्रीवसचिवं कपिम् ।
सोऽहं दूत्येन रामस्य त्वत्सकाशमिहागतः
5.58.133.e: 'I am a vanara, a messenger of Rama and minister of Sugriva.You may know that I have come here to convey the message of Rama to you.

w: in accordance with dharma wealth and wellbeing
5.58.134.t:
सुग्रीवश्च महातेजास्सत्वां कुशलमब्रवीत् ।
धर्मार्थकामसहितं हितं पथ्यमुवाच च
5.58.134.e: 'Highly powerful Sugriva enquires your welfare. He sends beneficial advice to you for your righteousness, pleasures and wellbeing.

5.58.135.t:
वसतो ऋश्यमूके मे पर्वते विपुलद्रुमे ।
राघवो रणविक्रान्तो मित्त्रत्वं समुपागतः
5.58.135.e: 'While I was dwelling at the woodedmountain in Rshyamuka, a treaty of friendship was made with Rama, who is skilled in war.

5.58.136.t:
तेन मे कथितं राज्ञा भार्या मे रक्षसा हृता ।
तत्र साहाय्यमस्माकं कार्यं सर्वात्मना त्वया
5.58.136.e: 'The king said, ' My wife was abducted by a demon. I request your help by all means to get her'.

5.58.137.t:
मया च कथितं तस्मै वालिनश्च वधं प्रति ।
तत्र साहाय्यहेतोर्मे समयं कर्तुमर्हसि
5.58.137.e: 'Sugriva told the story of Vali in turn and asked for his help and to make agreement to kill Vali.

5.58.139.t:
तेन वालिनमुत्पाट्य शरेणैकेन संयुगे ।
वानराणां महाराजः कृतस्स प्लवतां प्रभुः
5.58.139.e: 'In the combat Rama killed Vali with a single arrow and made Sugriva the king of vanaras.

5.58.140.t:
तस्य साहाय्यमस्माभिः कार्यं सर्वात्मना त्विह ।
तेन प्रस्थापितस्तुभ्यं समीपमिह धर्मतः
5.58.140.e: 'We too have to help him in this task. So a message is sent to you on righteous grounds.

5.58.141.t:
क्षिप्रमानीयतां सीता दीयतां राघवाय च ।
यावन्न हरयो वीरा विधमन्ति बलं तव
5.58.141.e: 'Before the heroic vanaras exterminate your entire army, return Sita at once to Rama.

5.58.142.t:
वानराणां प्रभावो हि न केन विदितः पुरा ।
देवतानां सङ्काशं च ये गच्छन्ति निमन्त्रिताः
5.58.142.e: 'Who knows not the power of Vanaras in the past? Even gods had sought their help.

5.58.147.t:
दूतवध्या न दृष्टा हि राजशास्त्रेषु राक्षस ।
दूतेन वेदितव्यं च यथार्थं हितवादिना
5.58.147.e: 'The royal code prohibits the murder of an emissary. A wellwishing emissary should convey the truth.

5.58.148.t:
सुमहत्यपराधेऽपि दूतस्यातुलविक्रमः ।
विरूपकरणं दृष्टं न वधोऽस्तीति शास्त्रतः
5.58.148.e: 'O Ravana of immeasurable courage even if the emissary has done any kind of harm he may be mutilated but not murdered. Nowhere do the sastras allow killing (of an ambassador).

5.58.149.t:
विभीषणेनैवमुक्तो रावणस्सन्दिदेश तान् ।
राक्षसानेतदेवास्य लाङ्गूलं दह्यतामिति
5.58.149.e: 'On hearing Vibhishana, Ravana instructed the demons to burn my tail.

5.58.151.t:
राक्षसाः सिद्धसन्नाहास्ततस्ते चण्डविक्रमाः ।
तदाऽदह्यन्त मे पुच्छं निघ्नन्त: काष्ठमुष्टिभिः बद्धस्य बहुभिः पाशैर्यन्त्रितस्य च राक्षसैः ।
5.58.151.e: "Many ferociously courageous demons got ready. They bound me and hit me with firesticks and fists. They fastened my tail with ropes and set in on fire.

w: of me who wished to see
5.58.151.1.t:
बद्धस्य बहुभिः पाशैर्यन्त्रितस्य च राक्षसैः ।
न मे पीडाभवत् काचिद् दिदृक्षोर्नगरी दिवा
5.58.151.1.e: "Though I was bound with many bonds and fettered by the rakshasas, no distress came to me, for I wished to see the city by day."

5.58.153.t:
ततोऽहं सुमहद्रूपं संक्षिप्य पुनरात्मनः विमोचयित्वा तं बन्धं प्रकृतिस्थः स्थितः पुनः ।
आयसं परिघं गृह्य तानि रक्षांस्यसूदयम्
5.58.153.e: "I reduced my form and rid of the bondage. Then again I assumed my original huge form and took up an iron bar lying near and killed all the demons (present).

w: not even one place was left unburnt
5.58.156.t: विनष्टा जानकी व्यक्तं न ह्यदग्धः प्रदृश्यते लङ्कायां कश्चिदुद्धेशः सर्वा भस्मीकृता पुरी ।
5.58.156.e: "Clearly Janaki must have been burnt with Lanka; perhaps, so I thought, no place at all was left unburnt."

5.58.157.t: दहता च मया लङ्कां दग्धा सीता न संशयः रामस्य हि महत्कार्यं मयेदं वितथीकृतम् ।
5.58.157.e: "Lanka has been burnt by me and Sita might have also been burnt. There is no doubt. The great purpose of Rama has been spoilt by me'.

5.58.158.t:
इति शोकसमाविष्टश्चिन्तामहमुपागतः अथाहं वाचमश्रौषं चारणानां शुभाक्षराम् ।
जानकी न च दग्धेति विस्मयोदन्तभाषिणाम्
5.58.158.e: "Thus I was overtaken by sorrow and worry. Just then I heard the wonderful propitious utterances of charanas announcing that Sita was not burnt.

5.58.160.t:
ततो मे बुद्धिरुत्पन्ना श्रुत्वा तामद्भुतां गिरम् ।
अदग्धा जानकीत्येवं निमित्तैश्चोपलक्षिता
5.58.160.e: "It was amazing to hear the words of the charanas. On hearing that Jankai had not been burnt, I understood that it is on her account (that he is also not burnt  although his tail was ignited.)

5.58.161.t:
दीप्यमाने तु लाङ्गूले न मां दहति पावकः ।
हृदयं च प्रहृष्टं मे वातास्सुरभिगन्धिनः
5.58.161.e: "My tail was burning but I was not burnt by fire. There was joy in my heart. The wind carried sweet fragrance.

w: uttered by the words of sages
5.58.162.t:
तैर्निमित्तैश्च दृष्टाथै: कारणैश्च महागुणैः ।
ऋषिवाक्यैश्च सिद्धार्थैरभवं हृष्टमानसः
5.58.162.e: "For these two auspicious signs and the highly propitious words uttered by the sages I felt glad at heart.

5.58.166.t: एतत्सर्वं मया तत्र यथावदुपपादितम् अत्र यन्न कृतं शेषं तत्सर्वं क्रियतामिति ।
5.58.166.e: "Let all that could not be done there and still remains to be done, be accomplished by you. I have presented the entire thing". इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये सुन्दरकाण्डे अष्टपञ्चाशस्सर्गः।। Thus ends the fiftyeighth sarga of Sundarakanda of the holy Ramayana, the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

5.59.1.t:
एतदाख्याय तत्सर्वं हनुमान्मारुतात्मजः ।
भूयस्समुपचक्राम वचनं वक्तुमुत्तरम्
5.59.1.e: Hanuman, son of the Windgod having narrated in detail all that had happened again started disclosing further details৷৷

5.59.2.t:
सफलो राघवोद्योग स्सुग्रीवस्य च सम्भ्रमः ।
शीलमासाद्य सीताया मम च प्रवणं मनः
5.59.2.e: "It is due to Rama's exertions, Sugriva's endeavour and Sita's conduct that I have been successful. My devotion to Sita has further deepened.

5.59.4.t:
तस्य तां स्पृशतो गात्रं तपसा न विनाशितम् ।
न तदग्निशिखा कुर्यात्संस्पृष्टा पाणिना सती जनकस्यात्मजा कुर्याद्यत्क्रोधकलुषीकृता ।
5.59.4.e: "Sita can burn Ravana with the mere touch of her body but because of the power of his penance, he was not burnt even though he touched her hand. If enraged, Janaki can burn the whole world (by virtue of her chastity) in a way that even the flame of fire can not do. (But she desired that her husband should kill him.)

w: with Jambavan and other important people
5.59.5.t:
जाम्बवत्प्रमुखान् सर्वाननुज्ञाप्य महाहरीन् अस्मिन्नेवं गते कार्ये भवतां च निवेदिते ।
न्याय्यं स्म सह वैदेह्या द्रष्टुं तौ पार्थिवात्मजौ
5.59.5.e: "Now that this task of yours has been reported to you, and things have gone thus —

5.59.7.t:
अहमेकोऽपि पर्याप्तस्सराक्षसगणां पुरीम् ।
तां लङ्कां तरसा हन्तुं रावणं च महाबलम्
5.59.7.e: "I alone am enough to slay quickly all the demon troops of that city of Lanka, its great army and Ravana too."

5.59.8.t:
किं पुन स्सहितो वीरैर्बलवद्भिः कृतात्मभिः ।
कृतास्त्रै: प्लवगैश्शूरैर्भवद्भिविजयैषिभिः
5.59.8.e: "When strong, wise and accomplished persons are there with me desiring victory  why speak again?

5.59.9.t:
अहं तु रावणं युद्धे ससैन्यं सपुरस्सरम् ।
सहपुत्त्रं वधिष्यामि सहोदरयुतं युधि
5.59.9.e: "I can also kill all the army,  his followers, sons and brothers of Ravana in war.

5.59.11.t:
भवतामभ्यनुज्ञातो विक्रमो मे रुणद्धि तम् मयातुला विसृष्टा हि शैलवृष्टिर्निरन्तरा ।
देवानपि रणे हन्यात्किं पुनस्तान्निशाचरान्
5.59.11.e: Now if I am permitted, I shall repulse them and destroy them with my valour. A  ceaseless shower of rocks sent forth by me in war is enough to destroy even gods what to say about the nightrangers?

5.59.13.t:
सागरोऽप्यतियाद्वेलां मन्दरः प्रचलेदपि ।
न जाम्बवन्तं समरे कम्पयेदरिवाहिनी
5.59.13.e: "The ocean may exceed its limits, the mountain Mandara may be shaken from its position but  no hostile army can move Jambavan in war.

w: by the speed of his thighs
5.59.15.t:
पनसस्योरुवेगेन नीलस्य च महात्मनः ।
मन्दरोऽप्यवशीर्येत किंपुनर्युधि राक्षसाः ।
 ।
.. ।
5.59.15.e: "Even the mountain Mandara would be shattered by great Panasa or Nila by the speed of their thighs. What to say in a battle against ogres?

5.59.16.t:
सदेवासुरयक्षेषु गन्धर्वोरगपक्षिषु ।
मैन्दस्य प्रतियोद्धारं शंसत द्विविदस्य वा
5.59.16.e: "Who among gods, yakshas, gandharvas, nagas and birds can contend Mainda or Dvivida in battle?Tell me.

w: Brahma the grandfather of all worlds
5.59.19.e: "Earlier Brahma, the grandsire of all worlds has given the Aswini sons immeasurable invulnerability to honour them.

5.59.21.t:
एतावेव हि सङ्कृद्धौ सवाजिरथकुञ्जराम् ।
लङ्कां नाशयितुं शक्तौ सर्वे तिष्ठन्तु वानराः
5.59.21.e: "If these two become angry they have the power to destroy Lanka, the cavalry, chariots and also the elephants even if the vanaras stay away.

5.59.22.t:
मयैव निहता लङ्का दग्धा भस्मीकृता पुनः ।
राजमार्गेषु सर्वत्र नाम विश्रावितं मया
5.59.22.e: "I have burnt Lanka and have made my name popular even on the highways.

5.59.23.t:
जयत्यतिबलो रामो लक्ष्मणश्च महाबलः ।
राजा जयति सुग्रीवो राघवेणाभिपालितः अहं कोसलराजस्य दासः पवनसम्भवः ।
हनुमानिति सर्वत्र नाम विश्रावितं मया
5.59.23.e: "Mighty Rama and Lakshmana and King Sugriva protected by Rama are renowned for their valour. I am Hanuman, son of the Windgod, a servant of Rama. This I announced.

w: in the midst of Ashoka garden
5.59.25.t:
अशोकवनिकामध्ये रावणस्य दुरात्मनः ।
अध स्ताच्छिंशुपावृक्षे साध्वी करुणमास्थिता राक्षसीभिः परिवृता शोकसंतापकर्शिता ।
मेघलेखापरिवृता चन्द्रलेखेव निष्प्रभा ।
अचिन्तयन्ती वैदेही रावणं बलदर्पितम् ।
5.59.25.e: "In the wicked, Ravana's Ashoka garden under the Simsupa tree the noble lady Sita surrounded by ogresses, is sitting, tormented by tears. Her brightness is like the Moon's, veiled by flakes of clouds. She does not care for Ravana's glory. She is brooding over Rama only.

w: like Sachi the wife of Indra
5.59.27.t:
पतिव्रता च सुश्रोणी अवष्टब्धा च जानकी अनुरक्ता हि वैदेही रामं सर्वात्मना शुभा ।
अनन्यचित्ता रामे च पौलोमीव पुरन्दरे
5.59.27.e: "Chaste Sita of beautiful hips, an auspicious lady though bound is wholly devoted to Rama alone like Sachi, the wife of Indra who was bound by Nahusha.

w: thinking of her husband all the time
5.59.30.t:
सा मया राक्षसीमध्ये तर्ज्यमाना मुहुर्मुहुः ।
राक्षसीभिर्विरूपाभिर्दृष्टा हि प्रमदावने एकवेणीधरा दीना भर्तृचिन्तापरायणा ।
अधश्शय्या विवर्णाङ्गी पद्मिनीव हिमागमे रावणाद्विनिवृत्तार्था मर्तव्यकृतनिश्चया ।
5.59.30.e: "I saw Sita often threatened by uglylooking ogresses. Wearing a single braid, she looked pathetic, thinking always about her husband, lying on the bare ground. She was like a lustreless lotus in winter. Spurning the advances by Ravana, she is rather determined to commit suicide.

5.59.34.t:
नियतस्समुदाचारो भक्तिर्भर्तरि चोत्तमा ।
यन्न हन्ति दशग्रीवं सा महात्मा कृतागसम्
5.59.34.e: "Ravana is a great soul because, even though he has done harm to her, he is not killed. This is because Sita being a chaste woman of good conduct and deep devotion towards her husband (she refrained from killing Ravana as she wanted her husband to do that.)

w: by the separation from her husband
just as a student on the new Moon day
5.59.35.t:
निमित्तमात्रं रामस्तु वधे तस्य भविष्यति ।
सा प्रकृत्यैव तन्वङ्गी तद्वियोगाच्च कर्शिता प्रतिपत्पाठशीलस्य विद्येव तनुमतां गता ।
5.59.35.e: "To Rama, killing Ravana is easy (since Ravana's power of penance has already declined by his abduction of Sita). Separated from her husband she is naturally emaciated. She has become slender just like a student on the new Moon day (on the first day of study).

5.60.1.t:
तस्य तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा वालिसूनुरभाषत ।
अयुक्तं तु विना देवीं दृष्टवद्भिश्च वानराः समीपं गन्तुमस्माभी राघवस्य महात्मनः ।
5.60.1.e: After hearing Hanuman,  Vali's son said" O vanaras (Hanuman) having seen Sita it is not proper on our part to go without Sita to the great soul Rama.

5.60.3.1.t:
जित्वा लङ्कां सरक्षौघां हत्वा तं रावणं रणे ।
सीतामादाय गच्छामः सिद्धार्था हृष्टमानसाः
5.60.3.1.e: "Having conquered Lanka with its hosts of rakshasas and slain Ravana in battle, let us take Sita and go, our purpose accomplished and glad at heart."

5.60.4.t: तेष्वेवं हतवीरेषु राक्षसेषु हनूमता किमन्यदत्र कर्तव्यं गृहीत्वा याम जानकीम् ।
5.60.4.e: "Hence, having killed the heroes among ogres what other task has Hanuman to do? Let us get Sita.

5.60.4.1.t:
रामलक्ष्मणयोर्मध्ये न्यस्याम जनकात्मजाम् ।
किं व्यलीकैस्तु तान् सर्वान् वानरान्वानरर्षभान्
5.60.4.1.e: "Let us set the daughter of Janaka in the midst of Rama and Lakshmana. But with what falsehoods shall we deal with all those vanaras, bulls among vanaras?"

w: knower of ways of execution of tasks
5.60.5.t: तमेवं कृतसङ्कल्पं जाम्बवान् हरिसत्तमः उवाच परमप्रीतो वाक्यमर्थवदर्थवित् ।
5.60.5.e: "Jambavan, the noble vanara, skilled in the execution of tasks thus commanded in a determined manner:

5.60.6.t:
न तावदेषा मतिरक्षमा नो यथा भवान् पश्यति राजपुत्र ।
यथा तु रामस्य मतिर्निविष्टा तथा भवान् पश्यतु कार्यसिद्धिम्
5.60.6.e: "O prince what you think is  acceptable to us also. Even though we are capable of achieving, knowing what is in Rama's mind, we should act only according to his command to accomplish the task. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये सुन्दरकाण्डे षष्टितमस्सर्गः।। Thus ends the sixtieth sarga of Sundarakanda of the holy Ramyana, the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

w: from the summit of Mahendra mountain
led by the son of the Windgod
5.61.2.t:
प्रीतिमन्तस्ततः सर्वे वायुपुत्रपरस्पराः ।
महेन्द्राद्रिं परित्यज्य पुप्लुवुः प्लवगर्षभाः मेरुमन्दरसङ्काशा मत्ता इव महागजाः ।
छादयन्त इवाकाशं महाकाया महाबलाः सभाज्यमानं भूतैस्तमात्मवन्तं महाबलम् ।
हनूमन्तं महावेगं वहन्त इव दृष्टिभिः राघवे चार्थनिर्ववृत्तिं कर्तुं च परमं यशः ।
समाधाय समृद्धार्थाः सर्वेसिद्धिभिरुन्नता प्रियाख्यानोन्मुखाः सर्वे सर्वे युद्धाभिनन्दिनः ।
सर्वे रामप्रतीकारे निश्चितार्था मनस्स्विनः
5.61.2.e: Thereafter led by Hanuman, all the vanaras left Mahendra mountain and marched very happily. The vanaras were strong and huge like elephants and resembled mountain Meru. Moreover when they leaped up they seemed to cover the sky (so it was difficult to tell their numbers). Since Hanuman had accomplished the task, the vanaras were praising his strength, his swiftness and courage. They were looking at Hanuman without blinking their eyes, and seemed as though they were carrying him by their eyes. They were determined in their minds to please Rama. Remaining in a state of offering themselves, some of them more accomplished than others, collected together eager to wage war and talking pleasantly among themselves having resolved to assist Rama.

5.61.7.t:
प्लवमानाः खमाप्लुत्य ततस्ते काननौकसः ।
नन्दनोपमयासेदुर्वनं द्रुमलतायुतम्
5.61.7.e: "The monkeys leaped into the sky and entered the garden that resembled the garden of Indra filled with trees and creepers.

5.61.8.t:
यत्तन्मधुवनं नाम सुग्रीवस्याभिरक्षितम् ।
अधृष्यं सर्वभूतानां सर्वभूतमनोहरम्
5.61.8.e: The Madhuvanam of Sugriva was wellprotected  and was difficult to access for the vanaras. It was enchating to all beings.

5.61.10.t:
ते तद्वनमुपागम्य बभूवुः परमोत्कटाः ।
वानरा वानरेन्द्रस्य मनः कान्ततमं महत्
5.61.10.e: On reaching the vanara king's extensive, delightful garden all the vanaras highly rejoiced.

5.61.11.t:
ततस्ते वानरा हृष्टा दृष्टवा मधुवनं महत् ।
कुमारमभ्ययाचन्त मधूनि मधुपिङ्गलाः
5.61.11.e: The honeycoloured monkeys felt happy on seeing the Madhuvanam and sought Angada's permission to drink honey.

5.61.12.t:
ततः कुमारस्तान् वृद्धान् जाम्बवत्प्रमुखान् कपीन् ।
अनुमान्य ददौ तेषां विसर्गं मधुभिक्षणे
5.61.12.e: Young Angada asked old Jambavan's permission for the vanaras to drink honey and Jambavan permitted them.

5.61.13.t:
ततश्चानुमता स्सर्वे सम्प्रहृष्टा वनौकसः ।
मुदिताः प्रेरिताश्चापि प्रनृत्यन्तोऽभवंस्तदा
5.61.13.e: Permitted thus to drink honey the forestdwelling monkeys were motivated. They rejoiced very happily and started dancing.

5.61.14.t:
गायन्ति केचित्प्रणमन्ति केचिन्नृत्यन्ति केचित्प्रहसन्ति केचित् ।
पतन्ति केचिद्विचरन्ति केचित्ल्पवन्ति केचित्प्रलपन्ति केचित्
5.61.14.e: Some sang, some prostrated on the ground, some danced, while some laughed, some jumped from the tree, some roamed about and some jumped up and down.

5.61.15.t:
परस्परं केचिदुपाश्रयन्ते परस्परं केचिदुपाक्रमन्ते ।
परस्परं केचिदुपब्रुवन्ते परस्परं केचिदुपारमन्ते
5.61.15.e: While some supported one another, some held each other, some exchanged secrets with one another, some entertained one another.

w: from the top of tree jumped down
5.61.16.t:
द्रुमाद्द्रुमं केचिदभिद्रवन्ते क्षितौ नगाग्रान्निपतन्ति केचित् ।
महीतलात्केचिदुदीर्णवेगा महाद्रुमाग्राण्यभिसम्पतन्ति
5.61.16.e: While some ran from one tree to another, some jumped down from broken branches, and some swiftfooted ones fell down from the top of trees.

w: asked them to stop and get out.
5.61.19.t:
ततो वनं तत्परिभक्ष्यमाणं द्रुमांश्च विध्वंसितपत्रपुष्पान् ।
समीक्ष्य कोपाद्धधिवक्रनामा निवारयामास कपिः कपींस्तान्
5.61.19.e: Beholding the destruction wrought by the vanaras to the garden, trees, leaves and flowers, and having drunk all the honey, Dadhimukha angrily asked them to stop and get out.

5.61.20.t:
स तैः प्रवृद्धैः परिभर्त्स्यमानो वनस्य गोप्ता हरिवीरवृद्धः ।
चकार भूयो मतिमुग्रतेजा वनस्य रक्षां प्रति वानरेभ्यः
5.61.20.e: The elderly Dadhimukha who was the powerful protector of the garden reprimanded them and devised yet again a plan to protect it.

w: with the palm of the hand
5.61.21.t:
उवाच कांश्चित्परुषाणि धृष्टमसक्तमन्यांश्च तलैर्जघान ।
समेत्य कैश्चित्कलहं चकार तथैव साम्नोपजगाम कांश्चित्
5.61.21.e: He spoke harshly to some, to others he asked not to talk, some he slapped on the hind part with the palm of his hand. To some he spoke pleasantly and with some he quarrelled. And to others he spoke in a conciliatory manner.

5.61.22.t:
स तैर्मदात्संपरिवार्य वाक्यैर्भलाच्छ तेन प्रतिवार्यमाणैः ।
प्रधर्षितस्त्यक्तभयै स्समेत्य प्रकृष्यते चाप्यनवेक्ष्य दोषम्
5.61.22.e: In their drunkenness they were using abusive language and with their strength they retaliated without fear. They invaded without considering their mistakes. They caught hold of Dadhimukha and pulled him.

5.61.23.t:
नखैस्तुदन्तो दशनैर्दशन्त स्तलैश्च पादैश्च समापयन्तः ।
मदात्कपिं तं कपय स्समग्रा महावनं निर्विषयं च चक्रुः
5.61.23.e: In their drunkenness some monkeys scratched Dadhimukha violently with their nails, some bit him with their teeth and others slapped and kicked him with their palms and legs.Getting together they looted the garden completely. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये सुन्दरकाण्डे एकषष्टितम स्सर्गः।। Thus ends the sixtyfirst sarga of Sundarakanda of the holy Ramayana, the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

w: devoid of any fear in your mind
5.62.1.t:
तानुवाच हरिश्रेष्ठो हनुमान्वानरर्षभः ।
अव्यग्रमनसो यूयं मधु सेवत वानराः अहमावारयिष्यामि युष्माकं परिपन्थिनः ।
5.62.1.e: Hanuman, the foremost of the monkeys, bull among vanaras said, 'Enjoy the honey devoid of any fear. I shall prevent those who object to your action'.

5.62.2.t: श्रुत्वा हनुमतो वाक्यं हरीणां प्रवरोऽङ्गदः प्रत्युवाच प्रसन्नात्मा पिबन्तु हरयो मधु ।
5.62.2.e: Pleased with Hanuman's words, the distinguished Angada permitted the monkeys to drink.

w: one who has accomplished the task
5.62.3.t: अवश्यं कृतकार्यस्य वाक्यं हनुमतो मया अकार्यमपि कर्तव्यं किमङ्ग पुनरीदृशम् ।
5.62.3.e: Even if Hanuman, the achiever, forbids me to do something, I will do it. And now when he has permitted you, why hesitate ?

5.62.4.t: अङ्गदस्य मुखाच्छ्रुत्वावचनं वानरर्षभाः साधुसाध्विति संहृष्टा वानराः प्रत्यपूजयन् ।
5.62.4.e: Having heard the words that came from Angada's mouth, the bulls among vanaras praised him for his generous approval.

5.62.5.t: पूजयित्वाङ्गदं सर्वे वानरा वानरर्षभम् जग्मुर्मधुवनं यत्र नदीवेग इव द्रुमम् ।
5.62.5.e: The vanaras praised Angada, the bull among vanaras and went to Madhuvanam swiftly like a fastflowing river going to uproot a tree.

5.62.8.t:
उत्पत्य च ततस्सर्वे वनपालान् समागतान् ।
ताडयन्ति स्म शतश स्सक्तान्मधुवने तदा
5.62.8.e: All the vanaras collected together, entered the Madhuvanam and attacked in many ways the guards protecting  the  garden.

5.62.11.t:
अपरे वृक्षमूले तु शाखां गृह्य व्यवस्थिताः ।
अत्यर्थं च मदग्लानाः पर्णान्यास्तीर्य शेरते
5.62.11.e: Some took branches of trees and rested at the root of trees. Some totally languid lay down spreading leaves due to drinking of sweet drinks.

5.62.13.t:
केचित् क्ष्वेलां प्रकुर्वन्ति केचित् कूजन्ति हृष्टवत् ।
हरयोमधुना मत्ताः केचित्सुप्ता महीतले
5.62.13.e: Some roared, some warbled happily, some felt drowsy, drinking honey and some dropped off to sleep on the ground.

5.62.14.t:
कृत्वा केचिद्धसन्त्यन्ये केचित्कुर्वन्ति चेतरत् ।
कृत्वा केचिद्वदन्त्यन्ये केचिद्बुध्यन्ति चेतरत्
5.62.14.e: Some made others laugh, some provoked others and some thought of doing something else having got over the intoxication.

5.62.15.t:
येऽप्यत्र मधुपाला स्स्युः प्रेष्या दधिमुखस्य तु ।
तेऽपि तैर्वानरैर्भीमैः प्रतिषिद्धा दिशो गताः
5.62.15.e: All the guards engaged in protecting the garden were driven away in all directions by the fierce vanaras.

5.62.16.t:
जानुभिस्तु प्रकृष्टाश्च देवमार्गं प्रदर्शिताः ।
अब्रुवन् परमोद्विग्ना गत्वा दधिमुखं वचः
5.62.16.e: Some were dragged on their knees and tossed up. Some monkeys exhibited their private parts, showing indecent behaviour. Dadhimukha, highly disturbed at this, said:

5.62.18.t:
ततो दधिमुख: क्रुद्धो वनपस्तत्र वानरः ।
हतं मधुवनं श्रुत्वा सान्त्वयामास तान् हरीन्
5.62.18.e: Then Dadhimukha, the guardian of the garden became furious on the vanaras. Having heard from the guards that the garden was destroyed, he said soothing words to them.

5.62.19.t:
इहागच्छत गच्छामो वानरान् बलदर्पितान् ।
बलेन वारयिष्यामो मधु भक्षयतो वयम्
5.62.19.e: "Come, we will all go there to Madhuvanam and prevent forcibly the vanaras who have consumed honey proud of their power.

5.62.20.t:
श्रुत्वा दधिमुखस्येदं वचनं वानरर्षभाः ।
पुनर्वीरा मधुवनं तेनैव सहसा ययुः
5.62.20.e: "The heroes, bulls among vanaras, heard Dadhimukha and quickly entered Madhuvanam along with him.

5.62.21.t:
मध्ये चैषां दधिमुखः प्रगृह्य तरसा तरुम् ।
समभ्यधावद्वेगेन ते च सर्वे प्लवङ्गमाः
5.62.21.e: On the way, the energetic Dadhimukha took up a tree and ran to the leaping vanaras swiftly with guards following him.

5.62.22.t:
ते शिलाः पादपांश्चापि पर्वतांश्चापि वानराः ।
गृहीत्वाऽऽभ्यगमन् क्रुद्धा यत्र ते कपिकुञ्जराः
5.62.22.e: The furious vanara guards lifted rocks, trees and even mountains and went behind Dadhimukha the elephant among the vanaras.

5.62.23.t:
ते स्वामिवचनं वीरा हृदयेष्ववसज्य तत् ।
त्वरया ह्यभ्यधावन्त सालतालशिलायुधाः
5.62.23.e: The heroic vanaras held Sala and Tala trees and rushed at once keeping their leader's words in mind.

5.62.25.t:
अथ दृष्ट्वा दधिमुखं क्रुद्धं वानरपुङ्गवाः ।
अभ्यधावन्त वेगेन हनुमत्प्रमुखास्तदा
5.62.25.e: Having seen the fury of Dadhimukha, Hanuman the leader of the vanaras went to him swiftly.

w: not understnding that (I am his granduncle)
5.62.27.t:
मदान्धश्च न वेदैनमार्यकोऽयं ममेति सः ।
अथैनं निष्पिपेषाशु वेगवद्वसुधातले
5.62.27.e: "Blinded by arrogance, the prince pushed him (Dadhimukha) on the floor forcibly,  forgetting that he was his revered granduncle.

5.62.30.t:
स कथञ्चिद्विमुक्तस्स्तैर्वानरैर्वानरर्षभः ।
उवाचैकान्तमाश्रित्य भृत्यान् स्वान् समुपागतान्
5.62.30.e: Escaping from the vanaras with great difficulty, Dadhimukha,  a bull among monkeys, repaired to a secluded place and said to his servants:

5.62.32.t:
सर्वं चैवाङ्गदे दोषं श्रावयिष्यामि पार्थिवे ।
अमर्षी वचनं श्रुत्वा घातयिष्यति वानरान्
5.62.32.e: "I shall let the king know all the mistakes in Angada. Hearing these words he will grow furious and will have the vanaras killed."

5.62.33.t:
इष्टं मधुवनं ह्येतत्पार्थिवस्य महात्मनः ।
पितृपैतामहं दिव्यं देवैरपि दुरासदम्
5.62.33.e: 'Madhuvan has come down to us from our forefather's time. Dear to the king, its entry is prohibited even to the gods.

5.62.36.t:
एवमुक्त्वा दधिमुखो वनपालान्महाबलः ।
जगाम सहसोत्पत्य वनपालैस्समन्वितः
5.62.36.e: Powerful Dadhimukha having said that to the guardians of the garden rose up to the sky and went off with them.

5.62.37.t:
निमेषान्तरमात्रेण स हि प्राप्तो वनालयः ।
सहस्रांशुसुतो धीमान् सुग्रीवो यत्र वानरः
5.62.37.e: In a moment, Dadhimukha reached the place where wise Sugriva, the son of Sungod was there

w: with a painful expression on the face
5.62.39.t:
सन्निपत्य महावीर्यस्सर्वैस्तै: परिवारितः ।
हरिर्दधिमुखः पालैः पालानां परमेश्वरः स दीनवदनो भूत्वा कृत्वा शिरसि चाञ्जलिम् ।
सुग्रीवस्य शुभौ मूर्ध्ना चरणौ पत्यपीडयत्
5.62.39.e: Dadhimukha, a great hero and king of the guards protecting Madhuvanam surrounded by his servants, with a sad expression on his face offered painful obeisance with folded hands bowing down his forehead at the feet of Sugriva. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये सुन्दरकाण्डे द्विषष्टितमस्सर्गः।। Thus ends the sixtysecond sarga of Sundarakanda of the holy Ramayana, the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

5.63.1.t:
ततो मूर्ध्ना निपतितं वानरं वानरर्षभः ।
दृष्ट्वैवोद्विग्नहृदयो वाक्यमेतदुवाच ह
5.63.1.e: Feeling anxious on seeing Dadhimukha touching his feet with his forehead, Sugriva, the bull among vanaras said:

5.63.2.t:
उत्तिष्ठोत्तिष्ठ कस्मात्त्वं पादयोः पतितो मम ।
अभयं ते भवेद्वीर सर्वमेवाभिधीयताम्
5.63.2.e: "O heroic Dadhimukha, get up. Tell me why you have fallen at my feet. I give you protection from all.

5.63.3.t:
स तु विश्वासितस्तेन सुग्रीवेण महात्मना ।
उत्थाय सुमहाप्राज्ञो वाक्यं दधिमुखोऽब्रवीत्
5.63.3.e: When great Sugriva gave assurance to wise Dadhimukha, he got up and said:

w: even at the time of Vali
5.63.4.t:
नैवर्क्षरजसा राजन्न त्वया नापि वालिना ।
वनं निसृष्टपूर्वं हि भक्षितं तच्च वानरैः
5.63.4.e: "O king in your time or even before, during the time of Vali, that (Madhuvanam) was forbidden for entry. Now it has been laid waste by the trespassing vanaras.

5.63.5.t:
एभिः प्रधर्षिताश्चैव वानरा वनरक्षिभिः ।
मधून्यचिन्तयित्वेमान् भक्षयन्ति पिबन्ति च
5.63.5.e: "Even though the garden guards forcibly tried to prevent them they did not care and have devoured all the honey.

w: raising to show (a sign of arrogance)
5.63.6.t:
शिष्टमत्रापविध्यन्ति भक्षयन्ति तथापरे ।
निवार्यमाणास्ते सर्वे भ्रुवो वै दर्शयन्ति हि
5.63.6.e: "Some have thrown off the leftovers, when others were prevented from drinking off the honey, they raised their eyebrows (to show their grouch).

5.63.7.t:
इमे हि संरब्धतरास्तथा तैस्सम्प्रधर्षिताः ।
वारयन्तो वनात्तस्मात्क्रुद्धैर्वानरपुङ्गवैः
5.63.7.e: "When the guards asked the vanaras to leave the garden the enraged vanaras misbehaved with them.

5.63.8.e: "O Sugriva the vanara guards were chased away by the many heroic monkeys, angry and redeyed.

5.63.9.t:
पाणिभिर्निहताः केचित्केचिज्जानुभिराहताः ।
प्रकृष्टाश्च यथाकामं देवमार्गं च दर्शिताः
5.63.9.e: "Some were struck with hands, some beaten on their knees and were dragged as they liked and showed up their private parts.

5.63.10.t:
एवमेते हताश्शूरास्त्वयि तिष्ठति भर्तरि ।
कृत्स्नं मधुवनं चैव प्रकामं तैः प्रभक्ष्यते
5.63.10.e: These heroes struck that way devoured the Madhuvanam on the earth at their will and devoured the honey even when you are there as king.

5.63.11.t:
एवं विज्ञाप्यमानं तं सुग्रीवं वानरर्षभम् ।
अपृच्छत्तं महाप्राज्ञो लक्ष्मणः परवीरहा
5.63.11.e: While Dadhimukha appealed thus to wise Sugriva, Lakshmana the killer of enemies happened to see them and enquired:

5.63.14.t:
आर्य लक्ष्मण सम्प्राह वीरो दधिमुखः कपिः ।
अङ्गदप्रमुखैर्वीरैर्भक्षितं मधु वानरैः विचित्य दक्षिणामाशामागतैर्हरिपुङ्गवैः ।
5.63.14.e: 'O venerable Lakshmana Dadhimukha as complaining that the fruits and honey have been consumed by the vanara heroes, Angada and others who have come after their search for Sita in the southern direction.

w: if they had not accomplished their purpose
5.63.15.t:
नैषामकृत्यानामीदृशस्स्यादुपक्रमः आगतैश्च प्रमथितं यथा मधुवनं हि तैः ।
धर्षितं च वनं कृत्स्नमुपयुक्तं च वानरैः
5.63.15.e: "Those vanaras having entered Madhuvanam and broken the trees are quite right. Had they not accomplished their purpose they would not have indulged themselves that way.

5.63.19.t: जाम्बवान्यत्र नेता स्यादङ्गदश्च महाबलः हनुमांश्चाप्यधिष्ठाता न तस्य गतिरन्यथा ।
5.63.19.e: Where Jambavan, Angada and Hanuman are leaders directing the task of the army it must have been accomplished.

5.63.20.t: अङ्गदप्रमुखैर्वीरैर्हतं मधुवनं किल वारयन्तश्च सहितास्तदा जानुभिराहताः ।
5.63.20.e: When Angada and the other heroes had destroyed the Madhuvana, and those with them obstructed it, they then fell at his knees.

5.63.21.t: एतदर्थमयं प्राप्तो वक्तुं मधुरवागिह नाम्ना दधिमुखो नाम हरिः प्रख्यातविक्रमः ।
5.63.21.e: "Here is Dadhimukha, a vanara, known for his valour and sweet tongue. He came here this incident to tell.

w: that which was given as boon
5.63.23.t: न चाप्यदृष्ट्वा वैदेहीं विश्रुताः पुरुषर्षभ वनं दत्तवरं दिव्यं धर्षयेयुर्वनौकसः ।
5.63.23.e: "If the renowned vanaras had not seen Vaidehi, they would not have entered the wonderful garden granted as boon (by Brahma).

5.63.24.t:
ततः प्रहृष्टो धर्मात्मा लक्ष्मणस्सह राघवः श्रुत्वा कर्णसुखां वाणीं सुग्रीववदनाच्च्युताम् ।
प्राहृष्यत भृशं रामो लक्ष्मणश्च महाबलः
5.63.24.e: "Then righteous Rama and Lakshmana rejoiced to hear the words of Sugriva, which were pleasing to the ears.

5.63.26.t:
श्रुत्वा दधिमुखस्येदं सुग्रीवस्सम्प्रहृष्य च ।
वनपालं पुनर्वाक्यं सुग्रीवः प्रत्यभाषत
5.63.26.e: Beautifulnecked Sugriva heard Dadhimukha, the protector of the garden, felt very glad and replied:

5.63.27.t:
प्रीतोऽस्मि सोऽहं यद्भुक्तं वनं तैः कृतकर्मभिः ।
मर्षितं मर्षणीयं च चेष्टितं कृतकर्मणाम्
5.63.27.e: "They went to the garden to drink only after having performed their duty. I am glad about it. Since they have accomplished the purpose, they are to be excused for their behaviour. I have pardoned them.

w: with the majesty of the lion
5.63.28.t:
इच्छामि शीघ्रं हनुमत्प्रधानान् शाखामृगांस्तान् मृगराजदर्पान् ।
द्रष्टुं कृतार्थान् सह राघवाभ्यां श्रोतुं च सीताधिगमे प्रयत्नम्
5.63.28.e: Those tree-dwelling vanaras led by Hanuman, with the majesty of lions and their purpose accomplished, came before Rama and the others.

5.63.29.t:
प्रीतिस्फीताक्षौ सम्प्रहृष्टौ कुमारौ दृष्ट्वा सिद्धार्थौ वानराणां च राजा ।
अङ्गैः संहृष्टैः कर्मसिद्धिं विदित्वा बाह्वोरासन्नां सोऽतिमात्रं ननन्द
5.63.29.e: "Beholding young Rama and Lakshmana extremely delighted, their eyes filled with joy out of fulfilment of the purpose, Sugriva who was also highly delighted felt an auspicious thrill on his limbs and knew that good time had come. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये सुन्दरकाण्डे त्रिषष्टितमस्सर्गः।। Thus ends the sixtythird sarga of Sundarakanda of the holy Ramayana, the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

5.64.2.t:
स प्रणम्य च सुग्रीवं राघवौ च महाबलौ ।
वानरैः सहितः शूरैर्दिवमेवोत्पपात ह
5.64.2.e: Dadhimukha offered his obeisance to Sugriva and the mighty Rama and Lakshmana  and rose up to the sky followed by the vanaras.

5.64.3.t:
स यथैवाऽगतः पूर्वं तथैव त्वरितं गतः ।
निपत्य गगनाद्भूमौतद्वनं प्रविवेश ह स प्रविष्टो मधुवनं ददर्श हरियूथपान् ।
विमदानुत्थितान्सर्वान् मेहमानान्मधूदकम्
5.64.3.e: Descending into Madhuvanam, Dadhimukha saw all the monkey troops free from intoxication (of honeywine).

5.64.5.t:
स तानुपागमद्वीरो बद्ध्वा करपुटाञ्जलिम् ।
उवाच वचनं श्लक्ष्णमिदं हृष्टवदङ्गदम्
5.64.5.e: Heroic Dadhimukha went to Angada, holding his cupped palms reverentially and spoke these conciliatory words with joy:

5.64.6.t:
सौम्य रोषो न कर्तव्यो यदेतत्परिवारितम् ।
अज्ञानाद्रक्षिभिः क्रोधाद्भवन्तः प्रतिषेधिताः
5.64.6.e: "O handsome one, do not react harshly at these guards who have obstructed your companions out of ignorance and fury.

5.64.8.t:
आख्यातं हि मया गत्वा पितृव्यस्य तवानघ ।
इहोपयातं सर्वेषामेतेषां वनचारिणाम्
