5.64.8.e: "O blameless prince I have already told your father's elder brother and all the forestdwellers about your arrival here.

5.64.9.t:
स त्वदागमनं श्रुत्वा सहैभिर्हरियूथपैः ।
प्रहृष्टो न तु रुष्टोऽसौ वनं श्रुत्वा प्रधर्षितम्
5.64.9.e: "He was not angry at your destruction of the garden. On the other hand, he was very glad to hear about your arrival.

5.64.10.t:
प्रहृष्टो मां पितृव्यस्ते सुग्रीवो वानरेश्वरः ।
शीघ्रं प्रेषय सर्वांस्तानिति होवाच पार्थिवः
5.64.10.e: "Your father's brother, Sugriva, the lord of vanaras felt very glad and indeed asked me to send you quickly."

5.64.11.t:
श्रुत्वा दधिमुखस्येदं वचनं श्लक्ष्णमङ्गदः ।
अब्रवीत्तान् हरिश्रेष्ठो वाक्यं वाक्यविशारदः
5.64.11.e: At these good words from Dadhimukha, Angada, the monkey leader, an eloquent speaker said this:.

5.64.12.t:
शङ्के श्रुतोऽयं वृत्तान्तो रामेण हरियूथपाः ।
तत्क्षमं नेह नः स्थातुं कृते कार्ये परन्तपाः
5.64.12.e: "O scorcher of enemies I presume Rama has already heard the news of our arrival on accomplishment of the task. Hence it is not proper for us to tarry here.

5.64.13.t:
पीत्वा मधु यथाकामं विश्रान्ता वनचारिणः ।
किं शेषं गमनं तत्र सुग्रीवो यत्र मे गुरुः
5.64.13.e: "The vanaras of the forest have taken rest after drinking as much honey as they desired. What is left here to do? We have to go wherever Sugriva is."

5.64.15.t:
नाज्ञापयितुमीशोऽहं युवराजोऽस्मि यद्यपि ।
अयुक्तं कृतकर्माणो यूयं धर्षयितुं मया
5.64.15.e: "Even though I am heir apparent, it is not proper for me to order you.You have accomplished the purpose and to command you is not befitting on my part."

5.64.17.t:
एवं वक्ष्यति को राजन् प्रभुस्सन्वानरर्षभ ।
ऐश्वर्यमदमत्तो हि सर्वोऽहमिति मन्यते
5.64.17.e: "O king O bull among monkeys we think you are an exception to those to whom prosperity brings arrogance.

5.64.19.t:
सर्वे वयमपि प्राप्तास्तत्र गन्तुं कृतक्षणाः ।
स यत्र हरिवीराणां सुग्रीवः पतिरव्ययः
5.64.19.e: "All of us have come here. Where that immortal Sugriva, lord of the vanara heroes, is, thither we have resolved to go."

5.64.20.t:
त्वया ह्यनुक्तैर्हरिभिर्नैव शक्यं पदात्पदम् ।
क्वचिद्गन्तुं हरिश्रेष्ठ ब्रूमः सत्यमिदं तु ते
5.64.20.e: "O Angada the best of vanaras without your command none will find it possible to put forward even a single step."

5.64.21.t:
एवं तु वदतां तेषामङ्गदः प्रत्युवाच ह ।
बाढं गच्छाम इत्युक्त्वा खमुत्पेतुर्महाबलाः
5.64.21.e: Thus addressed by all the vanaras, Angada said 'Well, let us go'. Then the powerful vanaras rose up the sky.

w: as if there is no sky
5.64.22.t:
उत्पतन्तमनूत्पेतु स्सर्वे ते हरियूथपाः ।
कृत्वाकाशं निराकाशं यन्त्रोत्क्षिप्ता इवाचलाः
5.64.22.e: All the vanara troops sprang up into the air as though there was no sky, like stones shattered by machines from the  mountains rise up.

5.64.24.t:
अङ्गदे ह्यननुप्राप्ते सुग्रीवो वानराधिपः ।
उवाच शोकोपहतं रामं कमललोचनम्
5.64.24.e: Seeing the griefstricken, lotuseyed Rama, the lord of the vanaras Sugriva said this before the arrival of Angada:

5.64.28.t:
पितृपैतामहं चैतत्पूर्वकैरभिरक्षितम् ।
न मे मधुवनं हन्यादहृष्टः प्लवगेश्वरः कौसल्यासुप्रजा राम समाश्वसिहि सुव्रत ।
5.64.28.e: "If Angada, lord of the vanaras had not been happy, he would not have destroyed the Madhuvanam of my father's and my grandfather's time. O Rama, follower of righteous practices, Kausalya has an excellent son in you. Trust me.

w: in the pride of Hanuman's success
5.64.32.t:
मा भूश्चिन्तासमायुक्तस्सम्प्रत्यमितविक्रमः ततः किलकिलाशब्दं शुश्रावासन्नमम्बरे ।
हनुमत्कर्मदृप्तानां नार्धतां काननौकसाम् किष्किन्धामुपयातानां सिद्धिं कथयतामिव ।
5.64.32.e: "You are extremely valiant and it is unbecoming of you to be anxious at this time Rama. Just then chatterings of the monkeys were heard from the sky as they roared in pride talking of Hanuman's achievement. Having successfully completed the errand, they have arrived at Kishkinda.

w: Angada the chief of the army of monkeys
5.64.36.t: तेऽङ्गदप्रमुखा वीराः प्रहृष्ठाश्च मुदान्विताः निपेतुर्हरिराजस्य समीपे राघवस्य च ।
5.64.36.e: Angada the chief along with the heroic monkeys very joyfully and exuberantly descended close to Sugriva, the king of monkeys and Rama.

5.64.37.t: हनुमांश्च महाबाहुः प्रणम्य शिरसा ततः नियतामक्षतां देवीं राघवाय न्यवेदयत् ।
5.64.37.e: Then the strongarmed Hanuman with his head bowed down offered salutations and reported, 'Divine lady Sita with her constant devotion to Sri Rama is sound in body'.

5.64.38.t: दृष्टा देवीति हनुमद्वदनादमृतोपमम् आकर्ण्य वचनं रामो हर्षमाप सलक्ष्मणः ।
5.64.38.e: On hearing the nectarlike words from Hanuman that Sita was found, Rama and Lakshmana were delighted.

5.64.39.t: निश्चितार्थं ततस्तस्मिन् सुग्रीवं पवनात्मजे लक्ष्मणः प्रीतिमान् प्रीतं बहुमानादवैक्षत ।
5.64.39.e: Sugriva and Lakshmana glanced at Hanuman respectfully with affection thinking surely Hanuman alone has succeeded.

5.65.1.t:
ततः प्रस्रवणं शैलं ते गत्वा चित्रकाननम् ।
प्रणम्य शिरसा रामं लक्ष्मणं च महाबलम् युवराजं पुरस्कृत्य सुग्रीवमभिवाद्य च ।
प्रवृत्तिमथ सीतायाः प्रवक्तुमुपचक्रमुः
5.65.1.e: Thereafter the vanaras arrived at the Prasrvana mount, with wonderful forests and bowed down to Sri Rama and mighty Lakshaman and Sugriva placing their leader, heir apparent in front. Then they began telling the story of Sita and her state.

5.65.3.t:
रावणान्तः पुरे रोधं राक्षसीभिश्च तर्जनम् ।
रामे समनुरागं च यश्चायं समयः कृतः एतदाख्यान्ति ते सर्वे हरयो रामसन्निधौ ।
5.65.3.e: The monkeys in Rama's presence narrated all about Sita's detention in Ravana's Ashoka garden, the ogresses threatening her and the time limit fixed by Ravana (for her survival).

w: who was aware of Sita's position
5.65.6.t:
रामस्य गदितं श्रुत्वा हरयो रामसन्निधौ ।
चोदयन्ति हनूमन्तं सीतावृत्तान्तकोविदम्
5.65.6.e: On hearing the words from Rama, the vanaras requested Hanuman who was aware of  Sita's position to tell Rama all about her.

w: to the direction in which she was located
5.65.7.t:
श्रुत्वा तु वचनं तेषां हनुमान्मारुतात्मजः ।
प्रणम्य शिरसा देव्यै सीतायै तां दिशं प्रति उवाच वाक्यं वाक्यज्ञस्सीताया दर्शनं यथा ।
5.65.7.e: The son of the Wind god, Hanuman who was wise in speech heard the words of Rama, offered salutations to Sita in the direction in which she was located and narrated the story about her discovery.

5.65.7.1.t:
उवाच वाक्यं वाक्यज्ञः सीताया दर्शनं यथा ।
तं मणिं काञ्चनं दिव्यं दीप्यमानं स्वतेजसा
5.65.7.1.e: Skilled in speech, he told the sight of Sita just as it was, and showed that heavenly golden gem blazing with its own splendour.

5.65.8.t: समुद्रं लङ्घयित्वाहं शतयोजनमायतम् अगच्छं जानकीं सीतां मार्गमाणो दिदृक्षया ।
5.65.8.e: "Having crossed the sea consisting of a hundred yojanas in quest of Vaidehi, I found her.

5.65.11.t: दृष्टा मे राक्षसीमध्ये तर्ज्यमाना मुहुर्मुहुः राक्षसीभिर्विरूपाभी रक्षिता प्रमदावने ।
5.65.11.e: "I found her in the beautiful garden guarded by hideous ogresses threatening her again and again৷৷

w: in the inner palace of Ravana
wearing a single braid( a mark of desolation)
5.65.12.t:
दुःख मासाद्यते देवी तथाऽदुःखोचिता सती रावणान्तः पुरे रुद्धा राक्षसीभि स्सुरक्षिता ।
एकवेणीधरा दीना त्वयि चिन्तापरायणा अधःशय्या विवर्णाङ्गी पद्मिनीव हिमागमे ।
रावणाद्विनिवृत्तार्था मर्तव्यकृतनिश्चया देवी कथञ्चित्काकुत्स्थ त्वन्मना मार्गिता मया ।
5.65.12.e: "Sita, who did not deserve and yet was full of grief was detained by Ravana in his inner palace, guarded by ogresses. She had single braid (a sign of desolation), was pathetic,  and totally absorbed in your thought. She was lying on bare ground with her limbs turned pale, like lotus in winter. She was averse to Ravana and was determined to commit suicide. She has only Rama in her mind. Somehow I found her.

w: all about the glory of Ikshvaku race
5.65.15.t: इक्ष्वाकुवंशविख्यातिं शनैः कीर्तयतानघ सा मया नरशार्दूल विश्वासमुपपादिता ।
5.65.15.e: "O sinless one O tiger among men To inspire confidence in her I praised the glory of your Ikshvaku dynasty.

5.65.18.t:
एवं मया महाभागा दृष्टा जनकनन्दिनी ।
उग्रेण तपसा युक्ता त्वद्भक्त्या पुरुषर्षभ
5.65.18.e: "O bull among men I saw Janaki,the delight of Janaka, a formidable lady filled with devotion to you and richly endowed with austerity.

w: with an anecdote of a crow
5.65.19.t:
अभिज्ञानं च मे दत्तं यथा वृत्तं तवान्तिके ।
चित्रकूटे महाप्राज्ञ वायसं प्रति राघव
5.65.19.e: "O wise one, with your ring given her, she told me an anecdote of a crow that took place at Chitrakuta.

5.65.21.t:
अयं चास्मै प्रदातव्यो यत्नात्सुपरिरक्षितः ।
ब्रुवता वचनान्येवं सुग्रीवस्योपशृण्वतः
5.65.21.e: 'Within hearing of Sugriva, tell him about your efforts. Present this(signet) to Rama carefully preserved by me.

5.65.23.t:
एष निर्यातितश्श्रीमान्मया ते वारि सम्भवः ।
एतं दृष्ट्वा प्रहृष्यामि व्यसने त्वामिवानघ
5.65.23.e: 'O sinless one tell Rama that this auspicious Chudamani born in the ocean is sent to him and I was gazing at it as if it was him (Rama) and feeling happy.

w: in the inner palace of Ravana
5.65.25.t: इति मामब्रवीत्सीता कृशाङ्गी धर्मचारिणी रावणान्तः पुरे रुद्धा मृगीवोत्फुल्ललोचना ।
5.65.25.e: "With her limbs emaciated through austerities detained in Ravana's inner palace, eyes wide open in fear, Sita said this to me:

5.66.3.t:
यथैव धेनु स्स्रवति स्नेहाद्वत्सस्य वत्सला ।
तथा ममापि हृदयं मणिरत्नस्य दर्शनात्
5.66.3.e: "Just as a cow fond of its calf begins to distil milk from its teats at the sight of the calf, so does my heart melt at the sight of this excellent jewel.

5.66.6.t:
इमं दृष्ट्वा मणिश्रेष्ठं यथा तातस्य दर्शनम् ।
अद्यास्म्यवगतस्सौम्य वैदेहस्य तथा विभोः
5.66.6.e: "O noble Sugriva now when I see this excellent jewel, I get direct sight of my father and king of Videha (in the same way as I obtained the sight of Sita).

5.66.10.t:
चिरं जीवति वैदेही यदि मासं धरिष्यति ।
क्षणं सौम्य न जीवेयं विना तामसितेक्षणाम्
5.66.10.e: (Addressing Hanuman again) "O dear, if she can live for a month it is living for long. I would not live for a moment without the black-eyed Vaidehi.

5.66.12.t:
कथं सा मम सुश्रोणी भीरुभीरु स्सती सदा ।
भयावहानां घोराणां मध्ये तिष्ठति रक्षसाम्
5.66.12.e: "She is always very timid. How can my fairhipped beloved remain in the midst of dreadful and fearsome demons?

5.66.13.t:
शारद स्तिमिरोन्मुक्तो नूनं चन्द्रं इवांबुधैः ।
आवृतं वदनं तस्या न विराजति राक्षसैः
5.66.13.e: "Her face resembling the autumnal Moon bereft of its stain, though covered with rainclouds does not shine so bright.

5.66.14.t:
किमाह सीता हनुमंस्तत्त्वतः कथयाद्य मे ।
एतेन खलु जीविष्ये भेषजेनातुरो यथा
5.66.14.e: "O Hanuman Tell me now truly what has been told by her. I am eager to know. Indeed, it will keep me alive just as medicne does. (I shall survive on the strength of her message)

5.67.1.t:
एवमुक्तस्तु हनुमान् राघवेण महात्मना ।
सीताया भाषितं सर्वं न्यवेदयत राघवे
5.67.1.e: Thus asked by Sri Rama, Hanuman repeated everything spoken by Sita to Rama.

5.67.4.t:
पर्यायेण च सुप्तस्त्वं देव्यङ्के भरताग्रज ।
पुनश्च किल पक्षी स देव्या जनयति व्यथाम्
5.67.4.e: "O Bharata's brother, when Sita awoke from sleep you slept on her lap. The same crow again hurt her.

w: woke you up and informed you.
5.67.6.t:
वायसेन च तेनैव सततं बाध्यमानया ।
बोधितः किल देव्या त्वं सुखसुप्तः परन्तप
5.67.6.e: "O scorcher of enemies pained by the crow hurting her repeatedly, while you were sleeping happily, she woke you up and informed you about it.

5.67.9.t:
निरीक्षमाणस्सहसा वायसं समवैक्षथाः ।
नखै स्सरुधिरैस्तीक्ष्णैस्तामेवाभिमुखं स्थितम्
5.67.9.e: 'Seeing all over, at once I glanced at the crow that stood in front of her with sharp bloodstained nails'.

5.67.11.t:
ततस्तस्मिन्महाबाहो कोपसंवर्तितेक्षणः ।
वायसे त्वं कृथाः क्रूरां मतिं मतिमतां वर
5.67.11.e: 'O longarmed, wise and revered Rama, then in anguish you took a cruel decision'.

w: by the mantra of the weapon of Brahma
like the fire of the demon's day
5.67.12.t:
स दर्भं संस्तराद्गृह्य ब्रह्मास्त्रेण ह्ययोजयः ।
स दीप्त इव कालाग्निर्जज्वालाभिमुखः खगम्
5.67.12.e: 'You took out a blade of grass from your mat and chanted the mantra to invoke the weapon of Brahma (Brahmastra) and hurled it on the crow. It blazed like the fire of the doom's day.

5.67.13.t:
क्षिप्तवांस्त्वं प्रदीप्तं हि दर्भं तं वायसं प्रति ।
ततस्तु वायसं दीप्तस्स दर्भोऽनुजगाम ह
5.67.13.e: 'You hurled the blazing blade of grass on to the crow. That burning blade of grass chased the crow.

5.67.14.t:
स पित्रा च परित्यक्तस्सुरैश्च समहर्षिभिः ।
त्रीन् लोकान् सम्परिक्रम्य त्रातारं नाधिगच्छति
5.67.14.e: 'He was abandoned by his father, even by great sages and gods. Then he went round the three worlds but could not find a saviour.

5.67.19.t:
तव राम रणे शक्तास्तथा प्रतिसमासितुम् ।
तव वीर्यवतः कश्चिन्मयि यद्यस्ति सम्भ्रमः
5.67.19.e: "— are able so to contend with you in battle, Rama. If you the valorous have any concern for me —

5.67.20.t:
क्षिप्रं सुनिशितैर्बाणैर्हन्यतां युधि रावणः ।
भ्रातुरादेशमाज्ञाय लक्ष्मणो वा परंतपः
5.67.20.e: "— let Ravana be slain swiftly in battle with keen shafts; or let Lakshmana, scorcher of foes, receive his brother's command.

5.67.23.t:
समर्थौ सहितौ यन्मां न रक्षेते परंतपौ ।
वैदेह्या वचनं श्रुत्वा करुणं साधुभाषितम्
5.67.23.e: "— in that those two scorchers of foes, though able and together, do not protect me." Having heard the piteous and well-spoken word of Vaidehi,

w: their zeal roused by the sight of you
5.67.27.t:
त्वदर्शनकृतोत्साहौ लङ्कां भस्मीकरिष्यतः ।
हत्वा च समरे रौद्रं रावणं सहबान्धवम्
5.67.27.e: "their zeal roused by the sight of you, shall reduce Lanka to ashes; and having slain in battle the terrible Ravana with his kinsmen,

5.67.28.t:
राघवस्त्वां वरारोहे स्वपुरी नयिता ध्रुवम् ।
यत् तु रामो विजानीयादभिज्ञानमनिन्दिते
5.67.28.e: "Raghava shall assuredly lead you to his own city, fair one. And what token, blameless one, Rama would recognise,

5.67.29.t:
प्रीतिसंजननं तस्य प्रदातुं तत् त्वमर्हसि ।
साभिवीक्ष्य दिशः सर्वा वेण्युद्ग्रथनमुत्तमम्
5.67.29.e: "begetting joy in him, that you should give me." She looked round all the quarters, and from her garment

5.67.34.t:
यद् द्रक्ष्यसि महाबाहुं रामं कमललोचनम् ।
लक्ष्मणं च महाबाहुं देवरं मे यशस्विनम्
5.67.34.e: "'in that you shall see the mighty-armed and lotus-eyed Rama, and the mighty-armed and illustrious Lakshmana, my brother-in-law.'

5.67.35.t:
सीतयाप्येवमुक्तोऽहमब्रुवं मैथिली तथा ।
पृष्ठमारोह मे देवि क्षिप्रं जनकनन्दनि
5.67.35.e: "Addressed thus by Sita, I spoke to Maithili: 'Lady, delight of Janaka, mount swiftly upon my back,

5.67.36.t:
यावत्ते दर्शयाम्यद्य ससुग्रीवं सलक्ष्मणम् ।
राघवं च महाभागे भर्तारमसितेक्षणे
5.67.36.e: "'that today I may show you your lord Raghava, greatly blessed and dark-eyed one, with Sugriva and with Lakshmana.'

5.67.38.t:
पुरा च यदहं वीर स्पृष्टा गात्रेषु रक्षसा ।
तत्राहं किं करिष्यामि कालेनोपनिपीडिता
5.67.38.e: "'And formerly, hero, I was touched upon the limbs by the rakshasa; what could I do therein, sore pressed by time?

5.67.39.t:
गच्छ त्वं कपिशार्दूल यत्र तौ नृपतेः सुतौ ।
इत्येवं सा समाभाष्य भूयः संदेष्टमास्थिता
5.67.39.e: "'Go, tiger among monkeys, where those two sons of the king are.'" Having spoken thus, she set herself to send a further message.

5.67.40.t:
हनूमन् सिंहसंकाशौ तावुभौ रामलक्ष्मणौ ।
सुग्रीवं च सहामात्यं सर्वान् ब्रूया अनामयम्
5.67.40.e: "'Hanuman, ask after the welfare of those two, Rama and Lakshmana, like two lions, and of Sugriva with his ministers, and of all.

w: flood of sorrow that hems me in
5.67.41.t:
यथा च स महाबाहुर्मी तारयति राघवः ।
अस्माद्दुःखाम्बुसंरोधात् तत् त्वमाख्यातुमर्हसि
5.67.41.e: "'And how that mighty-armed Raghava shall carry me across this flood of sorrow that hems me in — that you should declare.

w: O foremost hero of the vanaras
5.67.42.t:
इदं च तीव्र मम शोकवेगं रक्षोभिरेभिः परिभर्त्सनं च ।
ब्रूयास्तु रामस्य गतः समीपं शिवश्च तेऽध्वास्तु हरिप्रवीर
5.67.42.e: "'Tell Rama, when you have come to his presence, of this fierce surge of grief of mine and of the threatening of these rakshasas; and may your road be auspicious, foremost hero of the vanaras.'"

5.67.43.t:
एतत् तवार्या नृप संयता सा सीता वचः प्राह विषादपूर्वम् ।
एतच्च बुद्ध्वा गदितं यथा त्वं श्रद्धत्स्व सीतां कुशलां समग्राम्
5.67.43.e: Self-restrained, that noble lady Sita spoke this word to you in sorrow, O king. Understanding it as it was uttered, believe Sita to be wholly in safety.

5.68.1.t:
अथाहमुत्तरं देव्या पुनरुक्त स्ससम्भ्रमम् ।
तव स्नेहान्नरव्याघ्र सौहार्दादनुमान्य वै
5.68.1.e: "O tiger among men In view of her regards for me and and her love for you she was confident and once again addressed me:

5.68.4.t:
मम चाप्यल्पभाग्यायास्सान्निध्यात्तव वीर्यवन् ।
अस्य शोकविपाकस्य मुहूर्तं स्याद्विमोक्षणम्
5.68.4.e: 'O valiant (Hanuman) by your presence here, the less fortunate me, will be relieved of sorrow for a while.

5.68.6.t:
तवादर्शनजश्शोको भूयो मां परितापयेत् ।
दुःखाद्दुःखपराभूतां दुर्गतां दुःखभागिनीम्
5.68.6.e: I am an unfortunate one, afflicted by sorrow and tormented (by demons). If I am not able to see you I will be lamenting in grief.

5.68.10.t:
तदस्मिन् कार्यनिर्योगे वीरैवं दुरतिक्रमे ।
किं पश्यसि समाधानं ब्रूहि कार्यविदां वरः
5.68.10.e: 'O heroic Hanuman you know how to succeed. But I wish to know what expedient you have to accomplish which is difficult by all means. O foremost vanara, please tell me .

5.68.12.t:
बलै स्समग्रैर्यदि मां हत्वा रावणमाहवे ।
विजयी स्वां पुरीं रामो नयेत्तत्स्याद्यशस्करम्
5.68.12.e: 'When Rama slays Ravana and his entire army and takes me to his city after becoming victorious it will add glory to him.

w: one who is a slayer of the enemy army
5.68.14.t:
बलैस्तु सङ्कुलां कृत्वा लङ्कां परबलार्दनः ।
मां नयेद्यदि काकुत्स्थस्तत्तस्य सदृशं भवेत्
5.68.14.e: 'If Rama, the slayer of the enemy army, could fill Lanka with his arrows and take me that will be a good sight for him to see.

5.68.16.t:
तदर्थोपहितं वाक्यं प्रश्रितं हेतुसंहितम् ।
निशम्याहं तत श्शेषं वाक्यमुत्तरमब्रुवम्
5.68.16.e: "Hearing the meaningful, courteous and reasonable words of Sita, I replied :

5.68.20.e: 'O great lady the mighty vanaras of extraordinary strength can fly with the wind and have  even circumambulated the earth.

5.68.24.t:
मम पृष्ठगतौ तौ च चन्द्रसूर्याविवोदितौ ।
त्वत्सकाशं महाभागे नृसिंहावागमिष्यतः
5.68.24.e: 'O noble lady the lions among men, Rama and Lakshmana who resemble Sun and Moon will ascend on my back and reach here.

5.68.25.t:
अरिघ्नं सिंहसङ्काशं क्षिप्रं द्रक्ष्यसि राघवम् ।
लक्ष्मणं च धनुष्पाणिं लङ्काद्वारमुपस्थितम्
5.68.25.e: 'You will see the lionlike Rama, a slayer of enemies and Lakshmana wielding bow in hand standing at the entrance of Lanka very soon.

5.68.29.t:
ततो मया वाग्भिरदीनभाषिणा शिवाभिरिष्टाभिरभिप्रसादिता ।
जगाम शान्तिं मम मैथिलात्मजा तवापि शोकेन तदाभिपीडिता
5.68.29.e: Sita though afflicted heard from me that you were also in excessive grief on account of separation from her and from my soothing, auspicious and welcome words, she derived comfort and remained quiet. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये सुन्दरकाण्डे अष्टषष्टितमस्सर्गः।। Thus ends the sixtyeighth sarga of Sundarakanda of the holy Ramayana, the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

savarna_dirgha.title: Two like vowels merge
savarna_dirgha.note: When the same vowel meets itself, the pair simply becomes one long vowel.

guna_vrddhi.title: अ raises the vowel after it
guna_vrddhi.note: अ and आ have no semi-vowel to turn into, so they vanish and push the following vowel up a grade instead.

yan.title: The vowel becomes a semi-vowel
yan.note: इ, उ and ऋ cannot sit beside an unlike vowel, so they harden into य्, व् or र्.

vowel_other.title: Vowels meet
vowel_other.note: Two vowels adjust to each other.

visarga_to_r.title: Visarga becomes र्
visarga_to_r.note: Before a voiced sound, a visarga that stands for an underlying र् returns to it.

visarga_a_to_o.title: अः becomes ओ
visarga_a_to_o.note: Releasing the breath after अ rounds the lips, and अ + उ is ओ.

visarga_aa_drop.title: आः becomes आ
visarga_aa_drop.note: आ is already long, so the visarga after it simply drops.

visarga_to_fricative.title: Visarga becomes a hissing sound
visarga_to_fricative.note: Before a voiceless sound the visarga turns into the fricative made at the same place in the mouth — स्, श् or ष्.

visarga_dropped.title: The visarga falls away
visarga_dropped.note: The visarga is lost where holding it would interrupt the flow.

anusvara.title: म् becomes anusvara
anusvara.note: A final म् before a consonant softens to the pure nasal hum ं.

jastva.title: Voicing matches
jastva.note: A voiceless consonant becomes voiced so the throat need not stop and start.

anunasika.title: The consonant turns nasal
anunasika.note: Turning the nose on suddenly is hard, so the earlier consonant nasalises first.

scutva.title: The dental turns palatal
scutva.note: A dental prepares for the palate that follows by moving there early.

stutva.title: The dental curls back
stutva.note: A dental anticipates a retroflex by curling the tongue in advance.

consonant_other.title: The consonant adapts
consonant_other.note: The first consonant shifts to sit comfortably before the next.
